cards.method: Analytic OLS on a CLOSED formula: a deterministic time trend (linear/quadratic) + the detrended series, or response ~ named numeric predictor columns
cards.when: a fast deterministic (analytic QR, no seed) linear model in the data layer: removing a deterministic trend (ols_trend->detrended) or a simple regression on explicitly named numeric columns (ols_regress); the formula is ALWAYS closed (an enum or bare names) through reformulate
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); a stochastic trend or unit root -> differencing and the unit-root tests of #2 (not a deterministic detrend, which would be spurious); categorical terms, interactions, weighted least squares or an offset (a numeric-only closed design); residual diagnostics -> pass the model handle to #76/#77

alternatives.criterion: explicit macro conventions (growth/deflate/rebase) rather than a model
a flexible/non-parametric trend rather than a low-order polynomial
the question is detrending vs differencing (trend- vs difference-stationary)

output_key_fields: coefficients: long-format -> term/estimate/std_error/statistic(t)/p_value (records)
glance: glance -> r_squared/adj_r_squared/sigma/AIC/BIC/log_lik/df_residual/nobs
fitted/residuals: numeric vectors; ols_trend adds detrended (=the trend residuals); n/k observations/parameters
model: the fitted lm — a producer handle (RDS bucket) for diagnostics/prediction nodes
interpretation_traps: gaps and infinities: the gates reject them up front — there is NO silent row-dropping that would change the sample (impute with #80 first)
detrend vs difference: ols_trend removes a DETERMINISTIC trend; on a unit-root series the residuals stay non-stationary -> difference instead
collinearity: perfectly collinear predictors leave a blank coefficient SILENTLY; here it is a rank-deficiency stop; n==k (saturated) gives sigma=NaN, gated by requiring n > k
sources: Wooldridge Introductory Econometrics (deterministic trend/detrending); Hamilton Time Series Analysis ch.3 (the trend- vs difference-stationary caveat)

cards.method: Bootstrap unit-root tests robust to heterogeneity/non-stationary volatility/missing data (boot ADF / union / panel GM / order of integration)
cards.when: unit root/stationarity when the asymptotic critical values do not apply (heteroskedasticity/nonstationary volatility); a residual bootstrap instead of fixed tables; single series (boot_adf/boot_union), panel GM (boot_panel, H0=all have a UR), or the order of integration + stationarisation (order_integration -> diff_data feeder)
cards.when_not: fixed critical-value tables suffice -> #2/#1; KPSS, whose H0 is stationarity; seasonal roots -> #89 HEGY; a fixed-N panel -> #6; charts (the frontend); the raw joint and FDR routines as direct nodes (they are reachable only through boot_order_integration)

alternatives.criterion: robust to the arbitrary choice of deterministics/detrending (a union of 4 specs)
an a-priori specification; QD ⇒ DF-GLS, more powerful near unity
general and robust; the moving- and stationary-block bootstraps do NOT handle unbalanced data or gaps; the stationary and wild variants are not for panels
the asymptotic critical values do apply — faster, no bootstrap

output_key_fields: statistic/p_value/estimate (gamma; blank for the union test)/stationary/decision/selected_lag(s)/alpha/seed
boot_panel: statistic(Group-Mean)/some_stationary + individual_statistics/pvalues/estimates/selected_lags (N×specs matrices) + series_names
order_integration: order_int (named I(d) per series) + classification + diff_data (the stationarised TxN matrix — a PRODUCER, register->Parquet)
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: H0=unit root ⇒ p<alpha ⇒ STATIONARY (the OPPOSITE of KPSS, where rejection ⇒ non-stationary)
the panel H0 is that ALL series have a UR; rejection ⇒ SOME are stationary (NOT all) — run a per-series follow-up
the union test has no single gamma across the four combinations, so its estimate is blank by definition — NOT an error
gaps: a silent trim of the leading and trailing values, then an internal error -> a hard no-gaps gate (run #80 first)
the seed is MANDATORY (the bootstrap is stochastic); do_parallel=False for determinism and caching
sources: Smeekes & Wilms 2023 JSS 106(12):1-39 (bootstrap unit root tests)
Palm, Smeekes & Urbain 2011, J. Econometrics 163(1):85-104 (panel GM test)
Smeekes & Wijler 2020, Unit roots and cointegration (order of integration)
precondition_tools: boot_adf
boot_union

cards.method: Covariate-Augmented Dickey-Fuller (CADF) unit-root test — the power gain from stationary covariates (Hansen 1995); a plain ADF when no covariates are supplied
cards.when: a unit root in a univariate series when stationary, correlated covariates are available (CADF is more powerful than ADF); or a plain ADF with full p-values and automatic lag selection when no covariates are supplied
cards.when_not: no genuinely stationary covariate -> a plain ADF/PP (#1) or #2; H0 = stationarity, the reverse polarity -> KPSS; a seasonal unit root -> #89; a structural break -> unitroot_zivot_andrews; a non-stationary X invalidates the theory

alternatives.criterion: you want the classic critical-value tables without covariates
fast univariate screening without covariates
automatic lag selection within [min,max]; the default 'none' pins a fixed max_lag_y

output_key_fields: method (ADF|CADF)
statistic (+statistic_label)
p_value (Costantini-Lupi-Popp)
rho2 (the nuisance parameter, CADF only; absent for a plain ADF)
estimate
null_value
alternative=less
max_lag_y/min_lag_X/max_lag_X (as selected)
info_criteria {AIC,BIC,HQC,MAIC}
decision
warnings
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: H0=unit root, rejection (p<alpha) => STATIONARITY (the OPPOSITE of KPSS)
silently wrong (gated): a silent gap-drop in y; silent acceptance of gaps or a misaligned X; a cryptic out-of-bounds error on a constant y, on min_lag_X>max_lag_X, or on excessive lags
the «Specified sample size may be too small» notice is printed to stdout (it is NOT a raised warning) -> it is exposed in warnings; the p-value is less reliable at small n
min_lag_X<0 means leads of the covariates (a documented feature, not an error)
the covariates X MUST be stationary; a non-stationary X invalidates the asymptotic theory, and the routine does not check it

cards.method: General-to-Specific (GETS) model selection + Indicator Saturation (IIS/SIS/TIS) for outliers & structural breaks
cards.when: set up the GUM (gts_ar_x: intercept+AR lags+regressors) -> a parsimonious final model (gts_model_selection, multi-path GETS+PET) or automatic detection of outliers/mean shifts/trend shifts (gts_indicator_saturation, IIS/SIS/TIS); deterministic (no seed)
cards.when_not: testing for a break at a single point with sup-F or CUSUM -> #3; ARIMA-intervention outliers -> #5; the log-variance variant is omitted; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: a hypothesis-driven break test at a known or unknown point rather than automatic multiple saturation
an unknown number or location of breaks -> data-driven saturation with a controlled gauge (~t_pval·n false positives)

output_key_fields: coefficients + mean_results (term/coef/std_error/t_stat/p_value) + sigma/rss/logl/r_squared + fitted/residuals + n/k/df
gts_ar_x / gts_indicator_saturation: model = the fitted object (a producer, registered to the binary bucket; a stub once serialised)
gts_indicator_saturation: is_names (e.g. sis41), n_indicators, and the saturation dates per indicator type (breaks/date/index/coef/coef_se/coef_t/coef_p)
gts_model_selection: specific_spec (the regressor numbers kept), terminals_results, n_estimations, the empty_model flag
interpretation_traps: sisNN=a step shift at observation NN (a permanent level change); iisNN=an impulse (a single outlier); tisNN=a trend shift — do not confuse them
gauge: a tighter t_pval ⇒ fewer false detections and lower power; the saturation default is t_pval=0.001, NOT 0.05
gts_model_selection may end at the empty model -> empty_model=True with coefficients of length 0 (NOT a silent blank)
SILENTLY WRONG (gated): a regressor matrix with more rows than y is accepted silently; t_pval>=1 is accepted silently -> hard gates

cards.method: Seasonality tests (combined/QS/Friedman/Kruskal-Wallis/seasonal-dummies/Welch/OCSB)
cards.when: the prechecks stage after stationarity (#1/#2), before seasonal adjustment (#3); the structural decision whether a monthly/quarterly/weekly series is seasonal; run_seasonality_test=a boolean gate (WO); ocsb=a seasonal unit root (nsdiffs)
cards.when_not: non-seasonal stationarity -> #1/#2; deseasonalisation -> X-13 (#4; this card only DETECTS); frequency=1 (a hard gate); charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: the objective is deseasonalization rather than detection
a suspected seasonal UNIT ROOT (stochastic) rather than deterministic seasonality
a fast default boolean decision (the WO combination rule)

output_key_fields: test/null_hypothesis/statistic/p_value/alpha/is_seasonal/decision/freq/n_obs (+ echoed args)
run_seasonality_test (combined): no single statistic; p_values carries the three named Webel-Ollech component p-values (QS, QS on the residuals, Kruskal-Wallis on the residuals)
ocsb: + method/augmentations/nrun/seed; the null is a seasonal unit root
interpretation_traps: POLARITY: combined/qs/fried/kw/seasdum/welch have H0=no seasonality (a small p => seasonal); ocsb has H0=A SEASONAL UNIT ROOT, REVERSED (fail to reject, p>=alpha => seasonal, the nsdiffs convention) -> which is why null_hypothesis is always returned
the combined test returns a LOGICAL decision (QS p<0.01 OR Kruskal-Wallis p<0.002), NOT a statistic; alpha does not affect it
gaps: SILENTLY WRONG — the tests accept them and return an incorrect decision -> a hard gate
isSeasonal does NOT support test='ocsb' (object 'seasonal' not found); run_seasonality_test routes ocsb directly
a pure deterministic sine is NOT detected by combined (it is residual-based); welch fails on a plain numeric ('intra' not found) -> normalise to a series

Osborn, Chui, Smith & Birchenhall (1988), Seasonality and the order of integration for consumption, Oxford Bull. Econ. Stat. 50(4):361-377 (OCSB)

alternatives.criterion: STL is robust and loess-based (the default; s_window periodic or an odd number >=7); the classical decomposition is only a baseline (fixed seasonality, blanks at the edges)
you need the official X-13-ARIMA-SEATS seasonal adjustment rather than loess/MA
a non-seasonal trend/cycle rather than a seasonal decomposition
you want the raw ACF/PACF rather than unified comparable feature metrics

output_key_fields: components: data_frame {index, observed, trend, seasonal, remainder, season_adjust} (canonical, parquet-able)

decomp (tsf_stl/tsf_classical_decomposition): mable mdl_df [PRODUCER -> RDS bucket]

interpretation_traps: STL on frequency==1 SILENTLY drops the seasonal component -> a frequency>1 gate (do not read it as 'no seasonality')
STL or the classical decomposition on a series with gaps yields an empty model and then a cryptic component error -> a gap gate plus an empty-model post-gate
classical multiplicative on non-positive values -> a silently inconsistent decomposition -> a >0 gate
the column naming differs (STL season_year/remainder vs classical seasonal/random) -> unified to seasonal/remainder
the classical trend is blank over roughly frequency/2 observations at each edge, because of the centred moving average (expected, not an error)
a trend/seasonal strength ~1 => a strong component, ~0 => negligible

cards.method: Data-driven locally-weighted regression decomposition of seasonality/trend (IPI optimal bandwidth) under short memory
cards.when: an equidistant seasonal ts (frequency>1); a non-parametric decomposition into trend + (slowly varying) seasonality + remainder with a DETERMINISTICALLY selected bandwidth (IPI/AMISE); it also returns detrended + seasonally-adjusted series
cards.when_not: frequency<=1 (non-seasonal -> a trend filter); the official model-based seasonal adjustment -> X-13 (#4); STL with explicit windows or robustness -> #126; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: you want STL (loess) with explicit trend/seasonal windows or robustness to outliers rather than a data-driven optimal bandwidth

output_key_fields: trend/seasonal/remainder/observations: the series taken from the fitted decomposition (Trend/Seasonality/Rest/Observations)

bwidth: the relative [0,1] data-driven IPI bandwidth (NOT a number of observations); sum_autocov: the estimated sum of autocovariances

interpretation_traps: the routine accepts a matrix SILENTLY (silently wrong) — the wrapper blocks multivariate input
bwidth is a RELATIVE bandwidth, not a number of observations
a gap gives the cryptic «Convergence of the bandwidth selection algorithm failed» (gated); the seasonality is assumed to vary SLOWLY

cards.method: Regularisation/decomposition & analysis of space-time series (turning points + Kendall info; a full descriptive table including normality; diff/LOESS trend-seasonal decomposition)
cards.when: a preparatory diagnostic BEFORE estimation: a full descriptive table (ps_descriptives) with normality criteria; locating peaks and pits plus a randomness test (ps_turning_points, the Kendall information); fast detrending or a seasonal loess decomposition (ps_decompose)
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); formal stationarity or unit-root testing -> #1/#2; the seasonal HEGY/CH tests -> #89; multiplicative seasonal adjustment -> #4; irregular-to-regular resampling WAS OMITTED

alternatives.criterion: you want ACF/PACF/rolling/correlation rather than a static summary table per series
you need a formal stationarity p-value rather than a turning-point/visual precheck
you want a full X-13 seasonal adjustment rather than a quick decdiff/decloess

output_key_fields: ps_turning_points: n_turns/n_peaks/n_pits/first_is_peak; tppos + peak_positions/pit_positions; proba/info (if calc_proba) — info=-log2(P), larger ⇒ more monotone/informative

ps_descriptives: stats_table records with a 'statistic' column (the names preserved) + one column per variable; skew_2se/kurt_2se > 1 ⇒ significantly different from 0; normtest_p is the Shapiro-Wilk p-value
ps_decompose: the components as a frame — differencing gives filtered/residuals; loess with trend=True gives trend/seasonal/residuals, and with trend=False deseasoned/seasonal
interpretation_traps: ps_descriptives on a NON-numeric input silently blanks everything (a hard gate: every column must be numeric)
the differencing route FILLS gaps in the input silently -> a single gap gate across the whole of ps_decompose
turnpoints with <3 unique values -> a warning & a degenerate result (gate unique>=3); decloess is additive ONLY and requires frequency>1 + >=2 periods
coef_var = std_dev/mean is unreliable when the mean is near zero; the information is in bits (Kendall), not a p-value
sources: Ibanez 1982, J. Exp. Mar. Biol. Ecol. 4:619-632 (turning-points information)
Cleveland et al. 1990, STL: Seasonal-Trend decomposition based on Loess, J. Official Stat. 6:3-73

cards.method: Robust descriptives + correlation prechecks (robust per-variable summary / correlation matrix with p-values / weighted mean-var-quantile)
cards.when: the preparatory layer BEFORE modelling; robust per-variable stats (pMedian/Gmd/distinct/missing/quantiles), a correlation matrix WITH p-values + pairwise n, weighted statistics with survey/frequency weights
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); formal stationarity -> category 01 (#1/#2); causality or lead-lag -> the CCF of #81, or Granger; layout-agnostic transformations -> #78

alternatives.criterion: a correlation matrix WITHOUT p-values/significance; use rdesc_correlation when you need asymptotic p-values + pairwise n
rank-based, robust to outliers/non-linearity vs pearson (linear)
observations with weights (survey/frequency) vs the unweighted rdesc_describe
the MLE Gaussian variance vs the unbiased/Bessel one (default)

output_key_fields: stats (rdesc_describe): a named record per variable (n/missing/distinct/Info/Mean/pMedian/Gmd + the .05 to .95 quantiles); rounded to digits (default 4)
r/P/n (rdesc_correlation): matrices (nested rows + labels); the diagonal of P is blank; pairwise deletion -> one n per pair
weighted_mean/weighted_var/weighted_sd/weighted_quantiles (rdesc_weighted_stats), named, plus probs/var_method/normwt/n/sum_weights
interpretation_traps: describe: quantiles ONLY for continuous variables (>10 distinct); discrete ones get no quantiles; the values are rounded to digits significant figures (raise digits for precision); pMedian=Hodges-Lehmann robust location, Gmd=Gini robust dispersion
the P matrix has a blank diagonal (there is no self-correlation p-value); with pairwise deletion a strong correlation on a small n is fragile (read the n matrix); Spearman is Pearson on the ranks

the weighted variance defaults to the unbiased (Bessel) form; 'ML' is the Gaussian MLE; a single effective observation gives var=NaN (the warning becomes a message); for the weights, a length mismatch silently blanks the result and negatives are accepted silently -> the gates block both
sources: Harrell, Regression Modeling Strategies 2nd ed. (describe/pseudomedian/Gini mean difference)
Hollander & Wolfe, Nonparametric Statistical Methods 1973 (rcorr midrank Spearman)

cards.method: Non-parametric trend & change-point tests (Mann-Kendall / Theil-Sen slope / Pettitt / Seasonal MK)
cards.when: detecting a monotone trend without a distributional assumption (rank-based, robust to outliers/non-normality); tr_mann_kendall=significance, tr_theil_sen=magnitude (a robust slope+CI), tr_pettitt=a single change point at position K, tr_seasonal_mann_kendall=seasonal series with frequency>1
cards.when_not: unit root or stationarity -> #1/#2 (Mann-Kendall is not a unit-root test); multiple or parametric breakpoints -> #3; charts (the frontend); strong autocorrelation (the p-value is unreliable, it over-rejects)

alternatives.criterion: you need the MAGNITUDE of the trend (slope + CI), not only the significance from tr_mann_kendall
the series is seasonal (frequency>1) — a plain tr_mann_kendall confuses seasonality with trend
multiple / parametric (regression-based) breakpoints rather than one non-parametric change point (Pettitt)
the question is trend stationarity (I(0) around a trend), not monotone direction

output_key_fields: tr_mann_kendall: statistic (z), p_value, S, varS, tau (∈[-1,1], the sign = the direction), decision
tr_theil_sen: slope (the median of the pairwise slopes per unit of time), conf_low/conf_high at conf_level, p_value/statistic from MK
tr_pettitt: change_point_index (an integer index 1.n, NOT a date), statistic (U*), Uk (the |U[k]| series, chart-data)
tr_seasonal_mann_kendall: overall statistic/p_value + season_S/season_varS/season_pvalue/season_z per-season vectors (length=frequency)
interpretation_traps: MK/Sen test MONOTONICITY, not linearity — a U shape gives a non-significant MK despite a strong non-monotone change
on autocorrelated data the p-value is understated (a spurious trend) — prewhiten or use a block bootstrap
the tr_theil_sen slope is per unit of time (NOT a %); tr_pettitt change_point_index is a position index (map it to a date); the Pettitt approximate p-value is valid only for p<=0.5
a constant series (var=0) gives p_value=NaN (silently wrong) — a hard gate; gaps are not allowed (complete observations only)
sources: Hipel & McLeod (1994) Time Series Modelling of Water Resources and Environmental Systems; Sen (1968) JASA 63:1379-1389; Pettitt (1979) Appl. Statist. 28:126-135; Hirsch, Slack & Smith (1982) Water Resources Research 18:107-121

cards.method: Intermittent / sparse-demand forecasting (Croston + SBA/SBJ variants, TSB, iMAPA auto-selection, Croston decomposition)
cards.when: demand series with many zeros (spare parts / rare events); a constant out-of-sample demand rate; automatic model selection (imapa) or a demand/interval decomposition
cards.when_not: a dense series with no zeros -> #7; charts (the frontend; plotting is off); continuous macro series

alternatives.criterion: bias-corrected Croston (SBA/SBJ) — less positive bias
declining demand / obsolescence (it models the demand probability, not the interval)
automatic robust model selection (a combination across aggregation levels)
the series is NOT intermittent (it is dense)

output_key_fields: forecast: the out-of-sample demand RATE (length h; a constant per-period rate, NOT discrete events)
fitted: the in-sample demand rate (with leading blanks); weights/initial: the smoothing and initialisation parameters; model: the selected model
the iMAPA summary: a matrix per aggregation level (level/n/p/cv2/model — 1=Croston, 2=SBA, 3=SES — and whether it was used); model_fit: the parameters per level
the Croston components: the in-sample and out-of-sample demand and interval, plus the SBA/SBJ scaling coefficient; decomp: demand + interval, of equal length
interpretation_traps: forecast = a demand RATE per period (e.g. 0.19 units/period), NOT a forecast of an individual order — sum it for total demand
tsi_croston does NOT validate the type -> silently wrong; negative values are silently accepted -> a non-negativity gate; h<=0 gives a silently empty forecast
intermittency gate: >=1 zero (otherwise it is dense -> #7) AND >=2 non-zero values; imapa ALs with use=0 (<4 obs) are ignored; deterministic (no seed)
sources: Kourentzes 2014, On intermittent demand model optimisation and selection, IJPE 156:180-190 (doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2014.06.007)
Petropoulos & Kourentzes 2015, Forecast Combinations for Intermittent Demand, JORS (doi:10.1057/jors.2014.62)

cards.method: Long memory / fractional integration ARFIMA(p,d,q) (ML fit + GPH/Sperio semiparametric d + fractional differencing)
cards.when: a slowly decaying ACF, between I(0) and I(1); estimating the memory parameter d (semiparametric GPH/Sperio or parametric ARFIMA ML) + fractional differencing to I(0)
cards.when_not: integer differencing -> ADF/KPSS plus differencing, category 01; a forecast object -> #7-#10; long-memory volatility -> GARCH, category 06

alternatives.criterion: a fast semiparametric estimate of d (GPH log-periodogram) — the exploration default
a more robust semiparametric d (smoothed periodogram, Parzen window) under short-run dynamics/noise
a full parametric ARFIMA(p,d,q) ML (d+AR/MA+SE together) when you need a model, not just d

output_key_fields: d + d_reading: d≈0 short memory (I0), d<0 anti-persistent, 0<d<0.5 stationary long memory, d>=0.5 non-stationary
arfima_gph/arfima_sperio: sd_asymptotic/sd_regression (two SE estimators for d -> a CI/significance of d!=0)
arfima_fit: d/ar/ma/sigma/log_likelihood/std_errors(order d,ar,ma)/covariance/correlation + model (a producer, rds)
arfima_difference: series (fractionally differenced; it preserves the ts attributes) + d + n
interpretation_traps: the arfima_fit drange default c(0,0.5) CONSTRAINS d to [0,0.5] — for d>=0.5 (non-stationary) widen drange explicitly
MA sign: this estimator uses the convention with REVERSED MA signs relative to the usual ARIMA parameterisation — do not compare the coefficients directly
BANDWIDTH GATE: arfima_gph and arfima_sperio with a zero bandwidth exponent return a blank d and an infinite standard error SILENTLY (silently wrong) -> a hard gate, 0 < bandwidth < 1
the covariance and standard errors of the ML fit can be inaccurate (a documented warning) — prefer the semiparametric standard error for inference on d
sources: Geweke & Porter-Hudak 1983 (J. Time Series Analysis 4(4):221-238, GPH)
Reisen 1994 (J. Time Series Analysis 15(1):335-350, smoothed periodogram)
Jensen & Nielsen 2014 (J. Time Series Analysis 35(5):428-436, fast fractional difference, doi:10.1111/jtsa.12074)
precondition_tools: the series precheck (a univariate numeric series with no gaps, NaN or infinities)
c00_data_utilities/descriptive_statistics.desc_acf (a slowly/linearly decaying ACF => evidence of long memory)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.unitroot_adf (ADF non-rejection + ambiguous stationarity => possible fractional integration)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_suite.unitroot_kpss (KPSS alongside ADF for an ambiguous I(0)/I(1))

cards.method: Distributed-lag & ARDL regression (finite DL / Koyck geometric / autoregressive DL / Almon polynomial DL)
cards.when: a lag-distributed effect of a predictor X on Y (short/long-run multipliers): a finite q, an infinite geometric decay (Koyck), an autoregressive DL(p,q), Almon polynomial smoothing of the lag weights
cards.when_not: pure univariate forecasting without X -> #7/#8; non-linear relations; I(1) long-run cointegration/ECM -> ARDL bounds (05); structural shocks/IRF -> 04

alternatives.criterion: x,y are I(1): a bounds test for long-run cointegration + an ECM instead of a level DL regression
an infinite geometric decay of the lag weights (a single rate phi, parsimony) rather than an explicit finite q
many lags with multicollinearity -> Almon polynomial smoothing of the lag weights
you need AR dynamics in Y (autoregressive) alongside the distributed lags of X

output_key_fields: coefficients: named numeric (intercept + lag terms); fitted/residuals: numeric
diagnostics: r_squared/adj_r_squared/sigma/df_residual/nobs/aic/bic (aic and bic are blank for the Koyck IV fit)
method-specific: q/k (finite/poly); order=c(p,q) (ardl); geometric_coefficients alpha/beta/phi (koyck); beta+beta_tvalue/beta_pvalue (poly); formula/removed (multi-formula mode)
interpretation_traps: Koyck: interpret the geometric_coefficients (alpha/beta/phi, with phi the decay rate), NOT the raw IV delta coefficients; aic and bic are blank because the IV fit has no log-likelihood — do not compare it with least-squares models
poly: beta (the original per-lag weights) is the interpretable quantity; the coefficients are the gamma of the z-transformed polynomial, NOT per-lag effects
q loses q initial observations (nobs = n - q); a length mismatch between x and y would be accepted SILENTLY -> a hard gate
closed formula: it is built from y_col ~ x_cols (reformulate), NEVER a free formula string; k>q -> singular (hard gate)
sources: Hill, Griffiths & Judge, Undergraduate Econometrics (Wiley); Baltagi, Econometrics 5th ed. (Springer)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (stationarity of x & y first — a level DL regression on non-cointegrated I(1) series is spurious)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test (confirmatory stationarity, the opposite H0)

cards.method: Maximum Entropy Bootstrap for time series (dependence/non-stationarity preserved)
cards.when: bootstrap ensemble replicates of a series for downstream inference/confidence bands WITHOUT assuming stationarity or tuning a block length (it preserves dependence/non-stationarity)
cards.when_not: parametric prediction intervals from a correctly specified model -> forecast #7; charts (frontend); panel pdata_frame ensembles (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: a well-specified parametric model exists -> model-based prediction intervals instead of resampling
preserve the CLT for the ensemble mean; False for non-gaussian tails, or for a trim with an xmin=0 non-negativity constraint

output_key_fields: ensemble: an n x reps matrix of replicates (nested rows) — the data and producer field
x: the original series (as input); xx: the ordered order statistics; z: the class-interval limits
xmin/xmax: the left/right tail limits; dvtrim: the trimmed mean deviations; kappa: the scale adjustment
n/reps/trim/seed: metadata + the applied arguments (the seed for reproducibility)
interpretation_traps: STOCHASTIC: the seed is MANDATORY (the generator is seeded before the draw); without a pinned seed the node is uncacheable
reps<10, or a trim outside [0,0.5), would be accepted SILENTLY -> hard gates here (silently wrong)
force_clt=True alters the ensemble so that its mean satisfies the CLT — it is NOT a raw resample
the elapsed-time report is forced off and omitted — it is non-deterministic and breaks caching

cards.method: Fractionally Cointegrated VAR (Johansen-Nielsen): fractional cointegration with estimated d/b + rank tests (asymptotic + wild bootstrap) + lag selection
cards.when: a system of >=2 series with fractional integration (long memory, non-integer I(d)) -> fractional cointegration; estimating d/b + the cointegrating beta + the adjustment alpha; lag_select -> rank_test -> boot_rank -> estimate (the PRODUCER)
cards.when_not: purely integer I(1) with no long memory -> the integer Johansen procedure (#23/#24); a single equation of mixed order -> #25/#26; hypothesis restrictions and forecasting are omitted

alternatives.criterion: the integer Johansen VECM when d~=1 (standard critical values, simpler)
the integer Johansen WITH p-values
a small sample -> the asymptotic LR rank test is unreliable, you need the wild bootstrap

output_key_fields: fcv_estimate: d/b (fractional params), beta (p x r cointegrating), alpha (p x r adjustment), Pi=alpha*beta', Gamma/Omega/mu, log_lik/fp/SE, roots (re/im/mod), object (the FCVAR_model PRODUCER)
fcv_rank_test: LRstat/pv vectors of length p+1 (entry i -> rank=i-1); the rank is read bottom-up, at the first non-rejected H0; the p-value is 999 or blank when unavailable
fcv_lag_select: aic/bic (+ i_aic/i_bic, the selected lag), pvWNQ/pvWNLM white-noise tests per lag
fcv_boot_rank: LRbs (B simulated LR — chart-data), LRstat (the observed one), pv_bs (the bootstrap p-value = H.pvBS)
interpretation_traps: the raw opt object (~40 fields) is NOT exposed; it is built internally from a curated surface (bounds/restrict_db/constrained/level_param/constants/grid_search)

grid_search defaults to False (a deliberate deviation from the reference default); the switching optimiser converges on its own, and the grid search is an expensive accuracy refinement for local maxima in d and b
the bootstrap p-value is reported in the H_pvBS field; the plain pv field comes back empty
FCVAR does NOT enforce r1<r2 (a silently wrong negative LR) -> the wrapper gates it
full rank r=p -> a singular Hessian in the SE (silenced); it means no rank reduction (stationary fractional differences); r>p -> a cryptic non-conformable arguments error
sources: Johansen & Nielsen 2012 (Econometrica 80:2667-2732, Likelihood inference for a fractionally cointegrated VAR)
Cavaliere, Rahbek & Taylor 2010 (J. Econometrics 158:7-24, wild-bootstrap rank test)
Doornik 2018 (Scand. J. Statist. 45(2), accelerated switching algorithm)
FCVAR 0.1.4 reference manual (FCVARoptions/FCVARestn/FCVARrankTests/FCVARlagSelect/FCVARbootRank) — live-verified via Rd + votingJNP2014 probes

cards.method: Nonlinear (asymmetric) ARDL — NARDL (Shin-Yu-Greenwood-Nimmo) + PSS bounds + CUSUM/CUSUMQ stability
cards.when: Single-equation cointegration with an ASYMMETRIC relation: the regressor acts differently on increases vs decreases (positive/negative partial sums); regressors of mixed order I(0)/I(1); EXACTLY one decomposed regressor; long-run beta+/beta- + a Wald test of asymmetry + PSS bounds + CUSUM/CUSUMQ.
cards.when_not: A symmetric relation (a linear ARDL suffices) -> #25; any I(2) series (the bounds test breaks down); multiple cointegrating relations / a system -> Johansen #23/#24; >1 decomposed regressor (nardl accepts EXACTLY one).

alternatives.criterion: The relation is SYMMETRIC (a linear ARDL/UECM + bounds suffices).
You want stochastic counterfactual simulation + residual diagnostics.
A system / multiple cointegrating relations.

output_key_fields: long_run: a table of long-run coefficients x_p (positive) / x_n (negative) + SE/t/p
asym_lr / asym_sr: the Wald test of asymmetry (statistic, p_value); H0 of asym_lr: beta+ = beta- (long-run symmetry)
ect_coef: the coefficient on the lagged DV (error correction; it must be negative)
fstat / orders / case / k / Nobs; normality (Shapiro) & arch (Engle) htests
nar_bounds: statistic + bounds (a data_frame level/I0/I1 10/5/1%) + decision + report (the raw pssbounds display)
nar_stability: cusum & cusumq -> x/process/lower/upper/breach (chart-data, NOT a plot)
interpretation_traps: Decision (bounds): F > the upper I(1) 5% bound ⇒ cointegration; F < the lower I(0) bound ⇒ none; BETWEEN ⇒ inconclusive (no conclusion).
case: ONLY 3 (unrestricted intercept, no trend) or 5 (+trend) are supported; 1/2/4 -> a cryptic error in nardl (the gate blocks it).
a NON-significant asym_lr ⇒ the asymmetry is NOT justified -> go back to the linear ARDL #25.
nar_fit accepts EXACTLY one decomposed regressor; the bounds test takes k from the fit, following the documented convention.

CUSUM and CUSUMQ take k and n from the selected-model fields, not from the top-level k and n, which stay at 1 and the number of differenced rows when plotting is off — that would give silently wrong bounds.
sources: Shin, Yu & Greenwood-Nimmo 2014 (Festschrift in Honor of Peter Schmidt, Ch.9: Modelling Asymmetric Cointegration and Dynamic Multipliers in a NARDL Framework)
nardl reference manual + source (nardl, pssbounds, cusum, cumsq)

c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test (confirmatory)

cards.method: Consistent monitoring of stationarity & cointegration (Wagner-Wied): calibration-period estimation + a sequential detector (FM/D/IM-OLS)
cards.when: You have an established cointegration relation (or a stationary series) and you monitor whether it BREAKS DOWN in a later period; estimation only on a break-free calibration sample [1.floor(m*N)] -> detector -> break point.
cards.when_not: A full-sample one-shot test for the existence of cointegration (#23/#25/#26); estimating beta (#27); you cannot assume a break-free calibration period.

alternatives.criterion: A univariate series (level/trend stationarity) rather than a relation.
The default; semiparametric long-run variance correction (Phillips-Hansen).
D-OLS (=DOLS); leads/lags of the differenced regressors.
IM-OLS; integrated-modified, robust without bandwidth tuning at the estimation point.
A full-sample TEST for the existence of cointegration (rank), not sequential monitoring.
ESTIMATING the cointegrating vector beta, not monitoring.

output_key_fields: statistic: the detector value (H_sm)
critical_value: the critical value at signif_level
detected: the DECISION — a break/deviation was detected (boolean)
detection_time: the detection index (blank when there is none; the raw infinite time is not exposed)
statistics_path: the detector path, blank over the calibration period (chart data)
p_value: bounded to ∈ [0.01, 0.1] (not an exact p)
residuals: modified-OLS residuals (cmo_cointegration only)
calibration: the fraction m_frac + the index floor(m*N)
kernel/bandwidth/trend/model: the options that were used
object: the monitor handle (not a producer; a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: m = the CALIBRATION fraction ∈ [0.1,0.9]; the last observation = floor(m*N); a bad calibration (containing a break) invalidates the procedure.
p_value is bounded to [0.01,0.1] (0.1=far from rejection, 0.01=strong) — NOT an exact p-value.
detected=False with a blank detection_time (an infinite raw time) means no break, not an error.
model='D'=DOLS, 'IM'=Integrated-Modified; there is NO 'DOLS'/'CCR' token.
Silently wrong: a multi-column y, a gap, or an x whose row count does not match y — the underlying routine only WARNS and returns garbage; hard-gated here.
Fully deterministic (no RNG/bootstrap) -> reproducible without a seed; computational (no register).
sources: Wagner & Wied 2015 (SSRN DOI:10.2139/ssrn.2624657, Monitoring Stationarity and Cointegration)

c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test

cards.method: High-dimensional penalized VAR (structured penalties + rolling-CV lambda)
cards.when: a multivariate VAR with a large k·p relative to T (an OLS VAR over-fits); a structured VARX-L/HLAG penalty + rolling-OOS selection of lambda; a data-driven lag order (HLAG)
cards.when_not: a short sample wanting Minnesota shrinkage in levels with fan charts -> #12; frequentist Granger tests and p-values -> #11; a very large n with factor structure -> #15; mixed frequency -> #17

alternatives.criterion: a short sample, Bayesian shrinkage in LEVELS + posterior fan charts
a small k·p, you want frequentist Granger/IRF/diagnostics
a very large n with few common factors

output_key_fields: optimal_lambda: the best lambda (minimum in-sample MSFE); oos_msfe = the OOS MSFE on the test set (vs mean/RW/AIC/BIC)
coefficients: a k x (kp+1) sparse matrix (intercept + Y{i}L{l}); sparsity = the share of zeros
forecast (bvr_predict): a horizon x k path, built step by step; confint=True adds the lower/upper 95% band
model: the fitted producer handle -> bvr_predict / bvr_coef
interpretation_traps: stationarity: this estimator shrinks towards ZERO (MN=False by default, NOT a random-walk prior) -> apply it to STATIONARY data and difference I(1) series FIRST, the opposite of #12, which wants levels; I(1) and cointegrated -> consider a VECM, #23
the estimator DISCARDS the column names of Y: the variables come back as Y1..Yk by column order, consistently across fit/predict/coef -> map the positions in the frontend
struct: EFX is VARX ONLY (a pure VAR -> stop); HLAG*/Tapered are VAR-only; the non-convex MCP/SCAD are out of scope
the underlying predict returns only the final horizon (k x 1); the wrapper builds the full horizon x k path step by step
gran = c(penalty_grid_depth, number_of_lambda), two positive integers; too few rows for the rolling-CV window -> a clean stop (too few rows)
determinism: penalized (convex) + rolling/LOO CV = deterministic, no seed
sources: Nicholson-Wilms-Bien-Matteson 2020 JMLR 21(166) High-dim forecasting via interpretable VAR

c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test

cards.method: Hierarchical global-local shrinkage Bayesian VAR + stochastic volatility (HS/DL/R2D2/NG/SSVS priors, posterior fan charts + LPL)
cards.when: a multivariate BVAR (small to medium k) with global-local shrinkage that adapts sparse-vs-dense in a data-driven way (HS/DL/R2D2/NG/SSVS/normal on Phi) + stochastic volatility; posterior median/quantiles, predictive fan charts, LPL density forecasts
cards.when_not: a Minnesota random-walk prior in LEVELS with an IRF/FEVD toolkit -> #12; a frequentist penalized rolling-CV fit -> #142; time-varying coefficients -> #14; mixed frequency -> #17; a large-n factor model -> #15/#144; structural identification -> category 04 (bvs_irf is reduced-form)

alternatives.criterion: a Minnesota RW prior in LEVELS + a ready-made IRF/FEVD/companion/sign-restrictions toolkit
a frequentist penalized VAR-L, rolling-OOS lambda, deterministic (no posterior)
time-varying coefficients (TVP-VAR) + SV
reduced-form posterior impulse responses from the same fit

output_key_fields: phi_median: the posterior median Phi (K x M); phi_quantiles: an nq x K x M grid (2.5/25/50/75/97.5%)
convergence: n_retained/min_ess/n_stable/phi_finite/min_draws/ess_min/seed; converged + nonconvergence_reasons
model: the bayesianVARs_bvar producer handle -> bvs_predict/bvs_irf (register field=model, bucket=rds)
quants (bvs_predict): an nq x horizon x M predictive fan grid; mean: horizon x M; LPL and LPL_univariate when LPL=True (the density forecast)
irf_median (bvs_irf): M x shocks x horizon; irf_quantiles: nq x M x shocks x horizon (reduced-form bands)
interpretation_traps: stationarity: a prior mean of 0 shrinks towards ZERO (like #142, NOT a random-walk prior in levels like #12) -> use STATIONARY or growth data and difference I(1) series FIRST; precheck with ADF/KPSS

single-chain convergence: there is NO split-Rhat -> the gate is on the retained and stable draws, and DEGENERATE cases (an entirely blank ESS when the sampler is stuck, a non-finite Phi, zero stable draws) count as non-convergence; allow_nonconvergence overrides it (mirroring #68 and #61); a low ESS on TINY draw counts is NOT an error -> raise the number of draws

determinism: bvs_estimate and bvs_predict are stochastic and take NO seed argument of their own -> the seed is MANDATORY and the generator is seeded before the sampling (live-verified: seed=42 reproduces PHI exactly, and bvs_predict with seed=7 is identical); bvs_irf is deterministic

LPL: Y_obs must be the [ahead x M] realised values (a wrong dimension -> an upstream recycling warning; the wrapper blocks it); bvs_irf is reduced-form (shocks=1, no orthogonalization) -> structural shocks live in 04-structural-shocks
sources: Gruber & Kastner 2023 Forecasting macroeconomic data with Bayesian VARs: Sparse or dense? It depends! (arXiv:2206.04902)
Vehtari et al. 2021 Bayesian Analysis 16(2):667-718 rank-normalized ESS

cards.method: High-dimensional mixed-frequency regression via MIDAS-ML sparse-group LASSO (Legendre/Gegenbauer weighted high-frequency blocks -> a low-frequency target, sg-LASSO lambda + mixing gamma, CV-tuned)
cards.when: Forecasting/nowcasting one low-frequency variable from MANY high-frequency indicators with many lags; each predictor (group) -> an orthonormal Legendre/Gegenbauer basis (degree+1) & a sparse-group LASSO for simultaneous group selection + within-group sparsity; gamma=the mixing weight (0 group-LASSO, 1 LASSO), lambda=the penalty (tuned with mml_cv).
cards.when_not: Few high-frequency regressors with an interpretable weight shape -> #18; factor structure or a large n -> #15/#144; a Bayesian mixed-frequency VAR with latent states -> #17; a same-frequency high-dimensional VAR -> #142; it is not multi-equation and has no IRF (a single low-frequency target).

alternatives.criterion: Few high-frequency regressors + an interpretable parametric weight shape theta (not sparse selection).
A large n; a latent factor structure summarises better than sparse selection.
A principled choice of lambda (lambda_min or lambda_1se) instead of the mml_fit path default, which is the smallest lambda.

output_key_fields: mml_fit: model (an 'mml_model' producer -> register field=model, bucket=rds); beta = (n_basis x nlambda) BASIS coefficients per lambda; the lambda/df/intercept path; n_groups/n_basis/gamma/degree/weight/s_default

mml_cv: lambda_min (minimising the CV error) and lambda_1se (the one-standard-error, more parsimonious choice); cvm/cvsd/cvupper/cvlower (the CV curve, chart data); nzero; beta_min/beta_1se + intercept_min/intercept_1se; seed (blank when unset)
mml_predict: fitted (length==nrow(newx)) + s + kind
interpretation_traps: mml_predict newx = the RAW high-frequency block (the same group/ncol as at fit time); the wrapper applies the SAME MIDAS transform internally — do NOT pass a pre-transformed design.
beta is in BASIS coefficients (Legendre/Gegenbauer functions), NOT per-lag weights; the per-lag shape = Psi %*% beta_group.
mml_fit (convex coordinate descent) is DETERMINISTIC (no seed); mml_cv partitions the folds RANDOMLY -> it REQUIRES a seed for reproducibility/caching (otherwise lambda_min fluctuates).
s: on a cross-validated model use lambda_min or lambda_1se; on a path model give a numeric lambda (the default is the smallest, that is the richest and least regularized model).
weighted basis: every group MUST have jmax >= degree+1 for a well-posed orthonormal basis; gamma ∈ [0,1] (the routine enforces it and the gate gives a clean message).
sources: Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas 2022 'Machine Learning Time Series Regressions With an Application to Nowcasting' JBES 40(3):1094-1106 (doi:10.1080/07350015.2021.1899933)
Babii, Ghysels & Striaukas 2021 (sparse-group LASSO with dependent/heteroskedastic data)

cards.method: Time-Varying-Parameter VAR with stochastic volatility + dynamic global-local shrinkage (triple/double gamma or ridge)
cards.when: A multivariate VAR (k>=2) where the relations EVOLVE smoothly over time (time-varying coefficients) AND the volatility changes (stochastic volatility), while MANY coefficients are in practice 0/constant -> dynamic shrinkage (triple/double gamma) automatically picks which ones are genuinely time-varying. The classic macro case: changing monetary transmission, structural breaks without explicit breakpoints.
cards.when_not: Constant (time-invariant) coefficients suffice -> #12/#11; time-varying parameters WITHOUT shrinkage but with explicit identification and IRF -> #14 (Primiceri); a single-equation TVP regression rather than a VAR -> #183; a high-dimensional penalized point estimate -> #142; nowcasting a panel with gaps -> #144.

alternatives.criterion: You want a TVP-VAR-SV with explicit Cholesky identification + structural IRFs (Primiceri), WITHOUT automatic variable selection.
The coefficients are plausibly constant -> a hierarchical Minnesota BVAR (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
You want more aggressive shrinkage/sparsity (triple gamma) than the default double gamma; ridge = no selection.

output_key_fields: stv_estimate: model (the producer handle), converged/min_ess/retained_draws/n_varying_params (the convergence gate), variables/n_vars/p/mod_type/const
stv_forecast: quants (a named list per variable: a [probs x horizon] posterior predictive fan) + mean [variables x horizon] + probs/horizon
stv_tvp: paths (a named list per coefficient L<lag>.<var> & intercept: [probs x time] posterior bands) + coefficients/time/variable — the time-varying paths
interpretation_traps: Convergence: a single-chain sampler has NO split-Rhat; the gate is the minimum ESS over the beta_mean draws, IGNORING coefficients shrunk to constants (legitimate shrinkage, NOT poor convergence). A DEGENERATE entirely-blank ESS (every parameter constant) counts as NON-CONVERGENCE; it passes ONLY with allow_nonconvergence=True.
the seed is MANDATORY: without it the MCMC is not reproducible (the generator is seeded before the sampling).
SV is INHERENT (it is always a TVP-VAR-SV); there is NO sv toggle — the only shrinkage knob is mod_type. ONLY the VAR-coefficient draws are returned (not those of the variance-covariance).
the min_ess default (10) is a FLOOR for tiny-draw development; production runs (niter>=5000) must raise ess_min (>=200).
stv_tvp equation = the index of the TARGET equation (the response); the paths are the time-varying loadings of the lagged variables in it.
sources: Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus (2020), 'Triple the Gamma—A Unifying Shrinkage Prior..', Econometrics 8(2):20 (doi:10.3390/econometrics8020020)
Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2021 JSS 100(13) (shrinkage in the TVP model framework)

c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test

cards.method: Bayesian Structural VAR identified through heteroskedasticity/non-normality (SV / Markov-switching heteroskedasticity / Student-t) + IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks + a Savage-Dickey (SDDR) identification check
cards.when: A multivariate series (K>=2) where you want a BAYESIAN structural VAR with shock identification through STATISTICAL STRUCTURE (not theoretical restrictions): sv=stochastic volatility, msh=Markov-switching heteroskedasticity (M regimes), t=Student-t non-normality. Posterior IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks with credible bands + an SDDR identification check (bsv_verify).
cards.when_not: Reduced-form work or forecasting suffices -> #11; FREQUENTIST data-driven identification (Rigobon changes-in-volatility, distance covariance, non-Gaussian ML) -> #20; theoretical A/B or Blanchard-Quah restrictions -> #19; sign-restriction set identification -> #21; regime-dependent DYNAMICS, not just the variance -> #150.

alternatives.criterion: Frequentist changes-in-volatility (Rigobon) identification instead of Bayesian; a point estimate + wild/MB bootstrap bands.
Plain recursive (Cholesky) identification without the Bayesian machinery.
Reduced-form dynamics/forecasting suffice (no structural identification).
Before interpreting IRF/FEVD: confirm that the statistical structure identifies the shocks (a negative logSDDR).

output_key_fields: bsv_estimate: model (the producer posterior 'PosteriorBSVAR*' handle) + B_mean/A_mean (posterior-mean structural/AR matrices) + model_type/p/K/S/burnin/thin/n_draws/seed/converged
bsv_irf/bsv_fevd: a long df (response|variable x shock x horizon + mean/lower/upper) — the posterior mean + quantile bands (default 16%/84%); horizon 0 = the impact
bsv_hd: a long df (variable x shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the historical contribution of each shock per period (time = real ts time)
bsv_shocks: a long df (shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the estimated structural disturbances
bsv_verify: logSDDR (a vector of length K per shock for SV/MSH; a scalar for t) + logSDDR_se (SV/MSH) or the SDDR ratio (t) + identified (per-shock logSDDR<0) + type/degenerate
interpretation_traps: SDDR sign: a NEGATIVE logSDDR is evidence AGAINST non-identification (the shock IS identified through heteroskedasticity or non-normality); a positive one means it adds no identification beyond the default lower-triangular structure. Minus infinity is VALID (strong evidence, the t model); a NaN or blank value is degenerate -> block.

The default identification is a lower-triangular B (recursive; the variable ORDER matters); the heteroskedasticity allows the exclusion restrictions to be TESTED/relaxed, it does not replace the recursive structure by default.
Degenerate diagnostics count as non-convergence: non-finite posterior draws (bsv_estimate) or a NaN/blank logSDDR (bsv_verify) -> a hard stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True.

[#148] Bayesian Structural VAR identified through heteroskedasticity/non-normality (SV / Markov-switching heteroskedasticity / Student-t) + IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks + a Savage-Dickey (SDDR) identification check
Category: 04-structural-shocks
Nodes: bsv_estimate · bsv_irf · bsv_fevd · bsv_hd · bsv_shocks · bsv_verify
WHEN: A multivariate series (K>=2) where you want a BAYESIAN structural VAR with shock identification through STATISTICAL STRUCTURE (not theoretical restrictions): sv=stochastic volatility, msh=Markov-switching heteroskedasticity (M regimes), t=Student-t non-normality. Posterior IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks with credible bands + an SDDR identification check (bsv_verify).
NOT when: Reduced-form work or forecasting suffices -> #11; FREQUENTIST data-driven identification (Rigobon changes-in-volatility, distance covariance, non-Gaussian ML) -> #20; theoretical A/B or Blanchard-Quah restrictions -> #19; sign-restriction set identification -> #21; regime-dependent DYNAMICS, not just the variance -> #150.
Alternatives: 04-structural-shocks/svar_id_volatility_change (Frequentist changes-in-volatility (Rigobon) identification instead of Bayesian; a point estimate + wild/MB bootstrap bands.) · 04-structural-shocks/svar_id_cholesky (Plain recursive (Cholesky) identification without the Bayesian machinery.) · 03-multivariate-nowcasting/Vars-vr_fit (Reduced-form dynamics/forecasting suffice (no structural identification).) · bsv_verify (Before interpreting IRF/FEVD: confirm that the statistical structure identifies the shocks (a negative logSDDR).)
Output: bsv_estimate: model (the producer posterior 'PosteriorBSVAR*' handle) + B_mean/A_mean (posterior-mean structural/AR matrices) + model_type/p/K/S/burnin/thin/n_draws/seed/converged · bsv_irf/bsv_fevd: a long df (response|variable x shock x horizon + mean/lower/upper) — the posterior mean + quantile bands (default 16%/84%); horizon 0 = the impact · bsv_hd: a long df (variable x shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the historical contribution of each shock per period (time = real ts time) · bsv_shocks: a long df (shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the estimated structural disturbances · bsv_verify: logSDDR (a vector of length K per shock for SV/MSH; a scalar for t) + logSDDR_se (SV/MSH) or the SDDR ratio (t) + identified (per-shock logSDDR<0) + type/degenerate
Pitfalls: SDDR sign: a NEGATIVE logSDDR is evidence AGAINST non-identification (the shock IS identified through heteroskedasticity or non-normality); a positive one means it adds no identification beyond the default lower-triangular structure. Minus infinity is VALID (strong evidence, the t model); a NaN or blank value is degenerate -> block. · The default identification is a lower-triangular B (recursive; the variable ORDER matters); the heteroskedasticity allows the exclusion restrictions to be TESTED/relaxed, it does not replace the recursive structure by default. · Degenerate diagnostics count as non-convergence: non-finite posterior draws (bsv_estimate) or a NaN/blank logSDDR (bsv_verify) -> a hard stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True. · TINY defaults (S=100, burnin=50): production runs raise the draw counts; the seed is MANDATORY (seeding the generator covers the burn-in and the retained draws across two sequential estimate calls; without a seed the run is not reproducible). · bsv_hd time axis: the labels are read as real numbers, NOT truncated to integers (1.25 would become 1 and destroy the axis); model='msh' requires M>=2.
Sources: Lütkepohl H., Woźniak T. 2020. Bayesian Inference for Structural Vector Autoregressions Identified by Markov-Switching Heteroskedasticity. University of Melbourne Working Paper, arXiv:2404.11057. · Woźniak 2024 (Bayesian estimation of structural vector autoregressive models)

cards.method: Bayesian Structural VAR with SIGN + ZERO + NARRATIVE restrictions (set-identified, importance sampling; a Waggoner-Zha Gibbs sampler + a uniform rotation Q)
cards.when: A multivariate series (N>=2) with structural shocks identified through THEORETICAL restrictions: sign restrictions (IRF signs), zero restrictions (0 entries in sign_irf; importance sampling), narrative sign restrictions (historical episodes). Set-identified Bayesian work -> posterior credible bands on IRF/FEVD + a predictive/conditional forecast.
cards.when_not: Exclusion or recursive identification with a known order, or statistical identification from heteroskedasticity or non-Gaussianity -> #20/#19; purely reduced-form forecasting or nowcasting -> #11/#12; regime-dependent (nonlinear) structural dynamics -> #150.

alternatives.criterion: Frequentist data-driven ID (heteroskedasticity/non-Gaussianity) or a recursive Cholesky — there are no theoretical sign/zero restrictions.
Purely reduced-form work (forecasting/Granger) without structural shock identification.
Regime-dependent (nonlinear/smooth-transition) structural dynamics.
You want predictive/conditional forecast bands rather than structural IRF/FEVD bands (bss_irf).

output_key_fields: bss_estimate: model (the 'PosteriorBSVARSIGN' producer handle) + B_median (the posterior median of the contemporaneous B) + ess (the importance-sampling ESS) + n_draws + ess_ratio + converged + restrictions (the active restrictions) + K/p/S/seed
bss_irf: irf = a long-format long data_frame (response, shock, horizon, median, lower, upper) — the set-identified band per (response,shock,horizon), chart-data
bss_fevd: fevd = long-format long (variable, shock, horizon, median share + lower/upper)
bss_forecast: forecast is a long frame (variable, horizon, median, lower, upper) + conditional (True when a conditional forecast was supplied)
interpretation_traps: SET identification, NOT point: the IRF is a posterior DISTRIBUTION -> read the median + the credible band, NEVER a single 'true' response; the band reflects identification AND estimation uncertainty.

ESS is a degeneracy diagnostic (mirroring #68 and #61): sign-only -> ess==n_draws (uniform); zero or narrative restrictions -> ess<n_draws (importance reweighting); a very low ess/n_draws means very few valid rotations -> an UNRELIABLE posterior -> STOP (ess_min_ratio, overridable with allow_nonconvergence).
Zero restrictions are written as 0 in the SAME sign_irf array (NOT a separate argument); they trigger importance sampling (Arias et al. 2018).
Impossible/excessive restrictions -> the sampler spends an enormous time searching for a valid rotation Q (the L1 default max_tries=Inf can hang; the node uses a finite default).
Stochasticity: bss_estimate (Gibbs) & bss_forecast (predictive sampling) require a seed (identical draws were verified); bss_irf/bss_fevd are deterministic transformations of the draws.
sources: Wang & Woźniak (Bayesian structural VARs with sign, zero and narrative restrictions)
Rubio-Ramírez J., Waggoner D., Zha T. 2010. Structural Vector Autoregressions: Theory of Identification and Algorithms for Inference. Review of Economic Studies, 77:2, 665-696.
Arias J., Rubio-Ramírez J., Waggoner D. 2018. Inference Based on SVARs Identified with Sign and Zero Restrictions. Econometrica, 86:2, 685-720.
Antolín-Díaz J., Rubio-Ramírez J. 2018. Narrative Sign Restrictions for SVARs. American Economic Review, 108:10, 2802-2829.
Waggoner D., Zha T. 2003. A Gibbs sampler for structural vector autoregressions. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 28:2, 349-366.
Giannone D., Lenza M., Primiceri G. 2015. Prior Selection for Vector Autoregressions. Review of Economics and Statistics, 97:2, 436-451.

cards.method: Smooth-transition / threshold / (m)logistic STRUCTURAL VAR (nonlinear, regime-dependent dynamics) + GIRF/GFEVD/linear IRF
cards.when: A multivariate series (d>=2) whose dynamics CHANGE by regime (recession vs expansion, high vs low volatility, monetary regime) — a smooth-transition or threshold switch between M regimes. You want regime-/state-dependent generalized impulse responses (GIRF), a generalized FEVD, or the linear IRF of one regime. weight_function: relative_dens/logistic/mlogit/exponential/threshold/exogenous.
cards.when_not: Linear, time-invariant dynamics suffice -> #11/#12; SMOOTH continuous variation of the coefficients WITHOUT discrete regimes -> #146/#14; linear structural shock identification -> #20/#19; fully structural non-Gaussian identification (outside the surface).

alternatives.criterion: Linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice — there are no regimes (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
Smooth CONTINUOUS variation of the coefficients (NOT discrete regimes) + stochastic volatility.
A linear structural VAR — data-driven shock identification within one regime (heteroskedasticity/non-Gaussianity).
You want the linear IRF of one fixed regime rather than a regime-/state-dependent GIRF (sst_girf).

output_key_fields: sst_fit: model (the 'stvar' producer handle) + loglik/IC (AIC/HQIC/BIC) + params + transition_weights ((T-p)xM regime probabilities, chart-data) + identification (reduced_form)/p/M/d
sst_girf: girf (a named list per shock: point_est [(N+1) x (d+M-1)] + conf_ints; row 1 = the impact at n=0) + which_shocks/N/ci — regime-dependent generalized responses
sst_gfevd: gfevd (a 3D array [horizon x variable x shock]) + initval_type/N — the generalized variance decomposition
sst_linear_irf: point_est (a 3-D array [variables x shock x horizon], slice 1 = the impact) + conf_ints (wild-bootstrap bands, or absent) + regime/N
interpretation_traps: The GIRF is NON-LINEAR & NON-SYMMETRIC: the response depends on the size/sign of the shock AND on the initial state (init_regime) — NOT like a linear IRF.
linear_IRF/GIRF on a reduced-form model -> an automatic lower-triangular recursive (Cholesky) ID (the variable ORDER matters); structural without an order -> the non-Gaussian fitSSTVAR.
the sst_linear_irf bootstrap bands exist ONLY for models with linear AR dynamics; on a genuinely regime-dependent STVAR they are absent (use the GIRF).

The stochastic GA log-likelihood is multimodal: small nrounds/ngen (the defaults are TINY) -> a local maximum; production runs raise nrounds/ngen. The seed is MANDATORY (without it the run is not reproducible).

sst_fit filters out unsuitable solutions (near-singular Sigma with eig<0.002, companion modulus>0.9985); if no appropriate solution is found -> rescale the series to a similar magnitude or run more rounds.
relative_dens => a Gaussian cond_dist ONLY; logistic/exponential => M=2; a non-relative_dens weight function => weightfun_pars is mandatory (e.g. c(switch_var, lag)).
sources: Lanne M., Virolainen S. 2025. A Gaussian smooth transition vector autoregressive model. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 178, 105162.
Virolainen S. (in press). Identification by non-Gaussianity in structural smooth transition VAR models. Econometric Reviews.
Hubrich K., Teräsvirta T. 2013. Thresholds and Smooth Transitions in VAR Models. CREATES Research Paper 2013-18, Aarhus University.
Tsay R. 1998. Testing and Modeling Multivariate Threshold Models. JASA, 93:443, 1188-1202.
Lanne M., Nyberg H. 2016. Generalized Forecast Error Variance Decomposition for Linear and Nonlinear Multivariate Models. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 78:4, 595-603.
Kilian L., Lütkepohl H. 2017. Structural Vector Autoregressive Analysis. Cambridge University Press.

cards.method: Gaussian / Student's-t Mixture VAR (regime switching through mixture-density weights) + GIRF/GFEVD/linear IRF
cards.when: A multivariate series (d>=2) whose dynamics SWITCH between M regimes with mixture-density weights that depend on the past (recession vs expansion, high vs low volatility, monetary regime). The regimes are Gaussian (GMVAR), Student's-t (StMVAR) or mixed (G-StMVAR). You want regime-/state-dependent GIRF, a generalized FEVD, or the linear IRF of one regime, with optional structural ID through conditional heteroskedasticity (W).
cards.when_not: Linear, time-invariant dynamics suffice -> #11/#12; a smooth-transition, threshold or (m)logistic switch rather than mixture-density weights -> #150; smooth CONTINUOUS variation of the coefficients rather than discrete regimes -> #146/#14; linear data-driven structural identification -> #20; the univariate case (d=1) is out of scope.

alternatives.criterion: The switch is smooth-transition/threshold/(m)logistic/exogenous — NOT mixture-density weights (the closest successor).
Linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice — there are no regimes (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
A linear structural VAR — data-driven shock identification within one regime.
You want the linear IRF of one fixed regime rather than a regime-/state-dependent GIRF (gmv_girf).

output_key_fields: gmv_fit: model (the 'gsmvar' producer handle) + loglik/IC (AIC/HQIC/BIC) + params/std_errors + mixing_weights (a T x M regime-probability path, chart-data) + M/d/p/model_type/structural/converged/n_converged
gmv_girf: girf (a named list per shock: point_est [(N+1) x variables] + conf_ints; row 1 is the impact at n=0) + which_shocks/N/ci — the non-linear generalized responses
gmv_gfevd: gfevd (a 3D array [(N+1) x variable x shock]) + initval_type/N — the generalized variance decomposition
gmv_linear_irf: point_est (a 3-D array [variables x shock x (N+1)], slice 1 = the impact) + conf_ints (4-D wild-bootstrap bands, or absent) + regime/N
interpretation_traps: The GIRF is NON-LINEAR & NON-SYMMETRIC: the response depends on the size/sign of the shock AND on the initial state (init_regimes) — NOT like a linear IRF
linear_IRF/GIRF on a reduced-form model -> an automatic lower-triangular recursive (Cholesky) ID (the variable ORDER matters); genuine structural ID -> structural_W (which requires M>=2)
the gmv_linear_irf bootstrap bands exist ONLY for models with linear AR dynamics (M==1, or constrained identical); with genuine regime switching they are absent (use the GIRF)
The GFEVD seeds length DEPENDS on initval_type (live-verified): nrow(data)-p+1 for 'data', R2 for 'random'; the wrapper computes it automatically

A stochastic genetic algorithm on a multimodal log-likelihood: a small ncalls (the TINY default of 2) lands on a local maximum; production uses ncalls=(M+1)^5. The seed is MANDATORY. Convergence post-gate: degenerate (no round converged, or a non-finite log-likelihood) => stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True
G-StMVAR requires M=c(M1,M2) (M1 Gaussian + M2 Student's-t regimes); Student's-t df near the boundary => effectively Gaussian
sources: Kalliovirta L., Meitz M., Saikkonen P. 2016. Gaussian mixture vector autoregression. Journal of Econometrics, 192:2, 485-498.
Virolainen S. 2022. A mixture autoregressive model based on Gaussian and Student's t-distributions. Studies in Nonlinear Dynamics & Econometrics, 26:4, 559-580.
Virolainen S. 2025. A statistically identified structural vector autoregression with endogenously switching volatility regime. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 43:1, 44-54.
Lanne M., Nyberg H. 2016. Generalized Forecast Error Variance Decomposition for Linear and Nonlinear Multivariate Models. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 78:4, 595-603.

cards.method: Desparsified/debiased LASSO inference (high-dimensional time series) + high-dimensional local projections (HDLP) with valid CIs — Adamek-Smeekes-Wilms
cards.when: High-dimensional inference: a point estimate + honest CIs + a z/Wald test for the target coefficient(s) when N (regressors) is large/≈T (dlasso_inference); or an IRF via local projection with MANY controls & valid asymptotic CIs (HAC/LRV variance) when a plain LP would be over-parameterised (dlasso_local_projection); optionally a state-dependent IRF (Ramey-Zubairy). The shock must already be identified/exogenous.
cards.when_not: A low-dimensional local projection with few controls -> #22 (OLS + Newey-West, no penalty); full-system FEVD/HD and efficiency -> #19/#20; shock identification from sign priors -> #21 (this card does NOT identify shocks, it takes them as given); pure forecasting rather than inference -> the shrinkage and ML forecasters.

alternatives.criterion: A low-dimensional LP/LP-IV: few controls, standard OLS + Newey-West bands suffice (no high-dimensional penalty/debiasing).
A full-system IRF/FEVD/HD with efficiency & lower variance at long horizons (not high-dimensional).
The shock is identified ONLY through sign restrictions; this card presupposes an already identified shock.

output_key_fields: coefficients (dlasso_inference): a frame of variable/bhat/se (debiased estimates, on the original scale)
intervals (dlasso_inference): a frame of variable + lower/upper per alpha (honest intervals)
joint_test (dlasso_inference): H0 is R*beta=q (by default all of H jointly zero) -> statistic/p_value
row_tests (dlasso_inference): the per-row z statistics + intervals (ONLY when the restriction matrix or q is supplied); n_selected: the number of non-zeros in the initial lasso
irf (dlasso_local_projection): a named list per state, each a frame of horizon + lower/bhat/upper per alpha (the interval bands — chart data)
dlasso_local_projection: states/n_states/hmax/lags/cumulate_y/OLS/seed
interpretation_traps: STOCHASTICITY (live-verified): although the debiasing is convex+analytic, the lambda selection uses RANDOM CV folds -> WITHOUT a seed two calls give different bhat. The seed is MANDATORY in both tools.
alphas is the significance level (0.05 -> a 95% CI); the column 'lower 0.05'/'upper 0.05' corresponds to alpha=0.05 (NOT the 5% quantile).
dlasso_local_projection: a hard gate requires hmax + lags < T. Beyond it the routine itself SILENTLY truncates hmax (to 0.8*eff - lags); the wrapper surfaces that as a message instead of losing it.
this card does NOT identify a structural shock — x must already be exogenous and identified (a proxy, an instrument, or an orthogonalised series). The validity of the inference rests on that.
q in dlasso_local_projection = the 'fast' controls (the high-dimensional space); q in dlasso_inference = the RHS of H0 the reference*beta=q. The SAME NAME but a DIFFERENT meaning.
OLS=True only in the low-dimensional case (otherwise the system is singular); state_variables: each column must be categorical OR a binary indicator of one regime.
sources: Adamek, Smeekes & Wilms 2021 'LASSO inference for high-dimensional time series' (arXiv:2007.10952)
van de Geer, Buhlmann, Ritov & Dezeure 2014 'On asymptotically optimal confidence regions and tests for high-dimensional models' (Annals of Statistics 42(3):1166-1202)
Plagborg-Moller & Wolf 2021 'Local projections and VARs estimate the same impulse responses' (Econometrica 89(2):955-980)
Ramey & Zubairy 2018 'Government spending multipliers in good times and in bad' (JPE 126(2):850-901); Andrews 1991 (Econometrica 59(3):817-858)

cards.method: Residual diagnostics for a reduced-form VAR: a multivariate LM autocorrelation test (+HC-robust/univariate) + a combined bootstrap ARCH test (CA/ET/MARCH) + a wild-bootstrap AC test
cards.when: After estimating a reduced-form VAR (vr_fit #11 -> varest, or the native vtt_fit -> VARfit): checking the adequacy of the residuals before structural ID/IRF. Autocorrelation (the Ahlgren-Catani multivariate LM + HC0-HC3 + per equation), ARCH/volatility clustering (the combined CA + Eklund-Terasvirta CCC-ARCH + multivariate MARCH, bootstrapped), wild-bootstrap AC p-values for a small/heteroskedastic sample.
cards.when_not: Estimating or selecting the VAR lags -> #11 (vr_fit); a cointegration bootstrap -> category 05; residual normality (this card has NO normality test); producing IRF/FEVD (it is purely diagnostics); a bare residual matrix as input (the LM auxiliary regressions need the whole fitted model).

alternatives.criterion: A small sample or heteroskedastic errors: wild-bootstrap p-values (Ahlgren-Catani Algorithm 1/2) instead of the asymptotic chi^2 of vtt_portmanteau.
The test concerns ARCH/volatility clustering in the residuals (not autocorrelation).
Autocorrelation is rejected -> increase the lags of the reduced-form VAR and re-test.

output_key_fields: vtt_portmanteau: a multivariate frame (HCtype, the statistic Q, p_value, df=K^2*h, decision) + h/K/alpha/inputType; univariate=True adds a per-equation frame (df=h)

vtt_arch: one entry per test -> CA {statistic = 1-min_i p(LM_i), boot_p, uni_stat, uni_boot_p, decision}; MARCH {statistic, asymp_p, boot_p, df=K^2(K+1)^2 h/4, decision}; ET {statistic, asymp_p, boot_p, df=K*h, decision} + B/dist/seed
vtt_wildboot: a wild data_frame (HCtype, the statistic from ACtest, WB.p, df, decision) + WBtype/WBdist/numberOfErrors/numberOfNA/seed
vtt_fit: the model handle (a 'VARfit' producer) + K/p/N/variables/residuals (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: Polarity: H0 = CLEAN residuals (no AC / no ARCH). p<alpha => reject => misspecification is present (autocorrelation/ARCH) => the VAR FAILS the test (not the other way round).
vtt_arch & vtt_wildboot are bootstrap-based => the seed is MANDATORY; the same seed => the same bootstrap p-values (cache key); without a seed they are uncacheable.

The CA (Catani-Ahlgren) test ALWAYS runs inside vtt_arch: switching it off makes the routine fail. The CA statistic is bootstrap-only (there is no asymptotic p or df); only the ET and MARCH toggles are exposed.
The input is a fitted VAR, NOT a bare residual matrix: residuals alone give silently wrong LM auxiliary regressions (the vtt_check_fit gate blocks it).

univariate takes only False or True — the third documented value fails (blocked). The MARCH df = K^2(K+1)^2 h/4 grows fast with K, so a small sample gives low power. The wild-bootstrap p-values arrive as WBr_pv (recursive) or WBf_pv (fixed).
sources: Ahlgren, N. & Catani, P. (2016), 'Wild bootstrap tests for autocorrelation in vector autoregressive models', Statistical Papers, doi:10.1007/s00362-016-0744-0

Catani & Ahlgren 2016 (the combined bootstrap LM ARCH test); Eklund & Teräsvirta 2007 (CCC-ARCH LM); Lütkepohl 2006, New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis, sect. 16.5 (multivariate ARCH-LM); MacKinnon & White 1985 (HCCME)

vtt_fit

cards.method: Univariate GARCH family (vanilla/egarch/gjr/aparch/component)
cards.when: modelling conditional volatility in univariate returns (volatility clustering); ML estimation of a GARCH + an h-step forecast of sigma_t + a rolling backtest; a modern API with a numerical optimiser and automatic-differentiation standard errors
cards.when_not: multivariate volatility or correlation (-> #29/#155); regime-switching volatility (-> #31); return levels with no ARCH effects (a non-significant run_arch_test); realized or intraday volatility (-> #156)

alternatives.criterion: you need the fGARCH or component-GARCH submodels, or a VaR rolling backtest with coverage tests
multivariate conditional covariance/correlation (>=2 assets)
the volatility switches between regimes (Markov switching)
a large sample + you want a fixed unconditional variance without estimating omega

output_key_fields: coefficients: named (mu/omega/alpha*/beta*/gamma*/shape/skew..) depending on the model/distribution
persistence: sum(alpha+beta) ~ the persistence; ~1 => near-integrated (IGARCH-like), see near_nonstationary
sigma: the conditional standard-deviation series (chart data); sigma_forecast (tg_predict): the h-step sigma_t
converged/kkt1/kkt2: the optimisation KKT conditions (converged=KKT1, first order); a stateless capture
aic/bic/loglik: for comparing the model and the distribution; table (tg_backtest): sigma/actual/convergence per forecast
interpretation_traps: y MUST be returns (log/simple), NOT price levels — the wrapper does not difference
persistence>=0.999 (near_nonstationary=True) => the unconditional variance explodes and the long-horizon sigma_t forecast is unreliable
egarch persistence is measured on the log-variance (a different scale from the vanilla alpha+beta)
converged=False (the first-order conditions are not met) => the solution is not an optimum; do not interpret the coefficients or their standard errors
the standard errors are absent or NaN when the Hessian is not positive definite (common at boundary persistence)
tg_estimate/tg_backtest are deterministic (ML); only tg_predict with nsim>0 is stochastic (seeded 2025)
sources: Galanos 2024 (univariate GARCH models estimated with automatic differentiation)
Glosten Jagannathan Runkle 1993 (J. Finance 48:1779, GJR); Ding Granger Engle 1993 (APARCH)

c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the returns from a file)

cards.method: Multivariate GARCH — Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC/aDCC/CCC)
cards.when: time-varying covariance/correlation of >=2 return series; volatility spillovers, time-varying correlation, dynamic hedge ratios, portfolio risk (the long-format )
cards.when_not: univariate volatility (-> #28/#154); many assets (N above roughly 10; the DCC parameter and estimation burden -> GO-GARCH or factor models); level or non-stationary series (take returns first); regime-switching volatility (-> #31)

alternatives.criterion: the older pipeline of #28/#29, or the copula and GO-GARCH variants that are not exposed here
the correlation does not vary appreciably (the Engle-Sheppard test / a ~constant tm_cov) — fewer parameters
heavy tails/joint tail dependence in the standardized returns
copula dependence or orthogonalisation for a larger N

output_key_fields: coefficients: the DCC dynamic parameters (alpha_1/beta_1; gamma_1 for adcc; shape for mvt); constant -> empty (no dynamics)
coef_table: term/Estimate/Std. Error/t value/Pr(>|t|) of the DCC parameters
correlation_last / covariance_last: the N×N last in-sample conditional matrix (chart-data)
loglik/AIC/BIC/nobs/n_series/n_pars; converged: convergence of the second stage (a stateless capture)
covariance/correlation (tm_cov): an N×N×T array; forecast_covariance/forecast_correlation (tm_predict): N×N×h (the mean)
interpretation_traps: alpha+beta ~ 1 -> high persistence of the correlation; alpha ~ 0 -> ~constant (the DCC adds nothing)
with constant dynamics the tm_cov correlation is N×N×1 (time-invariant); only the covariance varies, through the GARCH variances
the internal autodiff object MUST be kept: without it the dynamic DCC/aDCC second stage fails
converged=False, or an enormous or NaN standard error in coef_table -> a degenerate solution; do not interpret the DCC parameters
the mean forecast (distribution=False) is the centre; the uncertainty lives in the simulated paths and is not exposed flat
sources: Cappiello, Engle & Sheppard 2006 asymmetric DCC (J. Financial Econometrics 4:537)

c15_model_evaluation/arch.run_arch_test (ARCH-LM: there must be ARCH effects in each series, otherwise GARCH is pointless)
tm_cov (post: check whether the dynamic correlation really varies — if not, a constant/CCC suffices)

cards.method: Realized (co)variance & intraday spot volatility from high-frequency data
cards.when: you have intraday data and you want the ex-post realized volatility/covariance of ONE day (rCov=the sum of r², the jump-robust rBPCov/medRV, the noise-robust rKernelCov/rTSCov), a semivariance decomposition, or an intraday spot-volatility pattern
cards.when_not: daily or low-frequency series -> a parametric GARCH (#28/#154); conditional or forecast volatility -> GARCH; a multi-day dynamic covariance -> DCC (#29/#155); you have no intraday observations

alternatives.criterion: conditional/forecast volatility from daily returns rather than an ex-post realized measure
a dynamic multi-day correlation/covariance rather than a per-day realized covariance
suspected jumps in the intraday series (a jump-robust integrated variance)
market microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce) -> noise-robust estimators
you want downside/upside (negative/positive/mixed/concordant) semicovariance

output_key_fields: hf_realized_var: realized_variance (the scalar sum or a robust version) + realized_vol=sqrt; K (rTSCov only); n_obs/n_returns
hf_realized_cov: rcov (the N×N covariance, or the correlation when cor=True); correlation (derived from the covariance when cor=False); asset_names; n_assets
hf_realized_cov with measure=rSemiCov: semicov=list{mixed,negative,positive,concordant} N×N + rcov (=the sum)
hf_spot_vol: spot_vol (the numeric intraday series); timestamps; daily (per day); periodic (the intraday pattern); n_na
interpretation_traps: the multivariate two-scale covariance requires a LIST of per-asset series; a single multi-column input reduces SILENTLY to a scalar — the wrapper handles that, so do not bypass it
measure='medRV' -> rMedRVar (rMedRV is deprecated in 1.0.3)
the two-scale and kernel covariances require PRICES (the returns are formed internally); the two-scale estimator needs n>=10*K, otherwise the gate stops
alignBy is NOT exposed for the realized measures: the data must ALREADY be sampled (e.g. 5-min) intraday data for ONE day; the value is timestamp-invariant without alignBy
spotVol with method='detPer' ideally wants >=50 days; fewer -> a warning (unstable periodicity), not an error; read n_na
realized variance ≠ conditional/forecast variance: it is an ex-post estimate of one day's integrated variance, not a forecast
sources: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004 Econometrica 72(3) (realized covariation); Zhang, Mykland & Aït-Sahalia 2005 JASA 100(472) (two-scale realized volatility)
Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003 (Econometrica 71:579) — realized volatility
Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004 (J. Financial Econometrics) — bipower variation (rBPCov)
Andersen, Dobrev & Schaumburg 2012 (J. Econometrics 169:75) — MedRV, jump-robust
Barndorff-Nielsen, Hansen, Lunde & Shephard 2008 (Econometrica 76:1481) — realized kernels (rKernelCov)
Bollerslev, Li, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2020 (J. Econometrics 217:411) — realized semicovariance (rSemiCov)
Boudt, Croux & Laurent 2011 (J. Empirical Finance 18:353) — deterministic periodicity spot vol (spotVol detPer)

hf_realized_cov (a multivariate realized covariance/semicovariance; >=2 assets)
