cards.method: GARCH-MIDAS (a short-run GARCH × a long-run MIDAS macro component)
cards.when: you want to link the volatility of high-frequency returns (y) to a slow macro variable (x; e.g. industrial production, the NFCI) through MIDAS; the volatility = tau_t (long run, macro-driven) × g_t (short-run GARCH). mfg_fit -> mfg_predict; mfg_simulate = a standalone DGP
cards.when_not: a purely univariate GARCH with no exogenous macro driver -> #28/#154; regime-switching volatility -> #31; multivariate work -> #29/#155; you have no low-frequency variable that stays constant within each period

alternatives.criterion: there is no macro long-run driver; a plain univariate GARCH
a regime change (not a slow macro trend) drives the volatility
you want free (non-monotone) MIDAS weighting -> an extra w1 parameter

output_key_fields: par: a named vector of estimates (mu/alpha/beta/gamma/m/theta/w2[+w1 in the unrestricted case])
coefficients: a frame of estimate/rob_std_err/p_value/opg_std_err/opg_p_value
tau: the long-run component (chart); g: the short-run component (chart); tau×g = the total variance
variance_ratio: the share of variance explained by the long-run component; tau_forecast: the one-step long-run value
llh/bic; convergence (the integer optim code); converged (logical)
interpretation_traps: silent non-convergence: optim RETURNS a fit even when convergence!=0 — CHECK the converged field before interpreting
x MUST be constant within each low_freq period; mixed values trip the 'a SINGLE unique value' gate (not a silent error)
a column literally NAMED 'date' with a date dtype is mandatory, AND the low_freq column must be a date as well; otherwise it is blocked
K must be smaller than the number of low_freq periods (otherwise the MIDAS lag builds negative-length vectors)
beta_restricted pins w1=1 (a monotonically decreasing weighting); beta_unrestricted adds a free w1 parameter
mfg_predict returns the total conditional variance per horizon (not tau or g separately)
sources: Engle, Ghysels & Sohn 2013 'Stock Market Volatility and Macroeconomic Fundamentals' (REStat 95:776)
Conrad & Kleen 2020 'Two are better than one: Volatility forecasting using multiplicative component GARCH-MIDAS' (J. Applied Econometrics 35:19)

cards.method: BEKK-family multivariate GARCH (BEKK/diagonal/scalar) + multivariate VaR + Volatility IRF
cards.when: N-dimensional returns; you want the full BEKK dynamic conditional covariance (spillovers/co-volatility) + risk (a portfolio VaR) or volatility impulse responses
cards.when_not: a large N (BEKK carries roughly O(N²) parameters -> the curse of dimensionality; go to DCC, #155/#29); a univariate series (-> #28); you need an asymmetric VIRF (not implemented)

alternatives.criterion: a large N / you want a scalable conditional correlation rather than a full BEKK
fewer parameters (diagonal/scalar) when the full BEKK is not identified
a non-model-based (historical/gaussian/modified) VaR without MGARCH dynamics

the VIRF exists only for a SYMMETRIC BEKK (asymmetric=False); an asymmetric fit is blocked by a gate
portfolio_weights left unset gives a per-series VaR (N columns); a vector of length N gives a portfolio VaR (1 column)
the BEKK curse of dimensionality: ~O(N²) parameters; for N>~4 prefer DCC (#155/#29)

cards.method: (Hierarchical) Hidden Markov Models + Viterbi global decoding + forecasting
cards.when: a univariate series (returns/observations) with latent discrete regimes; you want a full HMM with probabilistic state-dependent distributions (normal/t/gamma/..) + decoding of the most likely state sequence
cards.when_not: regime-conditional GARCH volatility (-> #31, msg_fit_*); a linear Markov-switching model with regressors (-> #30, ms_fit); threshold (self-exciting) non-Markovian regimes (-> #32, setar_fit); hierarchical two-level data (the hierarchy switch is not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: the regimes concern volatility clustering (the conditional variance), not the level/mean
a Markov-switching linear model with exogenous regressors
the regimes are determined by an observable threshold variable, not by a latent Markov chain
fat tails in the returns within a regime

output_key_fields: hmm_fit: log_lik/AIC/BIC/npar/nobs; estimates (a data_frame parameter/lb/estimate/ub — the Gamma_ij transitions + mu/sigma/df per state); nstates/sdd
hmm_fit convergence: nlm_code (1/2=OK); converged (bool); n_accepted_runs — check them BEFORE interpreting (a stateless node: stderr is lost)
hmm_decode: states (an integer sequence of length T); state_counts/state_labels; n_states_used; degenerate (True => fewer than nstates were actually used)
hmm_predict: state_probs (ahead × nstates probabilities); forecast (ahead × {lb,estimate,ub} observations); it decodes internally (predict requires it)
interpretation_traps: state labelling is not inherently ordered (label switching); identify the states through the mu/sigma in estimates, not through the index 1/2
degenerate=True or converged=False => the solution collapsed or did not converge — do NOT interpret the regimes; raise the number of runs or change the state-dependent distribution
AIC/BIC are comparable ONLY on the same data & sdd family (a different nstates is nested; a different sdd is non-nested)
gamma/lognormal require strictly positive values, poisson non-negative integers — for raw returns use normal/t
the artificial date column is a placeholder the fitter requires; it does not affect the estimation, so do not read it as a real calendar
sources: Oelschläger, Adam & Michels 2024 JSS (hidden Markov models for financial time series)
Zucchini, MacDonald & Langrock 2016, 'Hidden Markov Models for Time Series' 2nd ed. (Viterbi global decoding §5)

cards.when: a univariate return series; you want the latent (unobserved) volatility as a stochastic process with a full Bayesian posterior (uncertainty bands on the volatility), not a deterministic GARCH-type recursion
cards.when_not: you want a point or ML volatility estimate, or closed-form forecasting -> #28/#154; multivariate volatility or correlation -> #29/#155; regime-switching volatility -> #31; very large samples on a tight latency budget (the MCMC is expensive)

alternatives.criterion: you want a deterministic ML GARCH with closed-form forecasts rather than latent-SV MCMC
the volatility changes regime (Markov switching) rather than following a continuous AR(1) log-volatility
multivariate volatility + a time-varying correlation
fat tails in the returns beyond what the stochastic volatility delivers
asymmetry: negative returns raise the volatility more (the leverage effect)

output_key_fields: para_summary: a matrix mean/sd/5%/50%/95%/ESS per parameter (mu=the level, phi=persistence, sigma=vol-of-vol, [nu],[rho])
ess / min_ess / converged: the convergence capture — converged=False ⇒ insufficient mixing, do not interpret the posteriors
vol_mean (with vol_time): the posterior mean of exp(h_t/2) per time point (chart data; absent when keeptime='last')
sv_predict: vol_mean/vol_median + vol_lower(5%)/vol_upper(95%) per step — posterior predictive bands of the future volatility
sv_simulate: y (returns) + vol (the true latent volatility) + para — chart-data for a synthetic path
interpretation_traps: check the converged flag first: SV MCMC can silently suffer monstrous autocorrelation (a very low phi ESS); 500 draws is a smoke test — for production raise draws/burnin
phi≈1 ⇒ an almost non-stationary log-volatility (high persistence); phi near 0 ⇒ the volatility is nearly white noise
y is returns (roughly mean-zero), NOT price levels; otherwise the log(y^2) offset produces nonsense
vol_mean refers to exp(h_t/2) (a standard deviation), not a variance; do not compare it directly with a GARCH conditional variance
predict/simulate are stochastic -> seed=2025 by default; the same seed ⇒ the same draws (a reproducible node)
keeptime='last' discards the latent path (vol_mean is absent) — use it only when you do not need the volatility chart

cards.method: Multivariate factor stochastic volatility (Bayesian MCMC) + model-implied & predictive covariance/correlation
cards.when: multivariate returns (a small to medium N); you want a time-varying covariance/correlation through a few latent factors with stochastic-volatility dynamics + Bayesian posterior uncertainty
cards.when_not: a univariate series (-> #162, sv_sample); you want a parametric multivariate GARCH point estimate, DCC or GO-GARCH (-> #29/#155); a very large N with no factor structure; too few observations (below roughly 50) for reliable MCMC

alternatives.criterion: you want a parametric DCC/GO-GARCH point-estimate MGARCH rather than a Bayesian factor structure
a univariate series — you do not need a multivariate covariance
you need identification/interpretation of the factor loadings (not only the covariance) — it stabilises the MCMC

output_key_fields: facload_mean (fsv_sample): the posterior-mean matrix of factor loadings (N × factors); it shows which series load on the common factors
communalities / communality_total (fsv_sample): the share of variance per series, and in total, explained by the factors
para_mean (fsv_sample): the posterior-mean mu/phi/sigma of each idiosyncratic and factor log-volatility process (phi -> 1 means high persistence)
ledermann_bound / exceeds_ledermann (fsv_sample): the static bound on identifiable factors; True means take care when interpreting the loadings
cov_mean/cor_mean, with their _sd (fsv_cov): the posterior mean and posterior standard deviation of the conditional covariance and correlation at the last t
pred_cov_mean/pred_cor_mean (fsv_predict): a list of posterior-mean matrices per horizon, keyed by the horizon
interpretation_traps: restrict='none' is preferable for ESTIMATING the covariance/forecast; 'upper' only when you want identifiable/interpretable loadings (a strong a-priori assumption)

exceeds_ledermann=True is NOT an error: the sampler deliberately allows more factors than the static Ledermann bound, since identification comes from the time-varying volatilities; it is a caveat for interpreting the loadings, nothing more
the signs of the factor loadings & factors are not identified by the likelihood (sign switching); interpret magnitudes/patterns, not absolute signs
fsv_cov returns ONLY the last time point (keeptime='last') = the current conditional covariance, not the whole path
MCMC: few draws/burnin -> noise in the posterior; the posterior_sd fields show the uncertainty, do not read only the means

Kastner, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Lopes 2017, 'Efficient Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Factor Stochastic Volatility Models', JCGS 26(4):905-917
Kastner 2019, 'Sparse Bayesian time-varying covariance estimation in many dimensions', J. Econometrics 210(1):98-115 (the Normal-Gamma shrinkage prior)

fsv_predict (the posterior predictive h-step cov/cor)

cards.method: Discrete-time Markov chain: estimating the transition matrix (MLE/Laplace/bootstrap CI) + long-run analytics (the stationary distribution, mean first passage times, irreducibility, period)
cards.when: a discrete sequence of states (regimes/ratings/states); you want the estimated transition matrix, the long-run (stationary) distribution, expected first passage times, or an irreducibility/period check
cards.when_not: continuous return or volatility series -> #28/#154; latent regime switching on continuous observations -> #30/#31; a continuous-time Markov chain; higher-order dependence or order selection

alternatives.criterion: the regimes are latent on a continuous observed series, not directly observed states
Markov switching in the variance of continuous returns
a hidden Markov model with emission distributions rather than observed states

output_key_fields: transitionMatrix: the estimated transition matrix (rows=from, they sum to 1)
standardError / lowerEndpointMatrix / upperEndpointMatrix: the SE + CI per element (confidenceLevel)
log_likelihood: the log-likelihood of the fit
steadyStates: the stationary distribution (a matrix; >1 row if there are several recurrent classes)
the mean first-passage time: the expected number of steps i->j (the diagonal is 0); absent, with mfpt_note, when the chain is not ergodic
is_irreducible / period: the irreducibility flag + the period (blank, with period_note, when it is not irreducible)
interpretation_traps: the fitter does NOT fail on a gap (it treats it as a separate state) and it accepts a single state — the wrapper's gates block both explicitly
steadyStates returns a MATRIX: >1 row means several closed recurrent classes (a non-unique stationary distribution)
the period computation emits a WARNING rather than an error on a non-irreducible chain -> the wrapper returns a blank plus a note; do not interpret an invalid value
the mean first-passage time requires an ergodic (irreducible) chain -> otherwise it is absent, with a note, rather than an error that would crash the node
method='bootstrap' is STOCHASTIC (resampling CI) -> use the same seed for reproducibility; mle/laplace are deterministic
sources: Spedicato 2017 (discrete-time Markov chains: estimation and analysis)
Norris 1997, Markov Chains (CUP) — the stationary distribution, first passage, periodicity

cards.method: Instrumental variables / 2SLS (a three-part formula) + weak-instruments / Wu-Hausman / Sargan diagnostics
cards.when: endogenous regressor(s) — the regressor is correlated with the error (simultaneity/omitted variables/measurement error); you have valid external instruments; you want a consistent causal estimate with 2SLS + full identification/endogeneity/over-identification diagnostics
cards.when_not: all regressors are exogenous (use OLS); fewer instruments than endogenous regressors (under-identified); weak instruments (the weak-IV bias calls for Anderson-Rubin or weak-IV-robust inference); panel fixed-effects IV -> #33; ML-driven high-dimensional controls -> #45

alternatives.criterion: the classic two-part IV formula 'y ~ x | z'
high-dimensional fixed effects + IV in the same fit (panel)
many/non-linear controls, ML nuisance, debiased inference
outliers or heavy tails -> a robust IV fit

output_key_fields: coefficients / coef_table: the 2SLS estimates + Estimate/Std. Error/t/p (the structural equation)
conf_int: coefficient CIs at conf_level; sigma/df_residual/nobs/r_squared/adj_r_squared
n_endogenous / n_instruments: the identification counts (over-identified <=> excluded instruments > endogenous regressors)
weak_instruments: a list {df1,df2,statistic,p_value} PER endogenous regressor (the first-stage F); weak_instruments_flag = any F<10 (Staiger-Stock)
wu_hausman: {df1,df2,statistic,p_value}, the endogeneity test (rejection -> the regressor really is endogenous, IV is justified)
sargan: {df1, df2, statistic, p_value}, the over-identification test; df1=0 with a blank statistic when just-identified; plus the overidentified flag
diagnostics: the full table (chart-data); fitted/residuals: chart-data
interpretation_traps: three-part only: 'y ~ exog | endog | instruments'; a 2-part formula is blocked (go to #34 AER); an explicit gate on the number of RHS parts
weak instruments: F<10 (weak_instruments_flag) => 2SLS bias + invalid standard CIs -> use weak-IV-robust inference; do NOT trust coef_table
the Sargan test is meaningful ONLY when the model is over-identified (df1>0); just-identified gives df1=0 and a blank value — not an error, there is simply no test
Wu-Hausman: if it is NOT rejected, OLS is consistent+efficient — IV only loses efficiency (larger SE)
method='M'/'MM' changes the estimator (robust), not only the SE; the diagnostics are interpreted on the robust fit
sources: Fox, Kleiber & Zeileis (instrumental-variables regression by two-stage least squares)
Wu 1973 / Hausman 1978 endogeneity test; Staiger & Stock 1997 (Econometrica 65:557) the weak-instruments F>10 rule

cards.method: Heterogeneity-robust dynamic DiD event study (de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille; non-binary/non-absorbing treatments)
cards.when: a staggered panel where the treatment is non-binary AND/OR non-absorbing (it can switch off or change intensity) and past treatments affect the current outcome; you want dynamic event-study effects + a placebo pre-trends test + an average total effect, robust to heterogeneous effects (without the negative-weights bias of the TWFE)
cards.when_not: the treatment is binary AND absorbing (clean staggered adoption) -> #36/#37, which are more direct; a simple 2x2 -> an interaction in #33; heterogeneity by covariates (CATE) rather than by event time -> #44

alternatives.criterion: the treatment is binary & absorbing; a doubly-robust ATT(g,t) + bootstrap bands
an absorbing design; imputation-based, analytic SE, speed
heterogeneity by covariates (CATE) rather than by relative event time
robustness to parallel-trends violations; it REQUIRES reordering coef_b/coef_vcov into chronological order (pre-periods=placebos first) before chaining

output_key_fields: estimate/se/lb_ci/ub_ci in effects: the event-study path — the dynamic treatment effects per relative period
ate_estimate/ate_available: the average total effect per unit of treatment (blank and False when trends_lin=True)
estimate/se in placebos: the placebo (pre-trend) estimators — E[placebo]=0 under parallel trends and no anticipation
p_jointeffects (effects>=2) / p_jointplacebo (placebo>=2): the joint tests; p_equality_effects when effects_equal=True
coef_b / coef_vcov: the full coefficient vector + its covariance, ordered [effects.., placebos..] with the post-periods first; for #168 reorder them chronologically, the placebos first
interpretation_traps: chaining TRAP for #168: coef_b is ordered [effects.., placebos..], post-periods first, while #168 expects CHRONOLOGICAL order (pre-periods first, with numPrePeriods equal to the number of placebos); passing coef_b AS IS produces silently wrong robust intervals — reorder it first
a placebo ~0 SUPPORTS (does not prove) parallel trends/no anticipation; a high p_jointplacebo means the hypothesis is not rejected
trends_lin=True => the ATE is NOT computed (ate_available=False, ate_estimate blank) — do not read it as 0
placebo>effects: the routine SILENTLY clamps placebo down to effects -> the wrapper hard-blocks it, so there is no silent result
a gap in a core column makes the routine silently drop rows (a partial sample) -> the wrapper hard-blocks it; the full sample is required
ci_level>=100 is accepted silently by the routine -> the wrapper blocks it; it must lie in (0,100)
a bootstrap gives stochastic standard errors; the seed (default 2025) makes them reproducible; the analytical standard errors are deterministic
sources: de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2020 AER 110(9) (fuzzy DiD / heterogeneous treatment effects)
de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2024 Econometrics Journal (dynamic/event-study non-absorbing DiD)
Rambachan & Roth 2023 ReStud (a more credible approach to parallel trends) — the consumer of coef_b/coef_vcov

Pitfalls: chaining TRAP for #168: coef_b is ordered [effects.., placebos..], post-periods first, while #168 expects CHRONOLOGICAL order (pre-periods first, with numPrePeriods equal to the number of placebos); passing coef_b AS IS produces silently wrong robust intervals — reorder it first · a placebo ~0 SUPPORTS (does not prove) parallel trends/no anticipation; a high p_jointplacebo means the hypothesis is not rejected · trends_lin=True => the ATE is NOT computed (ate_available=False, ate_estimate blank) — do not read it as 0 · placebo>effects: the routine SILENTLY clamps placebo down to effects -> the wrapper hard-blocks it, so there is no silent result · a gap in a core column makes the routine silently drop rows (a partial sample) -> the wrapper hard-blocks it; the full sample is required · ci_level>=100 is accepted silently by the routine -> the wrapper blocks it; it must lie in (0,100) · a bootstrap gives stochastic standard errors; the seed (default 2025) makes them reproducible; the analytical standard errors are deterministic
Sources: de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2020 AER 110(9) (fuzzy DiD / heterogeneous treatment effects) · de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2024 Econometrics Journal (dynamic/event-study non-absorbing DiD) · Rambachan & Roth 2023 ReStud (a more credible approach to parallel trends) — the consumer of coef_b/coef_vcov

cards.method: Goodman-Bacon decomposition of the TWFE DiD coefficient (staggered adoption)
cards.when: you ran a two-way fixed-effects DiD (unit+time FE) on a panel with STAGGERED adoption of the intervention and you want to see WHAT the single TWFE coefficient is made of — which 2x2 comparisons feed it and with what weights
cards.when_not: an unbalanced panel (it fails deliberately); simultaneous adoption by everyone (no staggered variation, so the decomposition is trivial); you want an ESTIMATOR that is unbiased under staggering — that is #36/#37, not a diagnostic; a continuous or non-binary treatment

alternatives.criterion: you want an UNBIASED group-time ATT rather than a diagnostic; a never/late-treated control group exists
you want an efficient imputation estimator robust to heterogeneity
you want cohort-interacted event-study estimates, not a diagnosis of the TWFE

output_key_fields: two_by_twos: a data_frame per 2x2 comparison {treated, untreated (99999=never-treated), estimate, weight, type}
type_summary: aggregate weights + the weighted mean estimate per comparison type (chart-data for the Goodman-Bacon table)
twfe_estimate: the overall TWFE beta as a weighted-average identity (= sum(w*est); with covariates = Omega*beta_hat_w + (1-Omega)*sum(w*est))
total_weight: the sum of the 2x2 weights (~1); n_2x2: the number of comparisons
has_covariates/within_estimate/within_weight: the share and estimate of the within component (Omega, beta_hat_w); blank without covariates
interpretation_traps: WATCH the 'Later vs Earlier Treated' comparison: it uses ALREADY-treated units as controls -> a forbidden comparison; a LARGE weight here means the TWFE is contaminated by negative-weighting/heterogeneity bias
untreated=99999 denotes the never-treated group (the 'clean' 'Treated vs Untreated' type); it is not a real time value
negative weights, or negative estimates under staggering, signal that the TWFE coefficient may carry the wrong sign -> move to an unbiased estimator (#36/#37)
with time-varying covariates the within component enters (Omega>0); the identity still holds, but the decomposition approximates the TWFE through FWL
it REQUIRES a strongly balanced panel; an unbalanced one -> a hard error (not a silent mistake)
sources: Goodman-Bacon 2021 (J. Econometrics 225:254, 'Difference-in-Differences with Variation in Treatment Timing')
the TWFE identity was verified numerically against lm(y ~ treated + factor(id) + factor(time)) (exact)
precondition_tools: c07_causality_policy/fixed_effects_ols.fx_fit (the source of the TWFE coefficient being decomposed — unit+time FE)
c01_preparation_prechecks/panel_unit_root.run_panel_unit_root (macro/large-T only: stationarity before a panel DiD)

cards.method: Honest/robust inference under relaxed parallel trends (Rambachan-Roth sensitivity analysis)
cards.when: you have an event-study/DiD estimate (betahat + vcov per period) and you want an interval that does NOT break down when the parallel-trends assumption is violated slightly; the sensitivity of the inference to that violation
cards.when_not: you have no per-period event-study coefficients (an upstream leads/lags estimation is needed); a single post-period with no pre-periods (no basis for relative magnitudes); you do not care about robustness to parallel trends (the classic CI suffices)

alternatives.criterion: when the violation is expected to be SMOOTH (bounded curvature of the trend) — you parameterise it with M
when you do not want to choose M in absolute units — you bound the post-period violation as a multiple (Mbar) of the observed pre-period violation

alternatives.alt: #33 fx_fit event study, without the honest correction
alternatives.criterion: when you are willing to assume strict parallel trends (no sensitivity analysis)

output_key_fields: results: a data_frame lb/ub per value of M (smoothness) or Mbar (relmag) — chart-data for a sensitivity plot
lb/ub: numeric vectors of the robust CI bounds per value of the bound
method: the CI method that was used (FLCI/Conditional/C-F/C-LF)
Delta: the restriction set (DeltaSD for smoothness, DeltaRM for relmag, Original for the baseline)
M (smoothness) / Mbar (relmag): the value of the bound in each row; numPrePeriods/numPostPeriods/alpha
interpretation_traps: the CI WIDENS as M/Mbar grows — that is the point (robustness), not a problem
the breakdown value = the largest M/Mbar at which the CI does NOT contain 0; compare it with honest_original_cs (the baseline)
Mbar=1 (relmag) => the post-period violation is allowed to be as large as the LARGEST pre-period violation — often the natural reference
M is in ABSOLUTE units (the maximum second difference); Mbar is RELATIVE (in units of the pre-trend) — do not confuse them
betahat/sigma MUST be in time order (pre then post, or consistent with the indices); the wrong order -> a silently wrong CI
negative M or Mbar are accepted silently by the routine — they are blocked here (gate)
sources: Rambachan & Roth 2023, 'A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends', Review of Economic Studies 90(5):2555-2591
precondition_tools: c07_causality_policy/fixed_effects_ols.fx_fit (event-study leads/lags -> betahat, sigma)
c07_causality_policy/staggered_did.did_aggregate_att (Callaway-Sant'Anna aggregation -> dynamic effects)
c07_causality_policy/hac_robust_standard.vcov_hac (a robust vcov -> the sigma matrix)
honest_original_cs (the baseline CI under strict parallel trends — the reference point)

cards.method: RD with multiple cutoffs / multiple scores (multi-cutoff & multi-score RD, robust bias-corrected)
cards.when: an RD design with MULTIPLE cutoffs (rdmc: C varies by unit) or cumulative cutoffs on one score (rdms); you want a pooled estimand + per-cutoff estimates, robust bias-corrected (Cattaneo-Titiunik-Vazquez-Bare)
cards.when_not: a single cutoff -> #38; a manipulation or density test (McCrary); sharp versus fuzzy without multiple cutoffs; a two-score design with a second running variable (deliberately excluded — the range matrix is fragile)

alternatives.criterion: a single cutoff (single-cutoff sharp/fuzzy RD)
parametric/non-parametric RD with an IK bandwidth, one cutoff
cumulative cutoffs on ONE score & you want a pooled estimand
conventional (not robust bias-corrected) p-values/CI for comparison

output_key_fields: pooled: {tau, se, pv, ci_l, ci_r, hl, hr, Nhl, Nhr} — the pooled estimand (always for rd_multi_cutoff; for rd_multi_score only with xnorm, otherwise available=False)
per_cutoff: a data_frame {cutoff, coef, se, ci_l, ci_r, pv, Nh_left, Nh_right, Nh_total[, weight]} = chart-data per cutoff
weighted (rdmc): {coef, se, pv, ci_l, ci_r} — the weighted average of all cutoff-specific estimates
cutoffs / n_cutoffs: the cutoff values (rdmc: sort(unique(C)); rdms: C as supplied)
cfail / n_failed: the cutoffs where the RD fit failed (degeneracy); n_failed>0 -> a suspect estimate
kernel / p / bwselect / level / conventional: the settings that were actually used
interpretation_traps: rdmc: C is a per-observation cutoff variable (the SAME length as X); rdms: C is a vector of cutoff values — do not confuse them (a wrong length -> silent recycling, blocked by a gate)
a gap in Y, X or the fuzzy assignment is ignored SILENTLY (N falls with no warning) -> a gate forbids gaps
the rd_multi_score pooled estimate is blank without xnorm; check the pooled 'available' flag before reading its tau
robust bias-corrected (the default): the CI is NOT symmetric around the (conventional) coefficient — do not read it as coef±1.96·se
cutoff-specific estimates at cutoffs with few observations (a small Nh_total) are noisy; look at Nh_total/n_failed
a single cutoff in rd_multi_cutoff gives a cryptic error; use #38 (a gate here requires at least two cutoffs)
sources: Cattaneo, Titiunik & Vazquez-Bare (2020), 'Analysis of RD Designs with Multiple Cutoffs or Multiple Scores', Stata Journal 20(4):866-891
Calonico, Cattaneo & Titiunik 2014 Econometrica 82:2295 (robust bias-corrected inference — the backbone of this card)
Cattaneo, Idrobo & Titiunik (2024) 'A Practical Introduction to RD Designs: Extensions' (CUP Elements) §multi-cutoff/multi-score

cards.method: Sensitivity analysis to unobserved confounding / omitted-variable bias (robustness value + OVB bounds)
cards.when: you have estimated a treatment effect with OLS (selection on observables) and you want to quantify how strong an UNOBSERVED confounder would have to be to change/eliminate the result (the robustness value, partial R², OVB-adjusted bounds relative to benchmark covariates)
cards.when_not: there is no credible linear design (RD/DiD/IV/synthetic control -> #38-#45); you want a point-identified effect under confounding (that needs a design, not a sensitivity analysis); a non-linear or GLM outcome (the least-squares route does not apply); pre-trend sensitivity in an event study (-> #168)

alternatives.criterion: you want heterogeneous effects under unconfoundedness, not a diagnosis of its violation
high-dimensional controls / debiased estimation instead of post-hoc sensitivity analysis
a valid instrument exists -> point identification instead of bounds
you want hypothetical confounding scenarios without a benchmark covariate (scoped out here)

output_key_fields: robustness_value (rv_q): how much partial R² (of a confounder with BOTH the treatment AND the outcome) is needed to reduce the effect by q·100%; close to 0 = fragile
robustness_value_alpha (rv_qa): the same, but for statistical non-significance at alpha
partial_r2_treatment (r2yd_x): the partial R² of the treatment with the outcome; an upper bound on what the treatment explains given the controls
ovb_bounds: a table per (benchmark × kd/ky) with adjusted_estimate/se/lower_CI/upper_CI — the effect IF the confounder were kd/ky times stronger than the benchmark covariate
unadjusted_estimate/se/t_statistic/dof: the original OLS estimate + the degrees of freedom
interpretation_traps: the RV is NOT a p-value: a small RV = little confounder strength is required = a fragile result (not the other way round)
reduce=True (the default) assumes the confounder REDUCES the effect; if the confounding would inflate it instead, set reduce=False
the bounds are conditional on the assumption 'kd times stronger than the benchmark' — their credibility rests on whether the benchmark covariate really is comparable to the plausible confounder
sensitivity ≠ identification: the tool does NOT correct the bias; it only says how much confounding would overturn it (design-based safety remains the user's responsibility)
least squares only: the alternative fixed-effects, formula and numeric routes are deliberately excluded; supply a fitted least-squares model, or a formula with its data
sources: Cinelli & Hazlett (2020), 'Making Sense of Sensitivity: Extending Omitted Variable Bias', JRSS-B 82(1):39-67
Cinelli, Ferwerda & Hazlett 2020 (sensitivity analysis tools for OLS, SSRN 3588978)
precondition_tools: sens_analyze (the formula+data route: it fits the lm internally)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the cross-section before the formula+data route)
c00_data_utilities/analytic_ols_closed.ols_regress (an ALREADY fitted least-squares model is passed as the object; the consuming route accepts nothing else)

cards.method: IPW / double-ML treatment effects (ATE/ATET, IV-LATE/LATT, causal mediation)
cards.when: selection-on-observables treatment evaluation with ready-made y/d/x vectors (NOT a formula): DML-ATE for a discrete treatment (cw_treatment_dml); IPW ATE/ATET for a binary treatment (cw_treatment_ipw); IV-LATE/LATT with a binary instrument (cw_late_ipw); a direct/indirect split through a mediator (cw_mediation_dml)
cards.when_not: you have no observable confounders (unconfoundedness fails -> RD/DiD/synthetic control); a panel with staggered adoption (-> #36/#37/#43); heterogeneous CATE by covariate (-> #44); linear IV with a formula (-> #34/#33); a time-series intervention (-> #90)

alternatives.criterion: you want the full double-ML framework (random-forest or elastic-net learners, ATTE, tuning) rather than IPW or the efficient score
heterogeneous CATE by covariate, not only a population ATE
linear 2SLS IV with a formula (a continuous treatment/instrument; a global LATE assuming linearity)
you want doubly-robust/ML nuisance (Neyman orthogonality) rather than plain IPW; or a multi-valued discrete treatment

output_key_fields: effect: the main causal effect (ATE/ATET/LATE/LATT); se: the standard error; pval: the p-value
cw_treatment_ipw: y1/y0 (the mean potential outcomes); estimand 'ATE'/'ATET'
cw_late_ipw: first (+se_first/pval_first) = the complier share/first stage; ITT (+se_ITT/pval_ITT) = intention to treat
cw_mediation_dml: ate + dir_treat/dir_control (natural direct) + indir_treat/indir_control (natural indirect); se/pval of length 6 (a 3x6 results matrix)
ntrimmed: the number of observations dropped because of extreme propensity scores (an overlap diagnostic)
interpretation_traps: unconfoundedness is an UNTESTABLE assumption — the SE do not certify it; a high ntrimmed = weak overlap, and the estimate then rests on a few units
the IV-LATE (cw_late_ipw) is an effect ONLY on the compliers, not on the population; a small 'first' -> a weak instrument, the effect explodes/is unstable
mediation (cw_mediation_dml) ADDITIONALLY requires sequential ignorability of the mediator; the direct+indirect split is not fully experimentally identified
stochasticity: treatDML/medDML (cross-fitting fold splits) & treatweight/lateweight (bootstrap) -> the same effect ONLY with the same seed (default 2025)
MLmethod='lasso' in cw_mediation_dml (hdm rlasso) can throw 'subscript out of bounds' at small n -> use 'parametric'/'randomforest' or a larger sample
d must be 0/1 (treatweight/lateweight/medDML) & z 0/1 (lateweight); a non-binary d/z is blocked (otherwise a cryptic 'y values must be 0<=y<=1' from the probit)
sources: Chernozhukov et al. 2018, 'Double/debiased machine learning', Econometrics Journal 21:C1-C68
Farbmacher, Huber, Laffers, Langen, Spindler 2022, 'Causal mediation analysis with double machine learning', Econometrics Journal 25:277-300
Tchetgen Tchetgen & Shpitser 2012 (Annals of Statistics 40:1816) — semiparametric mediation
precondition_tools: cw_treatment_ipw (unconfoundedness + common support: check ntrimmed/overlap before the ATE)
cw_late_ipw (the first stage 'first' = the complier share: a weak instrument if it is ~0)
c07_causality_policy/double_debiased.dml_irm (cross-check the ATE with an independent DML implementation)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the tabular dataset; build the y/d/x/z/m vectors)

NOT when: you have no observable confounders (unconfoundedness fails -> RD/DiD/synthetic control); a panel with staggered adoption (-> #36/#37/#43); heterogeneous CATE by covariate (-> #44); linear IV with a formula (-> #34/#33); a time-series intervention (-> #90)
Alternatives: 07-causality-policy/dml_irm (you want the full double-ML framework (random-forest or elastic-net learners, ATTE, tuning) rather than IPW or the efficient score) · 07-causality-policy/causal_forest_fit (heterogeneous CATE by covariate, not only a population ATE) · 07-causality-policy/iv_fit (linear 2SLS IV with a formula (a continuous treatment/instrument; a global LATE assuming linearity)) · cw_treatment_dml instead of cw_treatment_ipw (you want doubly-robust/ML nuisance (Neyman orthogonality) rather than plain IPW; or a multi-valued discrete treatment)

Pitfalls: unconfoundedness is an UNTESTABLE assumption — the SE do not certify it; a high ntrimmed = weak overlap, and the estimate then rests on a few units · the IV-LATE (cw_late_ipw) is an effect ONLY on the compliers, not on the population; a small 'first' -> a weak instrument, the effect explodes/is unstable · mediation (cw_mediation_dml) ADDITIONALLY requires sequential ignorability of the mediator; the direct+indirect split is not fully experimentally identified · stochasticity: treatDML/medDML (cross-fitting fold splits) & treatweight/lateweight (bootstrap) -> the same effect ONLY with the same seed (default 2025) · MLmethod='lasso' in cw_mediation_dml (hdm rlasso) can throw 'subscript out of bounds' at small n -> use 'parametric'/'randomforest' or a larger sample · d must be 0/1 (treatweight/lateweight/medDML) & z 0/1 (lateweight); a non-binary d/z is blocked (otherwise a cryptic 'y values must be 0<=y<=1' from the probit)

cards.when: over-identified linear IV / moment-condition estimation (Euler equations, macro/finance) where you want efficient GMM + HAC-robust inference + a test of instrument validity (Hansen J)
cards.when_not: just-identified 2SLS with a single endogenous regressor (-> #34/#165); non-linear user-supplied moment functions (NOT exposed — that would be an evaluation surface); dynamic panel GMM (Arellano-Bond -> #47)

alternatives.criterion: just-identified 2SLS, or you want rich IV diagnostics (the weak-instruments F, Wu-Hausman endogeneity, Sargan)
classic 2SLS with the simple formula 'y ~ x | z'
high-dimensional fixed effects + IV together
you want a 2SLS-equivalent estimate (identity weighting) rather than efficient GMM

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named numeric vector — the coefficient estimates (e.g. the slope on the endogenous regressor)
coef_table: a matrix Estimate/Std. Error/z value/Pr(>|z|) — asymptotic normal inference (the SE come from the chosen vcov)
vcov / std_errors: the covariance matrix of the coefficients and the SE (they correspond to the vcov argument)
J_test: {statistic, df, p_value}, the Hansen over-identification test; df = instruments - coefficients (df=0 means just-identified, and the p-value is blank)
df / nobs / type / wmatrix / vcov_type: the over-identifying degrees of freedom, the observations left after the gap gate, and the estimator settings
interpretation_traps: Hansen J: a SMALL p_value (rejecting H0) => the instruments/moment conditions are NOT valid (misspecification), NOT 'a significant result'
just-identified (df=0): the J test is NOT defined — gmm_j_test returns a statistic near 0 with a note and a blank p-value; do not read it as a 'perfect fit'
the estimator drops rows with gaps SILENTLY (only a warning) — the wrapper blocks that with a gate; nobs counts the rows after cleaning
vcov='HAC' (the default): autocorrelation-robust — for a pure cross-section prefer vcov='iid'/'MDS'; the SE change substantially with the vcov
under-identification (moments < coefficients) is blocked by a clean gate before the call — add instruments
SECURITY: only the formula/linear interface is exposed; a user-supplied moment function (gmm(g=<fn>)) is NOT supported (an eval surface)
sources: Hansen (1982) 'Large Sample Properties of GMM Estimators', Econometrica 50:1029
Chaussé 2010 JSS 34(11) (computing generalized method of moments estimators)
Hall (2005) Generalized Method of Moments, Oxford — the Sargan-Hansen J over-identification test

cards.method: Fixed-Effects Individual-Slopes (FEIS) + a slope-heterogeneity Hausman test (artificial & bootstrapped)
cards.when: a panel (i,t) where the effect of a trend/slope variable (e.g. time/experience) differs by unit; you want consistency even when the unit-specific slope is correlated with the regressors (detrending instead of demeaning)
cards.when_not: no theoretical slope heterogeneity (conventional FE #46 suffices); fewer than q+1 observations per unit (q=the number of slope parameters); a dynamic panel / lagged dependent variable (Nickell -> #47 GMM); time-invariant regressors of interest (detrending removes them)

alternatives.criterion: no slope heterogeneity; feis_test art1 does not reject
a dynamic panel / endogenous regressors
hierarchical shrinkage of the slopes / a full posterior / non-gaussian

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of regressor effects in the detrended space
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|); the standard errors are robust when robust=True (vcov_arg records it)
slopevars: the slope variables (the right-hand side of '|'); r2 and adj_r2 in the detrended space; n_groups after dropping units with fewer than q+1 observations
feis_test/feis_bootstrap_test: art_feis_vs_fe / art_fe_vs_re / art_feis_vs_re = {chi2, df, p_value}; the ones not requested are absent
slopes (feis_slopes): an N x J matrix of alpha_i indexed by unit id; it includes the intercept
interpretation_traps: the coefficients/r2 are in the DETRENDED space — not directly comparable with within/pooling FE
art1 (FEIS vs FE) rejection -> the slope heterogeneity matters; do NOT fall back to conventional FE
feis silently drops units with <q+1 observations (a warning); check n_groups against the original N
time-invariant regressors vanish under the detrending — they are not estimated here
feis_bootstrap_test is STOCHASTIC (a pairs-cluster bootstrap); the same seed -> the same p (seed=2025 by default); a low number of reps gives a noisy p
feis_test and feis_bootstrap_test return nothing for the components outside the selected type (art1/bs1 give only art_feis_vs_fe)
sources: Ruettenauer & Ludwig 2020, Sociological Methods & Research (FEIS), doi:10.1177/0049124120926211
Bruederl & Ludwig 2015, Sage Handbook of Regression Analysis §Fixed-Effects Panel Regression
Wooldridge 2010 Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data 2nd ed. §10.7 (regression-based Hausman), §11 (heterogeneous slopes)
Mundlak 1978 (Econometrica 46:69) — the CRE specification behind feistest
precondition_tools: feis_test (a regression-based Hausman test: rejecting art1 -> FEIS over FE)
feis_bootstrap_test (the bootstrapped Hausman test; more reliable at small N)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_hausman_test (the classic FE vs RE test before considering slope heterogeneity)

cards.method: Beck-Katz Panel-Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) for pooled TSCS/OLS
cards.when: pooled OLS on time-series cross-section data (N units × T periods, with T not << N); you want SE robust to panel heteroskedasticity + contemporaneous (cross-unit) correlation, keeping the OLS coefficients
cards.when_not: a lagged dependent variable / endogeneity (Nickell bias -> #47 GMM); within/random effects (#46); an N >> T micro panel (prefer clustered/Driscoll-Kraay); serial correlation as the main problem (Prais-Winsten/Newey-West)

alternatives.criterion: unit-specific effects correlated/uncorrelated with the regressors — FE/RE instead of pooling
N >> T or strong cross-sectional dependence with a large N
Beck-Katz PCSE inside a panel model rather than on a pooled least-squares fit

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of OLS coefficients (they do NOT change under the PCSE correction)
coef_table: Estimate/PCSE/t value/Pr(>|t|) — the SE are panel-corrected
pcse: a named vector of the panel-corrected SE; vcov: the full PCSE covariance matrix
df/nobs/nmiss: degrees of freedom, valid observations, missing panel cells
pairwise: True = pairwise, False = casewise; balanced: no missing cells
interpretation_traps: PCSE corrects ONLY the SE — the coefficients remain pooled OLS (non-robust point estimates)
casewise (pairwise=False) uses only the balanced rectangle; on a heavily unbalanced panel set pairwise=True
an unset pairwise flag runs silently wrong — the wrapper blocks it explicitly
Beck-Katz assumes T is not << N; with N >> T the PCSE are unreliable -> Driscoll-Kraay/clustered
vcov = the PCSE covariance (NOT the classical OLS vcov); read the inference from coef_table/pcse
gaps in the model or index columns drop rows inside the fit -> a length mismatch; the wrapper requires complete cases
sources: Beck & Katz 1995, 'What to Do (and Not to Do) with Time-Series Cross-Section Data', APSR 89(3):634-647
Beck 2001, Annual Review of Political Science 4:271-293 (TSCS practice)

cards.method: Hierarchical / multilevel (mixed) models — linear & generalized (partial pooling)
cards.when: hierarchical/nested data (e.g. regions within countries, years within units); you want partial pooling — random intercepts/slopes per group with shrinkage — instead of full pooling or entirely separate models per group
cards.when_not: the group effects are correlated with the regressors (endogeneity -> the within estimator, #46); a lagged dependent variable on the right-hand side (Nickell bias -> #47); a single hierarchical level with no repeated sampling; you want a full Bayesian posterior with priors (-> #69, category 14)

alternatives.criterion: the individual effects are correlated with the regressors -> partial pooling causes bias, use FE
one level, linear, a panel (i,t); GLS variance components suffice without the full mixed-model machinery
you want priors / a full posterior / a more complex likelihood, or hierarchical shrinkage with uncertainty quantification

output_key_fields: fixef: a named vector of population-level (fixed) coefficients
coef_table: Estimate/Std.Error/t (lmer) or +z/Pr(>|z|) (glmer) — NOTE: lmer gives NO p-value by design
varcorr: long-format records {grp,var1,var2,vcov,sdcor} — the variance/covariance/correlation of the random effects
sigma: the residual scale (== the residual scale of the variance components); ngrps: the number of groups per grouping factor; nobs
ranef: records {grpvar,term,grp,condval,condsd} — the BLUPs (shrunk group deviations) + the conditional SD
log_lik/AIC/BIC: model fit (AIC/BIC are comparable only ML-vs-ML; REML likelihoods are NOT comparable across different fixed effects)

singular (the logical isSingular)/converged (logical)/conv_messages (char): they record degeneracy & convergence IN THE SAME output — under a stateless node contract stderr is lost, so check these instead of relying on warnings
interpretation_traps: REML=True likelihoods are NOT comparable across models with different fixed effects — for a likelihood-ratio test or AIC on the fixed effects set REML=False (plain ML)

the linear mixed fit returns NO p-values (there is no default degrees-of-freedom convention) — coef_table carries only the t value; judge significance with an interval or a likelihood-ratio test, never from a p that does not exist
ranef are conditional modes (BLUPs), NOT parameters — they are shrunk towards 0; do NOT read them as separate fixed effects per group

a 'boundary (singular) fit' (the group standard deviation goes to 0) means the random effect is not supported by the data — too few groups, or zero between-group variance; the wrapper records it explicitly as singular=True, and it must not be ignored: the variance components are degenerate
partial pooling presupposes random effects UNCORRELATED with the regressors (as in RE/Hausman) — otherwise prefer within/FE (#46)
the family of lme_fit_glm is a closed enum; gaussian is NOT allowed there (use lme_fit)
sources: Bates, Mächler, Bolker & Walker 2015 JSS 67(1) (fitting linear mixed-effects models)
Gelman & Hill 2007, Data Analysis Using Regression and Multilevel/Hierarchical Models
Pinheiro & Bates 2000, Mixed-Effects Models in S and S-PLUS (BLUP/partial pooling)
precondition_tools: lme_fit (a linear response; register the model handle for ranef/varcorr)
lme_fit_glm (a non-gaussian response: binomial, poisson, Gamma or inverse-gaussian)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_fit (comparison: FE/within when the effects are endogenous)

cards.method: Bayesian Global VAR (multi-country shrinkage + SV): estimation + generalized-FEVD spillovers/GIRF + a posterior-predictive forecast
cards.when: a multi-country (N>=2) system with cross-country spillovers; you want a Bayesian GVAR with shrinkage (MN/SSVS/NG), optional stochastic volatility, generalized spillover matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) and density forecasts tied to a weight matrix W (trade/spatial)
cards.when_not: one country or equation (-> category 03); pure spillover connectedness with no global-VAR structure (-> #51); a frequentist global VAR with no Bayesian shrinkage (-> #50); a single-equation spatial regression with a weights matrix (-> #53)

alternatives.criterion: a frequentist GVAR (OLS country VARs) — a small model, you want point estimates without Bayesian shrinkage/SV
you want only spillover/connectedness matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) without a full global-VAR structural model & W
many countries·variables -> stronger/adaptive shrinkage (MN = the fast baseline)

output_key_fields: bgvar_fit: object (the register handle for spillover/predict); max_eigenvalue/stable_draw_share/trim_info (eigen-trimming of unstable draws); geweke_perc/geweke_exceed_share (Geweke convergence); K/variables/country_names; xglobal (the stacked data)
bgvar_spillover type=gfevd: spillover_matrix K x K (GFEVD[i,j]=the contribution of j to the variance of i, rows sum to 1); from_others/to_others/net (Diebold-Yilmaz %); total_spillover_index
bgvar_spillover with type=girf: irf_median, K x (horizon+1), the posterior median responses to the shock; plus the quantiles
bgvar_predict: forecast, K x horizon x quantiles, plus forecast_median (chart data); has_holdout; lps and rmse are present ONLY when hold_out>0 at fit time
interpretation_traps: GFEVD orientation (Lanne-Nyberg 2016 corrected): the ROWS sum to 1; spillover_matrix[i,j] = the contribution OF j TO the variance of i; from_i=sum over {j≠i}, to_j=sum over {i≠j} — do not confuse them

max_eigenvalue>=1 or a low stable_draw_share -> the VAR has unstable draws; a high geweke_exceed_share -> the MCMC did not converge (raise draws/burnin) — do NOT interpret spillovers/forecasts before checking these (a stateless node: they are returned in the list, NOT to the console)
lps and rmse are absent when the fit used hold_out=0; for an out-of-sample evaluation you MUST set hold_out>0 in bgvar_fit (the has_holdout flag records it)
naming convention: country AND variable names must NOT contain a dot '.' (it is the Country.Variable separator); W must have diag=0 & row sums=1 (row-standardized) with the countries as names
the prior default here is 'MN' (the first enum value, and the fast one) whereas the reference default is 'NG'; the horseshoe was deliberately left out
sources: Boeck, Feldkircher & Huber 2022 JSS (Bayesian global vector autoregressions with shrinkage priors)
Pesaran, Schuermann & Weiner 2004 (the GVAR framework); Lanne & Nyberg 2016 (the corrected GFEVD, J. Time Ser. Econom.)
Diebold & Yilmaz 2012/2014 (the spillover/connectedness index from generalized variance decompositions)
Koop, Pesaran & Potter 1996 (generalized impulse response functions)

[#176] Bayesian Global VAR (multi-country shrinkage + SV): estimation + generalized-FEVD spillovers/GIRF + a posterior-predictive forecast
Category: 09-cross-section-networks
Nodes: bgvar_fit · bgvar_spillover · bgvar_predict
WHEN: a multi-country (N>=2) system with cross-country spillovers; you want a Bayesian GVAR with shrinkage (MN/SSVS/NG), optional stochastic volatility, generalized spillover matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) and density forecasts tied to a weight matrix W (trade/spatial)
NOT when: one country or equation (-> category 03); pure spillover connectedness with no global-VAR structure (-> #51); a frequentist global VAR with no Bayesian shrinkage (-> #50); a single-equation spatial regression with a weights matrix (-> #53)
Alternatives: #50 global VAR (gv_fit) (a frequentist GVAR (OLS country VARs) — a small model, you want point estimates without Bayesian shrinkage/SV) · #51 dy_time_connectedness (you want only spillover/connectedness matrices (Diebold-Yilmaz) without a full global-VAR structural model & W) · prior='NG' or 'SSVS' (many countries·variables -> stronger/adaptive shrinkage (MN = the fast baseline))
Output: bgvar_fit: object (the register handle for spillover/predict); max_eigenvalue/stable_draw_share/trim_info (eigen-trimming of unstable draws); geweke_perc/geweke_exceed_share (Geweke convergence); K/variables/country_names; xglobal (the stacked data) · bgvar_spillover type=gfevd: spillover_matrix K x K (GFEVD[i,j]=the contribution of j to the variance of i, rows sum to 1); from_others/to_others/net (Diebold-Yilmaz %); total_spillover_index · bgvar_spillover with type=girf: irf_median, K x (horizon+1), the posterior median responses to the shock; plus the quantiles · bgvar_predict: forecast, K x horizon x quantiles, plus forecast_median (chart data); has_holdout; lps and rmse are present ONLY when hold_out>0 at fit time
Pitfalls: GFEVD orientation (Lanne-Nyberg 2016 corrected): the ROWS sum to 1; spillover_matrix[i,j] = the contribution OF j TO the variance of i; from_i=sum over {j≠i}, to_j=sum over {i≠j} — do not confuse them · max_eigenvalue>=1 or a low stable_draw_share -> the VAR has unstable draws; a high geweke_exceed_share -> the MCMC did not converge (raise draws/burnin) — do NOT interpret spillovers/forecasts before checking these (a stateless node: they are returned in the list, NOT to the console) · lps and rmse are absent when the fit used hold_out=0; for an out-of-sample evaluation you MUST set hold_out>0 in bgvar_fit (the has_holdout flag records it) · naming convention: country AND variable names must NOT contain a dot '.' (it is the Country.Variable separator); W must have diag=0 & row sums=1 (row-standardized) with the countries as names · the prior default here is 'MN' (the first enum value, and the fast one) whereas the reference default is 'NG'; the horseshoe was deliberately left out
Sources: Boeck, Feldkircher & Huber 2022 JSS (Bayesian global vector autoregressions with shrinkage priors) · Pesaran, Schuermann & Weiner 2004 (the GVAR framework); Lanne & Nyberg 2016 (the corrected GFEVD, J. Time Ser. Econom.) · Diebold & Yilmaz 2012/2014 (the spillover/connectedness index from generalized variance decompositions) · Koop, Pesaran & Potter 1996 (generalized impulse response functions)

cards.method: Spatial panel models (SAR/SEM/SDM · FE/RE/pooling) — ML & GM + spatial LM tests
cards.when: a panel (i,t) with SPATIAL dependence between units (geographic/network neighbours); you want a spatial lag (Wy) and/or a spatial error with an FE/RE test; you have an n x n weight matrix W
cards.when_not: no spatial structure (lag=False and error=none -> a plain panel, #46); a dynamic panel with a lagged dependent variable (-> #47); a pure cross-section with no panel (-> #53); an unbalanced panel (the ML and GM routes do not support it)

alternatives.criterion: a pure cross-section (not a panel) spatial regression
a panel with no spatial dependence (the LM tests do not reject)
endogeneity/robust GM/IV instead of ML, or when the ML optimisation does not converge
the spatial-specific effects are uncorrelated with the regressors (Hausman does not reject)

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector (the regressors + the spatial parameters rho/lambda; the names depend on lag/error/model)
coef_table: terms/estimate/std_error/statistic/p_value (the summary CoefTable)
ar_table / errcomp_table: the AR-coefficient and error-component tables (the random model only; absent in the within case, where they are merged into coef_table)
errcomp: the variance components (phi=the idiosyncratic share, rho=the spatial error); random only
rho (spgm): the spatial autoregressive (lag) coefficient; sigma2: the idiosyncratic variance
sp_panel_lm_tests: statistic/p_value/method/alternative (lml -> the lag test, lme -> the error test)
interpretation_traps: naming: 'rho' and 'lambda' swap roles between the ML and GM routes — in the ML coefficient table lambda is the spatial error and rho the spatial lag, while in the GM route the spatial-lag coefficient sits in the rho field and lambda holds the error; read the labels, do not assume
the within (fixed-effects) model puts the spatial parameters into coef_table, NOT into a separate ar_table or errcomp_table (those are absent) — only the random model separates them
an unbalanced panel fails (a clean 'balanced' gate); gaps in the data fail cryptically when the weights are subset -> a gap gate
the number of spatial units MUST == nrow(W); the order of the units in W must match the order of the index (a silent misalignment otherwise)
LM tests: lml tests the spatial LAG, lme the spatial ERROR; the robust ones (rlml/rlme) are robust to the presence of the other form — prefer them when both plain LM tests reject
sources: Millo & Piras 2012 JSS 47(1) (spatial panel data models)
Baltagi, Song, Koh 2003; Kapoor, Kelejian, Prucha 2007 (KKP error components)
Anselin 1988 Spatial Econometrics; Elhorst 2014 Spatial Econometrics: From Cross-Sectional Data to Spatial Panels
precondition_tools: c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (is there any spatial autocorrelation at all before a spatial panel?)
sp_panel_lm_tests (lml=lag vs lme=error; the robust rlml/rlme -> which spatial form)
c08_panel_data/static_panel_estimators.pd_hausman_test (the FE vs RE dimension, on the non-spatial baseline)
c01_preparation_prechecks/panel_unit_root.run_panel_unit_root (macro/large-T only: a panel unit-root test first)

cards.method: Spatial GMM / GS2SLS (SARAR/lag/error) with heteroskedasticity-robust SEs
cards.when: a cross-sectional spatial regression with possible heteroskedasticity; you want GMM/GS2SLS (not ML) estimation of a spatial lag (Wy) and/or a spatial error (Wu) with het-robust standard errors (Kelejian-Prucha/Arraiz); you have a square spatial weight matrix W
cards.when_not: homoskedastic errors where you want ML efficiency and impacts (-> #53); panel data (-> #177); you need direct/indirect/total spillover effects (pass the fit to #53); time-series or non-spatial data

alternatives.criterion: homoskedastic errors; you want maximum-likelihood efficiency + impacts spillover effects
spatial dependence only in the errors (a nuisance), not a substantive Wy
a substantive spatial spillover in Wy, clean errors
a non-spatial baseline/benchmark

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector — the beta regressors + lambda (the spatial LAG, Wy) + rho (the spatial ERROR, Wu)
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|); the standard errors are ALREADY heteroskedasticity-robust when het=True
spatial_lag: the Wy coefficient (labelled 'lambda' here); spatial_error: the Wu coefficient (labelled 'rho' here); blank when the model does not include them
vcov: the coefficient covariance; s2: the residual variance; residuals/nobs
nonstationary: True when the absolute spatial coefficient reaches 1; se_na: True when a robust standard error came back blank
interpretation_traps: the OPPOSITE convention to #53: here lambda is the spatial LAG (Wy) and rho the spatial ERROR (Wu), while #53 has rho as the lag and lambda as the error. ALWAYS read spatial_lag and spatial_error, the explicit names, never the raw lambda/rho
het=True => the standard errors in coef_table are ALREADY heteroskedasticity-robust; do NOT apply a robust covariance again
the GMM / GS2SLS route does not produce direct, indirect or total impacts; to interpret the spillovers of a spatial lag model you need the impacts of #53
nonstationary=True (an absolute coefficient of at least 1) => the spatial process is not invertible and the results are suspect (check the row standardization of the weights)
a very large q (spatial instruments) with a small n => singular/'Hin not found' — keep q small (2)
sources: Piras 2010 JSS 35(1) (spatial models with heteroskedastic innovations)
Kelejian & Prucha 1998 (JREE 17:99), 1999 (Int. Econ. Rev. 40:509) — the GM/GS2SLS spatial estimator
Arraiz, Drukker, Kelejian & Prucha 2010 (J. Regional Sci. 50:592) — het-robust GMM
precondition_tools: c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (Moran's I: is there any spatial autocorrelation to model?)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_weights (building/checking a spatial-weights object from adjacency; here W is supplied as a matrix)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading cross-section data)

cards.method: Spatial dynamic panel data model (Lee-Yu QML, fixed effects) + direct/indirect/total effects
cards.when: a balanced spatial panel (i,t) with spatial dependence; estimating a SAR/SDM with fixed effects, static or dynamic (a time and space-time lag of the dependent variable), and interpreting it through direct/indirect/total spatial spillovers
cards.when_not: a non-spatial panel (-> #46/#47); a spatial CROSS-SECTION of one period (-> #53); an unbalanced panel (blocked); a pure spatial error with no lag ('sem' is not supported here); a very small N, or an N with no reliable weights matrix

alternatives.criterion: a spatial cross-section of one period (not a panel)
a static spatial panel without dynamics/Lee-Yu bias correction, or a spatial error (SEM) component
there is no spatial dependence; a plain static/dynamic panel
the spillovers of the regressors (W*X) are substantive — otherwise direct≈total

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector of regressor coefficients (in an SDM & in the dynamic case it includes the W*X and time-lag terms)
coef_table: Estimate/Std. Error/t-value/Pr(>|t|) per regressor
rho / rho_se / rho_tstat / rho_pval: the spatial autoregressive coefficient (spatial dependence)
sige, log_likelihood, r_squared, adj_r_squared: fit diagnostics; model/effect/dynamic: the configuration that was estimated
n_units/n_times: the panel dimensions; converged: True when rho and the log-likelihood are both finite
impacts: direct/indirect/total (matrices Estimate/SE/t/p) + estimates/std_errors/t_stats/p_values
interpretation_traps: The beta coefficient is NOT the marginal effect when rho!=0 — read the impacts (direct=own unit, indirect=spillover, total=direct+indirect); the same feedback loop as in #178
'sem' is not supported (the enum allows only sar and sdm); for a spatial-error component go to #177
impactsSDPDm is STOCHASTIC (an NSIM simulation) — the SE/p depend on the seed; always keep the seed fixed
A BALANCED panel is required; gaps or an unbalanced panel are blocked (the estimator does not handle unbalanced data)
W should ideally be row-standardized (rowstand=True by default); a zero row, meaning an isolated unit, is blocked during the row standardization
dynamic=True: the time-lag settings control y_{t-1} and W*y_{t-1}; at least one of the two is needed
converged=False, or entirely blank coefficients -> do not trust the fit (the node is stateless, so this is caught in the output rather than on stderr)
sources: Yu, De Jong & Lee 2008 (J. Econometrics 146:118-134) — QML spatial dynamic panel, n & T large
Lee & Yu 2010 (J. Econometrics 154:165-185) — SAR panel fixed-effects estimation/bias correction
Lee & Yu 2010 (Econometric Theory 26:564-597) — a spatial dynamic panel with time + individual FE
LeSage & Pace 2009, Introduction to Spatial Econometrics — the direct/indirect/total effects interpretation
precondition_tools: sp_dynpanel (the estimation itself: balanced-panel + square-W gates; it returns a converged flag)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_weights (building/checking the spatial neighbourhoods before you build W)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the long-format panel from a file)

cards.method: Moran eigenvector spatial regression — eigenvector spatial filtering (ESF) & random-effects ESF (RE-ESF, an approximate Gaussian process)
cards.when: a cross-section with spatial dependence; you want to clean the spatial autocorrelation out of the residuals with Moran eigenvectors (ESF fixed effects) or to model it as a spatial random effect (RE-ESF ~ a Gaussian process), without imposing a SAR/SEM structure
cards.when_not: you want an explicit SAR/SEM/SDM with spatial lag and error parameters plus impacts (-> #53); panel data indexed by unit and time (-> #177); a pure autocorrelation diagnostic with no model (-> #54, Moran/Geary); no valid weights matrix

alternatives.criterion: you want an explicit SAR/SEM/SDM parameter (rho/lambda) + impacts (direct/indirect/total)
you want a spatial random effect (an approximate GP) & variance components rather than stepwise fixed eigenvectors; better for a large N / a smooth surface
only an autocorrelation diagnostic, not a regression

output_key_fields: coefficients: a frame of Estimate/SE/t_value/p_value per regressor (the intercept plus x); with no x, a named intercept-only vector
moran_i: the scaled Moran's I in [0,1] of the estimated spatial component (0.25-0.50 weak, 0.50-0.70 moderate, 0.70-0.90 strong, 0.90-1.00 very strong — Griffith 2003)
spatial_sd / random_sd: the standard deviation of the spatial (ESF) / spatial-random (RE-ESF) component
gof: resid_SE/adjR2/log_lik/AIC/BIC (esf) · resid_SE/adjR2(cond)/rlog_lik/AIC/BIC (resf)
spatial_effect: the N x 1 estimated spatial component/random effect (chart-data); fitted/residuals
n_eigenvectors / eigenvalues / eigenvectors: (sp_moran_eigenvectors) the count & the scaled eigenvalues (max=1) & the N x L matrix (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: sp_eigenvector_filter and sp_random_effects_filter CONSUME the object produced by sp_moran_eigenvectors (the raw handle 'object'); they do not rebuild the eigenvectors — if you changed W, re-run sp_moran_eigenvectors
moran_i is SCALED to [0,1] (Moran.I/max(Moran.I)), NOT the raw Moran's I — do not compare it with the spw_moran_test statistic

ESF (sp_eigenvector_filter) = fixed eigenvectors chosen stepwise (fn=r2/aic/bic); RE-ESF (sp_random_effects_filter) = a spatial random effect (an approximate GP) — a different interpretation of the spatial term
with no x the fit is intercept-only, and the filter coefficients come back as a named numeric vector rather than a frame — handle both shapes
W is symmetrised internally ((W+t(W))/2); an asymmetric input does not error but loses the directionality
sources: Griffith 2003 Spatial Autocorrelation and Spatial Filtering (Springer) — the scaled Moran's I bands
Tiefelsdorf & Griffith 2007 (Environment and Planning A 39:1193) — eigenvector ESF
Murakami & Griffith 2015 (J Geographical Systems 17:311) — random-effects ESF
Murakami & Griffith 2019 (Geographical Analysis 51:23) — ESF for large data sets (fixed & random)
Dray, Legendre & Peres-Neto 2006 (Ecological Modelling 196:483) — the PCNM/MEM basis
precondition_tools: sp_moran_eigenvectors (the PRODUCER: it extracts the Moran eigenvectors from W; run it FIRST, and its object feeds sp_eigenvector_filter and sp_random_effects_filter)
c09_cross_section_networks/spatial_weights_diagnostics.spw_moran_test (confirm that spatial autocorrelation EXISTS before the ESF)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load y/x/coords from a file)

cards.method: Network estimation for time series — a sparse VAR (Granger network) + a concentration/partial-correlation network via the NETS LASSO
cards.when: a multivariate system (a small N ~4-6); you want SIMULTANEOUSLY (a) a Granger/directed network from a sparse VAR and (b) the contemporaneous partial-correlation network of the innovations, with LASSO sparsity instead of a dense VAR
cards.when_not: a large N with no sparsity assumption (a dense VAR -> #11); you want spillover or variance-decomposition connectedness (Diebold-Yilmaz -> #51); a single-equation spatial regression with a known weights matrix (-> #53/#54); you want point forecasts (this is a network node, not a forecaster)

alternatives.criterion: you want FEVD-based spillover/connectedness (Diebold-Yilmaz) rather than a LASSO Granger/partial-correlation network
connectedness per frequency (short/long-run bands)
a small N, you want a full dense VAR + IRF/FEVD with no sparsity penalty
you want only the directed Granger network
you want only the partial-correlation network without the autoregressive structure (p->0)

output_key_fields: granger_network: an N x N 0/1 directed adjacency, the Granger network read off the AR matrices; absent when GN=False
concentration_network: an N x N 0/1 undirected adjacency, the partial-correlation network; absent when CN=False
partial_correlation: an N x N matrix of partial correlations -C_ij/sqrt(C_ii C_jj), diagonal 1 (chart data); absent when CN=False or the fit is degenerate
concentration_matrix: the precision matrix of the innovations; longrun_network: the long-run adjacency; ar_matrices: an N x N x P array
lambda_used/selected_lambda/ic_table: the penalty that was used; (grid) the selection + a table {lambda,rss,npar,ic}
rss/npar/p_used/N/T/degenerate_concentration: fit diagnostics + a degeneracy flag for C.hat
interpretation_traps: the Granger network is DIRECTED, read off the AR matrices, while the concentration network and the partial correlations are UNDIRECTED and contemporaneous — do not confuse them
lambda controls the sparsity: a large lambda -> a sparser network; the graph structure DEPENDS on lambda (use lambda_grid+ic for a data-driven choice)
a length-2 lambda = [the AR penalty, the concentration penalty] separately; it is allowed ONLY with GN&CN; length-3 values and negatives are accepted silently by nets -> blocked by a gate
GN=False leaves the Granger fields absent and ignores p; CN=False leaves the concentration and partial-correlation fields absent
NETS assumes stationary series; non-stationary ones -> a spurious network structure; difference them first
degenerate_concentration=True means the precision matrix has a non-positive diagonal and the partial correlations were not computed — do not read a network out of a degenerate fit
sources: Barigozzi, M. & Brownlees, C. (2019) 'NETS: Network Estimation for Time Series', Journal of Applied Econometrics 34(3):347-364
Peng, J., Wang, P., Zhou, N. & Zhu, J. (2009) 'Partial Correlation Estimation by Joint Sparse Regression Models' (the space algorithm), JASA 104(486):735-746
precondition_tools: nets_fit (GN=True for the Granger network; CN=True for the partial-correlation network; and either lambda, or a lambda grid with an information criterion)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (the NETS VAR assumes stationary series; check/difference first)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_kpss_test (a complementary stationarity check before the network)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the T x N matrix of series)

cards.method: Factor-adjusted network estimation (high-dimensional TS): a common factor + an idiosyncratic VAR + Granger/partial-correlation networks
cards.when: many (high-dimensional) time series, T x N, with a strong common (factor) structure; you want to SEPARATE the common from the idiosyncratic part and estimate the idiosyncratic network (Granger + partial correlation) free of pervasive co-movement
cards.when_not: few series with no pervasive factors (go straight to a sparse VAR network -> #181); a single-equation panel indexed by unit and time (-> #46); a spatial cross-section with a known weights matrix (-> #53); pure forecasting with no interest in the network

alternatives.criterion: no pervasive factors -> a sparse VAR network directly, without factor adjustment
a cross-section with a known spatial weight matrix W rather than an estimated network
few series, the interest is in forecasting/IRF and not in a sparse network
a static approximate factor model (PCA) suffices; no dynamic (spectral) factors

output_key_fields: q: the estimated number of factors (or the input if a number was supplied)
granger_network: an N x N directed matrix (the sum of the VAR transition matrices over all lags, with a zero diagonal) — chart-data
pc_network: the N x N contemporaneous partial correlation of the VAR innovations (only with do_lrpc=True)
lrpc_network: the N x N long-run partial correlation (only with do_lrpc=True)
beta: the (N * var_order) x N VAR parameters (column j is the regression of variable j); Gamma: the innovation covariance; lambda: the regularisation
fnets_factor: loadings (2-D when restricted; a 3-D impulse-response array (p, q, trunc_lags+2) when unrestricted); factors (the factor series, the common shocks); plus the degenerate flag
interpretation_traps: the edge weights CAN be negative (entries of the VAR parameters/partial correlations) — they are not |weights|
granger_network[i,j] = the effect i -> j (the orientation of network(type=granger)); the diagonal is zeroed (self-lags are removed)
the partial-correlation and long-run partial-correlation blocks exist ONLY when do_lrpc=True; otherwise they are absent
q=0 is accepted silently (only a warning) -> a gate blocks any numeric q below 1, and fnets_factor then sets degenerate=True
unrestricted loadings are NOT classical factor loadings but impulse response functions (a 3-D array); the classical 2-D loadings appear only with fm_restricted=True
input orientation: the columns are the variables (T x N); a single column, or a gap or an infinity, fails with a cryptic low-level error -> explicit gates
sources: Barigozzi, Cho & Owens (2024+) FNETS: Factor-adjusted network estimation and forecasting for high-dimensional time series, JBES
Owens, Cho & Barigozzi 2024 (network estimation and forecasting via factor-adjusted VAR modelling)
Hallin & Liska (2007) JASA 102:603 (the number of dynamic factors); Avarucci et al. (2022); Ahn & Horenstein (2013) Econometrica 81:1203 (the eigenvalue ratio)
precondition_tools: fnets_factor (estimate the number of factors q first; degenerate=True, or q=0, means there is no common structure — consider #181 directly)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_csv_data (load the T x N matrix of series)

cards.method: Bayesian time-varying-parameter (TVP) regression with global-local shrinkage (triple/double/ridge) + SV
cards.when: a single equation y ~ x; you suspect the coefficients CHANGE over time (structural change, changing elasticities); you want a full posterior + automatic shrinkage towards a constant coefficient wherever no variation is needed
cards.when_not: constant coefficients suffice (OLS/#46); multivariate joint dynamics (a VAR, cat. 03); a pure trend/cycle decomposition of one series (#56-61 filters/state space); very large samples (MCMC cost)

alternatives.criterion: you want a structural trend/cycle/seasonal decomposition or Kalman filtering, not a TVP regression with shrinkage

alternatives.alt: #46 panel or OLS with constant coefficients
alternatives.criterion: theta_sr ~0 for ALL coefficients — there is no time variation, the constant model suffices
you want TVP without global-local shrinkage (a baseline; it does not shrink towards a constant)
a non-gaussian likelihood or a hierarchical structure beyond TVP+SV

output_key_fields: beta_paths: per covariate, the posterior median + 95% CI of the time-varying coefficient (chart-data, of length n_obs+1: the states t=0.T)
theta_sr_median: sqrt(theta), the state standard deviation per covariate; ~0 => the coefficient is CONSTANT (shrinkage collapsed it), a large value => substantive time variation
beta_mean_median: the constant (mean) level of each coefficient
sigma2_median: the observation variance — a scalar when sv=False, a path of length n_obs when sv=True
shrinkage: a_xi/a_tau (double/triple only)/kappa2_B/lambda2_B — the global shrinkage hyperparameters
stvp_forecast: pred_median/pred_lower/pred_upper per horizon; stvp_lpds: lpds (larger=a better forecast)
interpretation_traps: theta_sr is the sqrt of the variance AND non-centered (it can come out negative in the posterior sample; the ABSOLUTE value/distance from 0 is what matters) — |theta_sr|~0 means a constant coefficient, NOT a zero coefficient (see beta_mean)
beta_paths have n_obs+1 points (the initial state t=0 is included); beta_time runs 0.T
stvp_forecast REQUIRES future values of the regressors; it does not forecast x itself, and the new data must have at least as many rows as the horizon, otherwise it fails
stvp_lpds accepts EXACTLY one hold-out row (it fails otherwise); compare mod_type through the sum of the LPDS over a rolling hold-out
ridge has NO a_xi/a_tau (it performs no shrinkage selection); do not look for the shrinkage fields there
the MCMC is stochastic: the seed is mandatory; a different seed => different (but compatible) posterior summaries
sources: Knaus, Bitto-Nemling, Cadonna & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2021 JSS 100(13) (shrinkage in the time-varying parameter model framework)
Bitto & Frühwirth-Schnatter 2019 (J. Econometrics 210:75, the Normal-Gamma / double shrinkage prior)
Cadonna, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Knaus 2020 (Econometrics 8:20, the triple gamma prior)
Frühwirth-Schnatter & Wagner 2010 (J. Econometrics 154:85, the non-centered parameterization / theta_sr)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the panel/time series as a numeric data_frame)
stvp_lpds (the out-of-sample log predictive density: compare mod_type / TVP vs constant on a hold-out sample)
stvp_forecast (a predictive forecast with future regressor values)
