cards.method: Bayesian regression with time-varying (random-walk) coefficients — HMC (Stan)
cards.when: you want a regression whose coefficients EVOLVE over time (structural change / time-varying elasticities / a changing NAIRU slope), gaussian or counts (poisson/binomial), with a full posterior + CI
cards.when_not: constant coefficients (a classic lm/GLM); pure trend-cycle extraction without regressors (#56-61); you need a formal forecast (predict; outside the surface here); a very large n/many covariates (HMC is expensive)

alternatives.criterion: you want a hierarchical/multilevel or non-gaussian GLM WITHOUT a time-varying structure (constant or group-varying coefficients)
a general (non-linear/non-gaussian) state-space model with particle MCMC rather than the HMC-marginalised approach
a purely frequentist state-space trend/level WITHOUT time-varying regression coefficients

output_key_fields: converged / max_rhat / n_divergent (tvreg_fit): the convergence gate (converged=True only when max_rhat<1.1 and there are no divergences)
coef_names / n_time_varying (tvreg_fit): the names of the time-varying coefficients, including the time-varying intercept or level
sigma_summary (tvreg_fit): the posterior of the standard deviations (sigma_y is the observation sd; each sigma_rw is the rate of change of one coefficient)
fitted (tvreg_fit): the posterior mean fitted values — chart data
coef_table (tvreg_coef): long records {beta, time, median, lower, upper, mean, sd} — the time-varying posterior median with a 95% band (chart data)
interpretation_traps: convergence FIRST: when converged=False (max_rhat>=1.1, or any divergence) the estimates are unreliable — raise the iterations or tighten the priors, and do NOT interpret them
a small iter=400 -> low-ESS warnings; it is deliberately SMALL for a node — raise iter for a final analysis
poisson and binomial families put the coefficients on the LINK scale; use tvreg_coef with exponentiate=True for a multiplicative reading
sigma_rw*->0 ⇒ the coefficient is PRACTICALLY constant (negligible time variation); a large sigma_rw ⇒ strong variation
double intercept: the rw term adds its own time-varying level; the wrapper prepends '-1 +' so that only ONE remains (identifiability)
counts, silently wrong: walker_glm accepts non-integer y SILENTLY — the gate blocks it (non-negative integers; binomial requires y<=u)
sources: Helske 2022 (Bayesian generalized linear models with time-varying coefficients)
Vihola, Helske & Franks (2020), Importance sampling type estimators based on approximate marginal MCMC, Scandinavian J. of Statistics 47(4):1339-1376 (the walker_glm exact-approximate weighting)
Durbin & Koopman (2012), Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods 2nd ed. (the random-walk coefficient state-space representation)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a TIME-ordered data_frame; one row = one time point)
tvreg_fit (max_rhat/n_divergent/converged: check the HMC convergence BEFORE interpreting the coefficients)

cards.method: Particle-filter (bootstrap) log-likelihood + iterated filtering (IF2) MLE for non-linear non-Gaussian state-space models
cards.when: a non-linear / non-Gaussian state-space model where the Kalman filter does not apply; you want a particle-filter log-likelihood (pf_loglik) or a simulation-based MLE (pf_iterated_filtering) on one of the built-in templates gompertz/ricker/ou2
cards.when_not: a linear-Gaussian model (-> #58/#59/#60/#61, the exact Kalman filter); custom dynamics beyond the three templates (that would need compiled user code, blocked for security); a full Bayesian posterior over the parameters (-> #60)

alternatives.criterion: the model is linear-Gaussian -> an exact Kalman filter, not a particle approximation

alternatives.alt: the bootstrap or psi particle filter of #60
alternatives.criterion: you want Bayesian inference (MCMC) with a particle filter rather than a point MLE
a low min_ess (particle depletion) or a non-converging loglik_trace

output_key_fields: loglik: the particle-filter log-likelihood (pf_loglik) or the final IF2 loglik (pf_iterated_filtering); a Monte Carlo estimate, it varies with Np/the seed
eff_sample_size / min_ess (pf_loglik): the ESS per time point; a low min_ess -> particle depletion, raise Np
cond_log_lik (pf_loglik): the conditional log-likelihood per time point (chart-data)
estimates / estimated (pf_iterated_filtering): the final values of ALL the parameters + which names were estimated
loglik_trace / traces (pf_iterated_filtering): the loglik & the parameter path per IF2 iteration — a convergence diagnostic (chart-data)
converged: a finite loglik (& estimates); a stateless-node flag instead of stderr
interpretation_traps: the loglik is a STOCHASTIC Monte Carlo estimate — two runs with a different seed/Np give different values; compare only with the same seed/Np
a low min_ess (e.g. << Np) means particle depletion -> the loglik is unreliable, NOT that the model is bad; raise Np
IF2 (pf_iterated_filtering) has NO hard convergence test — judge convergence from the loglik_trace (it must stabilise) & the converged flag, not from a single run
the initial-value parameters (…_0, e.g. X_0/N_0/x1_0) are NOT perturbed by default; to estimate them pass them explicitly in estimate
SECURITY: ONLY the built-in templates are exposed; there is no way to supply custom C dynamics (the compile/eval surface is blocked)
sources: King, Nguyen & Ionides (2016), Journal of Statistical Software <
Ionides, Nguyen, Atchadé, Stoev & King 2015, 'Inference for dynamic and latent variable models via iterated, perturbed Bayes maps', PNAS 112(3):719 (the IF2 algorithm)
Arulampalam et al. 2002, IEEE Trans. Signal Processing 50(2):174 (the bootstrap particle filter)
precondition_tools: pf_loglik (run the particle filter first: check for a finite loglik & min_ess before IF2)
pf_iterated_filtering (the IF2 MLE; check the converged field & the loglik_trace for convergence)

cards.method: BEAST — a Bayesian decomposition into trend + seasonality + change points with posterior change probabilities
cards.when: you want to decompose a regular series into trend + seasonality AND simultaneously locate structural breaks / change points with PROBABILITIES (a posterior), not a point decision; ideal when the number/location of the breaks is unknown and you want uncertainty per time point
cards.when_not: irregular or unevenly sampled data (the irregular variant is outside this node's scope); a pure output-gap or potential-output estimate (-> #56/#92); one KNOWN break at a known date (-> #3); a state-space model with an explicit unobserved-components structure (-> #58/#59)

alternatives.criterion: you only want a trend/cycle gap without change-point uncertainty
a frequentist multiple-break test with explicit break dates + SC/BIC
an explicit linear-Gaussian state-space UC model (level+slope+seasonal) with smoothing
outside the engine — only a point forecast without posterior break probabilities

output_key_fields: Y and SD in trend: the fitted trend plus the posterior standard deviation per time point (a chart-ready band)
trend.cpOccPr: the per-time posterior change-probability curve (of length n, ∈[0,1]) — the MAIN chart-data
cp / cpPr / cpCI in trend: the change-point positions in decreasing probability, the probability of each, and the credible interval of the position
ncp / ncp_median / ncp_mode in trend: the posterior distribution of the number of change points
Y, cpOccPr and amp in season_component: the seasonal component and the seasonal change probability (absent when season='none')
R2 / RMSE / marg_lik / sig2: goodness of fit + the marginal likelihood + the noise
beast_changepoints: n_cp/cp/cpPr filtered by a threshold (with no NaN padding)
interpretation_traps: ncp is a posterior MEAN (non-integer, e.g. 0.14) — NOT a fixed number of breaks; read ncp_median/ncp_mode + cpPr for a decision
cp is returned with NaN padding at the end (the maximum slots); the wrapper already filters it — do not read the raw slots
a gap in y does not fail — it is INTERPOLATED silently; the wrapper blocks it with a hard gate, for determinism
harmonic/dummy seasonality WITHOUT a period -> BEAST silently guesses the periodicity (non-deterministic); the wrapper requires it explicitly
cpOccPr (the per-time curve) ≠ cpPr (per detected cp): the former is the chart-data, the latter is the probability of the top change points
stochastic MCMC: the same seed ⇒ an identical result; the default seed=2025
sources: Zhao et al. 2019 Remote Sensing of Environment 232 (a Bayesian estimator of abrupt change, seasonality and trend)
Zhao, Wulder et al. 2019, 'Detecting change-point, trend, and seasonality in satellite time series data..', Remote Sensing of Environment 232:111181 (the BEAST algorithm)
live introspection of the trend and season output blocks (cpOccPr/cp/cpPr/cpCI/ncp); reproducibility comes from the MCMC seed
precondition_tools: beast_decompose (the PRODUCER: run it first to obtain the fitted beast handle)
beast_changepoints (the CONSUMER: extracting change-point positions + probabilities with a threshold)

cards.method: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Regression (AutoSTR) — trend + multiple/complex seasonality + remainder with CIs per component
cards.when: a univariate seasonal series, possibly with several seasonal periods; you want a trend plus one or more seasonal components with confidence intervals, and/or the seasonally adjusted series; robust to outliers (robust=True)
cards.when_not: a non-seasonal series (frequency<2 -> the trend filters of #56); forecasting (this decomposition does not forecast — use #58-#60, or ARIMA); latent common factors across several series (-> #61); manual custom predictors (that needs the low-level interface, outside this node)

alternatives.criterion: a non-seasonal series — only a trend/cycle decomposition (the output gap)
common latent trends across MANY series, not one
a state-space trend+seasonal model with forecasting/filtering
you do not need CIs — a faster decomposition

output_key_fields: components: a named list of numeric vectors (Data/Trend/Seasonality <period>../Random) — chart-data
component_names: the column order; n_seasonal: the number of seasonal components (>1 for msts)
confidence_intervals: {lower, upper} per predictor component (absent when no confidence level is given)
fitted: {fitted, lower, upper}, the overall fit band (absent when no confidence level is given)
cvMSE: the cross-validated MSE of the lambda selection (blank on the robust path); plus the robust and confidence flags
seasadj (regdec_seasadj): the seasonally adjusted series = the sum of the included components (default Trend+Random)
interpretation_traps: seasadj.STR SILENTLY ignores unknown include names (a warning + skip) -> the node blocks them with a hard gate
the decomposition silently accepts gaps -> the node requires a complete series (a gap gate)
the seasonal component names are 'Seasonality <period>' (e.g. 'Seasonality 12'); msts -> several of them
cvMSE is blank on the robust path, where no cross-validated MSE is produced — do not read it as a perfect fit
STR is a decomposition, NOT a forecast; to forecast, apply state space/ARIMA to the seasadj series

Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice 3rd ed. §3.7 (STL/STR decomposition)

regdec_seasadj (the seasonally adjusted series; include must be a subset of the component names)

cards.method: STL decomposition (seasonal-trend-loess) tolerant of gaps and short series
cards.when: a univariate seasonal series; you want a seasonal/trend/remainder decomposition when there are gaps, or the series is short and does not cover a whole number of periods
cards.when_not: multiple or changing seasonality (-> X-13, #4, or an STL with several seasonal windows); a structural state-space model with uncertainty (-> #58/#59); a pure trend-cycle output gap (-> #56/#92)

alternatives.criterion: no gaps and complete whole periods; then the plain STL suffices
you want only trend/cycle (the output gap), not a seasonal term
an official seasonal adjustment with calendar/outlier regressors

output_key_fields: seasonal/trend/remainder: numeric vectors of length n (raw = seasonal + trend + remainder at the observed points)
raw: the original series, blank at the gaps; weights: the outer-loop robustness weights in [0,1], where a low value marks an outlier
time: the numeric time index; n_obs/n_missing: the number of observations and of gaps
n_p/periodic/s_window/t_window/l_window/s_degree/t_degree: the final parameters that were used
interpretation_traps: an even s_window or t_window is SILENTLY rounded up to the next odd value; the wrapper blocks it with an explicit odd-number gate, so you never believe the value you passed was the one used
s_window='periodic' forces s_degree=0 and an enormous internal span, fixing the seasonality; for an evolving seasonality supply a finite odd s_window
trend and seasonal have NO gaps even when raw does (they are interpolated across the blocks); the remainder stays blank at the original gaps
low weights (~0) mark points that the robust loop down-weighted as outliers, not an error
an s_degree of 1 or 2 requires enough points per subseries; for very short series prefer s_window='periodic'
sources: Cleveland, Cleveland, McRae & Terpenning 1990 (STL), J. Official Statistics 6:3-73
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the series when it is not already a series handle)

cards.method: Nonparametric detrending & output gap (loess / smoothing spline / Friedman super-smoother)
cards.when: you want a trend/cycle or output gap without a parametric trend form; a smooth, data-driven detrending of a series (loess, a smoothing spline, or the super-smoother); a fast atheoretical benchmark for the gap
cards.when_not: you want economic structure or potential output with shocks (-> #58-#61); a band-pass cycle at a specific frequency (-> #56); a real-time one-sided gap with no end-point revision (-> #92 or #57); very short series (n<4)

alternatives.criterion: you want an HP or band-pass cycle at a defined frequency rather than a free non-parametric trend
you need a real-time (one-sided) gap with no revision of the end points
you want a regression-based filter without the HP spurious-cycle problem
you want a structural unobserved-components/state-space potential output with shocks & credible bands
you want automatic smoothing selection instead of a manual span

output_key_fields: trend: numeric, of the same length as y (the non-parametric trend; chart-data)
cycle: y - trend (np_detrend; the cyclical component / gap in levels)
gap: the output gap by mode (np_output_gap; pct=% deviation, log=100*the log difference, level=y-trend)
smoother: the parameters per method — loess {span, degree, equivalent_df}; the smoothing spline {spar, lambda, df, crit, cv}; the super-smoother {span}
x/y/n: the index, the original series, the number of observations
interpretation_traps: atheoretical: the gap is statistical, NOT economic potential output — do not interpret it as structural

end-point instability: loess and the smoothing spline are two-sided, so the ends of the trend and the gap are revised as new data arrive (exactly as with the HP filter); for real-time work use #92 or #57

a higher smoothing-spline spar gives a less flexible trend, and so a larger gap; a larger span in loess or the super-smoother gives a smoother trend; the smoothing choice determines the amplitude of the gap
mode='pct' requires trend != 0; mode='log' requires y>0 & trend>0 (explicit gates; for rates/growth around 0 use mode='level')
supsmu sorts x internally; the trend is realigned back to the original order (approx) so that cycle = y - trend is correct
sources: Cleveland, Devlin & Grosse 1988 J. Econometrics 37(1) (regression by local fitting); Friedman 1984 (a variable-span smoother)
Cleveland, Grosse & Shyu 1992 (loess, local regression); Friedman 1984 SLAC PUB-3477 (the super smoother)
Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009 ESL §5 (smoothing splines, GCV)
Hamilton 2018 REStat 100:831 (the HP critique -> the motivation for atheoretical benchmarks)

cards.method: Price index numbers (bilateral/multilateral/spliced) + CPI-subindex contribution decompositions
cards.when: long-format scanner/CPI micro data (time,prices,quantities,prodID); you want a price index (bilateral or multilateral) or a decomposition of the change in the value of a CPI subindex into price/quantity contributions per product
cards.when_not: you already have a finished index-level series (an index level ts) — that is a transform/growth-rate task, not index-number construction; a macro aggregate without product-level micro data; a need for SPQ/model-based or chained bilateral batch indices (outside the curated surface)

alternatives.criterion: high product turnover / new-goods bias — the bilateral indices (Laspeyres/Paasche) suffer chain drift; you want a transitive multilateral index
you want a non-revisable extending multilateral series beyond a fixed window (a rolling-window splice)
you want a TFP/quantity index (Färe-Primont) rather than a price index

pi_splice: index (a scalar, or the full series when interval=True); method; splice; dates

contributions (pi_contributions): a per-product frame {prodID, value_differences, price_contributions, quantity_contributions}; plus n_products
interpretation_traps: start > end SILENTLY returns a wrong, inverted index — the wrapper blocks it with a gate; always keep start <= end

pi_contributions: the price_contributions of a product can be 0 when its price did not change — the quantity is a contribution to the value DIFFERENCE (an indicator, not an index ratio)
interval=False gives a single index, end against start (with the base at start = 1); interval=True gives a dated series for a chart

cards.method: Extreme Value Theory — GEV block maxima & GP/PP/Gumbel/Exponential threshold exceedances + return levels
cards.when: modelling the TAIL (tail risk) of a series: the size/frequency of extreme events, return levels/return periods (e.g. a 1-in-100 loss), stress thresholds — through the GEV (block maxima) or GP Peaks-Over-Threshold (POT)
cards.when_not: you care about the body of the distribution rather than the tail; a single fixed-quantile VaR or ES suffices (-> #65); a conditional or time-varying tail (GARCH-EVT, or the quantile-regression Growth-at-Risk of #64); non-stationary EVT with covariates (out of scope here)

alternatives.criterion: you want a fast historical/gaussian/Cornish-Fisher VaR/ES without a tail model — NO extrapolation beyond the sample
a conditional tail (Growth-at-Risk) with covariates rather than an unconditional EVT tail
you have the whole series (not only block maxima) -> POT exploits more tail data
only periodic maxima are available (e.g. annual), or there is no clean threshold

output_key_fields: par: a named vector of parameters — GEV/PP {location,scale,shape}; GP {scale,shape}; Gumbel {location,scale}; Exponential {scale}. shape>0 a heavy tail (Frechet); shape<0 bounded (Weibull); shape~0 light (Gumbel)
se/cov_theta: the standard errors and covariance (ML and generalized ML routes); absent for L-moments; nllh/AIC/BIC for model comparison (also absent for L-moments)
threshold/rate/npy/n_exceed: (GP/PP/Exp) the threshold, the exceedance rate, npy=the number of observations per period_basis (it sets the base of the return periods), the number of exceedances
convergence/converged: the optimiser code (0 means ok) and the converged flag (a blank code from the L-moment route counts as ok) — ALWAYS read it, since the node is stateless and stderr is lost
evt_return_level: return_periods + estimate + ci_lower/ci_upper (delta method) — chart-data for a return-level plot
evt_threshold_diag: mrl_* (the mean residual life with its band) and stab_* (the transformed scale and shape with their bands) per threshold — the grids for threshold selection, with NO plot
interpretation_traps: npy trap: for GP/PP, time_units sets npy (the default 'days'->365.25). Wrong time_units => the return levels are interpreted on the WRONG base (e.g. 'annual' on monthly data). Set time_units correctly and read npy from the output

the sign of shape = the tail regime: shape>0 (Frechet, a heavy tail, infinite moments of order>1/shape); shape<0 (Weibull, a bounded upper tail); shape≈0 (Gumbel/exponential). Large |shape| with few exceedances is unstable

threshold bias-variance: too low a threshold -> bias (a non-asymptotic GP); too high -> variance (few exceedances). evt_threshold_diag shows the lowest u above which the mean excess (linear) & shape stabilise

return period > 1: every return period must be > 1 (rlevd); the 100-year level = the 1-1/100 quantile, NOT 'the maximum in 100 years'. The normal-approximation CIs understate the uncertainty far into the tail

the L-moment route is robust but returns NO standard errors, AIC or negative log-likelihood, and covers GEV and GP only. For model comparison or inference use ML or generalized ML; the latter helps when the ML shape estimate is unstable on a small sample
sources: Coles 2001, An Introduction to Statistical Modeling of Extreme Values (GEV/GP, threshold selection, return levels)
Embrechts, Kluppelberg & Mikosch 1997, Modelling Extremal Events for Insurance and Finance (POT, tail index)
McNeil, Frey & Embrechts 2015, Quantitative Risk Management 2nd ed. §5-7 (EVT VaR/ES, mean excess)
precondition_tools: evt_threshold_diag (POT: choose the threshold BEFORE the GP/PP fit — mean-residual-life linearity + parameter stability)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (check stationarity/approximate iid behaviour: stationary EVT assumes approximately iid exceedances)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a loss/return series from a file)

cards.method: Expectile-based extreme tail risk (extreme/intermediate expectiles + marginal expected shortfall + the heavy-tail index)
cards.when: a heavy-tailed financial series (fat tails, gamma>0); you want coherent tail-risk measures BEYOND the sample — extreme expectiles (asymmetric minimization, coherent), the systemic marginal expected shortfall E[Y|X extreme], or the heavy-tail index gamma with asymptotic CIs
cards.when_not: light-tailed or bounded data (gamma near 0, where the Hill estimator breaks down); a small n (below roughly 100 for an extreme level); a plain in-sample historical or gaussian VaR and ES (-> #65); a quantile-based conditional Growth-at-Risk with covariates (-> #64)

alternatives.criterion: in-sample ES/CVaR (historical/gaussian/Cornish-Fisher) without extrapolation beyond the sample
a conditional downside quantile with covariates (Growth-at-Risk), not an unconditional extreme tail
coherent expectile-based systemic risk rather than the quantile-based QuantMES
the quantile-based indirect estimator when the direct LAWS one is unstable at the extreme level

output_key_fields: er_expectiles: expectile (the point estimate), level (intermediate or extreme), variance + ci_lower/ci_upper (the asymptotic band; absent when the variance is not requested), biasTerm
er_mes: mes (E[series1|series2 extreme]), estimator (quantile/expectile), variance + ci_lower/ci_upper, conf_level
er_tail_index: hill_gamma (the Hill estimate), hill_ci_lower/upper, hill_bias, eb_gamma (the expectile-based estimate; blank when tau was not supplied)
object: the full raw result (HatQMES, gammaHat, ExpctHat and the rest)
interpretation_traps: tau is the INTERMEDIATE level (tau_n->1); tau1 is the EXTREME level; tau1 > tau is required — reversing them -> a silently wrong prediction (the gate blocks it)
MES DIRECTION: MES = E[series1 (data) | series2 (data2) extreme]; data2 is the conditioning/systemic variable (column 2 internally), NOT data
an expectile != a quantile: the expectile minimises an asymmetric squared loss (a coherent risk measure); it is not the tau-quantile
gamma (the tail index) = 1/alpha (Pareto); gamma>=0.5 -> infinite variance, gamma>=1 -> an infinite mean; this is critical for the validity of the measures
k, the intermediate sequence, is a bias-variance tradeoff: a small k gives high variance, a large k gives bias; k>=n or k=0 silently return a blank or a zero (the gate blocks them)
the asym-Dep variance requires bigBlock/smallBlock (big blocks separated by small blocks); without them the variance is blocked by a clean gate instead of a cryptic error
fully deterministic: the CIs are ASYMPTOTIC (closed form), NOT bootstrap — no dependence on a seed
sources: Padoan, S.A. & Stupfler, G. (2022). Joint inference on extreme expectiles for multivariate heavy-tailed distributions. Bernoulli 28(2)
Davison, A.C., Padoan, S.A. & Stupfler, G. (2023). Tail Risk Inference via Expectiles in Heavy-Tailed Time Series. JBES 41(3) 876-889
Daouia, A., Girard, S. & Stupfler, G. (2018). Estimation of tail risk based on extreme expectiles. JRSS-B 80, 263-292
Hill, B.M. (1975). A simple general approach to inference about the tail of a distribution. Annals of Statistics 3, 1163-1174
precondition_tools: er_tail_index (the Hill gamma>0 & its CI: confirm the heavy tail BEFORE the extreme measures; gamma>=0.5 -> infinite variance)
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test (EVT wants (approximately) stationary data, not trending levels)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading a return series from a file)

cards.method: Conditional & unconditional expectiles (Expectiles-at-Risk / a GaR analogue, LAWS)
cards.when: you want least-asymmetrically-weighted-squares expectile curves in the tails of the conditional distribution — an Expectile-at-Risk / GaR analogue sensitive to the MAGNITUDE of the tail; or the unconditional expectile of a vector
cards.when_not: you want a plain quantile or VaR, non-crossing and robust to outliers -> #64; you want a full density forecast or a skew-t -> #95; you want a closed-form ES or CVaR -> #65

alternatives.criterion: you want the quantile/VaR interpretation (P[Y<q]=tau), robustness to outliers, non-crossing
you want a FULL parametric density forecast (skew-t) rather than tail points
the expectile curves cross -> impose monotonicity/no crossing
you want automatic selection of lambda (schall/gcv) rather than a manual lambda

output_key_fields: asymmetries: the expectile levels (asymmetry weights) that were estimated
intercepts: the expectile-specific intercept per level
coefficients: a list per covariate — a matrix [1 x #levels] of the effects per expectile
fitted: an n x #levels matrix with the conditional expectile curves (chart-data)
lambda: the smoothing parameters per term (after schall/gcv/.. or fixed)
expectiles (exr_expectile): one unconditional expectile per prob (0.5 = the arithmetic mean)
interpretation_traps: an expectile ≠ a quantile: the tau-expectile does NOT satisfy P[Y<=e]=tau; it is asymmetric L2 (sensitive to the magnitude of the tail, NOT robust to outliers the way a quantile is)
the 0.5-expectile EQUALS the (conditional) mean, not the median
estimate='laws' does NOT guarantee non-crossing expectile curves; use restricted/bundle/sheets if they cross
smooth='fixed' -> lambda is used as supplied; schall/gcv/ocv select it automatically (the returned lambda then differs from the input)
probs endpoints 0/1 in exr_expectile give the min/max; in the conditional fit the levels must lie strictly in (0,1)
sources: Schnabel & Eilers 2009 CSDA 53:4168 (optimal expectile smoothing, the LAWS algorithm)
Newey & Powell 1987, 'Asymmetric least squares estimation and testing', Econometrica 55:819
Bellini & Di Bernardino 2017, 'Risk management with expectiles', Eur. J. Finance 23:487 (Expectile-at-Risk)
precondition_tools: exr_expectile (the unconditional expectile: an asymmetry benchmark before the conditional fit)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the panel/series data_frame first)
c12_distribution_risk/quantile_regression.qr_growth_at_risk (compare with the GaR quantile before choosing an expectile)

cards.method: Joint (VaR, ES) regression (Fissler-Ziegel) + an ESR-based Expected Shortfall backtest
cards.when: jointly modelling Value-at-Risk & Expected Shortfall as functions of covariates (semiparametric FZ scoring); or evaluating (backtesting) external ES forecasts against realised returns
cards.when_not: a single quantile, VaR only -> #64; an unconditional VaR or ES from history or a gaussian -> #65; a coverage-only VaR backtest (Kupiec, Christoffersen) is not here; you need a full predictive distribution -> #94 or #95

alternatives.criterion: you want only the conditional quantile/VaR (Growth-at-Risk), not the ES jointly
an unconditional ES/CVaR from a return series without covariates
the ES forecasts/estimates are not guaranteed negative (types 1-3 require a negative domain)
you want to test the ES given the VaR (regressing on q & e) rather than a strict ES-only test

output_key_fields: es_joint_reg coefficients: named (bq_0. the VaR equation; be_0. the ES equation); coefficients_q / coefficients_e: the two parts separately
std_errors (es_joint_reg): the asymptotic sandwich standard errors (blank when the covariance failed); loss: the Fissler-Ziegel score at the optimum; nobs
vcov_ok/vcov_note (es_joint_reg): a convergence and degeneracy flag — False means the covariance failed, or gave negative variances, on a small or degenerate sample
es_backtest pvalue_twosided_asymptotic: the main p-value; version 3 adds pvalue_onesided_asymptotic; the pvalue_*_bootstrap fields fill only when B>0
es_all_negative (es_backtest): False means the ES forecasts are not all negative — a possible domain violation for the G2 types 1-3, so the p-value is suspect
interpretation_traps: the backtest H0 = the forecasts are correct; a SMALL p-value => REJECTION (a bad risk model), not the other way round
a singular design matrix in es_backtest: q/e are nearly constant — you need time-varying risk forecasts

blank standard errors from es_joint_reg (vcov_ok=False): the asymptotic sandwich fails on small or degenerate samples -> raise n or check the collinearity, and do NOT read the point estimates as significant
es_all_negative=False: the G2 scoring functions (types 1-3) require negative ES forecasts; positive values silently produce a suspect p-value
version 3 (Strict Intercept) tests whether the ES of the forecast error r-e is zero; version 1 (Strict ESR) regresses the returns on e only; a different hypothesis, they are not interchangeable
the bootstrap p-values are blank when B=0; they are stochastic, so the generator is seeded (2025) for reproducibility
sources: Dimitriadis & Bayer 2019, 'A joint quantile and expected shortfall regression framework' (Electronic J. Statistics 13:1823)
Bayer & Dimitriadis 2022, 'Regression-based expected shortfall backtesting' (J. Financial Econometrics 20:437, doi:10.1093/jjfinec/nbaa013)
Fissler & Ziegel 2016 (Annals of Statistics 44:1680, joint elicitability of VaR & ES)
precondition_tools: es_backtest (post: backtest the VaR/ES forecasts; H0 is correct calibration -> you want a LARGE p-value)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load returns + covariates into a data_frame before es_joint_reg)

cards.method: Quantile Regression Forests (nonparametric conditional quantiles / Growth-at-Risk)
cards.when: non-parametric conditional quantiles y|x with non-linearities/interactions & many predictors; a lower-tail quantile = a nonparametric Growth-at-Risk without imposing a linear form
cards.when_not: you want interpretable coefficients or inference per covariate -> #64; a very small n (the trees overfit and the out-of-bag R² is unreliable); a purely time-series volatility-driven tail -> GARCH; a descriptive tail with no covariates -> #65

alternatives.criterion: you want linear, interpretable coefficients + analytic/bootstrap inference per covariate rather than a black-box forest
you want the FULL growth density + expected shortfall from the fitted quantiles (ABG step 2)
you want honest splitting / treatment heterogeneity together with quantiles
you want a full posterior / non-crossing quantiles / an explicit skew-t likelihood

output_key_fields: qrf_fit: the fitted forest handle; ntree/nodesize/mtry/n/n_predictors/predictors; y_range (min and max)
qrf_fit: rsq_oob/mse_oob, the out-of-bag pseudo-R² and MSE diagnostics; degenerate (True when rsq_oob is blank -> an unreliable fit)
qrf_fit: importance (IncNodePurity per predictor; variable-importance chart-data); seed
qrf_predict: predictions (a matrix n_new x length(quantiles); one column per quantile — chart-data); quantiles; n_new; column labels
interpretation_traps: a categorical y is ACCEPTED at fit time but FAILS at the quantiles (a silent trap) — the wrapper blocks it in qrf_fit
the trees do NOT guarantee non-crossing; with a small n/few trees check the monotonicity of the predictions across quantiles empirically
the seed applies only to qrf_fit (stochastic bootstrap trees); qrf_predict is DETERMINISTIC (aggregating leaf values) — it takes no seed
degenerate=True (a blank out-of-bag R²) means a nearly constant response, or an excessive nodesize -> the quantiles are close to useless
quantiles outside [0,1] are blocked cleanly (the raw routine produced cryptic 'minimal/maximal values' errors)
newdata must contain ALL the predictor columns from training (gate); a single quantile is normalised to a 1-column matrix
sources: Breiman (2001) Random Forests (Machine Learning 45:5-32; the random-forest engine)
Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone (2019) 'Vulnerable Growth' AER 109:1263-1289 (the GaR context)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the frame of predictors and response; clean the gaps first — the forest does NOT accept them)
qrf_predict (conditional quantiles at new x; the mandatory second link after qrf_fit)
c12_distribution_risk/quantile_regression.qr_growth_at_risk (the parametric linear GaR as a benchmark/cross-check)

WHEN: non-parametric conditional quantiles y|x with non-linearities/interactions & many predictors; a lower-tail quantile = a nonparametric Growth-at-Risk without imposing a linear form
NOT when: you want interpretable coefficients or inference per covariate -> #64; a very small n (the trees overfit and the out-of-bag R² is unreliable); a purely time-series volatility-driven tail -> GARCH; a descriptive tail with no covariates -> #65
Alternatives: #64 qr_growth_at_risk (you want linear, interpretable coefficients + analytic/bootstrap inference per covariate rather than a black-box forest) · #95 sn skew-t (st_fit_quantiles) (you want the FULL growth density + expected shortfall from the fitted quantiles (ABG step 2)) · #44 the honest/causal forest family (you want honest splitting / treatment heterogeneity together with quantiles) · #69 distributional regression (category 14) (you want a full posterior / non-crossing quantiles / an explicit skew-t likelihood)
Output: qrf_fit: the fitted forest handle; ntree/nodesize/mtry/n/n_predictors/predictors; y_range (min and max) · qrf_fit: rsq_oob/mse_oob, the out-of-bag pseudo-R² and MSE diagnostics; degenerate (True when rsq_oob is blank -> an unreliable fit) · qrf_fit: importance (IncNodePurity per predictor; variable-importance chart-data); seed · qrf_predict: predictions (a matrix n_new x length(quantiles); one column per quantile — chart-data); quantiles; n_new; column labels
Pitfalls: a categorical y is ACCEPTED at fit time but FAILS at the quantiles (a silent trap) — the wrapper blocks it in qrf_fit · the trees do NOT guarantee non-crossing; with a small n/few trees check the monotonicity of the predictions across quantiles empirically · the seed applies only to qrf_fit (stochastic bootstrap trees); qrf_predict is DETERMINISTIC (aggregating leaf values) — it takes no seed · degenerate=True (a blank out-of-bag R²) means a nearly constant response, or an excessive nodesize -> the quantiles are close to useless · quantiles outside [0,1] are blocked cleanly (the raw routine produced cryptic 'minimal/maximal values' errors) · newdata must contain ALL the predictor columns from training (gate); a single quantile is normalised to a 1-column matrix
Sources: Meinshausen (2006) 'Quantile Regression Forests', JMLR 7:983-999 · Breiman (2001) Random Forests (Machine Learning 45:5-32; the random-forest engine) · Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone (2019) 'Vulnerable Growth' AER 109:1263-1289 (the GaR context)

cards.when: you have a univariate sample (returns/losses/counts) and you want to fit a parametric distribution, test how well it fits (KS/CvM/AD/chisq), and quantify the parameter uncertainty with a bootstrap
cards.when_not: regression or conditional quantiles (-> #64); explicit tail or EVT extremes (-> #191/#192); a time series with autocorrelation (fit the residuals, not the raw levels); censored data (out of scope)

alternatives.criterion: you want a conditional distribution/quantiles as a function of covariates, not an unconditional fit
only the tail matters (block maxima / POT), not the whole distribution
you want a skewed/heavy-tailed closed form fitted to already estimated quantiles
you want to minimise a GOF distance directly (tail-focused) rather than the likelihood

output_key_fields: fd_fit: estimate (the named parameters) + sd (SE from the vcov); aic/bic/loglik for model selection; convergence/converged (0 = OK); distname/method/discrete

fd_goodness_of_fit: ks/cvm/ad (the statistics; blank for discrete distributions); kstest/cvmtest/adtest (a verbal decision, or 'not computed'); aic/bic; chisq/chisqpvalue/chisqdf (the main criterion for discrete distributions)
fd_cullen_frey: skewness/kurtosis + boot_skewness/boot_kurtosis (the Cullen-Frey cloud as chart-data); min/max/median/mean/sd; n
fd_bootstrap_ci: CI (a matrix Median/2.5%/97.5% per parameter); boot_estimates (the full sample, chart-data); n_converged/conv_rate (degeneracy)
interpretation_traps: silently wrong support: nbinom on negative values and pois on non-integers produce SILENTLY false estimates -> explicit gates per distribution (positive>0; beta∈(0,1); counts = non-negative INTEGERS)
AIC/BIC are comparable ONLY across distributions on the SAME data with the same parameter-count penalty; lower = better, not absolute
cvmtest/adtest = 'not computed' for distributions where the p-value is undefined (e.g. norm); this does NOT mean a good fit
for discrete distributions (Poisson, negative binomial) the KS, CvM and AD statistics are blank — judge from chisq and its p-value
the Cullen-Frey bootstrap cloud is stochastic, so the generator is seeded (2025); the reference routine does not return the cloud at all, only a plot — it is reproduced explicitly here
bootstrap CIs assume the correct family; check fd_goodness_of_fit first — a CI under the wrong distribution is misleadingly narrow
sources: Delignette-Muller & Dutang 2015 JSS 64(4) (fitting distributions to data)
Cullen & Frey 1999, 'Probabilistic Techniques in Exposure Assessment' (the Cullen-Frey graph)
precondition_tools: fd_cullen_frey (before the fit: the Cullen-Frey skewness/kurtosis -> which families are plausible)
fd_goodness_of_fit (after the fit: KS/CvM/AD + AIC/BIC to compare candidate distributions)

cards.method: Copula dependence + tail dependence + goodness of fit (joint stress)
cards.when: modelling the DEPENDENCE of two (or more) series separately from the marginals; especially tail co-movement (crash/stress) in returns/losses; testing whether the candidate family fits the data
cards.when_not: univariate risk (the VaR/ES of one series -> #65); raw (non-uniform) data without pobs; temporal/dynamic dependence (a GARCH copula is out of scope); dim>2 for the tail index (it is defined only in the bivariate case)

alternatives.criterion: downside/crisis co-movement (lower-tail dependence; losses together)
upside co-movement / boom clustering (upper-tail dependence)
symmetric tail dependence at both ends (heavy joint tails)
dependence without extreme tail co-movement (Gaussian/Frank -> lambda=0)
univariate downside risk of one series, not joint dependence
d>2 with asymmetric pairwise dependences (a regular vine)

output_key_fields: estimate/std_errors (cop_fit): the named copula parameters (Clayton: alpha; Gumbel and Frank: param; normal and t: rho, plus df for the t); the standard errors come from the covariance and are blank when it was not computed, as for the t degrees of freedom
loglik/aic/bic/kendall_tau (cop_fit): the fit diagnostics; kendall_tau is the dependence implied by the fitted copula (blank above two dimensions)
convergence/converged (cop_fit): 0 and True mean the optimiser converged; blank for the inversion-of-tau and inversion-of-rho routes, which do not optimise
lower/upper (cop_tail_index): the coefficients of tail dependence in [0,1] (0 means asymptotic independence in that tail)
statistic/p_value (cop_gof): the Cramér-von Mises Sn plus a parametric-bootstrap p (H0 = the family fits, so a SMALL p is a rejection)
interpretation_traps: GoF polarity: a LARGE p_value is GOOD (the family is not rejected); a small p means the copula does NOT fit — the classic sign-reversal mistake
tailIndex is DEPRECATED -> the wrapper uses lambda (the same lower/upper; it avoids a future breakage)

clayton = the LOWER tail (co-crash); gumbel = the UPPER tail (co-boom); normal & frank give lambda 0 in both tails even when the overall correlation is high (the trap: a high rho does not imply tail dependence)
the input MUST be pseudo-observations in [0,1]^d; fitCopula does NOT check the range (a silently wrong log-likelihood) — the wrapper blocks it with a hard gate; run pobs first
the cop_gof p_value is STOCHASTIC (a parametric bootstrap with N replicates); the seed defaults to 2025 -> reproducible; a small N -> a noisy p
tail_index is bivariate ONLY (dim==2); for dim>2 the function blocks explicitly
sources: Hofert, Kojadinovic, Maechler & Yan 2018, 'Elements of Copula Modeling with the reference' (Springer)
Genest, Remillard & Beaudoin 2009 (Insurance: Math. & Econ. 44:199, the parametric-bootstrap GoF Sn)
Joe 2014, 'Dependence Modeling with Copulas' (CRC) §2 (tail dependence coefficients)
Nelsen 2006, 'An Introduction to Copulas' 2nd ed. (Archimedean families)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the series; then convert them to pseudo-observations with pobs)
cop_fit (fit FIRST; it produces the fitCopula handle for tail_index/gof)
cop_gof (post: a parametric-bootstrap GoF; a large p means the family is not rejected)

cards.method: Regular-vine copulas — a pair-copula construction of the joint dependence (structure selection + loglik + simulate)
cards.when: multivariate (d>=2) dependence with tail dependence/asymmetry beyond linear correlation; the input is pseudo-observations with uniform [0,1] margins (PIT/rank); you want a flexible joint model + scenario simulation
cards.when_not: linear correlation/Gaussian dependence suffices (use the covariance); raw returns without a margin transform (apply PIT/pobs first); temporal dependence/volatility (06-volatility); d=1

alternatives.criterion: symmetric dependence suffices; the pair-copula flexibility is not needed
univariate/bivariate tail risk without a full vine
portfolio risk decomposition under linear assumptions
there is one dominant variable driving the whole dependence (a star structure)

output_key_fields: Matrix: the lower-triangular structure matrix of the vine (which pairs sit in each tree)
family / family_names: the pair-copula codes & names per position (0 = independence)
par / par2: the parameters of each pair copula (par2 only for t/two-parameter families)
tau: the implied Kendall's tau per pair; log_lik / AIC / BIC: the fit-time goodness
all_independence: True when EVERY family is 0 (a degenerate, independent vine)
vine_loglik: loglik (a scalar or per observation), AIC, BIC, npars on NEW data
vine_sim: sim = an NxD matrix of simulated pseudo-observations in [0,1] (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: the input MUST be pseudo-observations in [0,1] (a PIT or rank transform), NOT raw returns; gaps are blocked explicitly, since the raw routine silently falls back to pairwise-complete data
a family of 0 at a position means an independence copula there; all_independence=True means the vine found no dependence at all
the par values are interpreted PER family (a Clayton theta != a Gumbel theta != a Frank one); read family_names alongside par
the AIC/BIC from vine_loglik are computed on the SUPPLIED data (for a holdout comparison); the fit-time AIC/BIC from vine_select are on the training set
vine_sim is STOCHASTIC -> the same seed => identical output (default 2025); the output is in copula space [0,1], an inverse margin transform is needed for return space
CVine vs RVine: a CVine imposes a star structure per tree (less flexible); the default is RVine (the Dissmann greedy MST)
sources: Aas, Czado, Frigessi & Bakken 2009, 'Pair-copula constructions of multiple dependence', Insurance: Math. & Econ. 44:182-198
Dissmann, Brechmann, Czado & Kurowicka 2013, 'Selecting and estimating regular vine copulae', CSDA 59:52-69 (the RVineStructureSelect algorithm)
Czado 2019, Analyzing Dependent Data with Vine Copulas (Springer Lecture Notes in Statistics)
precondition_tools: vine_loglik (in-sample vs holdout loglik: is the structure over-fitted?)
vine_sim (a posterior-predictive check: simulated vs empirical dependence)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the pseudo-observations)

cards.method: SDE scenario generation (short-rate/asset diffusion paths) + a martingale no-arbitrage check
cards.when: generating stochastic scenarios (Monte Carlo paths) for a short rate (Vasicek/CIR/OU) or an asset (GBM); stress testing/ESG cash-flow projection; checking the no-arbitrage property of the simulation
cards.when_not: you want to ESTIMATE SDE parameters from data (quasi-ML estimation is out of scope); jump, Lévy or COGARCH dynamics; fitting a distribution to fitted quantiles (-> #95); VaR or ES on historical returns (-> #65)

alternatives.criterion: VaR/ES on HISTORICAL returns, not a forward-looking simulation
a closed-form parametric distribution on fitted quantiles rather than path simulation

alternatives.alt: the jump, Lévy and quasi-ML extensions (not exposed)
alternatives.criterion: jumps, heavy tails, or parameter estimation from data (a future node)

output_key_fields: paths: a NUMERIC matrix (rows=time=n_steps+1, cols=paths) — chart-data; paths[1,]=xinit
time: the grid [0.T] of length n_steps+1; terminal_values: the values at T per path
summary_mean / summary_quantiles: the per-time mean & q5/q25/q50/q75/q95 (fan chart)
feller_ok: for the CIR process only, 2*kappa*theta >= sigma^2 — otherwise blank; a degeneracy flag, not a hard stop
esg_martingale_test: {theoretical_price, empirical_mean, diff, mc_se, within_ci, n_paths}
interpretation_traps: within_ci=True means the simulation is consistent with no arbitrage (the deflated bond matches the closed-form P(0,T)); False points to Euler bias, too few paths, or wrong parameters
vasicek and ou are THE SAME SDE (theta*(mu-x)dt+sigma dW); a different label, identical dynamics
esg_martingale_test is gated to {vasicek,cir}; gbm/ou (asset models) have NO bond price -> a hard stop, not a silent mistake
the CIR process under an Euler scheme can occasionally approach 0; feller_ok=False warns of a possible loss of positivity
the seed defaults to 2025; the same seed => bit-identical paths (node reproducibility)
sources: Brouste et al. 2014, 'The YUIMA Project', JSS 57(4) <https://www.jstatsoft.org/v57/i04/>
Vasicek 1977 (J. Financial Economics 5:177) — the closed-form P(0,T)
Cox, Ingersoll & Ross 1985 (Econometrica 53:385) — the CIR closed-form P(0,T)
precondition_tools: esg_simulate_diffusion (run it FIRST; its object output is the input to esg_martingale_test)
esg_martingale_test (a validation gate: E[exp(-∫r)] ≈ the closed-form P(0,T); vasicek/cir only)

cards.method: Small linear(ized) DSGE: Klein (2000) solution + Kalman-filter ML estimation, structural IRFs, forecasts and historical shock decomposition
cards.when: you have a SMALL linearized DSGE (log-linear equilibrium conditions with rational-expectations leads; e.g. a 3-equation New Keynesian or a linearized RBC model) and you want (a) to solve it at given parameters -> policy/transition matrices + saddle-path stability (dsge_solve), (b) to estimate the structural parameters on real observed macro data by ML through the Kalman filter (dsge_estimate), (c) structural IRFs to fundamental shocks (dsge_irf), (d) model-consistent forecasts (dsge_forecast), (e) a historical shock decomposition + smoothed structural shocks (dsge_shock_decomposition)
cards.when_not: a large or genuinely nonlinear DSGE, with occasionally binding constraints (that needs a higher-order perturbation solver — outside this linear-formula node); atheoretical multivariate forecasting -> #11-#15; a plain state-space model with no rational-expectations cross-equation restrictions -> #56-#61; a Bayesian DSGE with a random-walk Metropolis posterior (not exposed here); a shock count that differs from the observable count (the Klein solver requires equality)

alternatives.criterion: you want a general linear state-space model (local level or trend, unobserved components) WITHOUT rational-expectations cross-equation restrictions; the DSGE imposes theoretical restrictions that a plain state-space model does not
atheoretical reduced-form dynamics/forecasting without structural microfoundations; you do not want to impose equilibrium conditions
structural shocks + IRFs but with identification through restrictions on a VAR, not through the full DSGE cross-equation structure
you want posterior distributions/credible bands with priors (adaptive RWMH) rather than ML point estimates + delta-method SE

output_key_fields: dsge_solve: policy_matrix (G, controls×states); transition_matrix (H); shock_matrix (M); obs_matrix (D); eigenvalue_moduli + eigen_classification; stable (saddle path); n_stable/n_states; object=dsge_solution (register -> dsge_irf)

dsge_estimate: coefficients + se (the structural parameters + the log shock SD, delta method); loglik (Kalman); nobs; convergence (0=OK); stable; identification{identified,rank,condition_number,strength,summary}; the policy/transition matrices; object=dsge_fit (register)
dsge_irf: irf, a frame {period, impulse, response, value[, se, lower, upper]}; has_se (True only for an estimated fit); impulses/responses; source_class
dsge_forecast: forecasts {period,variable,value}; horizon; states (h×n_states); obs_matrix (h×n_obs); variables
dsge_shock_decomposition: decomposition_by_obs (per observable: T×{shocks..,initial}); obs_names; shock_names; observed (T×n_obs deviations); smoothed_shocks ((T-1)×n_shocks) + smoothed_shock_names
interpretation_traps: saddle-path stability is a PREREQUISITE: stable=False means the solution is neither unique nor stable (a Blanchard-Kahn violation) — do NOT interpret the impulse responses or forecasts; change the parameters or the specification
the number of exogenous state shocks MUST equal the number of observed controls (the Klein solver): the wrapper gates it explicitly (#state_eqs == #obs_eqs); fewer shocks -> stochastic singularity
lead(x) or E(x) in the formula is the rational-expectations forward term E_t[x_{t+1}], NOT a real future value; a state is always an exogenous AR process carrying a shock (shock=True)

standard errors on the impulse responses exist ONLY when the object is an estimated fit (the delta method on an estimated covariance); on a calibrated solution se is ignored and has_se=False — there is no sampling uncertainty at fixed parameters
dsge_forecast/dsge_shock_decomposition require a dsge_fit (they need Kalman-filtered/smoothed states from an estimation on data); a bare dsge_solve is not enough -> a hard gate

dsge_estimate: a non-zero convergence code, or an unidentified model, means the coefficients and standard errors are not reliable (a flat likelihood, or weak identification); check the condition number and the per-parameter strength before interpreting them
demean=True removes only the mean — the observables must already be stationary (log deviations); trending or unit-root data give a wrong likelihood
ML point estimates + delta-method SE (NOT Bayesian): for posterior uncertainty with priors you need the Bayesian node (bayes_dsge)

[#200] Small linear(ized) DSGE: Klein (2000) solution + Kalman-filter ML estimation, structural IRFs, forecasts and historical shock decomposition
Category: 13-heterogeneous-agent-ge
Nodes: dsge_solve · dsge_estimate · dsge_irf · dsge_forecast · dsge_shock_decomposition
WHEN: you have a SMALL linearized DSGE (log-linear equilibrium conditions with rational-expectations leads; e.g. a 3-equation New Keynesian or a linearized RBC model) and you want (a) to solve it at given parameters -> policy/transition matrices + saddle-path stability (dsge_solve), (b) to estimate the structural parameters on real observed macro data by ML through the Kalman filter (dsge_estimate), (c) structural IRFs to fundamental shocks (dsge_irf), (d) model-consistent forecasts (dsge_forecast), (e) a historical shock decomposition + smoothed structural shocks (dsge_shock_decomposition)

cards.method: Structural simultaneous-equation macro-econometric model (FRB/US-style): MDL definition → estimate → deterministic/stochastic simulation → policy multipliers
cards.when: you have a structural system of simultaneous macro-model equations (behavioral equations with coefficients to estimate + accounting identities) defined in an MDL string; you want (a) coefficient estimation (OLS/IV) per equation, (b) deterministic/stochastic simulation or a forecast/scenario for the endogenous variables, (c) a table of policy multipliers (impact/interim/dynamic) of the endogenous variables with respect to exogenous instruments
cards.when_not: a single-equation model (single-equation OLS or IV -> category 07); a reduced-form VAR or VECM with no theoretical identities (-> categories 03/05); a micro-founded DSGE with rational expectations, Bellman equations and structural shocks (this card solves a backward-looking structural form, NOT a general rational-expectations DSGE); you do not have data covering ALL the variables over the estimation and simulation period

alternatives.criterion: you want a projection/scenario (DYNAMIC/FORECAST) or a stochastic simulation of the endogenous variables after estimation
you want impact/interim/dynamic policy multipliers (endogenous targets with respect to exogenous instruments)
a single-equation causal estimate with an endogenous regressor (not a whole system)
reduced-form dynamics without theoretical identities/behavioral restrictions
a micro-founded rational-expectations DSGE (structural shocks, IRFs) rather than a backward-looking structural form

output_key_fields: sem_estimate: coefficients (a named list per behavioral equation: named numeric); statistics (RSquared/AdjustedRSquared/DurbinWatson/Fstatistics/SER/AIC/BIC/LogLikelihood per behavioral equation); residuals (a series per behavioral equation); endogenous/exogenous/behaviorals/identities; estTech; object (the registry handle)
sem_simulate (deterministic): mode='deterministic'; simulation (a named list of ts per endogenous variable); simType; simAlgo; tsrange
sem_simulate (stochastic): mode='stochastic'; sim_mean & sim_sd (a named list of ts per endogenous variable); stoch_replica; seed
sem_multipliers: multiplier_matrix (a TARGET×INSTRUMENT matrix with var_period axis labels); target_labels (row labels); instrument_labels (column labels); tsrange
interpretation_traps: the data must extend AT LEAST one period before the start of the estimation or simulation whenever the equations contain a lag operator (otherwise a clean stop; the raw routine gives a cryptic error)
simulation, stochastic simulation and the multiplier matrix all require an estimated model with no blank coefficients; the node gates them, so an unestimated model is blocked

in the multipliers: when the INSTRUMENT period is later than the TARGET period the cell is 0 (causality does not run backwards); a single-period TSRANGE => impact multipliers, a multi-period one => interim/dynamic multipliers

stochastic=True adds an automatic normal disturbance with the regression standard error, ONLY in the behavioural equations and never in the identities; the seed is mandatory for reproducibility (default 2025)
FORECAST vs DYNAMIC: FORECAST uses simulated values for the lagged endogenous variables AND beyond the historical data; STATIC uses the actual lagged values — do not confuse them

estTech='IV' requires IV expressions inside the model definition, or in the iv argument; otherwise the routine errors (blocked); the Chow test, PDL, restrictions and automatic error structure are all declared INSIDE the model-definition string
sources: Brayton & Tinsley 1996 (a guide to FRB/US: a macroeconometric model of the United States)
Klein, L. (1950) 'Economic Fluctuations in the United States 1921–1941', Cowles Commission Monograph 11 (Klein Model I, the reference model)
Pindyck, R.S. & Rubinfeld, D.L. (1998) 'Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts', 4th ed., McGraw-Hill (structural simultaneous-equation estimation & simulation, multipliers)
Fair, R.C. (1984) 'Specification, Estimation, and Analysis of Macroeconometric Models', Harvard University Press (FRB/US-style structural macro modelling)

c00_data_utilities/series_layout_conversion.ts_convert (a long frame -> a wide multi-series frame; one column per model variable)
sem_estimate (the PRODUCER: the estimated BIMETS_MODEL handle -> sem_simulate/sem_multipliers)

cards.method: Computable/Applied General Equilibrium — a structural dynamic model (sdm) with a Leontief/Cobb-Douglas/CES demand structure; equilibrium prices, activity levels, growth rate
cards.when: you have a technology/demand structure in IO/SAM form (a demand-coefficient matrix A, or Cobb-Douglas/CES shares Beta+alpha[+sigma]) + a supply matrix B + exogenous supplies S0Exg (labour/capital/off-network); you want to COMPUTE the general equilibrium — relative prices p (a numeraire), activity/output levels z, the demand matrix A·diag(z), the growth rate (in a purely productive economy); a fixed point (the Li structural dynamic model / a Sraffa system); optionally the time paths of the price adjustment towards equilibrium (ts=True)
cards.when_not: you want a linearized DSGE with rational expectations, impulse responses or Bayesian estimation on data (-> #200); stock-flow-consistent macro accounting with behavioural equations (-> #203); econometric structural macro-model estimation and simulation (-> #201); you have time series and want a regression or forecast rather than a calibrated general equilibrium; the multi-money, policy-experiment and intertemporal-path features are outside the curated surface

alternatives.criterion: you want a linearized rational-expectations DSGE (policy functions, IRFs, forecast, shock decomposition) rather than a calibrated Walrasian GE on an IO/SAM structure
stock-flow-consistent macro accounting with behavioral equations & balance-sheet consistency rather than market-clearing GE
an econometric structural macro model (estimated equations + multipliers) rather than a calibrated GE
you want price-responsive demand with a tunable elasticity of substitution (sigma) — CD is the special limit sigma->0

output_key_fields: p / p_normalized: the equilibrium prices (an n-vector) & the same normalised to the commodity-1 numeraire (p/p[1]; ONLY relative prices are meaningful)
z: the equilibrium levels of activity/output/utility (an m-vector)
demand_matrix: A_eq %*% diag(z) — the demand matrix at equilibrium (chart-data); S: the supply matrix of the initial period
A_eq: the equilibrium demand-coefficient matrix (for CD/CES it differs from the inputs — it is computed at the equilibrium prices)
growth_rate: the endogenous equilibrium growth rate (a purely productive economy with no exogenous supply; blank otherwise)
tolerance / tolCond / converged: the convergence error against the threshold; converged=True exactly when tolerance<=tolCond
ts_p/ts_z/ts_S/ts_q (only with ts=True): the adjustment paths of the prices, levels, supply and sales rate in the last iteration
interpretation_traps: ONLY relative prices: a GE determines prices up to scale; ALWAYS use p_normalized (numeraire=commodity 1); the absolute p values are arbitrary
converged=False means the solution is NOT an equilibrium (tolerance>tolCond); raise maxIteration or check the structure; the node is stateless, so there is no silent retry
CD requires every column of Beta to sum to 1 (Cobb-Douglas shares); CES does NOT (non-negative shares suffice); the wrapper gates it
CES sigma: the elasticity parameter (sigma<0 is usual; sigma->0 => the Cobb-Douglas limit, sigma->-inf => Leontief); it is NOT the elasticity of substitution 1/(1-sigma) — do not confuse them
S0Exg: blank means an endogenous commodity, a non-zero value an exogenous supply (labour, land); 0 is FORBIDDEN, and the wrapper blocks it
dstype='constant' = price-INDEPENDENT demand (Leontief/Sraffa); CD/CES = price-responsive (A is recomputed at every iteration); a different economic interpretation
maxIteration=1 gives a pure dynamic simulation rather than an equilibrium computation; combine it with ts=True for the adjustment paths
sources: LI Wu (2019, ISBN 9787521804225) General Equilibrium and Structural Dynamics: Perspectives of New Structural Economics; LI Wu (2010) A Structural Growth Model and its Applications to Sraffa's System (IIOA 18th conf.)
Torres, Jose L. (2016, ISBN 9781622730452) Introduction to Dynamic Macroeconomic General Equilibrium Models (2nd ed.), Vernon Press
Varian, Hal R. (1992, ISBN 0393957357) Microeconomic Analysis, W. W. Norton — general equilibrium, p.352
precondition_tools: cge_solve (constant demand first as a Leontief/Sraffa baseline; then CD/CES for price-responsive demand)
c00_data_utilities/canonical_disk_format.arw_read_parquet (loading the IO/SAM demand/supply matrices A/B/S0Exg from Parquet)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (alternatively: loading the coefficient matrices from CSV)

cards.method: Stock-Flow-Consistent (Godley-Lavoie) macro simulation — a baseline steady-state solve, policy scenarios (shocks), balance-sheet/transactions-flow accounting validation
cards.when: you have a THEORETICALLY SPECIFIED SFC model (a system of accounting identities + behavioral equations in the Godley-Lavoie tradition) and you want to SOLVE it to a steady state (sfc_simulate), to run policy scenarios with shocks to exogenous variables/parameters (sfc_scenario_run), and to VERIFY that the balance-sheet/transactions-flow matrix is water-tight (sfc_balance_check). A deterministic simulation with block-ordered Gauss-Seidel/Broyden/Newton root solving.
cards.when_not: you want to ESTIMATE parameters from data (SFC is calibrated/theory-driven, not estimated — go to an econometric structural model); you want a micro-founded DSGE with rational expectations/optimisation & log-linearization (a different paradigm); you have a single behavioral equation (run a regression, cat. 07/08); you want a stochastic/Monte Carlo ensemble or a sensitivity sweep (sfcr_multis/sfcr_random — deliberately outside the deterministic node)

alternatives.criterion: you want a counterfactual/policy shock (e.g. higher government spending, a higher tax rate) on an already solved baseline
you want to certify that the accounting identities close (every column/row of the TFM/BS sums correctly; locating a leak)
you want an ESTIMATED structural macro-econometric model (Klein type) with simulation/multiplier analysis rather than a calibrated SFC model
you want empirically identified shocks & IRFs from data rather than a theory-driven counterfactual

output_key_fields: sfc_simulate: paths (a data_frame period × all the variables; chart-data); steady_state (the values of the last period); variables/n_variables; method; converged; object (the baseline sfcr_tbl handle -> scenario/balance)
sfc_scenario_run: paths (the scenario data_frame; chart-data); final_values; shocked_vars; shock_start/shock_end; object (the scenario sfcr_tbl handle)

sfc_balance_check: consistent (a boolean; True means water-tight); leaking_rows/leaking_cols (the names that leak); max_row_residual/max_col_residual (the largest absolute accounting residual); row_residual_by_period/col_residual_by_period (chart data); plus a message
interpretation_traps: the underlying validation returns NO value — it either prints 'Water tight!' or aborts; the wrapper traps that into a consistent flag with the leaking rows and columns, AND computes explicit numeric residuals per period, which would otherwise never surface
SFC is calibrated/theory-driven, NOT estimated; the parameters (alpha1, theta,..) are given exogenously — do not 'estimate' them; the steady state depends on them (e.g. SIM: Y* = G/theta)

in growth models, where the stocks increase perpetually, the hidden equation and the validation must use a relative tolerance (rhtol=True) rather than an absolute one — otherwise computational buildup produces a spurious failure
the hidden equation (a redundant identity, e.g. Hh=Hs in SIM): if supplied, it is checked; its failure = a mis-specified model (a leak in the logic)

the scenario INHERITS the block structure & the final state from the baseline; a shock applied BEFORE the baseline has converged produces a transient that is not a policy effect; run the baseline for enough periods (~50+) first

sfcr_matrix rows: the first element = the row name, the rest are name-value pairs per code; do NOT add a manual 'sum' column to a TFM (it is generated automatically); in a BS the non-zero rows need an explicit 'Sum' column

a large max_col_residual or max_row_residual alongside consistent=True is impossible within tol; consistent=False with small residuals means the tolerance should be raised (stationary against growth models)
sources: Godley & Lavoie 2007, Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth

Godley W. & Lavoie M. (2007) Monetary Economics: An Integrated Approach to Credit, Money, Income, Production and Wealth, Palgrave Macmillan (the SIM/PC/.. models, transactions-flow & balance-sheet matrices, water-tight accounting)

Kinsella S. & OShea T. (2010) Solution and Simulation of Large Stock Flow Consistent Monetary Production Models via the Gauss Seidel Algorithm, SSRN, doi:10.2139/ssrn.1729205 (the Gauss-Seidel method, cited in the sfcr_baseline help)
Peressini A.L., Sullivan F.E., Uhl J.J. (1988) The Mathematics of Nonlinear Programming, Springer (the Broyden & Newton-Raphson algorithms, cited in the sfcr_baseline help)
precondition_tools: sfc_simulate (solve the baseline FIRST; sfc_scenario_run & sfc_balance_check REQUIRE a solved sfcr_tbl handle)
sfc_scenario_run (a scenario = baseline + shock; it needs the baseline object)
sfc_balance_check (run it AFTER simulate/scenario to certify accounting consistency — a water-tight check)

cards.method: Bayesian Structural Time Series (state specification: local/semilocal trend + seasonal + AR + spike-and-slab regression) with MCMC
cards.when: you want a Bayesian structural decomposition/forecast of a univariate series with explicitly interpretable state components (trend + seasonality + AR) and FULL posterior uncertainty (not a point estimate); or a Bayesian regression on a time series with variable SELECTION through spike-and-slab (expected_model_size) when you have many candidate regressors; you want the posterior mean contribution of each component (nowcasting/decomposition) + predictive quantile bands
cards.when_not: you want a point or frequentist state-space estimate with no MCMC (-> #58/#59, category 10); multivariate or cointegration dynamics (VAR/VECM/Bayesian VAR); a fully custom likelihood or hierarchical model (-> #68/#69/#70); a plain ARIMA or ETS forecast with no component decomposition; a very long series where the MCMC cost is not justified against a fast Kalman filter

alternatives.criterion: you want a Bayesian state-space model with an explicit prior specification / custom observation models (SV/non-Gaussian) rather than the flag-driven structural builder
you want a point/frequentist MLE state-space model (a fast Kalman filter, no MCMC) — the same structural decomposition without posterior draws
you need a fully custom hierarchical/state model that cannot be expressed with the BSTS state components
outliers / heavy tails in the observation — a robust observation model instead of gaussian
long forecast horizons — a mean-reverting slope avoids the explosive trend of the local linear model

output_key_fields: bsts_fit: state_components (the component names — trend, seasonal, AR, regression); residual_sd (the posterior mean observation sigma); sigma_obs_quantiles; coefficients {variable, inclusion_prob, posterior_mean, posterior_mean_incl} for the regression only; burn; fitted_series with its time index; plus the handle
bsts_predict: mean/median (chart-data); lower/upper predictive bands at the quantiles; step; has_regression
bsts_components: contributions (time x component posterior mean; a stacked decomposition); contributions_lower/upper bands; components; time; burn
interpretation_traps: DETERMINISM: this is MCMC with its own compiled generator — reproducibility requires seeding BOTH the process generator and the sampler itself; the wrapper does both, in the fit AND in the prediction, and the seed is MANDATORY

local_linear_trend vs semilocal: the local linear trend has a random-walk slope that can 'explode' at long horizons; the semilocal one (an AR(1) mean-reverting slope) is safer for forecasting — the two are mutually exclusive (gate)

inclusion_prob (spike-and-slab): the posterior probability that the regressor is in the model; posterior_mean is the MEAN OVER ALL draws (it includes the zeros -> shrunk), posterior_mean_incl is conditional on inclusion — do NOT confuse them
expected_model_size applies ONLY in regression mode; it sets the prior number of non-zero coefficients (smaller => a stronger sparsity prior); in a pure structural model it is an error (gate)
regression forecast: newdata (the future regressors) is MANDATORY and must have nrow==horizon with the same predictor columns — otherwise a gate stop (the forecast needs future values of X)
burn-in: the default SuggestBurn(0.1) discards 10% as warm-up; too few niter => unstable posterior means; keep niter large enough (>=500 in production; 100-250 only for smoke tests)
seasonal.N.k naming: AddSeasonal with nseasons=12 gives the component 'seasonal.12.1'; season_duration>1 groups steps into a season (e.g. weekly seasonality in daily data)

Scott & Varian (2015) Bayesian Variable Selection for Nowcasting Economic Time Series, in Economic Analysis of the Digital Economy (NBER/Univ. Chicago Press)
Brodersen, Gallusser, Koehler, Remy & Scott (2015) Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models, Annals of Applied Statistics 9:247-274
Durbin & Koopman (2012) Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press (structural components + the Kalman filter foundation)
George & McCulloch (1997) Approaches for Bayesian variable selection, Statistica Sinica 7:339 (the spike-and-slab prior)
precondition_tools: bsts_fit (the PRODUCER: it builds the state specification from the flags, runs the MCMC fit, and returns the object handle that predict and components consume — the seed is MANDATORY)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the data_frame for regression mode: response + regressors)
c10_trend_cycle_statespace/kalman_filter_smoother.kf_local_linear_trend (a frequentist state-space baseline; compare before investing in MCMC)

cards.method: Sequential Monte Carlo / particle filters for non-linear/non-Gaussian state-space models (bootstrap / auxiliary / Liu-West / ensemble Kalman)
cards.when: you have a BUGS-style state-space (hidden Markov) model with latent states x[t] and observations y[t]; you want (a) an estimate of the marginal log-likelihood (for model comparison / particle MCMC / likelihood-based inference) and/or (b) the filtered distribution of the latent states f(x[t]|y[1:t]) per time point (mean/quantiles = chart-data). It handles NON-linear/NON-Gaussian transition & observation equations where the Kalman filter does not apply
cards.when_not: a linear-Gaussian state-space model (use the exact Kalman filter of #58/#59/#61 — analytic, with no Monte Carlo noise); you want a FULL Bayesian posterior over the parameters with MCMC diagnostics (-> #70, which gates on Rhat and ESS); structural-break or latent-regime work (category 06); simple smoothing with no latent-state model (-> #56)

alternatives.criterion: a linear-Gaussian SSM -> an exact Kalman filter/smoother (no Monte Carlo variance), a closed-form likelihood
you want a full Bayesian posterior over the parameters + convergence diagnostics (Rhat/ESS), not only latent-state filtering / a log_lik
a peaked/informative observation likelihood -> lookahead resampling reduces particle degeneracy relative to bootstrap
you want joint state+parameter online estimation in ONE pass (caution: didactic, often poor; no log_lik)
a high-dimensional latent state with additive normal observation error -> an EnKF Monte Carlo Kalman approximation (no log_lik)

output_key_fields: method: the selected filter; latent_vars: the names of the latent variable(s)

log_likelihood + log_likelihood_available: the estimated marginal log-likelihood (numeric for the bootstrap and auxiliary filters; blank with the flag False for the Liu-West and ensemble-Kalman filters — STRUCTURALLY so, never a fabricated value)
state_summary: a data_frame {node, mean, sd, q..} PER latent node/time — the per-time filtered summaries (chart-data); state_mean: the per-time posterior mean
filtered_samples: a named list of equally weighted samples (particles × latent nodes) per latent variable — for downstream reweighting/plots
ess + ess_available: the per-time effective sample size (numeric for the bootstrap and auxiliary filters; absent, with the flag False, otherwise)
param_summary + param_vars: for the Liu-West filter ONLY, the posterior summary of the top-level parameters; absent for the rest
n_particles / n_time / metadata (method/thresh/lookahead/d/seed/saveAll)
interpretation_traps: METHOD HETEROGENEITY (live-verified): ONLY the bootstrap and auxiliary filters return a log-likelihood estimate and a per-time ESS; the Liu-West and ensemble-Kalman filters return neither. The node declares this explicitly through log_likelihood_available and ess_available — do not read a blank log-likelihood as 'a bad model'; it is a structural limit of the method

particle depletion: too few particles, or a model-data mismatch, gives a log-likelihood of minus infinity or NaN samples; the node blocks it with a hard gate. Raise nParticles (default 1000); the log-likelihood estimate carries Monte Carlo variance, so model comparison must use the SAME seed and particle count

the Liu-West filter: its own documentation warns that it 'often performs poorly, provided primarily for didactic purposes'; the parameter posteriors can be over-concentrated (particle impoverishment). Prefer particle MCMC (outside the surface), or #70, for reliable parameter inference
filtered, NOT smoothed: what comes back is f(x[t]|y[1:t]) (saveAll=True, smoothing=False); it is not the full smoothing distribution f(x[t]|y[1:T])

thresh MUST ==1 (gate): resampling at every step => mvEWSamples is equally weighted everywhere => correct per-time summaries; thresh<1 is blocked (silently wrong otherwise); this applies ONLY to bootstrap (auxiliary ignores thresh)

latentNodes in TIME order: they must be stochastic nodes (for instance 'x' or 'x[1:10]'); the data must contain NO gaps, since a gap is treated as a node to be imputed — a hidden parameter, hence the gate
sources: Michaud, de Valpine, Turek, Paciorek & Nguyen 2021 JSS 100(3) (sequential Monte Carlo methods)
Gordon, Salmond & Smith (1993) 'Novel approach to nonlinear/non-Gaussian Bayesian state estimation', IEE Proc. F 140(2):107 (the bootstrap filter)
Pitt & Shephard (1999) 'Filtering via simulation: Auxiliary particle filters', JASA 94(446):590 (the auxiliary filter)
Liu & West (2001) 'Combined parameter and state estimation in simulation-based filtering', in Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in Practice, Springer, pp.197-223
Houtekamer & Mitchell (1998) 'Data assimilation using an ensemble Kalman filter technique', Monthly Weather Review 126(3):796
Doucet, de Freitas & Gordon (2001) Sequential Monte Carlo Methods in Practice, Springer
precondition_tools: smc_filter (the default method=bootstrap; only bootstrap/auxiliary return log_lik+ESS)
c14_bayesian_toolkit/general_bugs_style.bugs_style_mcmc (the same BUGS DSL; for a full parameter posterior rather than filtering)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the observations y as a series)
