cards.method: High-dimensional k-way fixed-effects GLM (binary logit/probit, Poisson count) with an analytic incidental-parameter bias correction (Fernández-Val/Weidner) + average partial effects
cards.when: panel/pseudo-panel micro data with MULTIPLE high-dimensional fixed effects (e.g. unit + time; or a network: exporter + importer) and a binary/count response — the probability of a recession/default/transition per unit; you want a consistent nonlinear FE estimate with a CORRECTION for the incidental-parameter bias (short-T panels) + interpretable average partial effects with SE
cards.when_not: no fixed effects (a plain GLM or probit); a single fixed effect with few levels (a classic conditional logit, or #83, suffices); you only want fitted probabilities or an AUC with no bias correction (-> #83); a continuous response (linear fixed effects -> #33/#46); average partial effects for a Poisson model (not supported); interactions or polynomials inside the partial effects (not supported)

alternatives.criterion: you want a plain binomial FE GLM with fitted probabilities/clustered SE/pseudo-R2 and you do NOT care about the incidental-parameter bias correction (a long T or large groups)
you have a fitted (+ bias-corrected) binary model and you want interpretable average partial effects (marginal effects) + delta-method SE rather than log-odds coefficients
a continuous response — linear fixed effects rather than a nonlinear GLM

output_key_fields: coefficients (hdfe_glm): the uncorrected structural beta (log-odds or log-rate); coefficients_bias_corrected: the bias-corrected beta (absent when bias_correct=False)
coef_table (hdfe_glm): a matrix of Estimate/Std. error/z value/Pr(>|z|) for the primary estimate (bias-corrected when that was requested)
deviance / null_deviance / converged / iterations (hdfe_glm): the fit diagnostics (converged=False is blocked by a hard gate)
nobs (full/na/pc/effective) · fe_names · fe_levels (the number of levels per fixed effect) · n_fe · bias_term/bandwidth/panel_structure, when the bias correction ran
ape (hdfe_average_partial_effects): the average partial effects per covariate, in probability units; ape_se: the delta-method standard error; ape_table: Estimate/SE/z/p; vcov: the covariance matrix
bias_corrected / panel_structure / sampling_fe / weak_exo / bandwidth / n_pop (hdfe_average_partial_effects): the estimation settings
interpretation_traps: incidental-parameter bias: in nonlinear fixed-effects models with a short T the ML coefficients are biased; bias_correct=True gives the corrected beta — compare coefficients against coefficients_bias_corrected, where the difference is often 20-30%

the bias correction and the partial effects are for binomial models ONLY: a Poisson fit is estimated, but bias_correct=True and hdfe_average_partial_effects are rejected by a hard gate, since the partial effects support binary choice only

coefficients != marginal effects: the feglm beta are log-odds (logit) / z-scores (probit) — do NOT interpret them as changes in probability; use hdfe_average_partial_effects for interpretable average partial effects

bandwidth L: 0 only if ALL the regressors are strictly exogenous; with a lagged outcome (a dynamic panel / state dependence) set L=1.4 (Fernández-Val/Weidner); the order of the FE in the formula matters when L>0

panel_structure, network against classic: for bilateral flows (trade: exporter, importer, time) use network; the wrong structure gives a wrong bias correction and a wrong partial-effect covariance (the wrapper reads the structure back off the bias-corrected fit, for consistency)

perfect classification: the fit silently drops the rows and fixed-effect groups that are perfectly predicted (counted in the perfect-classification tally of nobs); check nobs so that you do not read a reduced sample as an error
non-convergence: converged=False (hard-gated) usually means linear dependence between a regressor and the fixed effects; revise the specification
sources: Stammann, A. (2018) Fast and Feasible Estimation of Generalized Linear Models with High-Dimensional k-Way Fixed Effects, ArXiv e-prints
Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2016) Individual and time effects in nonlinear panel models with large N, T, J. Econometrics 192(1):291-312
Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2018) Fixed effects estimation of large-T panel data models, Annual Review of Economics 10:109-138
Neyman, J. & Scott, E.L. (1948) Consistent estimates based on partially consistent observations, Econometrica 16(1):1-32 (the incidental parameter problem)
Cruz-Gonzalez, M., Fernández-Val, I. & Weidner, M. (2017) Bias corrections for probit and logit models with two-way fixed effects, Stata Journal 17(3):517-545 (average partial effects)
Czarnowske, D. & Stammann, A. (2020) Fixed Effects Binary Choice Models: Estimation and Inference with Long Panels, ArXiv e-prints

cards.method: Online probabilistic forecast combination via CRPS-Learning (BOA/BEWA/ML-Poly/EWA aggregation of quantile expert forecasts)
cards.when: you have >=2 experts producing PROBABILISTIC (quantile) forecasts at the SAME tau levels and you want to combine them ADAPTIVELY online (the weights are learned sequentially from the past loss), optimally under CRPS; experts = a 3D array [T x quantiles(P) x experts(K)], y = a Tx1 realized series; appropriate when the relative performance of the experts changes over time (regime shifts) and you want per-quantile weights + the out-of-sample loss against each expert
cards.when_not: point-only forecasts rather than quantiles -> #85; hierarchical or temporal RECONCILIATION rather than combination -> reconcile_cross_temporal / reconcile_grouped; a single expert (K<2, so there is nothing to combine); batch or offline optimal fixed weights rather than online adaptivity (outside the curated surface); you simply want to EVALUATE a density forecast rather than combine -> #94 sr_crps_sample

alternatives.criterion: point-forecast combination (not probabilistic/quantile) over a single ts
hierarchical/temporal RECONCILIATION (coherence within a hierarchy) rather than learning weights from a loss
reconciliation over keyed series (#209), with MinT, WLS or OLS weights
you want ONLY the evaluation of a density/quantile forecast (CRPS/LogS/PIT), not a combination

output_key_fields: predictions: a T x P matrix, the combined probabilistic forecast per time and quantile level (chart data; sorted when allow_quantile_crossing=False)

final_weights: a P x K matrix (the adaptive weights at the last instant T+1; the weights with which the experts will be combined in the NEXT forecast; they sum to ~1 per quantile for method boa/bewa/ewa)
mean_weights: a P x K matrix (the average weight over time per expert × quantile — which expert dominated overall)
forecaster_loss_total / forecaster_loss_mean / forecaster_loss_per_quantile: the cumulative & mean CRPS-learning loss of the COMBINATION (per quantile, of length P)
expert_loss_total: a length-K cumulative loss for EACH single expert (the baseline); best_expert = the best single one
beats_best_expert: True when forecaster_loss_total <= min(expert_loss_total) — the combination beats the best single expert out of sample, which is the reason online learning exists
interpretation_traps: dims: experts MUST be [T x P x K] with dim1==length(y), dim2==length(tau); the wrong axis order (e.g. [T x K x P]) passes silently and gives a WRONG result -> a hard gate checks dim2==length(tau); double-check that the 2nd dimension is quantiles (in the same order as tau)

tau must be STRICTLY increasing & must match exactly the quantile levels at which the expert forecasts were computed; a mismatch -> an invalid loss (the gate blocks values outside (0,1)/unsorted values but NOT a semantic mismatch of levels — that is the caller's responsibility)

method: 'bewa' (default) = the BOA regret + an EWA weight update; 'boa' = the full BOA (second order); 'ewa' = plain exponential weighting; 'ml_poly'; different adaptivity — 'ewa'/'ml_poly' may not give simplex weights with thresholds
beats_best_expert=False is NOT a failure: with a small T, or one dominant expert, online learning needs time to converge; look at mean_weights — is it learning the right expert? — before rejecting it
allow_quantile_crossing=False (the default) sorts the predictions per t, giving monotone quantiles; True allows crossing and hence an invalid CDF — leave it False for interpretable quantiles
smoothing (a B-spline/P-spline across quantiles) is NOT exposed (the defaults mean no smoothing); for smooth per-quantile weights you need a custom fit outside the node
predict/update (incremental on new data) are NOT exposed: a stateless node -> every call is a complete re-fit over the supplied window
sources: Berrisch, J. & Ziel, F. (2023) CRPS Learning, Journal of Econometrics 237(2):105221 <doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.11.008>
Gaillard, P. & Goude, Y. (2015) Forecasting electricity consumption by aggregating experts (BOA/ML-Poly online aggregation)
Wintenberger, O. (2017) Optimal learning with Bernstein Online Aggregation, Machine Learning 106:119
precondition_tools: c02_univariate_forecasting/grouped_arima_ets.run_grouped_arima (it produces the quantile forecasts of one expert; repeat per model and stack them into a [T x P x K] array)
c02_univariate_forecasting/grouped_arima_ets.run_grouped_ets (a second expert for the array; at least two are needed)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the realized y values)

cards.method: Coherent forecast reconciliation (cross-sectional / temporal / cross-temporal) via an optimal least-squares projection (MinT: ols/str/wls/shr/sam)
cards.when: you have INCOHERENT base forecasts of a linearly constrained (hierarchical/grouped) multiple series — e.g. GDP = the sum of sectors, national = the sum of regions, or annual = the sum of quarters — and you want to make them COHERENT (the aggregates equal the sum of the components exactly) while ALSO improving accuracy through MinT (Wickramasuriya 2019). type: 'cs' a cross-sectional hierarchy, 'te' temporal (one series, several frequencies), 'ct' cross-temporal (both at once)
cards.when_not: a single series with no hierarchical or temporal constraint structure (there is nothing to reconcile); you want to COMBINE alternative forecasts of the SAME series, an ensemble or model average (-> #85, or the combination of #209); you do not have base forecasts for ALL the levels of the hierarchy; you want probabilistic or bootstrap reconciled paths (outside the curated surface)

alternatives.criterion: MinT shrinkage (Wickramasuriya 2019) — the normal default for accuracy when you have in-sample residuals; ols/str ignore the error covariance
you want simultaneous cross-sectional AND temporal coherence (e.g. quarterly regional series summing to an annual national total)
you want a COMBINATION of several models for ONE series (an ensemble), not the reconciliation of a hierarchy
the reconciled forecasts must be non-negative (e.g. counts, positive magnitudes)

output_key_fields: reconciled: the coherent forecasts — cs, an (h x n) matrix; te, a vector of length h*(k*+m) with labels; ct, an (n x h*(k*+m)) matrix (chart-data)
type/comb/approach/nn: the reconciliation that was performed
cs: n/n_upper/n_bottom/h + coherence_err (max|upper - agg_mat·bottom| ~0 => coherent, a post-check)
te/ct: agg_order/m/kt/h + tew; ct: n/n_upper/n_bottom
object: the foreco object (fitted)
interpretation_traps: the ORDER OF THE base COLUMNS/ROWS: cs columns = [upper.., bottom..] (the n_a upper series FIRST, then the n_b bottom ones) consistent with agg_mat; the wrong order => a silently wrong reconciliation (the wrapper checks ONLY the dimension n, not the semantic mapping)
comb DIFFERS by type: 'wlsv' is valid only for te/ct (NOT cs); 'oasd' only for cs; the wrapper blocks an invalid comb for a given type
MinT (shr/wls/sam/acov..) REQUIRES res (the in-sample residuals); without res -> a gate stop; ols/str/csstr/testr do NOT need res
temporal base ordering: LOW->HIGH frequency (the most aggregated first, e.g. annual, then semi-annual, then quarterly); the wrong order => a wrong result
a scalar agg_order m => ALL the divisors of m are used (k*+m = the sum of the divisors; m=4 -> 7, m=12 -> 28); length(base) must be a multiple of that
reconciliation is NOT an ensemble: it combines forecasts of DIFFERENT series/frequencies within one hierarchy so that they add up; it does NOT average models of the same series
sources: Wickramasuriya, S.L., Athanasopoulos, G. & Hyndman, R.J. (2019), Optimal forecast reconciliation through trace minimization (MinT), JASA 114(526):804-819. doi:10.1080/01621459.2018.1448825
Hyndman, R.J., Ahmed, R.A., Athanasopoulos, G. & Shang, H.L. (2011), Optimal combination forecasts for hierarchical time series, CSDA 55(9):2579-2589. doi:10.1016/j.csda.2011.03.006
Athanasopoulos, G., Hyndman, R.J., Kourentzes, N. & Petropoulos, F. (2017), Forecasting with temporal hierarchies, EJOR 262(1):60-74. doi:10.1016/j.ejor.2017.02.046

Di Fonzo, T. & Girolimetto, D. (2023), Cross-temporal forecast reconciliation: Optimal combination method and heuristic alternatives, Int. J. Forecasting 39(1):39-57. doi:10.1016/j.ijforecast.2021.08.004
Panagiotelis, A., Athanasopoulos, G., Gamakumara, P. & Hyndman, R.J. (2021), Forecast reconciliation: A geometric view, Int. J. Forecasting 37(1):343-359. doi:10.1016/j.ijforecast.2020.06.004

cards.method: Tidy hierarchical/grouped forecast reconciliation (aggregate_key + MinT/bottom_up) in the long-format forecasting framework
cards.when: you have a long panel (an index + >=1 key/grouping columns + a numeric value) that aggregates naturally into a hierarchy (e.g. region/sector -> national, or CPI sub-indices -> the headline) and you want COHERENT forecasts — the leaves must sum EXACTLY to the aggregates; one base model (ARIMA/ETS/SNAIVE) is fitted per node and reconciled with MinT (min_trace) or bottom_up
cards.when_not: a single univariate series with no hierarchy (-> #85, or a standalone ARIMA); you want an online adaptive combination of experts (-> #207); purely cross-temporal reconciliation of numeric matrices with no keyed table (-> #208); a value with a gap, or an irregular index; structural or causal analysis (VAR/VECM)

alternatives.criterion: you want cross-sectional, temporal or cross-temporal reconciliation of READY base forecasts as numeric matrices, not a keyed-table round trip
ONE series without a hierarchy — you want an ensemble of several models rather than a coherent hierarchy
a single node / no need for coherence — a plain ARIMA/ETS fit + forecast
you want a posterior-weighted combination with full uncertainty quantification rather than a MinT projection

output_key_fields: reconciled: data_frame records (the key columns + index + point + lower_L/upper_L per level) — the COHERENT forecast (chart-data); aggregated nodes are labelled '<aggregated>'
base: the corresponding records of the UNRECONCILED base forecasts (to compare the effect of the reconciliation)
hierarchy: a data_frame of the hierarchy nodes (each row = a key combination; '<aggregated>' = an aggregated level); n_series (leaves+aggregates); n_leaf
method / reconciliation: the selected method (min_trace(<method>) or bottom_up); structure (nested/grouped); base_model
object: the reconciled model table — stubbed by to_mcp, since nothing downstream in the category consumes it
interpretation_traps: coherence != accuracy: reconciliation GUARANTEES that the leaves sum to the aggregates, NOT that every node becomes more accurate — MinT (min_trace) typically improves matters, but bottom_up can worsen the top level if the leaves are noisy

choosing the MinT method: 'wls_struct' (default) = structural scaling, always robust; 'mint_shrink' (Wickramasuriya 2019) = shrinkage towards a diagonal, theoretically optimal but it NEEDS enough residuals — with short/few series it can be unstable; 'ols' ignores scale
'<aggregated>' in the key fields = an aggregated level (is_aggregated), NOT a category literally named '<aggregated>' — do not read it as a leaf

nested (grp1/grp2) vs grouped (grp1*grp2): nested => a genuine hierarchy (a region within a state); grouped => crossed without natural nesting (e.g. purpose x state) — the wrong choice changes which nodes exist

the PI come from the reconciled predictive distribution (hilo) — valid intervals per node, but the joint coherence concerns the points (the means), it does not guarantee joint coverage of the intervals
the value must aggregate meaningfully (a flow/stock): the coherence constraint is the sum of the leaves = the aggregate; ratios/percentages/index levels do NOT add up -> do not use them as the value
sources: Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos & Hyndman 2019 JASA 114(526) (optimal forecast reconciliation through trace minimization)
Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos & Hyndman (2019) Optimal forecast reconciliation for hierarchical and grouped time series through trace minimization, JASA 114(526):804
Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.), ch. 11 Forecasting hierarchical and grouped series (https://otexts.com/fpp3/hierarchical.html)
Hyndman, Ahmed, Athanasopoulos & Shang (2011) Optimal combination forecasts for hierarchical time series, CSDA 55:2579

cards.method: Parametric yield-curve factor models (Nelson-Siegel / Svensson / cubic spline, Diebold-Li dynamics on a panel) + curve transforms (spot/forward/discount/PCA)
cards.when: you have observed yields by maturity (a single cross-sectional curve AS a vector, or a time series of curves AS a time × maturity matrix) and you want (a) to compress them into level/slope/curvature factors (+ the extra Svensson term) with an explicit decay lambda, or (b) Diebold-Li factor dynamics (a Nelson-Siegel fit per date on a panel), or (c) to produce forward rates / discount factors / spot rates on a free maturity grid, or a PCA (Litterman-Scheinkman) of a yield panel
cards.when_not: you have coupon-bond cash-flow micro data (prices+coupons, not ready spot yields) -> #212 ycnp_estimate (nonparametric); you want a no-arbitrage/affine term-premium decomposition (ACM/ABG expectations vs term premium) — this is a descriptive fit ONLY, out of scope; you only want the simple 10y-2y slope spread (a transform, cat. 00); time-series stationarity/cointegration of one tenor (cat. 01/05); fewer pillars than parameters (NS<4, Svensson<6, cubic<3 = underdetermined)

alternatives.criterion: you want a date-indexed factor series ready to feed the recession probit of #83; or Diebold-Li through the established interface of #87
you want a four-factor Svensson fit on a date-indexed panel, with a spot-or-forward rate choice
you have a coupon-bond cash-flow panel (not ready spot yields); you want a nonparametric time-varying discount/yield surface with no parametric shape
you want empirical (data-driven) level/slope/curvature factors as loadings rather than a parametric Nelson-Siegel fit
you want an expectations against term-premium decomposition — outside this card, which is a descriptive fit only

output_key_fields: yc_fit (one curve): factors {level, slope, curvature}; params (the betas, and tau/tau1/tau2); lambda = 1/tau (Nelson-Siegel: one lambda; Svensson: lambda1 and lambda2; the cubic spline: none); fitted (chart-ready yields); residuals; rmse; plus the curve register handle

yc_fit (a panel, Diebold-Li): factors, a matrix [dates × {level,slope,curvature}]; params [dates × params]; lambda [dates × lambda(s)]; fitted [dates × maturities]; rmse per date; object = the panel matrix (the register handle -> pca)

yc_transform spot: maturity/rate on a grid (yc_predict); forward: maturity/forward_rate (instantaneous, or forward-forward with a horizon); discount: maturity/discount_factor (continuous/annual/semi_annual)
yc_transform pca: loadings [tenors × components]; scores [obs × components]; variance_explained; cumulative_variance; sdev; center; tenors
interpretation_traps: lambda = 1/tau is a decay rate (the hump position/loading), NOT a yield — do not use it as a spread; the NS lambda default comes from tau_init=1, but tau is estimated (optim), so the final lambda differs

the cubic spline has no parametric beta or tau, so lambda is blank; its level, slope and curvature are computed empirically from the curve rather than from beta coefficients — do not compare them one-to-one with the Nelson-Siegel betas
a panel + nelson_siegel = Diebold-Li: an INDEPENDENT fit per row (no common lambda/state space) — for joint dynamics run a VAR on the extracted factors (cat. 03)

the PCA default scale=False (on the covariance) is standard in yield-curve PCA; scale=True (on the correlation) changes the loadings — do not confuse them; the sign of the loadings and scores is arbitrary, since they are identified only up to sign

the maturities must be STRICTLY INCREASING and positive; duplicates or unsorted values are accepted silently by the raw routine (gate); an inconsistent unit — months against years — distorts lambda and the fit
a forward without a horizon = the instantaneous forward; with horizon>0 = a forward-forward rate (between maturity and maturity+horizon) — a different quantity, state it explicitly
n_components in the PCA is capped at min(n_obs-1, n_maturities); exceeding it is silently reduced by the raw routine, and the gate blocks that
sources: Nelson & Siegel 1987 J. Business 60(4); Svensson 1994 IMF WP 94/114; Litterman & Scheinkman 1991 J. Fixed Income 1(1) (the level, slope and curvature factors)
Nelson, C. R., & Siegel, A. F. (1987). Parsimonious Modeling of Yield Curves. Journal of Business, 60(4), 473-489
Svensson, L. E. O. (1994). Estimating and Interpreting Forward Interest Rates: Sweden 1992-1994. IMF Working Paper 94/114

yc_fit (the fit of one curve; register field='object' -> it feeds yc_transform as a handle)
c18_yield_curve/nelson_siegel_svensson.fit_nelson_siegel (the date-indexed baseline; compare the factors before changing method)

cards.method: Arbitrage-free affine (Gaussian) term-structure model — JSZ-style single-country JPS estimation with unspanned macro risks (risk-neutral Q + physical P parameters, model-implied yields, term-premia decomposition)
cards.when: you have a panel of bond yields (zero-coupon yields at many maturities) + macro factors (global & domestic) and you want an arbitrage-free affine model (JSZ/JPS): the risk-neutral (Q) + physical (P) dynamics of the risk factors, the model-implied (fitted) yields, and a DECOMPOSITION of the yield into the expected average short rate (the expectations component) + the TERM PREMIUM; unspanned macro risks (Eco_Act/Inflation) are incorporated beyond the spanned yield factors
cards.when_not: you want a simple static yield-curve fit for one date (Nelson-Siegel or Svensson -> #87/#210); you do not have a multi-maturity yield panel; you want multi-country global-VAR or joint-latent models (they need trade-flow weight matrices and a domestic-unit specification — outside this single-country node); you want a bias-corrected or bootstrap ensemble, or out-of-sample yield forecasts (stochastic and heavy, excluded); macro data outside the strict format (the yield row labels 'Y<mat>M_<economy>', the macro labels '<var> <economy>', and dates as column labels 'dd-mm-yyyy')

alternatives.criterion: you want only a static factor fit of the curve (level/slope/curvature) per date, NOT a dynamic arbitrage-free model with term premia
you want only the Q/P parameters + the maximum log-likelihood (faster, without the fit/term premia)
you want a general Gaussian state-space latent-factor model without no-arbitrage affine bond-pricing restrictions

output_key_fields: max_llk: the maximum log-likelihood of the JSZ MLE estimation
Q_params: the risk-neutral (Q) parameters {K1XQ (the Q-feedback eigenvalues), r0 (the short-rate intercept under Q), se (the measurement-error sd), VarYields (the per-maturity error variance)}
P_params: the physical (P) VAR(1) dynamics of the risk factors {K0Z (the drift), K1Z (the feedback), SSZ (the innovation covariance)}
fitted_yields / observed_yields: (time × maturities) model-implied vs observed yields + fit_rmse (chart-data)
term_premia: (time × maturities) the term-premium component per maturity (chart-data)
expected_component: (time × maturities) the expectations-hypothesis component (the average expected future short rate)
maturities / sample_dates / n_obs / pc_var_explained: sample metadata & the PCA variance of the spanned factors; object = the full ATSMModelOutputs
interpretation_traps: the identity yield = expected_component + term_premia: the term premium is the RESIDUAL above the expected future short rates; a negative term premium is valid (e.g. flight to quality)

the input format is STRICT: yield series 'Y<mat>M_<economy>' (e.g. 'Y120M_Brazil'), macro '<var> <economy>', date column labels 'dd-mm-yyyy'; wrong row labels -> the economy gate blocks it; a wrong data_freq -> a silently wrong annualization of dt

n_factors N = the country-specific SPANNED (yield-derived PCA) factors; N must be < the number of maturities; the macro variables (Eco_Act/Inflation) enter separately as UNSPANNED domestic factors (do not confuse them with N)

single country only: 'JPS original' (domestic-only spanned+macro) vs 'JPS global' (it adds global factors to the P dynamics); GVAR/JLL/JPS-multi were excluded (the trade-weight/domestic-unit machinery)
stationary_Q=True enforces a maximum absolute eigenvalue below 1 under Q, giving a stable long-run curve; False can produce explosive Q dynamics — check K1XQ
DETERMINISTIC (BFGS from a JSZ PCA/OLS initialisation, no RNG) -> no seed; the same input => the same max_llk
sources: Joslin, Singleton & Zhu 2011 Review of Financial Studies 24(3) (a new perspective on Gaussian dynamic term structure models)
Joslin, Singleton & Zhu (2011) 'A New Perspective on Gaussian Dynamic Term Structure Models', Review of Financial Studies 24(3):926-970 (the JSZ canonical form)
Joslin, Priebsch & Singleton (2014) 'Risk Premiums in Dynamic Term Structure Models with Unspanned Macro Risks', Journal of Finance 69(3):1197-1233 (JPS)
Candelon & Moura (2024) 'A Multicountry Model of the Term Structures of Interest Rates with a GVAR', Journal of Financial Econometrics 22(5):1558-1587
Le & Singleton (2018) 'A Small Package of Matlab Routines for the Estimation of Some Term Structure Models', EABCN Training School
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the yield and macro panels as matrices; alternatively leave them unset to use the built-in 'CM_2024' sample)
c18_yield_curve/parametric_yield_curve.yc_fit (a static Nelson-Siegel fit per date — a simpler alternative when you do not need a dynamic arbitrage-free model)
atsm_estimate (the term-premia decomposition is returned inside it: term_premia + expected_component)

cards.method: Nonparametric time-varying yield curve / discount function estimation from coupon-bond cash-flow data (the Koo-La Vecchia-Linton kernel estimator)
cards.when: you have coupon-bond cross-section+time-series micro data (a cash-flow panel: qdate, id, price, tupq=the time to the cash flow in days, pdint=the cash-flow amount) and you want to ESTIMATE non-parametrically the discount function d(tau,t) and the implied yield curve y(tau,t) that EVOLVE over time — without imposing a parametric shape (Nelson-Siegel/Svensson); appropriate for sparse/irregular coupon schedules
cards.when_not: you already have a matrix of spot yields by maturity (zero-coupon rates) — then #87 fit_nelson_siegel/fit_svensson (parametric factor fitting); you want level/slope/curvature factors for macro/probit work — #87; you want an affine term-structure/no-arbitrage model; you do not have cash-flow-level data (only aggregate yields); very few bonds/dates (the kernel estimator needs density around each x)

alternatives.criterion: you already have spot yields by maturity and you want a parametric 3-factor (level/slope/curvature) fit rather than nonparametric cash-flow estimation
a parametric 4-factor (Svensson/Diebold-Li) fit on a ready spot curve

output_key_fields: estimates: records {date, tau, discount, yield} — the estimated discount function + yield curve per (time, maturity) (chart-data)
yield_matrix: a numeric matrix [tau × date] — the yield surface (rows=maturities, cols=dates)
discount_matrix: a numeric matrix [tau × date] — the discount surface
x: the estimation time points (dates); tau: the maturities that were used; span_x; smooth
n_obs (the cash-flow rows), n_bonds (unique ids), n_dates, n_tau; plus the fitted nested estimate table
interpretation_traps: tupq is the time to EACH cash flow in DAYS (not years); pdint is the AMOUNT of the flow (a coupon, or a coupon+face value at maturity) — one row per (bond, cash flow), not per bond

x must lie INSIDE the range of qdate and have enough data around it (the kernel window ~ span_x): an x in a sparse region or at the edges -> non-finite/unstable estimates (the wrapper hard-gates non-finite values)
leaving tau unset lets the routine choose ITS OWN dense maturity grid (the percentiles of the observed maturities) rather than fixed pillars; supply an explicit tau for controlled maturities
span_x is measured in the number of regular intervals between consecutive qdate values (e.g. trading days): a small span_x -> noise/overfitting, a large one -> over-smoothing over time
smooth=True applies a loess over tau; with few tau values it produces 'span too small' warnings — the default False returns the raw estimator points, which are deterministic
yield = -log(discount)/tau (a transformation of the discount factor); it is a continuously compounded spot yield per maturity, NOT a par/coupon yield
sources: Koo, B., La Vecchia, D., & Linton, O. (2021). Estimation of a nonparametric model for bond prices from cross-section and time series information. Journal of Econometrics, 220(2), 562-588
Nelson, C. R., & Siegel, A. F. (1987). Parsimonious Modeling of Yield Curves. Journal of Business, 60(4), 473-489 (the DGP for ycevo_data)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the bond cash-flow panel; the columns qdate/id/price/tupq/pdint)
ycnp_estimate (the estimation returns the estimates + the yield/discount surface matrices inside it)

cards.method: Change-point detection in mean / variance / mean+variance (PELT/BinSeg/SegNeigh/AMOC)
cards.when: a univariate series; locating the POSITIONS of structural changes in the mean, the variance, or both (meanvar) with penalized exact/approximate segmentation; any frequency (not only quarterly)
cards.when_not: you want NBER-style expansion and recession phase dating (-> #88); probabilistic regimes (-> #30); breaks in regression coefficients with dates (-> #3); a continuous cyclical gap (the filters)

alternatives.criterion: you want cycle dating (peaks/troughs/phases) on a QUARTERLY series, not the positions of a structural break in the mean/variance
breaks in regression COEFFICIENTS (structural stability), not in the level's mean/variance
you want regime probabilities + endogenous transitions rather than deterministic break positions
mean: a level change; variance: a change in volatility (volatility regimes); meanvar: a simultaneous change in level & volatility

alternatives.alt: method PELT vs BinSeg vs SegNeigh vs AMOC
alternatives.criterion: PELT: exact, linear cost, an unknown number of breaks (default); BinSeg: approximate and fast up to Q; SegNeigh: exact but slow up to Q; AMOC: at most ONE break

output_key_fields: changepoints: 1-based SEGMENT-END INDICES (NOT the final n, NOT dates)
n_changepoints/n_segments: the number of breaks and of segments (=breaks+1)
segments: a frame of segment/start/end/length plus the per-segment parameter columns (mean, variance, scale, rate or lambda, depending on the test statistic)
segment_params/global_params: per-segment vs global (e.g. the Gamma shape, the assumed mean for a variance model) parameter estimates
penalty/method/test_stat/minseglen/Q/pen_value_used: the rules that produced the segmentation (an audit trail)
fit: the raw change-point fit (a stub once serialised; a register field for the changepoint_segments accessor node)
interpretation_traps: changepoints are SEGMENT-END INDICES (the last observation of a segment), 1-based; they do NOT include the final n; they are not dates

the parameter-estimate field names CHANGE with the test statistic: mean and variance for the normal; scale and shape for the gamma; rate for the exponential; lambda for the Poisson — do not always assume mean and variance
for a variance change point the mean is handled separately (estimated by ML, or supplied through know_mean/mu); it is a GLOBAL parameter, the assumed mean, not a per-segment one

the placement is STABLE even in the degenerate nseg==1 case (no change): the assumed common mean (variance/know_mean) and the Gamma 'shape' are ALWAYS in global_params, NEVER in segment_params/segments; per segment: mean(mean/meanvar)/variance/scale/rate/lambda
penalty='Manual' requires pen_value>0 (0 => no penalty => over-segmentation); 'None' segments at every point; 'Asymptotic' needs pen_value ∈ (0,1]

cards.method: Bayesian change point (the Barry-Hartigan Product-Partition Model, MCMC)
cards.when: a univariate sequential series; Bayesian detection of change points in the MEAN with a posterior probability of change at EVERY position (the Barry-Hartigan PPM, MCMC); you want soft/posterior probabilities & Bayesian model averaging rather than deterministic dates or a MAP segmentation
cards.when_not: you want NBER-style peaks and troughs with dated expansion and recession phases (-> #88); a change in variance or in the whole distribution, or multivariate data (-> #215/#213); a regression, panel or graph change point (scoped out); a length below 4 (a segfault gate)

alternatives.criterion: you want NBER-style peaks/troughs & dated phases (deterministic dates) rather than a posterior probability of a change in the mean
you want an exact MAP segmentation with a penalty (mean/var/meanvar), not Bayesian posterior averaging
a non-parametric change in the WHOLE distribution (not only the mean), multivariate
probabilistic regimes with endogenous transition probabilities rather than a partition/change point

output_key_fields: posterior_prob: an array of length n, the posterior probability of a change AT each position; the LAST element is blank, since the last position cannot host a change, and it serialises to null
posterior_mean: the smoothed posterior level per position (model-averaged, NOT constant within a block)
posterior_var: the posterior variance per position (finiteness/non-negativity gated; roundoff negatives ~-1e-14 → 0; genuine negatives < -1e-8 → a hard stop)
changepoint_index: the 1-based positions where posterior_prob exceeds the threshold (the final blank is excluded automatically)
changepoint_prob: the posterior probabilities at the detected positions; n_changepoints: the count
posterior_expected_blocks: the POST-BURN-IN mean(blocks[(burnin+1):(burnin+mcmc)]) — the expected number of segments (consistent with the other post-burn-in summaries; NOT the all-iteration mean)
threshold/p0/w0/burnin/mcmc/seed: the audit trail of the rules/parameters
bcp_fit: the raw fit (a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: the LAST posterior_prob is blank by construction — the last position cannot host a change, because there is no following block; do not read it as 0
a change AT position i ⇒ a block boundary AFTER i (the new segment starts at i+1); it is a position index, NOT a date
posterior_mean is NOT constant within a segment (it is a Bayesian average over partitions); no single 'best' partition is returned — that is deliberate (Barry-Hartigan)
STOCHASTIC (MCMC): the seed is mandatory for reproducibility; the same seed ⇒ an identical result, without reseeding two calls differ
the sampler accepts gaps and infinities SILENTLY and produces garbage (live-verified) -> a hard gate here
length(y) < 4 causes a SEGFAULT in the C core rcpp_bcpM (live-verified: n=2,3 crash) → a hard gate (>= 4)
p0 = the prior probability of a change (larger ⇒ more changes); w0 = the signal-to-noise prior; the detection depends on p0/w0 + the threshold — it is not unique
the p0 domain is (0,1] (a hard gate): p0=0 is REJECTED as a degenerate prior that structurally forbids any change (it would silently return zero change points for ANY series)
the regression, multivariate and graph cases are scoped out — this is a univariate mean change only

Erdman & Emerson 2007, Journal of Statistical Software 23(3)
Wang & Emerson 2015 'Bayesian change point analysis of linear models on graphs' (the bcp >= 4.0 methods)

cards.method: Energy-statistics nonparametric multivariate change-point detection (E-divisive / E-agglomerative)
cards.when: a multivariate (n×d) series; detecting MULTIPLE change points in the distribution (mean/variance/higher moments) without a parametric assumption, based on the energy distance; divisive = permutation-test significance, agglo = penalized bottom-up merging
cards.when_not: univariate turning-point dating of peaks and troughs (-> #88); you want probabilistic regimes (-> #30); you want a cyclical gap (the filters, category 10); you want a structural break in regression coefficients (-> #3); a very small n, below twice min_size

alternatives.criterion: you want a data-driven number of change points with formal permutation-test significance (p-values per split); stochastic → seeded; the default choice
you have an initial segmentation (member) or you want a deterministic bottom-up procedure with a penalized goodness of fit; no permutation test; faster with initial groups
univariate quarterly data; you want peaks/troughs & expansion/recession phases (turning points), not distributional change points
you want regime probabilities + endogenous transitions rather than discrete change points; gaussian/lm only
a break in the coefficients of a linear model/regression, not in the distribution of the data

output_key_fields: changepoints: the interior change points (sorted; position p = a change BEFORE observation p, 2<=p<=n); WITHOUT the boundaries 1 & n+1

n_changepoints / n_segments: the number of changes and of segments (divisive: n_segments==k_hat, n_changepoints==k_hat-1); agglo: n_segments == n_changepoints+1 (CONTIGUOUS temporal segments, NOT length(unique(cluster)) — the cyclic clustering reuses labels)
cluster: an integer vector assigning a segment to each observation (of length n)
estimates_raw: the raw estimate vector WITH the boundaries (an audit trail)

p_values (the divisive route): one p-value per split, in the order the splits were found; the LAST is the terminating, non-significant split; n_significant counts those with p<=sig_lvl, boundary-inclusive, matching the stopping rule; WHEN a fixed k is supplied the p-values are all blank and n_significant is blank too, since no permutation runs

significance_tested (the divisive route): True only when k is left unset and a permutation test actually ran; False when a fixed k is supplied, in which case the permutation count is forced to zero internally and the p-values are placeholders, NOT evidence
gof_progression/gof_final (agglo): the penalized goodness of fit per merging step
alpha/sig_lvl/permutations/min_size/k/penalty: the rules that produced the result (an audit trail)
seed (divisive): the seed that was used (reproducibility)
interpretation_traps: the raw estimates INCLUDE the boundaries 1 and n+1 on the divisive route, and a cyclic wrap on the agglomerative one — those are NOT change points; the wrapper removes them, so report ONLY the changepoints field
the divisive route is STOCHASTIC (it permutes); WITHOUT a seed the p-values, and the borderline splits, change from call to call — the wrapper seeds the generator internally (default 20240101)
silently wrong: a gap or an infinity in X makes the routine return NO change point rather than an error; the wrapper fences it
silently wrong: twice min_size above the number of rows silently yields no change point; the wrapper requires at least twice min_size rows
silently wrong: the reference=0 (or non-positive) → it RUNS but the p-values are meaningless; the wrapper requires a positive integer the reference

the p-values are NOT aligned with the sorted change points; they follow the order the splits were found, with one extra terminating, non-significant split — use n_significant for the count that matters

silently wrong: the divisive route with a fixed k forces the permutation count to zero, so the placeholder p-values are all 0; do NOT read them as significance (significance_tested=False, and both p_values and n_significant are blank); only the data-driven route, with k unset, gives tested significance

silently wrong: the agglo clustering is CYCLIC → length(unique(cluster)) counts distinct distributions, NOT contiguous regimes (e.g. a symmetric mean 0→5→0 gives 2 clusters but 3 segments); use n_segments (=changepoints+1)
alpha is the moment index of the energy distance, in (0,2] with a default of 1 — NOT a significance level; do not confuse it with sig_lvl
the agglomerative route with penalty='none' can over-segment noisy data; 'num_cp' penalizes the count; the dating is NOT unique, since it depends on alpha, the membership and the penalty
sources: Matteson & James 2014 JASA 109(505):334-345 (a nonparametric approach for multiple change point analysis of multivariate data)
James & Matteson 2014 JSS 62(7):1-25 (nonparametric multiple change point analysis of multivariate data — the divisive and agglomerative algorithms)
Székely G.J., Rizzo M.L. (2005) 'Hierarchical clustering via joint between-within distances' J. Classification 22 151-183 [the energy distance basis]

cards.method: Regularized regression: Lasso / Ridge / Elastic-Net (+ a k-fold CV path)
cards.when: many predictors p, or p much larger than n; you want shrinkage plus variable selection through a penalized regression; alpha=1 is the lasso (sparse), alpha=0 the ridge, and 0<alpha<1 the elastic net; enet_cv selects lambda (lambda_min minimises the CV error, lambda_1se is the parsimonious choice). Families: gaussian, binomial, poisson, multinomial
cards.when_not: a low dimension where you want inference and p-values (OLS or GLM); group-structured selection (-> #220); nonlinear or tree-based ML (-> #217/#218); Bayesian model averaging (-> #219); quantile or tail work (-> #64); you need unbiased coefficients (the shrinkage introduces bias — a feature, not a bug)

alternatives.criterion: you want a SPARSE model — variable selection; unstable with strongly correlated predictors (it picks one arbitrarily)
correlated predictors; you want to shrink everything (nothing is EXACTLY zero); better under multicollinearity
grouped selection under correlation — a compromise between Lasso and Ridge (Zou-Hastie)
the predictors have a KNOWN group structure (dummies, splines) — selecting whole groups
you want non-linearity/interactions (RF / boosting) rather than a linear penalized model
lambda_min gives the best prediction; lambda_1se is parsimonious and interpretable (the one-standard-error rule)

output_key_fields: path (enet_fit): a frame of step/lambda/df/dev_ratio — the regularization path
dev_ratio (enet_fit): the share of deviance explained at each lambda (rising as lambda falls, within [0,1))
cv_curve (enet_cv): a frame of lambda/cvm/cvsd/cvup/cvlo/nzero — the cross-validation curve
lambda_min / lambda_1se (enet_cv): the selected lambdas (1se is never below min)
selected_min / selected_1se (enet_cv): the NON-ZERO coefficients (class/term/coefficient)
nzero_min / nzero_1se, and dev_ratio_min / dev_ratio_1se (enet_cv): the model size and the fit at each of the two lambdas
selected (enet_coefficients): the non-zero coefficients at a given lambda; plus n_nonzero
predictions (enet_predict): a frame of row_id + prediction, or the per-class probabilities and predicted_class
model / cv: the raw fits (to_mcp -> a stub; registry chaining)
interpretation_traps: shrinkage means BIASED coefficients, pulled towards 0; do NOT read them as unbiased least-squares effects — penalized coefficients carry no valid p-value or interval
lambda_min against lambda_1se: lambda_1se is ALWAYS at least lambda_min, so it keeps fewer variables; the one-standard-error rule is more parsimonious, not 'a better prediction'
the cross-validation is STOCHASTIC through the fold split — without a fixed seed or an explicit fold assignment you get a DIFFERENT lambda every time; the wrapper seeds it (default 42)
the Lasso with correlated predictors picks ONE arbitrarily => the 'selection' is not stable; use Ridge/Elastic-Net for groups
standardize=True (the default) standardizes INTERNALLY but returns the coefficients on the original scale — compare magnitudes ONLY on a standardized scale
df = the number of non-zero coefficients (EXCLUDING the intercept); nzero from cv is the same; the intercept is not penalized
binomial: 2 classes (otherwise multinomial); multinomial: >=3; predict type=response = probabilities (the rows sum to 1 in the multinomial case), type=class = a label

the variable-selection count = nrow(selected_min)/nrow(selected_1se)/n_nonzero EXCLUDES the (Intercept) and equals nzero_min/nzero_1se — do NOT add 1 for the intercept; coef_min/coef_1se/coefficients do keep the intercept

multinomial prediction: the number of new rows always equals the number of prediction rows; for ONE new period the k values are the class probabilities of that ONE observation, laid out as columns, NOT k separate observations
sources: Friedman, Hastie & Tibshirani 2010 JSS 33(1) (regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent)
Tibshirani 1996 JRSS-B 58(1) 267-288 (the Lasso); Hoerl-Kennard 1970 Technometrics (Ridge); Zou-Hastie 2005 JRSS-B 67(2) 301-320 (the Elastic-Net)

Pitfalls: shrinkage means BIASED coefficients, pulled towards 0; do NOT read them as unbiased least-squares effects — penalized coefficients carry no valid p-value or interval · lambda_min against lambda_1se: lambda_1se is ALWAYS at least lambda_min, so it keeps fewer variables; the one-standard-error rule is more parsimonious, not 'a better prediction' · the cross-validation is STOCHASTIC through the fold split — without a fixed seed or an explicit fold assignment you get a DIFFERENT lambda every time; the wrapper seeds it (default 42) · the Lasso with correlated predictors picks ONE arbitrarily => the 'selection' is not stable; use Ridge/Elastic-Net for groups · standardize=True (the default) standardizes INTERNALLY but returns the coefficients on the original scale — compare magnitudes ONLY on a standardized scale · df = the number of non-zero coefficients (EXCLUDING the intercept); nzero from cv is the same; the intercept is not penalized · binomial: 2 classes (otherwise multinomial); multinomial: >=3; predict type=response = probabilities (the rows sum to 1 in the multinomial case), type=class = a label · the variable-selection count = nrow(selected_min)/nrow(selected_1se)/n_nonzero EXCLUDES the (Intercept) and equals nzero_min/nzero_1se — do NOT add 1 for the intercept; coef_min/coef_1se/coefficients do keep the intercept · multinomial prediction: the number of new rows always equals the number of prediction rows; for ONE new period the k values are the class probabilities of that ONE observation, laid out as columns, NOT k separate observations
Sources: Friedman, Hastie & Tibshirani 2010 JSS 33(1) (regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent) · Tibshirani 1996 JRSS-B 58(1) 267-288 (the Lasso); Hoerl-Kennard 1970 Technometrics (Ridge); Zou-Hastie 2005 JRSS-B 67(2) 301-320 (the Elastic-Net) · wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c20_highdim_shrinkage_ml/regularized_regression_lasso)

cards.method: Random forests: OOB error, variable importance, quantile regression forests
cards.when: a non-parametric, non-linear predictive baseline on a macro/financial cross-section or a pooled panel (a design matrix X + a response y); you want an OOB error estimate without a separate validation set, variable importance (non-linear importance/interactions), or the WHOLE conditional distribution through quantile regression forests (prediction intervals / tails); a regression, classification or probability forest
cards.when_not: you want interpretable coefficients or sparse variable selection -> #216/#220; linear relations with few variables (a forest is excessive and loses efficiency); a temporal structure or autocorrelation that must be modelled explicitly (a forest ignores the order — build lagged features); a conditional tail of a linear outcome with interpretable standard errors -> #64; extrapolation outside the training support (a forest does not extrapolate)

alternatives.criterion: you want sparse, interpretable linear coefficients + a regularization path/CV rather than black-box importance; a linear structure
you want custom losses (quantile/Huber) + automatic variable selection with additive interpretability
you want CAUSAL effects (CATE/heterogeneous treatment) with valid inference, not pure prediction
a linear conditional-quantile relation with interpretable coefficients + analytic SE rather than a forest-based distribution

output_key_fields: oob_prediction_error: the out-of-bag error — MSE (regression), the misclassification rate in [0,1] (classification), the Brier score (probability); NOT in-sample
variable_importance / importance_table: the named importance per variable (sorted in decreasing order); empty when importance='none'
r_squared: the out-of-bag R² for regression; blank for a classification or probability forest
treetype: 'Regression' / 'Classification' / 'Probability estimation' (it states which forest was trained)
num_trees/mtry/min_node_size: the ACTUAL values used (the built-in defaults for mtry and min_node_size when they are left unset)
is_quantile/is_classification/is_probability/classes: the mode flags and the class levels; seed: for reproducibility
model: the raw forest (registered as a raw handle for rf_predict; a stub once serialised)
rf_predict predictions: a numeric vector (regression), character labels (classification), a probability matrix (probability), a q<value> matrix (quantiles); se/se_table (type='se')
interpretation_traps: DETERMINISM: the forest is NON-reproducible with more than one thread EVEN with a fixed seed, because each thread carries its own generator stream; the wrapper PINS the thread count to 1 and does not expose it — do not bypass that

type='se' (the jackknife-after-bootstrap of Wager, Hastie & Efron) draws at random, so it was NON-deterministic; the wrapper seeds the generator BEFORE predicting. The infinitesimal-jackknife standard error can also be blank at a few points when the tree count is small — that is real, not an error

importance='impurity' is biased towards high-cardinality/continuous variables (Strobl 2007); for a reliable comparison use 'permutation' or 'impurity_corrected' (Nembrini 2018); the importance is NOT a causal effect and carries no sign/direction

type='quantiles' requires a forest trained in quantile mode (Meinshausen); the wrapper fences it by checking that the node values were retained; the quantiles are not theoretically guaranteed monotone, though crossing is rare in forests
the OOB error is NOT a test error under temporal/spatial dependence (the OOB samples leak information from neighbours); for time series use out-of-time validation, not OOB
an RF does NOT extrapolate: predictions at X outside the training support are pinned to the extremes of the training values (do not use it for out-of-sample scenarios)
the classification and probability modes convert a numeric y into a categorical; the classes are the codes as strings; quantile mode is incompatible with either (a hard stop)

rf_predict NAME-MATCH gate: newdata must have column labels matching (as a set) the training variables; an unnamed/wrongly named newdata → blocked-by-gate (NOT a silent positional match); the column order does NOT matter (matching is by NAME)
rf_predict accepts a newdata of ONE row (n_pred=1, a single out-of-sample/GaR point); the >=2-row rule applies ONLY at training; the quantiles must be DISTINCT (otherwise blocked-by-gate)

type='se' (infinitesimal or plain jackknife) is SEED-INDEPENDENT, being deterministic given the in-bag counts; the seed argument acts ONLY on the rf_fit bootstrap; the thread count is pinned to 1 for determinism
sources: Wright & Ziegler 2017 JSS 77(1):1-17 (a fast implementation of random forests for high-dimensional data)
Wager S., Hastie T., Efron B. (2014) 'Confidence Intervals for Random Forests: The Jackknife and the Infinitesimal Jackknife' JMLR 15 1625-1651 [type='se' infjack/jack]
Nembrini S., Koenig I., Wright M.N. (2018) 'The revival of the Gini importance?' Bioinformatics 34(21) 3711-3718 [impurity_corrected]
Strobl C. et al. (2007) 'Bias in random forest variable importance measures' BMC Bioinformatics 8:25 [permutation vs impurity bias]

cards.method: Component-wise gradient boosting — high-dimensional shrinkage + automatic variable selection with custom losses
cards.when: high-dimensional (p~n or p>n) macro/financial predictors X; you want shrinkage AND sparse variable selection SIMULTANEOUSLY (unselected variables get a coefficient of EXACTLY 0) with a selectable loss (L2 Gaussian; pinball QuantReg; L1 Laplace; robust Huber; logistic Binomial; count Poisson); mstop (the regularization) is chosen data-driven with a cross-validated risk (boost_glm_cv)
cards.when_not: you want non-linear or smooth effects (the spline base-learners are NOT exposed; see the footer); purely non-linear prediction with importance -> #217; heterogeneous CATE -> #44; debiased inference on ONE target coefficient -> #45; a linear Growth-at-Risk over several tau -> #64; a sparse VAR or lag-multivariate model -> #142/#145

alternatives.criterion: you want non-linear interactions + permutation importance rather than a linear sparse model; no strict sparsity
you want heterogeneous treatment effects (CATE), not predictor selection in a regression
you want an unbiased SE on ONE specific coefficient with ML nuisance controls, not a selection path
you want full multi-tau conditional-quantile inference (se/p-values) without boosting selection
you want an L1/elastic-net path with lambda (a convex penalty) rather than functional-gradient descent with mstop
you want non-linear P-spline effects — outside the surface, since the spline base-learners cannot be resolved without polluting the shared symbol table

output_key_fields: coefficients: a frame of term/coefficient/selected — COMPLETE, covering all p predictors with 0 for the unselected ones; on the centered scale when center=True
offset: the intercept level (with the centered scale the mean moves here; NOT 0)
selection_freq: term/n_selected/frequency — how often each predictor was updated along the boosting path (the sum of n_selected == mstop)
n_selected_vars / selected_vars: the number & names of the non-zero predictors (the sparsity)
path_risk / final_risk (boost_glm_fit): the empirical in-bag risk per step (chart-ready; monotonically decreasing)
optimal_mstop / optimal_mean_risk (boost_glm_cv): the data-driven mstop = the argmin of the cross-validated risk
cv_curve (boost_glm_cv): a data_frame mstop/mean_risk/se_risk — the CV curve (chart-ready)
family/tau/nu/mstop/center/n/p/cv_type/cv_B/seed: the rules that produced the result (an audit trail)
model: the raw glmboost fit — a register handle for downstream chaining; to_mcp -> a stub
interpretation_traps: the binomial coefficients are HALF the size of the corresponding GLM coefficients (the fitter emits a note about it); do NOT compare them directly with a logistic regression — multiply by 2 for the GLM scale
mstop IS the regularization knob: too large -> overfitting, too small -> underfitting; for an honest choice use boost_glm_cv (cross-validated), NOT an arbitrary fixed mstop
selection_freq counts the UPDATE FREQUENCY (its sum == mstop), NOT the effect size; a predictor with a large |coefficient| may have been selected few times and vice versa
center=True emits the benign warning 'model does not contain intercept' — the offset IS the intercept, and the fold-into-intercept switch is ignored; read the offset field rather than 0

the cross-validated risk is STOCHASTIC in how it draws the folds, so the generator is seeded internally (default 42) and the evaluation stays single-threaded; forking would break reproducibility. The boosting fit itself is deterministic
Binomial requires a binary y (a 2-level factor; the wrapper converts a numeric 2-value y); Poisson requires non-negative INTEGERS (counts) — hard gates
the QuantReg tau is the quantile in (0,1) of the pinball loss (default 0.5=the median); it is NOT a significance level

quantile calibration: the constant conditional-quantile LEVEL is the offset plus the intercept; the offset is ALWAYS the median of y and does NOT depend on tau — the tau dependence lives in the intercept, which is a movable base learner through the formula interface; take the calibrated fitted quantile from the model handle, and note that it needs a large enough mstop for P(y<=fitted) to approach tau

Binomial: the coefficients are HALF the GLM ones (the fitter models f = 0.5 * logit) — multiply by 2 for the logistic scale before interpreting them or forming odds ratios; the positive class is reported in positive_class, the second category level; see coef_scale
sources: Bühlmann P., Hothorn T. (2007) 'Boosting Algorithms: Regularization, Prediction and Model Fitting' Statistical Science 22(4) 477-505 [component-wise functional gradient descent]
Hofner, Mayr, Robinzonov & Schmid 2014 Computational Statistics 29:3-35 (a hands-on tutorial on model-based boosting)
Hothorn et al. 2010 JMLR 11:2109-2113 (model-based boosting 2.0 — the architecture, the cross-validated risk and the family objects)

cards.method: Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA, g-priors: enumeration + MCMC)
cards.when: model uncertainty in a LINEAR regression with many candidate regressors (a small to moderate K); you want Posterior Inclusion Probabilities (which regressors matter), model-averaged coefficients & sign certainty without choosing ONE model (growth/determinants regressions, Sala-i-Martin BACE style)
cards.when_not: a very large K, above roughly 30-40, with a sparsity objective -> penalized shrinkage (#216/#220); pure prediction with no inference -> the ML nodes (#217/#218); a time series with lags or stochastic volatility -> Bayesian VAR shrinkage (#12/#143, categories 03 and 14); non-linear interactions -> a random forest or BART

alternatives.criterion: K<=20 → an EXACT enumeration of all 2^K models (deterministic, exact PMP); prefer it whenever feasible

alternatives.alt: the birth-death or reversible-jump MCMC samplers
alternatives.criterion: K>20 → model sampling; CHECK corr_pmp>=~0.9 (convergence) & the seed for reproducibility

alternatives.alt: g=UIP vs BRIC/RIC/HQ or a custom number
alternatives.criterion: UIP (g=N) is a balanced default; BRIC/RIC (g=max(N,K^2)/K^2) are more conservative (a larger penalty); run a sensitivity check — the PIP depend on g (the Bartlett/Lindley paradox)
robustness with respect to the prior model size rather than a fixed inclusion probability of 0.5 (uniform)

alternatives.alt: penalized shrinkage (#216/#220, category 20), or spike-and-slab / SSVS in the Bayesian VAR nodes
alternatives.criterion: a very large K + sparsity (a point estimate); or a time-series/VAR context

output_key_fields: pip: the named PIP per regressor ∈[0,1] — the posterior probability that the regressor belongs in the model
coefficients: a data_frame term/idx/pip/post_mean/post_sd/cond_pos_sign/post_sign_prob (model-averaged, UNCONDITIONAL)
post_sign_prob: the sign certainty = P(the coefficient has the sign of post_mean) — the robustness of the sign
top_models: the PMP (exact vs mcmc) + the inclusion binary matrix + pmp_exact_share (the probability normalized within the retained set)
best_model: the highest-PMP model (included_terms, n_regressors, pmp_exact_share)
corr_pmp / corr_pmp_ok: the MCMC convergence diagnostic, the correlation between the analytical and frequency posterior model probabilities; blank under full enumeration
n_models_visited / modelspace(2^K) / pct_topmodels: the number of draws, the size of the space, the % of posterior mass in the top models
mean_n_regressors (=the sum of the PIP, the posterior E[#regressors]), shrinkage_av, K, N
bma: the raw fit (a stub once serialised; a register handle for chaining into bma_coefficients)
interpretation_traps: a PIP is not a p-value: under a uniform prior the prior-neutral point is 0.5; PIP>0.5 = 'supported'; the scale depends on mprior

post_mean and post_sd are UNCONDITIONAL, averaged over ALL models including those that exclude the regressor -> a low inclusion probability means a post_mean shrunk towards 0; it is NOT the conditional effect (read the conditional coefficient for that)
pmp_exact and pmp_mcmc are RAW marginal-likelihood weights — they do NOT sum to 1 over the retained set; the probability reading is pmp_exact_share
g-prior SENSITIVITY: a large g → less shrinkage but a stronger 'null penalty' (g→∞ ⇒ PIP→0, the Bartlett-Lindley paradox); UIP/BRIC/RIC give different PIP → a sensitivity check is mandatory
enumerate = exact PMP, deterministic (no seed); MCMC = CHECK corr_pmp>=~0.9 BEFORE trusting the PIP (a low value ⇒ a non-converged sampler, raise iter/burn; the corr_pmp_ok flag)
a gap or an infinity in the design -> a HARD STOP: the sampler silently drops those rows with only a warning, giving a silently wrong sample
the 1st column of X.data is the dependent variable y (NOT a regressor); the wrong column order ⇒ the wrong model

the birth-death and reversible-jump samplers are stochastic and NOT bit-reproducible even with a fixed seed — do not rely on run-to-run identity, nor on a cache hit being identical to a recompute; for an EXACTLY deterministic result enumerate the model space when K<=20 (see the deterministic and reproducibility fields)

pmp_exact & pmp_mcmc are NORMALIZED posterior model probabilities in [0,1] that sum to 1; under enumerate they coincide (analytical), under MCMC they differ (analytical vs sampling frequency); their correlation = corr_pmp (the convergence diagnostic)
sources: Zeugner & Feldkircher 2015 JSS 68(4) (Bayesian model averaging with fixed and flexible priors)
Fernández, Ley & Steel 2001 'Benchmark priors for Bayesian model averaging' J. Econometrics 100(2) 381-427 (the g-priors UIP/BRIC/RIC/HQ)
Sala-i-Martin, Doppelhofer & Miller 2004 'Determinants of Long-Term Growth: A BACE Approach' AER 94(4) 813-835
Ley & Steel 2009 'On the effect of prior assumptions in BMA' J. Applied Econometrics 24(4) 651-674 (the random model prior)

NOT when: a very large K, above roughly 30-40, with a sparsity objective -> penalized shrinkage (#216/#220); pure prediction with no inference -> the ML nodes (#217/#218); a time series with lags or stochastic volatility -> Bayesian VAR shrinkage (#12/#143, categories 03 and 14); non-linear interactions -> a random forest or BART
Alternatives: mcmc=enumerate (K<=20 → an EXACT enumeration of all 2^K models (deterministic, exact PMP); prefer it whenever feasible) · the birth-death or reversible-jump MCMC samplers (K>20 → model sampling; CHECK corr_pmp>=~0.9 (convergence) & the seed for reproducibility) · g=UIP vs BRIC/RIC/HQ or a custom number (UIP (g=N) is a balanced default; BRIC/RIC (g=max(N,K^2)/K^2) are more conservative (a larger penalty); run a sensitivity check — the PIP depend on g (the Bartlett/Lindley paradox)) · mprior=random (the Ley-Steel beta-binomial prior) (robustness with respect to the prior model size rather than a fixed inclusion probability of 0.5 (uniform)) · penalized shrinkage (#216/#220, category 20), or spike-and-slab / SSVS in the Bayesian VAR nodes (a very large K + sparsity (a point estimate); or a time-series/VAR context)
Output: pip: the named PIP per regressor ∈[0,1] — the posterior probability that the regressor belongs in the model · coefficients: a data_frame term/idx/pip/post_mean/post_sd/cond_pos_sign/post_sign_prob (model-averaged, UNCONDITIONAL) · post_sign_prob: the sign certainty = P(the coefficient has the sign of post_mean) — the robustness of the sign · top_models: the PMP (exact vs mcmc) + the inclusion binary matrix + pmp_exact_share (the probability normalized within the retained set) · best_model: the highest-PMP model (included_terms, n_regressors, pmp_exact_share) · corr_pmp / corr_pmp_ok: the MCMC convergence diagnostic, the correlation between the analytical and frequency posterior model probabilities; blank under full enumeration · n_models_visited / modelspace(2^K) / pct_topmodels: the number of draws, the size of the space, the % of posterior mass in the top models · mean_n_regressors (=the sum of the PIP, the posterior E[#regressors]), shrinkage_av, K, N · bma: the raw fit (a stub once serialised; a register handle for chaining into bma_coefficients)
Pitfalls: a PIP is not a p-value: under a uniform prior the prior-neutral point is 0.5; PIP>0.5 = 'supported'; the scale depends on mprior · post_mean and post_sd are UNCONDITIONAL, averaged over ALL models including those that exclude the regressor -> a low inclusion probability means a post_mean shrunk towards 0; it is NOT the conditional effect (read the conditional coefficient for that) · pmp_exact and pmp_mcmc are RAW marginal-likelihood weights — they do NOT sum to 1 over the retained set; the probability reading is pmp_exact_share · g-prior SENSITIVITY: a large g → less shrinkage but a stronger 'null penalty' (g→∞ ⇒ PIP→0, the Bartlett-Lindley paradox); UIP/BRIC/RIC give different PIP → a sensitivity check is mandatory · enumerate = exact PMP, deterministic (no seed); MCMC = CHECK corr_pmp>=~0.9 BEFORE trusting the PIP (a low value ⇒ a non-converged sampler, raise iter/burn; the corr_pmp_ok flag) · a gap or an infinity in the design -> a HARD STOP: the sampler silently drops those rows with only a warning, giving a silently wrong sample · the 1st column of X.data is the dependent variable y (NOT a regressor); the wrong column order ⇒ the wrong model · the birth-death and reversible-jump samplers are stochastic and NOT bit-reproducible even with a fixed seed — do not rely on run-to-run identity, nor on a cache hit being identical to a recompute; for an EXACTLY deterministic result enumerate the model space when K<=20 (see the deterministic and reproducibility fields) · pmp_exact & pmp_mcmc are NORMALIZED posterior model probabilities in [0,1] that sum to 1; under enumerate they coincide (analytical), under MCMC they differ (analytical vs sampling frequency); their correlation = corr_pmp (the convergence diagnostic)

Econometrics 100(2) 381-427 (the g-priors UIP/BRIC/RIC/HQ) · Sala-i-Martin, Doppelhofer & Miller 2004 'Determinants of Long-Term Growth: A BACE Approach' AER 94(4) 813-835 · Ley & Steel 2009 'On the effect of prior assumptions in BMA' J. Applied Econometrics 24(4) 651-674 (the random model prior) · wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c20_highdim_shrinkage_ml/bayesian_averaging)

cards.method: Grouped / bi-level penalized regression (group lasso, group MCP/SCAD, gel/cMCP)
cards.when: a high-dimensional regression where the regressors come in KNOWN GROUPS (lags of the same variable, the dummies of one categorical variable, indicators per sector) and you want sparse selection at the GROUP level; grLasso/grMCP/grSCAD select whole groups, gel/cMCP select bi-level (groups AND variables within a group); cv_group_penalized_regression gives the data-driven lambda_min
cards.when_not: no natural grouping of the columns -> a plain lasso or elastic net (#216, category 20); you want oracle-fair post-selection inference -> a separate inference node; a survival outcome (scoped out); you want a conditional tail or Growth-at-Risk -> #64; a low dimension p<<n with no sparsity -> OLS or GLM

alternatives.criterion: you want convex, stable all-or-nothing selection of a whole group; the default, less biased for large coefficients than MCP but with more shrinkage
you want nearly unbiased large coefficients (a nonconvex group penalty); grSCAD defaults to gamma=4, grMCP to gamma=3
you want sparsity BOTH BETWEEN groups AND WITHIN a group (not all-or-nothing) — only some variables inside a selected group are kept
the columns have NO natural grouping; you want individual-variable sparsity
you want a conditional tail (Growth-at-Risk) rather than a mean regression with group sparsity

output_key_fields: cv_curve: a data_frame lambda/cve/cvse/cvlo/cvup (the CV curve; cvlo/cvup = cve -/+ cvse)
lambda_min / min_index / cve_min: the CV-optimal lambda, its position, the minimum cross-validation error
coefficients: a frame of term/coefficient at lambda_min (the intercept plus the p columns, in the order of X)
selected_groups: the SELECTED, non-zero groups at lambda_min — taken from the group prediction, never from a manual threshold
selected_members: a data_frame variable/group of the members of the selected groups; n_nonzero_groups / n_nonzero_vars
path: a frame of step/lambda/df/deviance with a DECREASING lambda; group_structure of variable and group; plus group_multiplier
object: the raw fit (a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: the fit is DETERMINISTIC (coordinate descent, with no random draws); ONLY the cross-validation is stochastic, through the random fold assignment -> the seed defaults to 20240720; the same seed reproduces lambda_min and the CV error exactly, a different seed does not (live-verified)
group=all-or-nothing: grLasso/grMCP/grSCAD zero out a WHOLE group together; gel/cMCP allow partial selection within a group — do not confuse them
the selected groups come from the group and variable predictions, which are authoritative; do NOT threshold the coefficients by hand, since small non-zeros appear along the MCP and SCAD paths
a group value of 0 = an UNPENALIZED/always-in group (unpenalized covariates); it does not count towards n_groups — it is not a wrong label
the bi-level penalties return an UNNAMED group multiplier, while the group-level ones name it — the wrapper adds fallback labels from the non-zero groups
family='binomial' requires a BINARY {0,1} y, otherwise a 'non-binary data' error; family='poisson' rejects a negative y — both are hard gates
lambda is DECREASING (the first value = the most penalized/largest lambda, the last = the smallest); nfolds must satisfy 3<=nfolds<=n
sources: Yuan & Lin 2006 'Model selection and estimation in regression with grouped variables' JRSS-B 68(1) 49-67 [the group lasso]
Breheny & Huang 2015 Statistics and Computing 25:173-187 (group descent algorithms for nonconvex penalized linear and logistic regression with grouped predictors)
Breheny & Huang 2009 'Penalized methods for bi-level variable selection' Statistics and its Interface 2 369-380 [cMCP/gel bi-level]
Huang, Breheny & Ma 2012 'A selective review of group selection in high-dimensional models' Statistical Science 27(4) 481-499

cards.method: Market-based systemic risk: CoVaR / Delta-CoVaR (Adrian-Brunnermeier) + correlation-network measures
cards.when: a matrix of market returns (column 1 = the market/system index, columns 2. = the institutions); you want the contribution of each institution to systemic risk (CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR in the sense of Adrian-Brunnermeier, static or time-varying with state variables) or monthly correlation-network measures (degree/closeness/eigenvector centrality) + a system-wide index
cards.when_not: there is no market index in column 1; fewer than two institutions; you want the VaR or ES of a portfolio (-> #65), or a conditional Growth-at-Risk (-> #64); you want Diebold-Yilmaz spillover or FEVD connectedness (-> #51/#52, category 09); a quantile level other than 95%, which is hardcoded

alternatives.criterion: you want an unconditional CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR per institution — a single cross-sectional picture, without state variables
you want a conditional CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR that evolves with lagged macro-financial state variables (VIX/spreads) + the system-wide index Delta_CoVaR_t
you want the topology of the correlation network (centrality) + a systemic risk index (SR) per month, not a tail CoVaR
you want directional spillovers from an FEVD (to/from/net) rather than correlation-network centrality or a quantile CoVaR
you want the tail risk of ONE portfolio/series, not a cross-system contribution

output_key_fields: CoVaR_95 / CoVaR_50: the VaR of the system when institution i is at its VaR@95 / median (per institution)
Delta_CoVaR: the systemic contribution of institution i = CoVaR_95 - CoVaR_50 (an identity); loss-signed
CoVaR_i_q_t / Delta_CoVaR_i_q_t: time-varying matrices, (n-1) × institutions + dates
Delta_CoVaR_t: the system-wide index (the cross-sectional mean Delta-CoVaR times 100, where positive means higher risk); the first element is blank, an off-by-one
Degree/Closeness_Centrality/Eigenvector_Centrality: monthly network measures, min-max scaled to [0,1]
SR: the systemic risk index (a correlation-corrected realized portfolio volatility), min-max scaled to [0,1]
q=0.95, a hardcoded constant; n_institutions/n_state_variables/n_months/seed as the audit trail
network: it requires n_months>=3 (a post-gate, blocked-by-gate); ~>=100 daily rows — 90 rows give only 2 months, where the monthly min-max degenerates every measure to {0,1}
interpretation_traps: q=0.95 and q_50=0.5 ARE HARDCODED — the quantile level is NOT parameterisable (tau=0.05)
Delta_CoVaR = CoVaR_95 - CoVaR_50 EXACTLY; its sign follows the slope of the quantile regression (a positive co-movement with the market ⇒ Delta-CoVaR<0, a loss)
column 1 = the market/system index (the LHS), columns 2. = the institutions (the RHS) — NOT the other way round; the wrong order ⇒ a wrong CoVaR
the first Delta_CoVaR_t is structurally blank, an off-by-one at the first period — do not interpret it as 0
the network is fragile with few months, since the monthly sequence leaves gaps in the index; the gate requires at least 90 observations
the eigenvector centrality is non-deterministic at the 1e-18 level (the iterative eigensolver); the wrapper stabilises it by seeding the generator
a degenerate input (a constant column) gives a 'singular design matrix' error inside the quantile fit — a hard error, not a silent result
the VaR is computed parametrically (qnorm, assuming normality of the institution) — not as a historical/empirical quantile
sources: Adrian & Brunnermeier 2016 'CoVaR' American Economic Review 106(7) 1705-1741 (the definition of CoVaR/Delta-CoVaR)
Billio, Getmansky, Lo, Pelizzon 2012 'Econometric measures of connectedness and systemic risk' JFE 104(3) 535-559 (the correlation-network measures)
live introspection in the engine (an independent quantile-regression recomputation) — wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c21_systemic_risk/market_systemic_risk)
