cards.method: Multidimensional Scaling: CLASSICAL/metric (principal coordinates analysis + the Cailliez constant) · NON-METRIC after Kruskal · the NON-LINEAR Sammon mapping
cards.when: a SIMILARITY MAP in a few dimensions (typically 2D) FROM A `dist` DISTANCE MATRIX — «which countries/indicators are close to which» as a 2D scatter + a scree plot + quality measures. The typical producer of the `dist`: #240 dm_distance/dm_correlation_distance/dm_custom_distance or #243 dw_dist_matrix (DTW). The node is VISUALIZATION/EMBEDDING, NOT clustering
cards.when_not: ASSIGNMENT to groups (labels) -> #241, #242 or #244; a RAW data matrix with no preceding distance node (the input MUST be a distance object); dimension reduction of the VARIABLES with loadings and a biplot -> #117 pca_composite / pca_biplot_coords, since MDS maps OBJECTS from dissimilarities; MIXED I(0)/I(1) time series -> #256; subsequence embedding (the Keogh gate); charts (the frontend, §5 — only the coordinates are returned here)

alternatives.criterion: n_eig_negative > 0 or gof_abs < gof_pos ⇒ NON-Euclidean dissimilarities; the Cailliez (1983) additive constant makes them Euclidean (the `ac` field). Useless when there are no negative eigenvalues
the dissimilarities are ORDINAL / their ABSOLUTE scale is not trustworthy: non-metric MDS allows a MONOTONE transformation and keeps only the ORDER (Kruskal); it REQUIRES STRICTLY POSITIVE distances
you want the SMALL (local) distances preserved better: the stress is weighted by 1/d ⇒ it gives weight to the nearby pairs; it REQUIRES STRICTLY POSITIVE distances
the solution returns FEWER columns than k (the POSITIVE eigenvalues are < k; the live warning «only 7 of the first 9 eigenvalues are > 0») ⇒ the node blocks; k MUST lie in {1,., n-1}
you want dimension reduction of the VARIABLES with loadings/a biplot from a RAW data matrix; MDS starts from DISSIMILARITIES (and cmdscale on a euclidean distance COINCIDES with PCA on the scores)

output_key_fields: points: an n × k NUMERIC matrix with row labels = the labels and column labels = Dim1.Dimk — THE MAIN chart-data (the 2D scatter «similarity map»); common to all 3 methods (the SAME dimensions/labels)
labels / n / k + method ('cmdscale' | 'isoMDS' | 'sammon')

mds_classical: eig (ALL n eigenvalues — the scree data) + eig_retained + n_eig_positive + n_eig_negative (above 0 means NON-Euclidean dissimilarities) + var_explained_abs and var_explained_pos (the TWO definitions the classical scaling reports) + gof / gof_abs / gof_pos + ac, the Cailliez constant, which is 0 when add=False, + add
mds_nonmetric: stress AS A PERCENTAGE (the isoMDS routine «The final stress achieved (in percent)») + stress_fraction + maxit/tol/p + init_method='cmdscale'
mds_sammon: stress (Sammon — NOT a percentage, NOT comparable with the isoMDS one) + niter/magic/tol + init_method='cmdscale'

COMMON DIAGNOSTICS (ours, computed IDENTICALLY ⇒ COMPARABLE across the 3): stress_raw = sqrt(sum((d-dhat)^2)/sum(d^2)) (Kruskal stress-1 WITHOUT a monotone transformation, 0 = perfect) + fit_correlation = cor(d, dhat) (NA_real_ when either side is constant, e.g. an equilateral configuration) + dist_fitted = the distances of the configuration (Shepard chart-data)
interpretation_traps: THE CENTRAL GATE — the input MUST be a `dist` object: cmdscale ALSO accepts a matrix/data_frame («a full symmetric matrix») BUT it also SILENTLY accepts a NON-SYMMETRIC matrix (live: with m[1,2]=99 it returned a GOF of 0.577/0.99 WITHOUT a warning) ⇒ silently wrong. A `dist` is by definition symmetric with a zero diagonal; that is why the spec uses a raw_handle (the object is returned AS IS and the wrapper decides)

ZERO OR DUPLICATE DISTANCES — THE MAIN TRAP OF THIS NODE: mds_nonmetric AND mds_sammon require STRICTLY POSITIVE distances («Data are assumed to be dissimilarities... but must be positive except for self-distance») and they error with «zero or negative distance between objects i and j» on DUPLICATE ROWS (live-verified). The node blocks BEFORE the call and NAMES the offending objects, where the underlying routine gives only indices; mds_classical has no such restriction. The upstream signal is a non-zero n_zero_pairs from #243 dw_dist_matrix

SILENTLY WRONG (classical scaling): NEGATIVE dissimilarities are accepted SILENTLY and produce an invalid map (live: a goodness of fit of 0.668/0.818 with no error); all-zero distances give a NaN goodness of fit SILENTLY, since there is nothing to map. Both are hard gates; and because #240 does NOT error when it produces gaps (the normative gate spec §3b), there is an explicit gap, NaN and infinity check here

SILENTLY WRONG (the iteration arguments): maxit=0 or niter=0 are accepted SILENTLY and return the UNOPTIMISED INITIAL configuration; a non-positive tolerance is accepted silently and stops early (live: a stress of 0.44 instead of 0.0069); a non-positive step-size constant is accepted silently and does NOT optimise AT ALL, giving the same stress as niter=0; p=0 HANGS and never terminates, since the Minkowski distance is a metric only for p >= 1. ALL are hard gates

A DIMENSION POST-CHECK: cmdscale returns FEWER columns than k when the POSITIVE eigenvalues number fewer than k (live: k=9 -> 7 columns with the warning «only 7 of the first 9 eigenvalues are > 0») and isoMDS/sammon then fail with the cryptic «invalid initial configuration» ⇒ the node requires EXACTLY n × k and gives a clean message («ask for a smaller k»). The documented bound: k in {1, 2,., n-1} (the cmdscale routine)

THE STRESS VALUES ARE NOT COMPARABLE: the isoMDS stress is A PERCENTAGE and allows a MONOTONE transformation of the distances; the Sammon stress is WEIGHTED by 1/d and is NOT a percentage. That is why the node also computes OUR OWN stress_raw IDENTICALLY across all 3 methods — THAT is the comparable quantity

THE TWO GOF VALUES OF cmdscale: g_i = (sum_{j<=k} lambda_j) / (sum_j T_i(lambda_j)) with T_1 = |.| and T_2 = max(., 0) (the cmdscale routine) ⇒ gof_abs != gof_pos ONLY when NEGATIVE eigenvalues exist; var_explained_abs/var_explained_pos use the SAME two denominators (a post-check: the sum of var_explained_* == gof_abs/gof_pos)

NEVER INTERPRET THE SIGN OF AN AXIS: the configuration is determined ONLY up to translation/rotation/reflection (the cmdscale routine: «the reflection chosen may differ between the reference platforms»; the isoMDS routine/the sammon routine: «the result can vary considerably from machine to machine»). Inside the container the versions are pinned (the lockfile) ⇒ a stable result, but the INTERPRETATION must rest on the DISTANCES between points, not on signs/directions

DETERMINISM (§5): all 3 methods are FULLY deterministic (a spectral decomposition / an iterative descent from a CLASSICAL initialisation) ⇒ NO seed; the initialisation of isoMDS/sammon is passed EXPLICITLY (y = the cmdscale solution = the DOCUMENTED default; an IDENTICAL result, live-verified) so that the determinism does not depend on a future change of default; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests

NORMATIVE GATE 1 (Keogh): if the distance object carries the sliding_window_subsequences marker, the node REJECTS it explicitly — mapping subsequences is as meaningless as clustering them (Keogh, Lin & Truppel 2005). THE MARKER'S CONTRACT: from a distance object the original observations-by-features matrix is NOT recoverable, so the sliding-window detector cannot be re-run here, and the producers #240 and #243 stop AT THE SOURCE — no producer in the engine ever sets the attribute. It is an ACCEPTED-INPUT CONTRACT for EXTERNAL producers of a distance object (a raw handle, or a user matrix converted to a distance) — defence in depth, NOT the primary defence

NORMATIVE GATE 2 (NO imposed detrending): the node NEVER transforms the input — it takes the `dist` AS IT IS. The transform/distance choices are EXPLICIT gated options of the UPSTREAM distance node (#240/#243)

OMITTED: returning the heavy n×n doubly centred matrix; the eigenvalue and list switches are PINNED on, since the eigenvalues and the goodness of fit are always needed as chart data; the trace switch is PINNED off, as it only prints progress (§5); the initial configuration y is n×k DATA and never travels inline in the schema — the wrapper fills it EXPLICITLY; the Shepard diagram is unnecessary, since the same numbers arrive as dist_fitted, stress_raw and fit_correlation; and the majorization alternative was REJECTED in the normative gate spec §3b, the classical and non-metric routes being sufficient, live-verified on the goodness of fit. These are TERMINAL nodes: nothing is registered and nothing chains onward
sources: the cmdscale routine's documentation (stats): «Classical multidimensional scaling (MDS) of a data matrix. Also known as principal coordinates analysis (Gower 1966)»; k «must be in {1, 2,.., n-1}»; GOF = «a numeric vector of length 2.. g_i = (sum_{j=1.k} lambda_j)/(sum_{j=1.n} T_i(lambda_j)), T_1(v) = |v|, T_2(v) = max(v, 0)»; «The representation is only determined up to location, rotations and reflections.. the reflection chosen may differ between the reference platforms»
Gower, J.C. (1966) «Some Distance Properties of Latent Root and Vector Methods Used in Multivariate Analysis», Biometrika 53(3/4), 325 — principal coordinates analysis (cited by the cmdscale routine)

Mardia, K.V. (1978) «Some Properties of Classical Multi-dimensional Scaling», Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods 7(13), 1233-1241 — the analysis that cmdscale follows (cited by the cmdscale routine)
Cailliez 1983, Psychometrika 48(2):305-308 (the analytical solution of the additive constant problem) — the constant behind add=True, and the analytic solution the classical scaling uses

the non-metric scaling routine's documentation: «Kruskal's Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling»; «Data are assumed to be dissimilarities or relative distances, but must be positive except for self-distance»; «the input distances are allowed a monotonic transformation»; the stress is «The final stress achieved (in percent)»; and the default starting configuration is the classical solution

the Sammon routine's documentation: the stress is «the sum of squared differences between the input distances and those of the configuration, weighted by the distances, the whole sum being divided by the sum of input distances to make the stress scale-free»; and the step-size constant is the «initial value of the step size constant in diagonal Newton method»
Sammon, J.W. (1969) «A Non-Linear Mapping for Data Structure Analysis», IEEE Transactions on Computers C-18, 401-409 (cited by the sammon routine)
Kruskal, J.B. (1964) «Multidimensional Scaling by Optimizing Goodness of Fit to a Nonmetric Hypothesis», Psychometrika 29(1), 1-27 — the non-metric MDS that isoMDS implements

Cox, T.F. & Cox, M.A.A. (2001) Multidimensional Scaling, 2nd ed., Chapman & Hall; Venables, W.N. & Ripley, B.D. (2002) Modern Applied Statistics with S, 4th ed., Springer (cited by the cmdscale routine/the isoMDS routine/the sammon routine)

the normative gate spec §3b, live-verified: k must lie in {1, 2, ..., n-1} for both the cut and the classical scaling; a zero or negative distance between two objects means a gate on DUPLICATE ROWS; a distance computed over gaps does NOT error; gates 1 (Keogh) and 2 (no imposed detrending); and the majorization alternative was rejected
wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c29_unsupervised_clustering/multidimensional_scaling_classical) — all the gates and post-checks, and the live silently-wrong findings
precondition_tools: c29_unsupervised_clustering/distance_dissimilarity_matrix.dm_distance # the TYPICAL producer of the `dist` handle (or dm_correlation_distance / dm_custom_distance)
c29_unsupervised_clustering/dynamic_time_warping.dw_dist_matrix # DTW distances; READ the n_zero_pairs field: >0 ⇒ mds_nonmetric/mds_sammon WILL BLOCK (only mds_classical works)
mds_classical # ALWAYS first: it gives n_eig_negative & gof_abs/gof_pos (how non-Euclidean the dissimilarities are) and it is the INITIALISATION of the other two

cards.method: MULTIVARIATE outlier detection: CLASSICAL Mahalanobis distances vs the ROBUST MCD (Deterministic MCD) at the SAME chi-square(p) cutoff + a MASKING / SWAMPING diagnostic
cards.when: a numeric observations×variables matrix (countries × macro indicators, periods × variables) and the question is WHICH ROWS are outlying in the JOINT (multivariate) space — a COMBINATION of values that no univariate check sees (each individual value «normal», the combination impossible); the flow: mv_outliers (classical AND robust SIDE BY SIDE + masked/swamped) -> mv_mcd (only the robust center/cov/h/best subset) -> mv_mahalanobis (the classical distance, or OUT-OF-SAMPLE scoring with a GIVEN center/cov)
cards.when_not: ONE variable (p >= 2 is a hard gate; univariate tails or capping -> #114); TIME-SERIES outliers of type AO/LS/TC/IO in a univariate series -> #5; the LEVELS of non-stationary series, where a Mahalanobis distance is UNINTERPRETABLE — the population mean does not exist and the sample covariance diverges with T, so supply differences EXPLICITLY (§3b gate 3); missing data (impute FIRST, category 00); CLUSTERING rather than outlier detection -> category 29 (#241, #244); charts (the frontend, §5); robust REGRESSION — a different family (categories 06/07)

alternatives.alt: mv_outliers (the MAIN function of the card)
alternatives.criterion: you want THE DECISION: the classical AND robust distances at the same cutoff + masked/swamped counts + a ranking by decreasing robust D². It is the default path — the comparison of the two IS the result
you want ONLY the ROBUST center/cov (e.g. as fitted parameters for downstream scoring) with MAXIMUM robustness: h ~ n/2, a breakdown point of ~ (n-h+1)/n
you know the contamination is < 25% and you want HIGHER EFFICIENCY (a larger h) with less robustness — alpha controls EXACTLY that trade-off
the sample is PROVABLY clean (or you want the baseline for the comparison): purely algebraic, with no randomness and no MCD
an OUT-OF-SAMPLE APPLY (§3b gate 6): you pass back the center/cov of a previous mv_mcd => robust scoring of NEW observations; with BOTH supplied, n >= 1 suffices
the objective is UNIVARIATE tail cleaning per series (capping/trimming), not the detection of outlying COMBINATIONS
the input is a TIME SERIES and outliers are wanted BY TYPE (additive / level shift / transitory change), not by a multivariate distance

output_key_fields: mv_mahalanobis: distance (the named D² per observation — the main chart-data) + distance_sqrt + outlier/outlier_index/outlier_labels + n_outliers/share_outliers + cutoff = qchisq(quantile, df = p) + df = p + center/cov/cov_rcond + center_source/cov_source ('sample' or 'supplied') + max_distance/n/p/observations/variables

mv_mcd: center and cov (ROBUST, fit and apply) + cov_rcond + cor, ONLY when robust_cor=True and absent otherwise, + distance and raw_distance, after and before the reweighting, + raw_center and raw_cov + outlier/n_outliers/share_outliers + h, the subset size implied by alpha, n and p, with h_share, best_subset and in_best_subset + mcd_weight, binary 0/1, with n_zero_weight + crit, the log determinant, + cnp2 and raw_cnp2, the consistency and finite-sample factors, of length 2, + method, a deterministic subsampling scheme, i_best (1 to 6) and n_csteps per initial subset + small_sample (n < 2p) + alpha, use_correction and seed

mv_outliers: distance_table (an n×2 «classical | robust» table — THE CENTRAL chart-data) + classical/robust + outlier_classical/outlier_robust + masked / swamped / both (+ n_ and _labels for each) + order_robust / ranked_labels (by decreasing robust D², ties broken on the name) + classical_center/classical_cov/classical_rcond + robust_center/robust_cov/robust_rcond + h/h_share/best_subset/in_best_subset/mcd_weight/crit + cutoff/quantile/df/alpha/use_correction/small_sample/seed
ALL of them: observations/variables (the row/column names; if they are missing, obs1.obsN / v1.vP are generated) — every flag/distance is named PER ROW
interpretation_traps: MASKING AND SWAMPING ARE THE POINT OF THIS NODE: the classical mean and covariance are computed FROM the outlying points themselves, so an outlier «hides» itself by inflating the variance, while clean points look outlying. The MCD estimates from the «cleanest» subset h, so it is not corrupted. Do NOT read ONLY the classical column: read n_masked and n_swamped (live in the tests, the classical method found 2 of the 4 planted outliers while the MCD found all 4 — and no univariate check would have seen any of them)

alpha STRICTLY in [0.5, 1) — SILENTLY WRONG: the MCD routine(alpha = 0.2) does NOT error, it only warns «subsample size h < n/2 may be too small» and returns a fit with h = 9 out of 30 (a breakdown point > 50%: the «robust» subset can be ENTIRELY outlying). The reference documentation states «Allowed values are between 0.5 and 1» => OUR OWN hard gate

alpha = 1 DEGENERACY (a separate hard gate): «alpha = 1: The minimum covariance determinant estimates... are equal to the classical estimates», and the result then carries NO distance, best-subset or best-index fields AT ALL (live-verified) — zero robustness AND no distance

DETERMINISM (§5): the deterministic subsampling scheme is PINNED — the Deterministic MCD, which starts from the h most central points of SIX deterministic estimators; the alternative default draws 500 random subsamples. The seed is a SAFETY NET above the subsample threshold (1500 with the defaults), where the documentation states explicitly that «the initial search uses only a subsample»; it runs with the generator seeded and the caller's state RESTORED afterwards, keeping the layer pure. Live: identical over two runs, AND identical distances under a DIFFERENT seed

mcd_weight against outlier: the weights are binary and tied to the FIXED 0.975 cutoff of the original weight function — INDEPENDENT of our own 'quantile'. With a quantile other than 0.975, n_zero_weight does NOT equal n_outliers; that is not an error, it is a different cutoff

SILENTLY WRONG cases blocked by hard gates: p = 1, where the estimator does NOT error but returns a result WITHOUT any distance or best subset — a univariate path; a text column in a frame, which is silently coerced and then worked on as category CODES (live, a criterion of -2.300799); gaps, NaN and infinities, which SILENTLY drop rows; n <= p, or n == p+1, which give the cryptic «n <= p -- you can't be serious!» and «n == p+1 is too small sample size for MCD»; and a constant column or collinearity, where the distance fails with «system is exactly singular» or «system is computationally singular» — pre-checked against machine epsilon and exposed as cov_rcond

NO STANDARDIZATION, NO transform ARGUMENT (§3b gate 2): the Mahalanobis distance is AFFINE EQUIVARIANT — D²(x) = D²(Ax+b) — so scale(X) gives IDENTICAL distances (classical AND MCD, live-verified). A transform argument would be a no-op that implied a choice which does not exist

NON-STATIONARITY (§3b gate 3, Hamilton-Ma-Xi): this node is CROSS-SECTION / PANEL. On the LEVELS of I(1) series the population mean is undefined and the sample covariance diverges with T => the distances are uninterpretable. The user supplies differences EXPLICITLY — NEVER a silent correction here

cnp2 and raw_cnp2 have LENGTH 2 — the consistency factor AND the finite-sample correction (Pison et al. 2002); with use_correction=False the second element becomes 1. small_sample=True (n < 2p) corresponds to the «n < 2 * p» warning — a DIAGNOSTIC, not a gate

raw_distance against distance: distance is AFTER the reweighting, and typically considerably more efficient (Pison et al. 2002), while raw_distance is before it. best_subset and h ALWAYS refer to the RAW step, and the subset length equals the h implied by alpha, n and p — post-checked

a TERMINAL node (no register/handle chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers. The fit/apply split is EXPLICIT — the user passes center/cov back into mv_mahalanobis (modelled on the KNIME «Normalize Model»)
sources: the MCD routine (live, in the engine) — «Allowed values are between 0.5 and 1 and the default is 0.5»; the deterministic scheme «starts from the h most central observations of six (deterministic) estimators»; «When nmini*kmini < n, the initial search uses only a subsample of size nmini*kmini»; the retained count equals the h implied by alpha, n and p, and the best subset has exactly that length; the best index runs from 1 to 6, with a concentration-step count per initial subset; cnp2 holds the consistency and finite-sample factors; and the weight function is the original 0/1 rule (Rousseeuw & Van Driessen 1999)
Rousseeuw, P.J. & Van Driessen, K. (1999) «A fast algorithm for the minimum covariance determinant estimator», Technometrics 41, 212-223 (FastMCD)

Hubert, M., Rousseeuw, P.J. & Verdonck, T. (2012) «A deterministic algorithm for robust location and scatter», Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 21, 618-637 (DetMCD = the PINNED nsamp)
Pison, Van Aelst & Willems 2002, Metrika 55:111-123 (small sample corrections for LTS and MCD) — use_correction, cnp2, and the efficiency of the reweighting
Rousseeuw, P.J. & Leroy, A.M. (1987) Robust Regression and Outlier Detection, Wiley (the breakdown point; why the classical mean/cov collapses in the presence of outliers)

Hamilton, J.D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 — §3b gate 3 (why this node is cross-section/panel and not for the levels of I(1) series)

the normative gate spec §3b live-verified gates («the MCD routine: n == p+1 is too small sample size for MCD; alpha in [0.5,1]»; «the MCD routine(alpha=0.2) -> only a warning»; «mahalanobis with n<=p or collinear columns -> system is computationally singular»); DETERMINISM: «the MCD routine ⇒ nsamp="deterministic"»

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c01_preparation_prechecks/multivariate_outlier_detection) — all the silently-wrong cases (p=1, a text column, the silent dropping of rows with gaps, alpha=1 with no distance or best subset), and the affine-equivariance verification

cards.method: A battery of NORMALITY tests (the composite hypothesis): EDF omnibus tests (Anderson-Darling / Cramer-von Mises / Lilliefors) + the Pearson chi-square test on equiprobable classes + Shapiro-Francia, with a COMMON alpha and a long-format decision table
cards.when: ONE numeric univariate series (typically model RESIDUALS, returns, a macro series) and the question is whether its DISTRIBUTION is normal, with the parameters UNKNOWN (the composite hypothesis); nt_normality_battery = ALL the requested tests in ONE call -> a long-format table (statistic/p_value/decision) + a consensus summary; the 5 individual functions when you want ONE specific test (or when n rules some of them out)
cards.when_not: JARQUE-BERA, the moment-based test on skewness and kurtosis, ALREADY EXISTS as #1 run_jarque_bera_test and is NOT duplicated here (and BEWARE the incompatible missing-value policy — see the traps); a DESCRIPTIVE Shapiro-Wilk inside a descriptives table, with no gates and no decision -> #129 ps_descriptives; DESCRIPTIVE moments per column -> #248 dp_profile; SEVERAL columns at once (run the node PER COLUMN — a hard gate against a matrix or frame); missing values (impute FIRST, category 00 — a hard stop here); testing STATIONARITY (#1/#2) or AUTOCORRELATION (Ljung-Box; #81 desc_acf), which are different hypotheses; quantile plots (the frontend, §5); MULTIVARIATE normality -> #246

alternatives.criterion: you want THE DECISION with cross-checking: a long-format table + a consensus (reject_all / fail_to_reject_all / mixed) + a primary_test by a DOCUMENTED order of preference
ONE test, the RECOMMENDED EDF test after Stephens (1986); it gives MORE WEIGHT TO THE TAILS => the first choice when fat tails are the concern (returns, crises); it requires n > 7
a correlation-based test «known to perform well» (Royston 1993); the SECOND choice in the order of preference; it requires 5 <= n <= 5000 (it is RULED OUT for large samples)
an EDF omnibus test, the «second choice» after Anderson-Darling; it puts less weight on the tails and requires n > 7
the literature/reader asks for it explicitly (the best-known EDF test) — BUT it is «known to perform worse» than AD/CvM; it is the ONLY one that works for 5 <= n <= 7

alternatives.alt: nt_pearson_test, with adjust both True and False
alternatives.criterion: you want the chi-square test on equiprobable classes; it is «usually not recommended» (inferior power) AND the correct p-value is NEITHER of the two — it lies BETWEEN them (Moore 1986) => run it BOTH ways
you want a test of MOMENTS (skewness and kurtosis) rather than a deviation of the DISTRIBUTION FUNCTION — COMPLEMENTARY, not a substitute; CAUTION: a different missing-value policy

output_key_fields: nt_normality_battery: table = long-format records (test/test_label/method/statistic/statistic_name/p_value/df/n_classes/expected_per_class/n/alpha/reject/decision) — THE MAIN chart-data; the row order is CANONICAL (ad,cvm,lillie,pearson,sf) regardless of the order the user supplied

nt_normality_battery summary: statistic/p_value/reject, named PER TEST, + n_tests/n_reject/share_reject/reject_any/reject_all + consensus ('reject_all', 'fail_to_reject_all' or 'mixed') + min/max/median_p_value + primary_test/primary_p_value/primary_reject + alpha/n/mean/sd/series/na_policy='error' + results, the complete per-test output including the raw test record

the individual tests: test/test_label/method/statistic/statistic_name/p_value/alpha/reject/decision ('reject_normality' or 'fail_to_reject') + interpretation, a ready-made sentence, + n/series/na_policy + the raw test record
the Pearson chi-square ONLY: df / n_classes / expected_per_class / adjust / min_expected (blank in the other tests, which is how you see that they do NOT apply)
interpretation_traps: MIN-N PER TEST, NEVER A GLOBAL n (live-verified messages): Anderson-Darling and Cramér-von Mises need n > 7 («sample size must be greater than 7»); Lilliefors needs n > 4; Shapiro-Francia needs 5 <= n <= 5000 («sample size must be between 5 and 5000» — it RULES OUT large samples too); the Pearson chi-square has NO gate of its own (see below). In the battery there is NO silent skip: if a requested test does not fit, the call STOPS and the user removes it EXPLICITLY from 'tests' (blocked-by-gate, §5)

AN INCOMPATIBLE MISSING-VALUE POLICY — AN EXPLICIT PROJECT DECISION: the EDF tests declare «Missing values are allowed» and SILENTLY drop the incomplete cases (live, a gap in the input still returns a normal-looking result), whereas the EXISTING Jarque-Bera node (#1) ERRORS. On the SAME input the two normality nodes would give one result and one error, and the reported n would NOT be the n of the input, so the min-n gates would be read wrongly. THE CHOICE: ONE policy, the STRICTER one — a HARD STOP, with a message pointing at the imputation path (category 00); na_policy='error' is ALWAYS returned in the output

THE SILENTLY-WRONG CASES OF nt_pearson_test (the underlying routine has NO validity check at all): (a) n_classes = 3 with adjust=True gives df = 0 and therefore p = 0 EXACTLY, for ANY data (live, a p-value of 0 on NORMAL data); (b) n_classes = 2 with adjust=True gives df = -1, a «NaNs produced» warning and a blank p; (c) a non-integer n_classes such as 4.7 is accepted SILENTLY and truncated when the counts are formed; (d) an expected frequency n/k below 5 breaks the chi-square approximation (Cochran 1954; Moore 1986) and nothing warns; (e) an extreme value whose normal CDF is exactly 1 lands in a class beyond the last and is DROPPED from the counts (live, 199 counted for n = 200, WITH NO warning). EACH ONE is a hard gate here, with the PERMITTED RANGE of n_classes inside the message

the Pearson adjust switch: NEITHER of the two p-values is the correct one — «this is not (!) the correct p-value, lying somewhere between the two»; adjust=True gives df = k-3, correcting for the two estimated parameters, and False gives df = k-1. Run BOTH and read them as BOUNDS: the statistic is THE SAME, and only the degrees of freedom and the p-value change (live-verified)

Lilliefors != ks_test: «Although the test statistic obtained from lillie_test(x) is the same as that obtained from ks_test(x, "pnorm", mean(x), sd(x)), it is not correct to use the p-value from the latter for the composite hypothesis of normality (mean and variance unknown), since the distribution of the test statistic is different when the parameters are estimated» (the lillie_test routine). NEVER compare the two p-values

Shapiro-FRANCIA is NOT Shapiro-WILK: this card exposes Shapiro-Francia, the squared correlation with the expected normal quantiles; the Shapiro-Wilk test is NOT exposed as inference by any node — it appears ONLY descriptively in #129 ps_descriptives, with no gates and no decision

cards.method: Data profiling / a quality report: a PER-COLUMN profile (type/missing/uniqueness/Joanes-Gill moments) + a dataset-level summary + RULE-BASED quality flags (blocker/warning) with a rule and a source
cards.when: THE FIRST node of every workflow, BEFORE any statistical method runs: «what is this data and what is wrong with it?» — dp_profile (a long-format per-column profile + a dataset summary) -> dp_column_profile (ONE column in depth: a quantile grid + a histogram or a top-N frequency table) -> dp_quality_flags (structured flags with a severity, a rule and a source, so that the user knows WHAT will block downstream and WHY). It works on MIXED column types (numeric/integer/logical/character/factor/Date/timestamp) — the non-numeric columns are NOT lost and are NOT coerced
cards.when_not: TRANSFORMATION, imputation or standardization — the node DIAGNOSES, it does NOT alter (§3b gate 2; imputation -> category 00, #80); CROSS-VARIABLE missingness patterns, which columns are missing TOGETHER -> #249 (a separate node: «one wrapper = one node»); NORMALITY TESTS with a p-value and a decision -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera, since the moments here are DESCRIPTIVE; CORRELATIONS with p-values -> #130 rdesc_correlation; MULTIVARIATE outliers -> #246; TIME-SERIES DESCRIPTIVES (ACF/PACF/rolling) -> #81; a descriptive table with normality criteria -> #129; charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies ONLY breaks, counts and midpoints)

alternatives.criterion: you want THE PICTURE OF THE WHOLE dataset in one long-format table (one row per column) + a dataset-level summary; the cheapest first pass

you have spotted ONE suspicious column and you want depth: a quantile grid from p0 to p100, a histogram for a NUMERIC column, or a top-N frequency table for a categorical, boolean or date column, plus the category levels
you want a DECISION rather than numbers: structured blocker/warning flags with a rule, a detail and a value — what WILL BREAK downstream (constant/p>=n/duplicates/no complete rows) before it breaks
you want the G1/G2 estimator that is unbiased under normality (it needs n >= 3, or n >= 4, and is blank otherwise) — for instance to compare against SAS or SPSS output
you want b1/b2 — e.g. to compare with MINITAB OR with implementations whose OWN DEFAULT is type = 3 (our default is type1)
you need a specific quantile algorithm (Hyndman & Fan 1996, types 1.9); type 7 is the conventional default and is EXPLICITLY pinned for determinism
the question is not «how many are missing per column» but «WHICH columns are missing TOGETHER» (missingness patterns/pairs/runs)

output_key_fields: dp_profile: profile = long-format records PER COLUMN {column, type, n, n_missing, pct_missing, n_infinite, n_valid, n_unique, is_constant, n_zeros, min, q1, median, mean, q3, max, iqr, sd, skewness, kurtosis} — the main chart-data

dp_profile: dataset = {rows, cols, complete_rows, incomplete_rows, pct_complete_rows, duplicate_rows, distinct_rows, n_cells, n_missing_cells, pct_missing_cells, n_constant_cols, n_all_missing_cols, n_cols_with_missing, n_cols_with_infinite} + type_counts (a named integer over the 7 types) + columns

dp_column_profile: all the above fields for the ONE column + quantiles (named p0/p1/p5/p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p95/p99/p100) + quantile_probs + histogram {breaks, counts, mids, bins, degenerate} for a NUMERIC column, absent otherwise, + frequency, the top-N records {value, count, pct}, for non-numeric columns only, + n_levels and levels for a categorical column

dp_quality_flags: flags = long-format records {scope, column, issue, severity, detail, value} SORTED (blocker < warning < info, then issue, then column) + n_flags/n_blockers/n_warnings/has_blocker/blocked_columns + profile + dataset + thresholds
ALL of them: quantile_type + moment_type + kurtosis_excess=True (§3b gate 6 — TWO profiles are comparable ONLY under the SAME estimator)
interpretation_traps: AN EXPLICIT DEFINITION OF THE MOMENTS (NEVER «just skewness»): Joanes & Gill (1998), the standard three-type typology. m_r = (1/n) * sum (x_i - xbar)^r, the MOMENT estimator with divisor n rather than n-1. type1 (THE DEFAULT): g1 = m3/m2^(3/2), g2 = m4/m2^2 - 3; type2 (SAS and SPSS): G1 = g1*sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2) for n>=3, G2 = ((n+1)g2+6)(n-1)/((n-2)(n-3)) for n>=4; type3 (Minitab and BMDP): b1 = g1*((n-1)/n)^(3/2), b2 = (g2+3)(1-1/n)^2 - 3. THE KURTOSIS IS ALWAYS EXCESS — 0 under normality — in ALL THREE types, and that is declared explicitly as kurtosis_excess=True

COMPARABILITY: OUR default is type1, whereas other implementations default to type = 3 — TWO «skewness» values on the same data can differ because the ESTIMATOR changed, not the data. That is why moment_type/quantile_type/kurtosis_excess are ALWAYS returned (§3b gate 6). The tests pin identity against an INDEPENDENT recomputation AND against an independent implementation for all 3 types

NO SILENT COERCION (§3b gate 2): the non-numeric columns get the COUNT fields and a blank for the moments — they are NEVER turned into numbers. An UNKNOWN column dtype (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) is a HARD STOP: it was LIVE-VERIFIED as silently wrong that a duration is stored as a double, so without the gate it would be profiled as «numeric» with moments in UNKNOWN UNITS, days or seconds. The same stop covers a nested-list column, a frame column, a matrix column, a decomposed timestamp, and a complex column

NEVER NaN OR INFINITY IN THE OUTPUT (the dp_postcheck_finite check): the DOCUMENTED silently-wrong behaviours that are neutralised — the minimum or maximum of an ALL-MISSING column returns plus or minus infinity, with the warning «no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf», and here comes back blank; the moments of a constant column divide zero by zero and give NaN, and here come back blank; and a NUMERIC OVERFLOW, say 1e308 against -1e308, gives an infinite standard deviation WITHOUT an error, which here BLOCKS, since the profile would be numerically meaningless

NaN COUNTS AS MISSING, an infinity does NOT — it is counted separately in n_infinite, excluded from the moments AND flagged as a blocker. n_valid counts the values that are both present and finite. n_unique counts the DISTINCT present values — for a categorical column the levels actually PRESENT, not the declared level count, which is exposed separately as n_levels in dp_column_profile

EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested): an ALL-MISSING column gives n_unique = 0, a blank is_constant rather than False, and blank moments; a single valid value makes the minimum, quartiles, median, mean and maximum coincide, the interquartile range 0, and the standard deviation and both shape moments blank; a constant column gives a standard deviation of 0 but blank skewness and kurtosis, since the second moment is 0; and n_zeros is blank for NON-numeric columns, where «zero» is undefined

THE MOMENTS ARE DESCRIPTIVE, NOT INFERENCE: on an AUTOCORRELATED series they are NOT evidence of normality, nor a basis for a test (§3b gate 4: autocorrelation inflates the Type I error). For a normality decision -> #247 or #1; for inference under autocorrelation -> the HAC path (#35, category 07)

THE HISTOGRAM IS NOT THE CONVENTIONAL ONE: the Sturges breaks there are prettified, giving an UNPREDICTABLE number of bins; here they are EXACTLY equal-width, spanning the minimum to the maximum in bins+1 edges, and therefore reproducible. A constant column, where the minimum equals the maximum, gives ONE degenerate bin (degenerate=True) rather than degenerate equal breaks. A post-check confirms that the counts sum to the number of values, so nothing is lost. NO DRAWING — only breaks, counts and midpoints (§5)

dp_quality_flags: THE RULES ARE EXPLICIT AND SOURCED — all_missing (a blocker); high_missing above max_missing_pct (a warning; the default is 10%, the Bennett 2001 rule the detail itself cites); constant (a blocker: a correlation returns a blank with ONLY a warning, and a z-score divides by 0); infinite_values (a blocker); high_cardinality at or above max_unique_ratio (a warning: it looks like an identifier, not a variable); duplicate_rows (a warning: it breaks k-means with «more cluster centers than distinct data points», and non-metric scaling with «zero or negative distance»); few_rows below min_rows (a warning: the min-n of the normality tests); p_ge_n (a blocker: a singular covariance makes the Mahalanobis distance report «system is computationally singular», and model-based clustering does not even error); and no_complete_rows (a blocker). all_missing EXCLUDES high_missing — one flag per column for missingness

dp_quality_flags DOES NOT STOP EXECUTION: it produces STRUCTURED flags that the frontend displays educationally (blocked-by-gate as a STATE, not an error); the hard stop calls are ONLY for STRUCTURALLY invalid input (duplicate/empty column names, a list-column, an unknown class, a quantile_type outside 1.9)

DETERMINISM (§5): no RNG/seed, no sampling, no parallelism; ALL the orderings have an EXPLICIT tie-break — flags: severity -> issue -> column with method='radix' (locale-independent); frequency: DECREASING count with a LEXICOGRAPHIC tie-break on the value. identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (both the wrapper AND the node path)

WHY THE STANDARD LIBRARY AND NOT A PROFILING DEPENDENCY (the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED them): we take the FEATURE and reject the dependencies — they drag in a plotting stack, they DRAW by default, which violates §5, and one of them documents an INCONSISTENT default ordering, a determinism risk. Zero new dependencies here. The input is a df_handle, NOT a matrix_handle: coercing to a matrix WOULD DROP the non-numeric columns, which is precisely what the profiling is obliged to REPORT
sources: Joanes, D.N. & Gill, C.A. (1998) «Comparing measures of sample skewness and kurtosis», The Statistician (JRSS-D) 47, 183-189 — the type 1/2/3 typology of the skewness/kurtosis estimators

the skewness and kurtosis routines (live, the engine) — the EXACT formulas of type1/2/3 («g1 = m3/m2^(3/2)»; «G1 = g1*sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2). Used in SAS and SPSS»; «b1 = m3/s^3 = g1((n-1)/n)^(3/2). Used in MINITAB and BMDP»; «G2 = ((n+1)g2+6)(n-1)/((n-2)(n-3))»; «Only G2 (type = 2) is unbiased under normality») AND the type = 3 default used elsewhere, citing Joanes & Gill (1998)

Hyndman, R.J. & Fan, Y. (1996) «Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages», The American Statistician 50(4), 361-365, doi:10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566 — the 9 types of quantile (cited by the quantile routine); type 7 is the conventional default, EXPLICITLY pinned and exposed

Cochran-type rules do NOT apply here, since this node is DESCRIPTIVE; the few_rows, p_ge_n and duplicate_rows flags reproduce the live-verified gates of the normative gate spec §3b: the min-n per normality test (Anderson-Darling and Cramér-von Mises n>7, Lilliefors n>4, Shapiro-Francia 5<=n<=5000); a Mahalanobis distance with n<=p, or with collinear columns, reports «system is computationally singular»; model-based clustering with p>n does NOT error but returns a fit; k-means reports «more cluster centers than distinct data points»; non-metric scaling reports «zero or negative distance»; and a correlation on a zero-variance column only warns and returns a blank

the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED the third-party profiling and missingness dependencies: we TAKE the feature — implemented on the standard library in the data-profile and missing-pattern nodes — and reject the dependencies, which drag in a plotting stack, draw by default (a violation of §5), and document an inconsistent default ordering (a determinism risk); together with §3b gates 2 (no silent conversion) and 6 (fit-apply externalization)

[#248] Data profiling / a quality report: a PER-COLUMN profile (type/missing/uniqueness/Joanes-Gill moments) + a dataset-level summary + RULE-BASED quality flags (blocker/warning) with a rule and a source
Category: 01-preparation-prechecks
Nodes: dp_profile · dp_column_profile · dp_quality_flags
WHEN: THE FIRST node of every workflow, BEFORE any statistical method runs: «what is this data and what is wrong with it?» — dp_profile (a long-format per-column profile + a dataset summary) -> dp_column_profile (ONE column in depth: a quantile grid + a histogram or a top-N frequency table) -> dp_quality_flags (structured flags with a severity, a rule and a source, so that the user knows WHAT will block downstream and WHY). It works on MIXED column types (numeric/integer/logical/character/factor/Date/timestamp) — the non-numeric columns are NOT lost and are NOT coerced
NOT when: TRANSFORMATION, imputation or standardization — the node DIAGNOSES, it does NOT alter (§3b gate 2; imputation -> category 00, #80); CROSS-VARIABLE missingness patterns, which columns are missing TOGETHER -> #249 (a separate node: «one wrapper = one node»); NORMALITY TESTS with a p-value and a decision -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera, since the moments here are DESCRIPTIVE; CORRELATIONS with p-values -> #130 rdesc_correlation; MULTIVARIATE outliers -> #246; TIME-SERIES DESCRIPTIVES (ACF/PACF/rolling) -> #81; a descriptive table with normality criteria -> #129; charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies ONLY breaks, counts and midpoints)
Alternatives: dp_profile (you want THE PICTURE OF THE WHOLE dataset in one long-format table (one row per column) + a dataset-level summary; the cheapest first pass) · dp_column_profile (you have spotted ONE suspicious column and you want depth: a quantile grid from p0 to p100, a histogram for a NUMERIC column, or a top-N frequency table for a categorical, boolean or date column, plus the category levels) · dp_quality_flags (you want a DECISION rather than numbers: structured blocker/warning flags with a rule, a detail and a value — what WILL BREAK downstream (constant/p>=n/duplicates/no complete rows) before it breaks) · moment_type = 'type2' (SAS/SPSS) (you want the G1/G2 estimator that is unbiased under normality (it needs n >= 3, or n >= 4, and is blank otherwise) — for instance to compare against SAS or SPSS output) · moment_type = 'type3' (MINITAB/BMDP) (you want b1/b2 — e.g. to compare with MINITAB OR with implementations whose OWN DEFAULT is type = 3 (our default is type1)) · quantile_type != 7 (you need a specific quantile algorithm (Hyndman & Fan 1996, types 1.9); type 7 is the conventional default and is EXPLICITLY pinned for determinism) · #249 mp_pattern (missing-pattern) (the question is not «how many are missing per column» but «WHICH columns are missing TOGETHER» (missingness patterns/pairs/runs))
Output: dp_profile: profile = long-format records PER COLUMN {column, type, n, n_missing, pct_missing, n_infinite, n_valid, n_unique, is_constant, n_zeros, min, q1, median, mean, q3, max, iqr, sd, skewness, kurtosis} — the main chart-data · dp_profile: dataset = {rows, cols, complete_rows, incomplete_rows, pct_complete_rows, duplicate_rows, distinct_rows, n_cells, n_missing_cells, pct_missing_cells, n_constant_cols, n_all_missing_cols, n_cols_with_missing, n_cols_with_infinite} + type_counts (a named integer over the 7 types) + columns · dp_column_profile: all the above fields for the ONE column + quantiles (named p0/p1/p5/p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p95/p99/p100) + quantile_probs + histogram {breaks, counts, mids, bins, degenerate} for a NUMERIC column, absent otherwise, + frequency, the top-N records {value, count, pct}, for non-numeric columns only, + n_levels and levels for a categorical column · dp_quality_flags: flags = long-format records {scope, column, issue, severity, detail, value} SORTED (blocker < warning < info, then issue, then column) + n_flags/n_blockers/n_warnings/has_blocker/blocked_columns + profile + dataset + thresholds · ALL of them: quantile_type + moment_type + kurtosis_excess=True (§3b gate 6 — TWO profiles are comparable ONLY under the SAME estimator)
Pitfalls: AN EXPLICIT DEFINITION OF THE MOMENTS (NEVER «just skewness»): Joanes & Gill (1998), the standard three-type typology. m_r = (1/n) * sum (x_i - xbar)^r, the MOMENT estimator with divisor n rather than n-1. type1 (THE DEFAULT): g1 = m3/m2^(3/2), g2 = m4/m2^2 - 3; type2 (SAS and SPSS): G1 = g1*sqrt(n(n-1))/(n-2) for n>=3, G2 = ((n+1)g2+6)(n-1)/((n-2)(n-3)) for n>=4; type3 (Minitab and BMDP): b1 = g1*((n-1)/n)^(3/2), b2 = (g2+3)(1-1/n)^2 - 3. THE KURTOSIS IS ALWAYS EXCESS — 0 under normality — in ALL THREE types, and that is declared explicitly as kurtosis_excess=True · COMPARABILITY: OUR default is type1, whereas other implementations default to type = 3 — TWO «skewness» values on the same data can differ because the ESTIMATOR changed, not the data. That is why moment_type/quantile_type/kurtosis_excess are ALWAYS returned (§3b gate 6). The tests pin identity against an INDEPENDENT recomputation AND against an independent implementation for all 3 types · NO SILENT COERCION (§3b gate 2): the non-numeric columns get the COUNT fields and a blank for the moments — they are NEVER turned into numbers. An UNKNOWN column dtype (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) is a HARD STOP: it was LIVE-VERIFIED as silently wrong that a duration is stored as a double, so without the gate it would be profiled as «numeric» with moments in UNKNOWN UNITS, days or seconds. The same stop covers a nested-list column, a frame column, a matrix column, a decomposed timestamp, and a complex column · NEVER NaN OR INFINITY IN THE OUTPUT (the dp_postcheck_finite check): the DOCUMENTED silently-wrong behaviours that are neutralised — the minimum or maximum of an ALL-MISSING column returns plus or minus infinity, with the warning «no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf», and here comes back blank; the moments of a constant column divide zero by zero and give NaN, and here come back blank; and a NUMERIC OVERFLOW, say 1e308 against -1e308, gives an infinite standard deviation WITHOUT an error, which here BLOCKS, since the profile would be numerically meaningless · NaN COUNTS AS MISSING, an infinity does NOT — it is counted separately in n_infinite, excluded from the moments AND flagged as a blocker. n_valid counts the values that are both present and finite. n_unique counts the DISTINCT present values — for a categorical column the levels actually PRESENT, not the declared level count, which is exposed separately as n_levels in dp_column_profile · EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested): an ALL-MISSING column gives n_unique = 0, a blank is_constant rather than False, and blank moments; a single valid value makes the minimum, quartiles, median, mean and maximum coincide, the interquartile range 0, and the standard deviation and both shape moments blank; a constant column gives a standard deviation of 0 but blank skewness and kurtosis, since the second moment is 0; and n_zeros is blank for NON-numeric columns, where «zero» is undefined · THE MOMENTS ARE DESCRIPTIVE, NOT INFERENCE: on an AUTOCORRELATED series they are NOT evidence of normality, nor a basis for a test (§3b gate 4: autocorrelation inflates the Type I error). For a normality decision -> #247 or #1; for inference under autocorrelation -> the HAC path (#35, category 07) · THE HISTOGRAM IS NOT THE CONVENTIONAL ONE: the Sturges breaks there are prettified, giving an UNPREDICTABLE number of bins; here they are EXACTLY equal-width, spanning the minimum to the maximum in bins+1 edges, and therefore reproducible. A constant column, where the minimum equals the maximum, gives ONE degenerate bin (degenerate=True) rather than degenerate equal breaks. A post-check confirms that the counts sum to the number of values, so nothing is lost. NO DRAWING — only breaks, counts and midpoints (§5) · dp_quality_flags: THE RULES ARE EXPLICIT AND SOURCED — all_missing (a blocker); high_missing above max_missing_pct (a warning; the default is 10%, the Bennett 2001 rule the detail itself cites); constant (a blocker: a correlation returns a blank with ONLY a warning, and a z-score divides by 0); infinite_values (a blocker); high_cardinality at or above max_unique_ratio (a warning: it looks like an identifier, not a variable); duplicate_rows (a warning: it breaks k-means with «more cluster centers than distinct data points», and non-metric scaling with «zero or negative distance»); few_rows below min_rows (a warning: the min-n of the normality tests); p_ge_n (a blocker: a singular covariance makes the Mahalanobis distance report «system is computationally singular», and model-based clustering does not even error); and no_complete_rows (a blocker). all_missing EXCLUDES high_missing — one flag per column for missingness · dp_quality_flags DOES NOT STOP EXECUTION: it produces STRUCTURED flags that the frontend displays educationally (blocked-by-gate as a STATE, not an error); the hard stop calls are ONLY for STRUCTURALLY invalid input (duplicate/empty column names, a list-column, an unknown class, a quantile_type outside 1.9) · DETERMINISM (§5): no RNG/seed, no sampling, no parallelism; ALL the orderings have an EXPLICIT tie-break — flags: severity -> issue -> column with method='radix' (locale-independent); frequency: DECREASING count with a LEXICOGRAPHIC tie-break on the value. identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (both the wrapper AND the node path) · WHY THE STANDARD LIBRARY AND NOT A PROFILING DEPENDENCY (the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED them): we take the FEATURE and reject the dependencies — they drag in a plotting stack, they DRAW by default, which violates §5, and one of them documents an INCONSISTENT default ordering, a determinism risk. Zero new dependencies here. The input is a df_handle, NOT a matrix_handle: coercing to a matrix WOULD DROP the non-numeric columns, which is precisely what the profiling is obliged to REPORT
Sources: Joanes, D.N. & Gill, C.A. cards.method: Analysis of MISSINGNESS PATTERNS (CROSS-VARIABLE): a pattern matrix, 1 observed and 0 missing, + the counts per pattern + an EXACT MONOTONICITY check (Van Buuren) · the gap runs and spans per variable (a ragged edge, or mixed frequency) · co-missingness per PAIR (rr/rm/mr/mm)
cards.when: the question is NOT «how many are missing PER COLUMN» — that is #248 — but «WHICH COMBINATIONS of variables are missing TOGETHER»: 10% missing across 5 variables may be ONE common pattern, the same 10 countries, or 5 DISJOINT ones, giving 40% incomplete rows. The flow: mp_pattern (how many DISTINCT patterns, how many complete cases, and MONOTONICITY) -> mp_runs (WHERE the gaps sit in time: leading, internal or trailing, so mixed frequency against a ragged edge from a publication lag) -> mp_pairs (which PAIRS are missing together). It works on MIXED column types — the criterion is ONLY whether a value is present, with no coercion
cards.when_not: IMPUTATION, dropping rows or columns, or any alteration — the node DIAGNOSES (§3b gate 2; filling gaps in a time series -> #80); a per-column profile with moments, types and quality flags -> #248 («one wrapper = one node»); ESTIMATION with a ragged edge or mixed frequency, rather than DIAGNOSIS -> #15/#17/#18/#144; an MCAR TEST (Little 1988) — NOT exposed, since it requires normality and EM, and the autocorrelation of macro panels violates the assumptions (§3b gate 4); charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies ONLY the 0/1 matrices, the counts and the spans); data with no column names, or with DUPLICATE ones, where the patterns would be ambiguous

alternatives.criterion: you want the STRUCTURE of the missingness: how many DISTINCT patterns exist, how many rows per pattern, how many complete cases, and whether the pattern is MONOTONE (critical for which imputation mechanism is admissible)

the data are TIME-ORDERED and you want to know WHERE the gaps are: a trailing gap is a ragged edge from a publication lag, a leading gap a series that starts later, and an internal gap either mixed frequency or a silent hole. The pattern matrix does NOT distinguish the three cases

you want the PER-PAIR view: rr means both observed; rm the row observed and the column missing; mr the reverse; mm both missing — which shows which pairs NEVER have observations in common, since rr = 0 means no pairwise correlation is defined

you want the conventional MEANING of the row ordering, «increasing amounts of missing information»; the default, 'count', orders by a DECREASING number of rows, the most frequent pattern first. BOTH are TOTAL orderings with a complete tie-break, which the conventional implementation does not define
a STRICTLY INCREASING time column exists: it is excluded from the variables (it is the axis) and the spans get start_time/end_time LABELS; without it the positions are plain row indices
you need counts+moments PER COLUMN (#248) or the FILLING of the gaps (#80) — #249 NEVER alters the data

output_key_fields: mp_pattern: pattern_matrix (an n_patterns x n_cols INTEGER 0/1 matrix, axis labels pattern_i x the column name — THE MAIN chart-data) + pattern_counts + pattern (long-format records {pattern_id, pattern_key, count, pct, n_missing_vars, n_observed_vars, missing_vars, is_complete_case}) + variables ({variable, n_missing, n_observed, pct_missing}) + row_missing_counts (chart-data per ROW)
monotone (mp_pattern): {is_monotone, order — the names in the MONOTONE ordering — order_index, n_violating_rows, pct_violating_rows, first_violating_row}; an EXACT check, not a heuristic

summary (mp_pattern): {n_rows, n_cols, n_patterns, n_complete_cases, n_incomplete_cases, pct_complete_cases, n_cells, n_missing_cells, pct_missing_cells, n_cols_with_missing, n_all_missing_cols, n_complete_cols, any_missing}

mp_runs: runs is a long-format record set, ONE PER GAP SPAN {variable, run_id, start, end, length, position — leading, internal, trailing or all — start_time, end_time} + variables (with n_runs, longest_run, leading_na, trailing_na, n_internal_runs, n_internal_missing, first_obs and last_obs with their times, is_all_missing, is_complete) + na_counts_by_row

summary (mp_runs): {n_runs, n_vars_with_missing, n_vars_ragged_start, n_vars_ragged_end, n_vars_internal_gaps, max_leading_na, max_trailing_na, balanced_start, balanced_end, ragged_edge, n_all_missing_cols} — ragged_edge is THE decision field for nowcasting workflows

mp_pairs: rr / rm / mr / mm (FOUR p x p INTEGER matrices with axis labels — chart-data) + pairs (long-format records i<j {variable_1, variable_2, both_observed, both_missing, only_1_missing, only_2_missing, pct_both_missing}) + summary {n_pairs, n_pairs_co_missing, max_both_missing}

ALL of them: columns (ALWAYS in the INPUT ORDER) + time_name (+ sort_by in mp_pattern, time_labels in mp_runs) — §3b gate 6: ALL the parameters that determine the output are returned, so that two runs are COMPARABLE
interpretation_traps: WHY THE STANDARD LIBRARY AND NOT A MISSING-DATA DEPENDENCY (the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED it — a DOCUMENTED DECISION): we take the SEMANTICS of the pattern and pair matrices WITHOUT the dependency, because (a) it would shadow common verbs in the SHARED source environment and (b) its pattern function DRAWS by default, violating charter §5, «charts ONLY in the frontend». Here: ZERO new dependencies, ZERO drawing, only numeric chart data. The ENCODING — 1 observed, 0 missing — and the rr/rm/mr/mm convention are preserved

A DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM THE CONVENTIONAL IMPLEMENTATION: (i) the counts are NOT appended as the LAST ROW and COLUMN of the same matrix, since they would pollute the chart data with non-binary values — they are SEPARATE fields, pattern_counts and variables; (ii) the COLUMNS are NEVER reordered, whereas the conventional implementation «sorts rows and columns in increasing amounts of missing information», so the SAME schema with different data would give a DIFFERENT column order, and incomparable runs

A DETERMINISTIC ORDERING — AN EXPLICIT RULE (no RNG anywhere): the COLUMNS are ALWAYS in the input order. The pattern ROWS use THREE keys: sort_by='count' (default) => DECREASING count -> INCREASING n_missing_vars -> INCREASING pattern key; sort_by='missingness' => INCREASING n_missing_vars -> DECREASING count -> INCREASING pattern key. The pattern key is UNIQUE per pattern ⇒ the ordering is TOTAL (no tie is left unresolved). RUNS: the input order of the variables, then INCREASING start. PAIRS: DECREASING both_missing -> INCREASING i -> INCREASING j. ALL with method='radix' = the C locale ⇒ locale-independent (live-verified: order(c('a','B'), method='radix') = 2,1 whereas the default en_US gives 1,2)

MONOTONICITY — WHAT IT MEANS AND WHY THE CHECK IS EXACT: the Van Buuren definition (FIMD 2nd ed., §4.1.1) — «A missing data pattern is said to be monotone if the variables Y_j can be ordered such that if Y_j is missing then all variables Y_k with k>j are also missing». Equivalently: the sets M_j = {i : Y_ij is missing} are NESTED. The node does NOT search over p! orderings: it checks ONE (increasing |M_j|) and that SUFFICES, because nested sets have increasing cardinality and equinumerous nested sets are EQUAL. The tests verify this against a BRUTE-FORCE search over all p! orderings

THE DEFINITION OF MISSING (explicit, NEVER «just missingness»): a cell is missing when it holds no value. NaN COUNTS as missing (live-verified) while an infinity does NOT — an infinity is a VALUE. For infinity diagnostics -> #248 dp_profile, the n_infinite field

WHY THERE IS A GATE FOR A STRICTLY INCREASING TIME COLUMN: the gap runs and spans are defined ONLY when the row order IS the time order. With an unsorted or DUPLICATED time column — a panel rather than a series — the spans are MEANINGLESS and nothing errors (silently wrong) ⇒ a hard stop; and the axis itself may hold no gaps. The check sorts with a radix order and looks for duplicates, rather than testing sortedness on text, which would depend on the LOCALE

THE RUNS DEPEND ON THE ROW ORDER — the patterns, the counts and the monotonicity do NOT: the tests pin an UNCHANGED mp_pattern result under a RANDOM ROW PERMUTATION. THE ONLY order-dependent field of mp_pattern is first_violating_row inside monotone, which is a ROW INDEX by definition

COLUMN-TYPE GATES — AN ESSENTIAL DIFFERENCE FROM #248: here NO moment is computed and NO coercion happens, so the unusual ATOMIC dtypes (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) ARE ALLOWED, since the presence test is type-agnostic — whereas #248 BLOCKS them, because its moments would carry unknown units. What is blocked is EXACTLY the structures where the presence test does not return one flag per row: a matrix column and a frame column, which both return a MATRIX; a decomposed timestamp, internally a LIST of nine fields; a nested-list column, where the test looks inside each element rather than at the cell; and a complex column, which is not JSON-safe

POST-CHECKS AS MUTATION GUARDS (STRUCTURALLY impossible to trigger from a valid input; that is why they are SEPARATE functions that the tests call DIRECTLY): the sum of the pattern counts == nrow (the patterns PARTITION the rows); the complete cases derived from the patterns == a direct count; the sum of the run lengths per variable == its number of missing values (the completeness of the rle); rr+rm+mr+mm == nrow in EVERY cell

EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested, NEVER an error): NO missing values gives ONE pattern of all ones, n_patterns = 1, any_missing = False, monotone = True (empty sets are trivially nested), zero runs, and mm = 0 everywhere; an ALL-MISSING column gives ONE run with position='all', blank first and last observations, and does NOT break monotonicity; an ALL-MISSING dataset gives ONE pattern of all zeros and n_complete_cases = 0; a single row makes the per-column presence test return a VECTOR rather than a matrix (live-verified) ⇒ an explicit matrix fallback; and a single column makes mp_pairs return zero pairs with the CORRECT shape, rr and mm being 1x1

a df_handle AND NOT a matrix_handle at the node layer: coercing to a matrix WOULD DROP the NON-NUMERIC columns — that is, it would HIDE exactly the missing values the node exists to count, a silent data loss. These are TERMINAL nodes: nothing is registered and nothing chains onward
sources: van Buuren, S. «Flexible Imputation of Missing Data», 2nd ed., §4.1.1 — the definition of a MONOTONE pattern: «A missing data pattern is said to be monotone if the variables Y_j can be ordered such that if Y_j is missing then all variables Y_k with k>j are also missing»

the conventional missing-data pattern and pair documentation — «1=observed, 0=missing»; «Rows and columns are sorted in increasing amounts of missing information»; «The last column and row contain row and column counts»; the pattern function draws by default; and for the pairs, rr is «both variables are observed», rm «row observed, column missing», mr the reverse, and mm «both variables are missing». NOTE: that implementation is NOT a dependency of this project and is not installed — the semantics are reproduced, and recorded verbatim in the wrapper's footer

the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED the third-party profiling and missing-data dependencies: we TAKE the feature — implemented on the standard library in the data-profile and missing-pattern nodes — and reject the dependencies, one of which draws by default (a violation of §5) and another of which shadows common verbs; together with §3b gates 2 (no imposed conversion) and 6 (fit/apply externalization)

Little, R.J.A. (1988) «A Test of Missing Completely at Random for Multivariate Data with Missing Values», JASA 83(404), 1198-1202 — the MCAR test is NOT exposed by this node (it requires normality + EM; the autocorrelation of macro panels violates the assumptions, compare §3b gate 4)

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c01_preparation_prechecks/missingness_patterns) — the explicit definitions (missing, pattern, monotone, gap run), the proof that one candidate ordering suffices, the live-verified edge cases (a single row returning a vector rather than a matrix), and the four post-checks
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/profiling_quality_report.dp_profile # FIRST the per-column profile (#248: how many are missing per column); HERE the question WHICH are missing TOGETHER is answered
mp_pattern # run it FIRST: n_patterns, n_complete_cases and the is_monotone flag inside monotone decide whether mp_runs or mp_pairs are needed at all
