Alternatives: mp_pattern (you want the STRUCTURE of the missingness: how many DISTINCT patterns exist, how many rows per pattern, how many complete cases, and whether the pattern is MONOTONE (critical for which imputation mechanism is admissible)) · mp_runs (the data are TIME-ORDERED and you want to know WHERE the gaps are: a trailing gap is a ragged edge from a publication lag, a leading gap a series that starts later, and an internal gap either mixed frequency or a silent hole. The pattern matrix does NOT distinguish the three cases) · mp_pairs (you want the PER-PAIR view: rr means both observed; rm the row observed and the column missing; mr the reverse; mm both missing — which shows which pairs NEVER have observations in common, since rr = 0 means no pairwise correlation is defined) · sort_by = 'missingness' (you want the conventional MEANING of the row ordering, «increasing amounts of missing information»; the default, 'count', orders by a DECREASING number of rows, the most frequent pattern first. BOTH are TOTAL orderings with a complete tie-break, which the conventional implementation does not define) · time = <a column name> (a STRICTLY INCREASING time column exists: it is excluded from the variables (it is the axis) and the spans get start_time/end_time LABELS; without it the positions are plain row indices) · #248 dp_profile / #80 imputation (you need counts+moments PER COLUMN (#248) or the FILLING of the gaps (#80) — #249 NEVER alters the data)
Output: mp_pattern: pattern_matrix (an n_patterns x n_cols INTEGER 0/1 matrix, axis labels pattern_i x the column name — THE MAIN chart-data) + pattern_counts + pattern (long-format records {pattern_id, pattern_key, count, pct, n_missing_vars, n_observed_vars, missing_vars, is_complete_case}) + variables ({variable, n_missing, n_observed, pct_missing}) + row_missing_counts (chart-data per ROW) · monotone (mp_pattern): {is_monotone, order — the names in the MONOTONE ordering — order_index, n_violating_rows, pct_violating_rows, first_violating_row}; an EXACT check, not a heuristic · summary (mp_pattern): {n_rows, n_cols, n_patterns, n_complete_cases, n_incomplete_cases, pct_complete_cases, n_cells, n_missing_cells, pct_missing_cells, n_cols_with_missing, n_all_missing_cols, n_complete_cols, any_missing} · mp_runs: runs is a long-format record set, ONE PER GAP SPAN {variable, run_id, start, end, length, position — leading, internal, trailing or all — start_time, end_time} + variables (with n_runs, longest_run, leading_na, trailing_na, n_internal_runs, n_internal_missing, first_obs and last_obs with their times, is_all_missing, is_complete) + na_counts_by_row · summary (mp_runs): {n_runs, n_vars_with_missing, n_vars_ragged_start, n_vars_ragged_end, n_vars_internal_gaps, max_leading_na, max_trailing_na, balanced_start, balanced_end, ragged_edge, n_all_missing_cols} — ragged_edge is THE decision field for nowcasting workflows · mp_pairs: rr / rm / mr / mm (FOUR p x p INTEGER matrices with axis labels — chart-data) + pairs (long-format records i<j {variable_1, variable_2, both_observed, both_missing, only_1_missing, only_2_missing, pct_both_missing}) + summary {n_pairs, n_pairs_co_missing, max_both_missing} · ALL of them: columns (ALWAYS in the INPUT ORDER) + time_name (+ sort_by in mp_pattern, time_labels in mp_runs) — §3b gate 6: ALL the parameters that determine the output are returned, so that two runs are COMPARABLE
Pitfalls: WHY THE STANDARD LIBRARY AND NOT A MISSING-DATA DEPENDENCY (the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED it — a DOCUMENTED DECISION): we take the SEMANTICS of the pattern and pair matrices WITHOUT the dependency, because (a) it would shadow common verbs in the SHARED source environment and (b) its pattern function DRAWS by default, violating charter §5, «charts ONLY in the frontend». Here: ZERO new dependencies, ZERO drawing, only numeric chart data. The ENCODING — 1 observed, 0 missing — and the rr/rm/mr/mm convention are preserved · A DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM THE CONVENTIONAL IMPLEMENTATION: (i) the counts are NOT appended as the LAST ROW and COLUMN of the same matrix, since they would pollute the chart data with non-binary values — they are SEPARATE fields, pattern_counts and variables; (ii) the COLUMNS are NEVER reordered, whereas the conventional implementation «sorts rows and columns in increasing amounts of missing information», so the SAME schema with different data would give a DIFFERENT column order, and incomparable runs · A DETERMINISTIC ORDERING — AN EXPLICIT RULE (no RNG anywhere): the COLUMNS are ALWAYS in the input order. The pattern ROWS use THREE keys: sort_by='count' (default) => DECREASING count -> INCREASING n_missing_vars -> INCREASING pattern key; sort_by='missingness' => INCREASING n_missing_vars -> DECREASING count -> INCREASING pattern key. The pattern key is UNIQUE per pattern ⇒ the ordering is TOTAL (no tie is left unresolved). RUNS: the input order of the variables, then INCREASING start. PAIRS: DECREASING both_missing -> INCREASING i -> INCREASING j. ALL with method='radix' = the C locale ⇒ locale-independent (live-verified: order(c('a','B'), method='radix') = 2,1 whereas the default en_US gives 1,2) · MONOTONICITY — WHAT IT MEANS AND WHY THE CHECK IS EXACT: the Van Buuren definition (FIMD 2nd ed., §4.1.1) — «A missing data pattern is said to be monotone if the variables Y_j can be ordered such that if Y_j is missing then all variables Y_k with k>j are also missing». Equivalently: the sets M_j = {i : Y_ij is missing} are NESTED. The node does NOT search over p! orderings: it checks ONE (increasing |M_j|) and that SUFFICES, because nested sets have increasing cardinality and equinumerous nested sets are EQUAL. The tests verify this against a BRUTE-FORCE search over all p! orderings · THE DEFINITION OF MISSING (explicit, NEVER «just missingness»): a cell is missing when it holds no value. NaN COUNTS as missing (live-verified) while an infinity does NOT — an infinity is a VALUE. For infinity diagnostics -> #248 dp_profile, the n_infinite field · WHY THERE IS A GATE FOR A STRICTLY INCREASING TIME COLUMN: the gap runs and spans are defined ONLY when the row order IS the time order. With an unsorted or DUPLICATED time column — a panel rather than a series — the spans are MEANINGLESS and nothing errors (silently wrong) ⇒ a hard stop; and the axis itself may hold no gaps. The check sorts with a radix order and looks for duplicates, rather than testing sortedness on text, which would depend on the LOCALE · THE RUNS DEPEND ON THE ROW ORDER — the patterns, the counts and the monotonicity do NOT: the tests pin an UNCHANGED mp_pattern result under a RANDOM ROW PERMUTATION. THE ONLY order-dependent field of mp_pattern is first_violating_row inside monotone, which is a ROW INDEX by definition · COLUMN-TYPE GATES — AN ESSENTIAL DIFFERENCE FROM #248: here NO moment is computed and NO coercion happens, so the unusual ATOMIC dtypes (a duration, a time-indexed value, a unit-carrying value, a labelled value) ARE ALLOWED, since the presence test is type-agnostic — whereas #248 BLOCKS them, because its moments would carry unknown units. What is blocked is EXACTLY the structures where the presence test does not return one flag per row: a matrix column and a frame column, which both return a MATRIX; a decomposed timestamp, internally a LIST of nine fields; a nested-list column, where the test looks inside each element rather than at the cell; and a complex column, which is not JSON-safe · POST-CHECKS AS MUTATION GUARDS (STRUCTURALLY impossible to trigger from a valid input; that is why they are SEPARATE functions that the tests call DIRECTLY): the sum of the pattern counts == nrow (the patterns PARTITION the rows); the complete cases derived from the patterns == a direct count; the sum of the run lengths per variable == its number of missing values (the completeness of the rle); rr+rm+mr+mm == nrow in EVERY cell · EDGE-CASE BEHAVIOUR (documented and tested, NEVER an error): NO missing values gives ONE pattern of all ones, n_patterns = 1, any_missing = False, monotone = True (empty sets are trivially nested), zero runs, and mm = 0 everywhere; an ALL-MISSING column gives ONE run with position='all', blank first and last observations, and does NOT break monotonicity; an ALL-MISSING dataset gives ONE pattern of all zeros and n_complete_cases = 0; a single row makes the per-column presence test return a VECTOR rather than a matrix (live-verified) ⇒ an explicit matrix fallback; and a single column makes mp_pairs return zero pairs with the CORRECT shape, rr and mm being 1x1 · a df_handle AND NOT a matrix_handle at the node layer: coercing to a matrix WOULD DROP the NON-NUMERIC columns — that is, it would HIDE exactly the missing values the node exists to count, a silent data loss. These are TERMINAL nodes: nothing is registered and nothing chains onward
Sources: van Buuren, S. «Flexible Imputation of Missing Data», 2nd ed., §4.1.1 — the definition of a MONOTONE pattern: «A missing data pattern is said to be monotone if the variables Y_j can be ordered such that if Y_j is missing then all variables Y_k with k>j are also missing» · the conventional missing-data pattern and pair documentation — «1=observed, 0=missing»; «Rows and columns are sorted in increasing amounts of missing information»; «The last column and row contain row and column counts»; the pattern function draws by default; and for the pairs, rr is «both variables are observed», rm «row observed, column missing», mr the reverse, and mm «both variables are missing». NOTE: that implementation is NOT a dependency of this project and is not installed — the semantics are reproduced, and recorded verbatim in the wrapper's footer · the normative gate spec §3b REJECTED the third-party profiling and missing-data dependencies: we TAKE the feature — implemented on the standard library in the data-profile and missing-pattern nodes — and reject the dependencies, one of which draws by default (a violation of §5) and another of which shadows common verbs; together with §3b gates 2 (no imposed conversion) and 6 (fit/apply externalization) · Little, R.J.A. (1988) «A Test of Missing Completely at Random for Multivariate Data with Missing Values», JASA 83(404), 1198-1202 — the MCAR test is NOT exposed by this node (it requires normality + EM; the autocorrelation of macro panels violates the assumptions, compare §3b gate 4) · wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c01_preparation_prechecks/missingness_patterns) — the explicit definitions (missing, pattern, monotone, gap run), the proof that one candidate ordering suffices, the live-verified edge cases (a single row returning a vector rather than a matrix), and the four post-checks

cards.method: Battery of PARAMETRIC MEAN tests on CROSS-SECTION data: t-test (one sample / two samples Welch or Student pooled / paired) · one-way ANOVA (equal variances, a full ANOVA table) · the one-way Welch (1951) test WITHOUT the equal-variance assumption
cards.when: a FAST MEAN test on CROSS-SECTION data — countries, firms, households, survey respondents — BEFORE a heavy model is thrown at it: «does the sample's mean growth rate differ from 2%?» (tp_t_test one-sample) · «do euro and non-euro differ?» (two-sample; Welch = THE DEFAULT) · «did something change before/after the reform in the SAME units?» (paired) · «do THREE+ regions differ?» (tp_anova for the ANOVA table/eta^2; tp_welch when the variances are NOT equal or the n_i are very unequal)
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES or time-dependent data — a HARD GATE (§3b normative gate 4); the HAC path is #35 (category 07: vcov_hac, vcov_cluster, vcov_panel); NON-NORMAL or VERY SMALL samples -> #251, the rank-based battery; a normality DECISION -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera; TWO CATEGORICAL variables -> #257, chi-squared and Fisher; MULTI-FACTOR, repeated-measures, error-strata, weighted or contrast designs -> ANOTHER family, not exposed here, since this is ONE-WAY only; POST-HOC comparisons (Tukey HSD) -> not exposed; charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies n, mean and sd per group, and the ANOVA table as NUMBERS)

alternatives.criterion: TWO independent samples: Welch-Satterthwaite is the SAFE default, with separate variances; var_equal=True, the pooled Student test with df = n1+n2-2, ONLY when the variances really are equal — and ONLY in the two-sample unpaired design, since in the one-sample and paired designs it is IGNORED SILENTLY ⇒ a hard gate
the SAME units measured TWICE (before/after); it requires EQUAL lengths. ⚠️ The Ljung-Box precheck runs ON THE DIFFERENCES d = x - y (that is where the test's real input lies)
k >= 2 groups AND you want the FULL ANOVA table (df/SS/MS/F/p per term) + eta_squared = SS_group/SS_total + grand_mean; it presupposes EQUAL variances

k >= 2 groups with UNEQUAL variances, and/or very unequal group sizes: Welch (1951) generalises the two-sample Welch test to arbitrarily many samples; it does NOT produce an ANOVA table, only a test record
you want the CLASSICAL F AS A TEST, without the ANOVA table — an identical statistic to tp_anova (pinned in the tests)
normality does NOT hold (#247) or the sample is very small ⇒ the rank-based counterparts of the same designs
the data ARE time-dependent and inference MUST be done: HAC/Newey-West/clustered SE — NOT a bypass of the gate

output_key_fields: tp_t_test: a long-format test record -> method/statistic/statistic_name/parameter (df)/p_value/estimate/conf_low/conf_high/conf_level/null_value/stderr/alternative + alpha/reject/decision in {reject_H0, fail_to_reject_H0} + design in {one_sample, two_sample_welch, two_sample_student_pooled, paired} + paired/var_equal/mu/n_used/n_na/na_action/sample_names

tp_anova: anova_table = {term = c('group','Residuals'), df, sum_sq, mean_sq, f_value, p_value} AS NUMERIC COLUMNS (chart-data) + statistic(F)/parameter(num df, denom df)/p_value/alpha/reject/decision + eta_squared (= SS_group/SS_total) + ss_total/df_residual/grand_mean
tp_welch: a long-format test record (the statistic is F, and the parameters are the numerator df plus a NON-INTEGER Welch-Satterthwaite denominator df) + test in {oneway_welch, oneway_f} + var_equal
tp_anova/tp_welch (shared): levels (CANONICALLY sorted) / k / n / n_na / n_by_group / mean_by_group / sd_by_group / grand_mean / response / group — the per-group chart-data

ALL: cross_section_gate = {groups, lb_statistic, lb_p_value, lb_lag, n, n_na, gate_alpha, ordered, branch ∈ {ljung-box-tested, skipped-by-declaration}, tested, decision ∈ {pass, pass-untested, pass-unordered}} — the NUMERIC diagnostics of normative gate 4, ALWAYS in the output
interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (the normative gate spec §3b) — CROSS-SECTION ONLY: AUTOCORRELATION INFLATES THE TYPE I ERROR, since it shrinks the variance estimator, giving spuriously significant p-values. EVERY exported function calls the SHARED cross-section gate (written ONCE in the shared gates module, and shared with #251 and #257; NEVER copied). Two branches, BOTH a hard stop: (a) an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type; (b) a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5), the DOCUMENTED default of the residual check (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4; the fitted-parameter count is 0, because the input is DATA rather than residuals) — a rejection at alpha stops the call. The message points EXPLICITLY at the HAC path, #35 in category 07. A CONSEQUENCE: the minimum n rises to 3, and for n < 5 the rule gives a lag below 1 ⇒ an explicit tested=False with decision='pass-untested' (NEVER a silent pass)

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — DECOUPLED FROM THE TEST'S alpha: alpha determines ONLY the reject/decision of the output; the level of the cross-section gate is ITS OWN argument (gate_alpha). WHY: the Ljung-Box precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha, so BY CONSTRUCTION it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input (a false block). LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1% and n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for gate_alpha = 0.01/0.05/0.10. With the level tied, a «t-test at 10%» would raise the gate's false-block rate to ~10% WITHOUT any statistical justification

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: the Ljung-Box statistic is A FUNCTION OF THE ORDER — LIVE-VERIFIED that THE SAME 60 numbers pass unsorted and are BLOCKED once sorted, which is exactly how a cross-section file arrives (countries alphabetically, firms by size); the mean tests themselves are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT. ordered=False means the user DECLARES that the rows carry no order, the whiteness branch is SKIPPED EXPLICITLY (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered', tested=False everywhere), and ALL the structural checks — non-finite values, n>=3, zero variance — REMAIN. The time-indexed-type rejection ALWAYS APPLIES (branch='class-rejected'). Supplying lb_lag TOGETHER WITH ordered=False is a hard stop: it is contradictory, and would otherwise be a silent no-op

WHERE EXACTLY THE GATE RUNS (statistically precise, not mechanical): one-sample -> on x; two-sample -> on x AND y SEPARATELY (each sample has its own mean and variance); paired -> ONLY on the DIFFERENCES d = x - y (autocorrelation that CANCELS in the difference does NOT inflate the paired test's Type I error — a gate on x/y would reject VALID analyses); anova/welch -> PER GROUP (a named list per level)

⚠️ A DOCUMENTED LIMIT OF THE GATE: in tp_anova/tp_welch the response column is split into groups BEFORE it reaches the gate, and `[` on a series returns an UNCLASSED numeric ⇒ the «time-series class» branch does NOT see a series column inside a data_frame. The SUBSTANTIVE branch (Ljung-Box PER GROUP) stays fully active. In tp_t_test the vector arrives AS IS ⇒ both branches are active (covered in the tests)

SILENTLY WRONG (THE MOST SERIOUS, live-verified the engine): with a NUMERIC or LOGICAL grouping column aov does NOT do an ANOVA — it does a LINEAR REGRESSION (Df = 1 instead of k-1) WITHOUT any error/warning; oneway_test likewise accepts numeric groups ⇒ a HARD GATE: the column must be a factor or character (convert with factor EXPLICITLY)

SILENTLY WRONG: the t-test on NON-NUMERIC input does NOT error — it emits ONLY warnings, that the argument is not numeric and that the coercion introduced blanks, and returns a blank; with the warnings muffled, as the call path does, it would pass COMPLETELY silently ⇒ a hard input-type gate

SILENTLY WRONG (INCONSISTENT BEHAVIOUR ACROSS TESTS): on an infinity or a NaN both the t-test AND the one-way Welch test do NOT error — they return a NaN statistic and a NaN p-value (the documentation: «no longer errors and returns a still not very useful result»); the ANOVA DOES error ⇒ ONE uniform policy, a hard stop everywhere

SILENTLY WRONG: the pooled Student test does NOT error when one sample has n = 1, whose variance is not even defined, and still returns a p-value ⇒ n >= 2 is checked PER SAMPLE explicitly; and a group of size 1 in an ANOVA leaves df_residual = 0, so the table comes back WITHOUT the «F value» and «Pr(>F)» columns and WITHOUT an error — hence an explicit shape check rather than a silent empty result

SILENTLY WRONG (ZERO VARIANCE — TWO DIFFERENT POLICIES): tp_welch (zero_var='any') weights by n_i/s_i², so ONE SINGLE constant group gives a NaN statistic and a NaN p-value, while with var_equal=True the F is infinite and p is 0; tp_anova (zero_var='all'): when ALL the groups are constant the residual sum of squares is around 1e-31 and the ANOVA returns an F near 1.83e+31 with p near 4.4e-93 — numerical garbage — or a NaN F when the whole of y is constant. The gate runs BEFORE the shared cross-section gate, so that the message stays test-specific

AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the t-test and the ANOVA remove gaps SILENTLY — the documentation says missing values are silently removed, in pairs when the design is paired, and the ANOVA drops incomplete rows by default ⇒ the reported n is NOT the input n, and the design's BALANCE is altered. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT and a hard stop, while 'omit' removes EXPLICITLY and WITH a count — n_na is always in the output, dropping pairs in the paired design and ROWS in the ANOVA and Welch routes

NO formula ON THE SURFACE (a SECURITY rule): the one-way design has EXACTLY one term, so a formula adds no expressiveness — only attack surface. The user supplies COLUMN NAMES as strings, which are validated against the frame's columns and used ONLY as a lookup key; the model's formula is LITERALLY written in the code. There is ZERO path from a user string to a parse or an evaluation. The ANOVA table is returned with CANONICAL labels, term = ('group', 'Residuals'), plus the raw row names, so the frontend never sees the internal names

DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG (closed-form t/F + Welch-Satterthwaite df) ⇒ NO seed. The level order is CANONICAL — sort(unique(g)), NOT order of appearance — and the factor is built EXPLICITLY in that order, so that the ANOVA table, the mean_by_group/sd_by_group and the Welch statistic do NOT depend on the row sorting (pinned in the tests: identical over 2 runs AND over shuffled rows)

POST-CHECKS (a DEFENSIVE «second net» — with the pre-gates active they are NOT triggered by any public call, which is why the tests exercise them directly): the result really is a test record, or an ANOVA fit; the statistic is finite and of length 1; the p-value is finite and within [0,1]; df_residual >= 1; and the ANOVA table carries ALL five columns and EXACTLY two rows
sources: the t-test routine's documentation — missing values are silently removed, in pairs when the design is paired; when the variances are not assumed equal, each group's variance is estimated separately and the Welch modification to the degrees of freedom is applied; «'mu' must be a single number»; «'conf_level' must be a single number between 0 and 1»; «not enough 'x' observations»; «data are essentially constant»

the one-way test routine's documentation — with equal variances assumed it performs a simple F test for the equality of means in a one-way analysis of variance, and otherwise «an approximate method of Welch (1951) is used, which generalizes the commonly known 2-sample Welch test to the case of arbitrarily many samples»; plus the ANOVA routine (the one-way design and its missing-value handling) and its summary table (Df | Sum Sq | Mean Sq | F value | Pr(>F))

Welch, B.L. (1951) «On the Comparison of Several Mean Values: An Alternative Approach», Biometrika 38(3/4), 330, doi:10.2307/2332579 — the reference that the oneway_test routine ITSELF gives for the unequal-variance test

Ljung, G.M. & Box, G.E.P. (1978) «On a Measure of Lack of Fit in Time Series Models», Biometrika 65(2), 297-303, doi:10.1093/biomet/65.2.297 — the whiteness precheck of the shared gate; the Box.test routine's documentation Note: «Missing values are not handled» (which is why the gate blocks NaN/Inf itself)

Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G., «Forecasting: Principles and Practice», 3rd ed., §5.4 — the rule lag = min(10, n/5); IDENTICAL to the DOCUMENTED default of checkresiduals (live-verified help: «If missing, it is set to min(10, n/5) for non-seasonal data, and min(2m, n/5) for seasonal data»). Cross-section ⇒ there is no seasonal period m ⇒ the 2m branch never applies

the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 4 (cross-section-only for t-test/ANOVA/Wilcoxon/KW/Friedman/chi-square; «to be written ONCE as a shared helper, not 3 times») + the live-verified gates «t_test: not enough 'x' observations · data are essentially constant»

the project's security rule (the prohibition on evaluating user-supplied expressions — why no formula is exposed) + the charter §5 (charts only in the frontend; blocked-by-gate as a first-class state)

wrapper footers IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c01_preparation_prechecks/battery_parametric_mean and the shared gates module) — EVERY silently-wrong case is live-verified on the engine with the EXACT messages/values (aov as a linear regression with numeric groups; F ~ 1.83e+31 / p ~ 4.4e-93 under zero variances; an ANOVA table without F/Pr(>F) when df_residual = 0)
precondition_tools: c01_preparation_prechecks/battery_normality_edf.nt_normality_battery # (#247) a normality DECISION BEFORE you choose parametric vs #251
c01_preparation_prechecks/profiling_quality_report.dp_quality_flags # (#248) constant columns / Inf / few_rows — EXACTLY the gates that will block here
tp_welch # run BOTH: if tp_anova and tp_welch disagree, the EQUAL-VARIANCE assumption is the problem

[#250] Battery of PARAMETRIC MEAN tests on CROSS-SECTION data: t-test (one sample / two samples Welch or Student pooled / paired) · one-way ANOVA (equal variances, a full ANOVA table) · the one-way Welch (1951) test WITHOUT the equal-variance assumption
Category: 01-preparation-prechecks
Nodes: tp_t_test · tp_anova · tp_welch
WHEN: a FAST MEAN test on CROSS-SECTION data — countries, firms, households, survey respondents — BEFORE a heavy model is thrown at it: «does the sample's mean growth rate differ from 2%?» (tp_t_test one-sample) · «do euro and non-euro differ?» (two-sample; Welch = THE DEFAULT) · «did something change before/after the reform in the SAME units?» (paired) · «do THREE+ regions differ?» (tp_anova for the ANOVA table/eta^2; tp_welch when the variances are NOT equal or the n_i are very unequal)
NOT when: TIME SERIES or time-dependent data — a HARD GATE (§3b normative gate 4); the HAC path is #35 (category 07: vcov_hac, vcov_cluster, vcov_panel); NON-NORMAL or VERY SMALL samples -> #251, the rank-based battery; a normality DECISION -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera; TWO CATEGORICAL variables -> #257, chi-squared and Fisher; MULTI-FACTOR, repeated-measures, error-strata, weighted or contrast designs -> ANOTHER family, not exposed here, since this is ONE-WAY only; POST-HOC comparisons (Tukey HSD) -> not exposed; charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies n, mean and sd per group, and the ANOVA table as NUMBERS)
Alternatives: tp_t_test with var_equal=False — the DEFAULT (TWO independent samples: Welch-Satterthwaite is the SAFE default, with separate variances; var_equal=True, the pooled Student test with df = n1+n2-2, ONLY when the variances really are equal — and ONLY in the two-sample unpaired design, since in the one-sample and paired designs it is IGNORED SILENTLY ⇒ a hard gate) · tp_t_test with paired=True (the SAME units measured TWICE (before/after); it requires EQUAL lengths. ⚠️ The Ljung-Box precheck runs ON THE DIFFERENCES d = x - y (that is where the test's real input lies)) · tp_anova (k >= 2 groups AND you want the FULL ANOVA table (df/SS/MS/F/p per term) + eta_squared = SS_group/SS_total + grand_mean; it presupposes EQUAL variances) · tp_welch with var_equal=False (k >= 2 groups with UNEQUAL variances, and/or very unequal group sizes: Welch (1951) generalises the two-sample Welch test to arbitrarily many samples; it does NOT produce an ANOVA table, only a test record) · tp_welch with var_equal=True (you want the CLASSICAL F AS A TEST, without the ANOVA table — an identical statistic to tp_anova (pinned in the tests)) · #251 tn_wilcox / tn_kruskal (normality does NOT hold (#247) or the sample is very small ⇒ the rank-based counterparts of the same designs) · #35 HAC / robust standard errors (cat 07) (the data ARE time-dependent and inference MUST be done: HAC/Newey-West/clustered SE — NOT a bypass of the gate)

WHY: the Ljung-Box precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha, so BY CONSTRUCTION it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input (a false block). LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1% and n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for gate_alpha = 0.01/0.05/0.10. The time-indexed-type rejection ALWAYS APPLIES (branch='class-rejected'). The gate runs BEFORE the shared cross-section gate, so that the message stays test-specific · AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the t-test and the ANOVA remove gaps SILENTLY — the documentation says missing values are silently removed, in pairs when the design is paired, and the ANOVA drops incomplete rows by default ⇒ the reported n is NOT the input n, and the design's BALANCE is altered. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT and a hard stop, while 'omit' removes EXPLICITLY and WITH a count — n_na is always in the output, dropping pairs in the paired design and ROWS in the ANOVA and Welch routes · NO formula ON THE SURFACE (a SECURITY rule): the one-way design has EXACTLY one term, so a formula adds no expressiveness — only attack surface. The user supplies COLUMN NAMES as strings, which are validated against the frame's columns and used ONLY as a lookup key; the model's formula is LITERALLY written in the code. There is ZERO path from a user string to a parse or an evaluation. The ANOVA table is returned with CANONICAL labels, term = ('group', 'Residuals'), plus the raw row names, so the frontend never sees the internal names · DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG (closed-form t/F + Welch-Satterthwaite df) ⇒ NO seed. The level order is CANONICAL — sort(unique(g)), NOT order of appearance — and the factor is built EXPLICITLY in that order, so that the ANOVA table, the mean_by_group/sd_by_group and the Welch statistic do NOT depend on the row sorting (pinned in the tests: identical over 2 runs AND over shuffled rows) · POST-CHECKS (a DEFENSIVE «second net» — with the pre-gates active they are NOT triggered by any public call, which is why the tests exercise them directly): the result really is a test record, or an ANOVA fit; the statistic is finite and of length 1; the p-value is finite and within [0,1]; df_residual >= 1; and the ANOVA table carries ALL five columns and EXACTLY two rows

cards.method: Battery of NON-PARAMETRIC (rank-based) tests on CROSS-SECTION data: Wilcoxon signed rank (one sample / paired) & rank sum = Mann-Whitney (two independent) with an optional non-parametric CI + Hodges-Lehmann · Kruskal-Wallis (k >= 2 independent groups) · Friedman (unreplicated complete block design)
cards.when: the rank-based COUNTERPARTS of the parametric battery #250, when NORMALITY does NOT hold (#247) or the sample is very small: TWO independent groups of countries or firms -> tn_wilcox (rank sum, Mann-Whitney); BEFORE and AFTER on the SAME units -> tn_wilcox with paired=True, the signed rank of the differences; k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups -> tn_kruskal, the non-parametric one-way ANOVA; k methods or treatments MEASURED ON THE SAME blocks (say 3 forecasting methods across 6 countries) -> tn_friedman, the non-parametric repeated-measures test
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES or time-dependent data — a HARD GATE (§3b normative gate 4); the HAC path is #35 (category 07); normality DOES hold and you want MORE power, an ANOVA table or an eta² -> #250; TWO CATEGORICAL variables, a contingency table with chi-squared, Fisher or Cramér's V -> #257; a normality DECISION -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera; a Friedman test WEIGHTED by the block range — NOT exposed, being a DIFFERENT test that would need its own card; an INCOMPLETE or REPLICATED block design (Friedman requires EXACTLY one observation per block-and-group pair); charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies rank_means, rank_sums and within_block_ranks as NUMBERS)

alternatives.criterion: ONE sample: signed rank; H0 = the distribution of x is SYMMETRIC about mu

alternatives.alt: tn_wilcox with a second sample, paired=False
alternatives.criterion: TWO INDEPENDENT samples: rank sum / Mann-Whitney; H0 = the distributions differ by a location shift equal to mu
PAIRED measurements on the SAME units, of EQUAL length; equivalent to the signed rank of the differences — the gaps are removed PAIRWISE

you want a MAGNITUDE, not only a p-value: a non-parametric CI + the Hodges-Lehmann estimator (pseudomedian or difference in location). ⚠️ At small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (conf_level_achieved) and the interval may come out infinite (conf_int_finite)
k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups (list/matrix/data_frame): H0 = the same location parameter in every group; df = k-1

the k groups are NOT independent: they were ALL measured in EVERY block (country/unit); the ranks are computed WITHIN a block ⇒ the block effect is removed. WIDE (blocks x groups) or LONG (y + groups + blocks)
normality DOES hold: more power, an ANOVA table, eta^2 and confidence intervals for the means
NEITHER of the two variables is continuous — two CATEGORICAL answers per unit ⇒ a contingency table, not a comparison of medians
the data ARE time-dependent and inference MUST be done: HAC/clustered SE — NOT a bypass of the gate

output_key_fields: SHARED: tests = a ONE-row long-format record (test/method/statistic_name/statistic/(df)/p_value/alternative/n_*/n_omitted/exact_used/normal_approximation/ties_present…) + the same fields also as atomic scalars

tn_wilcox: test ∈ {rank_sum, signed_rank_one_sample, signed_rank_paired} + statistic (W or V) + p_value + mu + rank_means/rank_sums/group_sizes (chart-data: groups 'x','y' in the rank sum; 'positive','negative','zero' in the signed rank) + n_x/n_y/n_omitted
tn_wilcox (exact/asymptotic transparency): exact_requested / exact_used / normal_approximation / continuity_correction (READ FROM the stats method string ITSELF) + ties_present + zeroes_present
tn_wilcox with conf_int=True: conf_int + conf_level as REQUESTED + conf_level_achieved, as actually attained, + conf_int_finite + estimate and estimate_name (Hodges-Lehmann)
tn_kruskal: statistic (Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared) + df (= k-1) + p_value + rank_means/rank_sums/group_sizes PER GROUP (chart-data) + groups/n_groups/n_total/n_omitted/ties_present

tn_friedman: statistic (Friedman chi-squared) + df (= k-1) + p_value + rank_means/rank_sums (WITHIN-BLOCK ranks per group — chart-data) + within_block_ranks (a blocks x groups NUMERIC matrix) + groups/blocks/n_groups/n_blocks/n_blocks_dropped + input_form ∈ {wide, long}

ALL: cross_section_gate = {groups, statistic, p_value, lag, n, n_na, gate_alpha, ordered, branch ∈ {ljung-box-tested, skipped-by-declaration}, tested, decision ∈ {pass, pass-untested, pass-unordered}} — the NUMERIC diagnostics of normative gate 4
interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (the normative gate spec §3b) — CROSS-SECTION ONLY: all three tests presuppose INDEPENDENT observations, and autocorrelation INFLATES THE TYPE I ERROR ⇒ spuriously significant p-values. The rule is implemented ONCE in the SHARED cross-section gate (the shared gates module, shared with #250 and #257) and is CALLED here, NEVER copied: (a) an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type and (b) a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5), the DOCUMENTED default of the residual check (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4). The message points EXPLICITLY at the HAC path, #35 in category 07 (vcov_hac, vcov_cluster, vcov_panel). LIVE-VERIFIED: the Friedman routine accepts a time-indexed matrix WITHOUT COMPLAINT — ONLY the gate stops it. A CONSEQUENCE: the minimum n PER GROUP rises to 3, deliberately stricter than the underlying routine

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — THE LEVEL BELONGS EXCLUSIVELY TO THE GATE: the three non-parametric tests have no alpha of their own (no decision column), which is why the argument is called gate_alpha and NOT alpha. The precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input; LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1%, n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for 0.01/0.05/0.10

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: the Ljung-Box statistic depends on the ORDER (live-verified: the same 60 numbers pass unsorted and are blocked once sorted) whereas the three rank tests are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT — Friedman with respect to the order of the BLOCKS. ordered=False omits the whiteness branch explicitly (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered'), while ALL the structural checks and the time-indexed-type rejection (branch='class-rejected') stay ACTIVE. Supplying lb_lag together with ordered=False is a hard stop

WHY NOTHING IS CONVERTED BEFORE THE GATE: the input's TYPE must survive INTACT as far as the gate, which is the SOLE owner of the rule rejecting time-indexed input; hence the gate comes LAST before the test, and the conversion happens AFTER. A KNOWN LIMITATION: when na_action='omit' or 'drop_blocks' REMOVES values, the subset loses its type ⇒ a time-indexed input WITH gaps, plus an explicit omit, is checked only by the whiteness branch; and in the LONG form of tn_friedman the gate sees the RESHAPED wide matrix, which is correct, since a stacked long vector is NOT a time series

AN INCONSISTENT documented policy FOR NON-FINITE VALUES (live-verified): the wilcox_test routine says of x/y «Non-finite (e.g., infinite or missing) values will be omitted» — but in the TWO-SAMPLE branch the Inf values are KEPT as «very large» (the release notes) ⇒ THE SAME Inf changes meaning depending on the branch. A hard gate: NO Inf/-Inf in any input

AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routines remove gaps SILENTLY (live-verified: a gap in one sample runs normally) and the Friedman routine removes WHOLE BLOCKS («if y contains NAs, corresponding blocks are removed») ⇒ silent data loss. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT hard stop, 'omit' covers the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routes and works PAIRWISE in the paired design, and 'drop_blocks' covers Friedman — ALWAYS with a count (n_omitted, or n_blocks_dropped) and a check that at least two blocks remain

A DOCUMENTED CHANGE IN the reference >= 4.6.0 (A DEPARTURE FROM OLD KNOWLEDGE, live-verified): there is no longer a silent fallback to the normal approximation with the warning «cannot compute exact p-value with ties» — «If there are ties, exact inference is performed using the conditional/permutation distribution given the observed ranks, using an implementation of the Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm» (the wilcox_test routine; the reference NEWS 4.6.0, contributed by Torsten Hothorn). The node EXPOSES IT anyway as FIELDS (exact_used/normal_approximation/continuity_correction read FROM the method string; the release notes: «If exact computations are used, the result now has 'exact' in the method element») ⇒ if a future version falls back again, IT IS VISIBLE in the JSON instead of hidden

THE SAME SAMPLE, TWO V VALUES (a live finding in the engine): in the signed-rank test with ZERO differences the statistic is built in TWO WAYS — the exact route ranks the absolute differences with the zeros INSIDE and sums the ranks of the positive ones, while the asymptotic route DROPS the zeros FIRST. MEASURED on x = (0.6, 1, 1.4, 0.5, 1.3, 1.2, 1.3, 1.9) against mu = 1: V = 22 on the exact route against 17 on the asymptotic one. The node exposes zeroes_present and exact_used TOGETHER, and builds rank_means and rank_sums BY THE PATH THAT ACTUALLY RAN

A POST-CHECK OF THE IDENTITY between the chart data and the statistic (if it breaks, the frontend would draw NUMBERS OTHER than the p-value ⇒ a hard stop): for the two-sample rank sum, the rank sum of x minus n_x(n_x+1)/2 equals W, since the reference subtracts m(m+1)/2; for the signed rank, the positive rank sum equals V; for Kruskal-Wallis, the rank sums total N(N+1)/2; and for Friedman they total n_blocks * k(k+1)/2. The ranks are reproduced EXACTLY as the reference builds them — the same rank rounding, and the same shifted concatenation in the two-sample case

SILENTLY WRONG DEGENERACIES (live-verified, all hard-gated): ALL differences from mu zero -> the signed rank degenerates to V = 0, p = 1 WITHOUT an error; a completely constant pooled sample -> rank sum p = 1 / kruskal_test chi-squared = NaN & p = NaN WITHOUT an error (a 0/0 division in the tie correction); EVERY block with identical values -> friedman_test NaN/NaN WITHOUT an error

A SILENT DROP BY stats THAT IS AVOIDED STRUCTURALLY: kruskal_test documents «g is ignored with a warning if x is a list» ⇒ here the input is ALWAYS NORMALISED to a named list of groups (list/matrix/data_frame accepted), so that g can NEVER be ignored silently. Group names: NON-EMPTY and UNIQUE

FRIEDMAN IS AN UNREPLICATED COMPLETE BLOCK DESIGN («exactly one observation in y for each combination of levels of groups and blocks») ⇒ our own gates in the LONG form: NO REPLICATION and NO EMPTY block-and-group pair; at least 2 columns AND at least 2 rows, otherwise the routine throws a cryptic dimension error; and blank or empty labels are forbidden, since neither the groups nor the blocks may carry them. The ranks are WITHIN-BLOCK and are NOT compared across blocks

AN INTERVAL ONLY WHERE IT IS DOCUMENTED: conf_int and conf_level exist ONLY in tn_wilcox — the Kruskal-Wallis and Friedman routines document neither an interval nor an estimate, and nothing is invented. A live-verified trap: at small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (0.95 becomes 0.9609375) and the interval may come out (-Inf, Inf) WITHOUT a warning ⇒ conf_level, conf_level_achieved and conf_int_finite are exposed EXPLICITLY

digits_rank: when finite, the ranks are computed on the values rounded to that many significant digits — it stabilises tie detection when differences of order 1e-16 would hide them («For stability reasons, it may be advisable to use rounded data or to set the rank rounding to 7 significant digits»). The continuity correction is exposed ONLY as a boolean: its INTEGER form, 0 to 3 Edgeworth terms, is NOT recorded in the method string (live-verified: a value of 2 produces THE SAME «with continuity correction» text) ⇒ the output would be UNVERIFIABLE, and a numeric argument kind would turn True into 1, meaning «one Edgeworth term» — a silent change of meaning

DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG path — no seed, no Monte-Carlo/permutation simulation. The exact distributions are closed-form (psignrank/pwilcox) or, under ties, the DETERMINISTIC Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (the wrapper AND the node path)

[#251] Battery of NON-PARAMETRIC (rank-based) tests on CROSS-SECTION data: Wilcoxon signed rank (one sample / paired) & rank sum = Mann-Whitney (two independent) with an optional non-parametric CI + Hodges-Lehmann · Kruskal-Wallis (k >= 2 independent groups) · Friedman (unreplicated complete block design)
Category: 01-preparation-prechecks
Nodes: tn_wilcox · tn_kruskal · tn_friedman
WHEN: the rank-based COUNTERPARTS of the parametric battery #250, when NORMALITY does NOT hold (#247) or the sample is very small: TWO independent groups of countries or firms -> tn_wilcox (rank sum, Mann-Whitney); BEFORE and AFTER on the SAME units -> tn_wilcox with paired=True, the signed rank of the differences; k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups -> tn_kruskal, the non-parametric one-way ANOVA; k methods or treatments MEASURED ON THE SAME blocks (say 3 forecasting methods across 6 countries) -> tn_friedman, the non-parametric repeated-measures test
NOT when: TIME SERIES or time-dependent data — a HARD GATE (§3b normative gate 4); the HAC path is #35 (category 07); normality DOES hold and you want MORE power, an ANOVA table or an eta² -> #250; TWO CATEGORICAL variables, a contingency table with chi-squared, Fisher or Cramér's V -> #257; a normality DECISION -> #247, or #1 Jarque-Bera; a Friedman test WEIGHTED by the block range — NOT exposed, being a DIFFERENT test that would need its own card; an INCOMPLETE or REPLICATED block design (Friedman requires EXACTLY one observation per block-and-group pair); charts (the frontend, §5 — the node supplies rank_means, rank_sums and within_block_ranks as NUMBERS)
Alternatives: tn_wilcox with no second sample (ONE sample: signed rank; H0 = the distribution of x is SYMMETRIC about mu) · tn_wilcox with a second sample, paired=False (TWO INDEPENDENT samples: rank sum / Mann-Whitney; H0 = the distributions differ by a location shift equal to mu) · tn_wilcox with paired=True (PAIRED measurements on the SAME units, of EQUAL length; equivalent to the signed rank of the differences — the gaps are removed PAIRWISE) · tn_wilcox with conf_int=True (you want a MAGNITUDE, not only a p-value: a non-parametric CI + the Hodges-Lehmann estimator (pseudomedian or difference in location). ⚠️ At small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (conf_level_achieved) and the interval may come out infinite (conf_int_finite)) · tn_kruskal (k >= 2 INDEPENDENT groups (list/matrix/data_frame): H0 = the same location parameter in every group; df = k-1) · tn_friedman (the k groups are NOT independent: they were ALL measured in EVERY block (country/unit); the ranks are computed WITHIN a block ⇒ the block effect is removed. WIDE (blocks x groups) or LONG (y + groups + blocks)) · #250 tp_t_test / tp_anova / tp_welch (normality DOES hold: more power, an ANOVA table, eta^2 and confidence intervals for the means) · #257 ca_chisq / ca_fisher (NEITHER of the two variables is continuous — two CATEGORICAL answers per unit ⇒ a contingency table, not a comparison of medians) · #35 HAC / robust standard errors (cat 07) (the data ARE time-dependent and inference MUST be done: HAC/clustered SE — NOT a bypass of the gate)
Output: SHARED: tests = a ONE-row long-format record (test/method/statistic_name/statistic/(df)/p_value/alternative/n_*/n_omitted/exact_used/normal_approximation/ties_present…) + the same fields also as atomic scalars · tn_wilcox: test ∈ {rank_sum, signed_rank_one_sample, signed_rank_paired} + statistic (W or V) + p_value + mu + rank_means/rank_sums/group_sizes (chart-data: groups 'x','y' in the rank sum; 'positive','negative','zero' in the signed rank) + n_x/n_y/n_omitted · tn_wilcox (exact/asymptotic transparency): exact_requested / exact_used / normal_approximation / continuity_correction (READ FROM the stats method string ITSELF) + ties_present + zeroes_present · tn_wilcox with conf_int=True: conf_int + conf_level as REQUESTED + conf_level_achieved, as actually attained, + conf_int_finite + estimate and estimate_name (Hodges-Lehmann) · tn_kruskal: statistic (Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared) + df (= k-1) + p_value + rank_means/rank_sums/group_sizes PER GROUP (chart-data) + groups/n_groups/n_total/n_omitted/ties_present · tn_friedman: statistic (Friedman chi-squared) + df (= k-1) + p_value + rank_means/rank_sums (WITHIN-BLOCK ranks per group — chart-data) + within_block_ranks (a blocks x groups NUMERIC matrix) + groups/blocks/n_groups/n_blocks/n_blocks_dropped + input_form ∈ {wide, long} · ALL: cross_section_gate = {groups, statistic, p_value, lag, n, n_na, gate_alpha, ordered, branch ∈ {ljung-box-tested, skipped-by-declaration}, tested, decision ∈ {pass, pass-untested, pass-unordered}} — the NUMERIC diagnostics of normative gate 4
Pitfalls: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (the normative gate spec §3b) — CROSS-SECTION ONLY: all three tests presuppose INDEPENDENT observations, and autocorrelation INFLATES THE TYPE I ERROR ⇒ spuriously significant p-values. The rule is implemented ONCE in the SHARED cross-section gate (the shared gates module, shared with #250 and #257) and is CALLED here, NEVER copied: (a) an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type and (b) a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5), the DOCUMENTED default of the residual check (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4). The message points EXPLICITLY at the HAC path, #35 in category 07 (vcov_hac, vcov_cluster, vcov_panel). LIVE-VERIFIED: the Friedman routine accepts a time-indexed matrix WITHOUT COMPLAINT — ONLY the gate stops it. A CONSEQUENCE: the minimum n PER GROUP rises to 3, deliberately stricter than the underlying routine · gate_alpha (default 0.05) — THE LEVEL BELONGS EXCLUSIVELY TO THE GATE: the three non-parametric tests have no alpha of their own (no decision column), which is why the argument is called gate_alpha and NOT alpha. The precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input; LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1%, n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for 0.01/0.05/0.10 · ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: the Ljung-Box statistic depends on the ORDER (live-verified: the same 60 numbers pass unsorted and are blocked once sorted) whereas the three rank tests are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT — Friedman with respect to the order of the BLOCKS. ordered=False omits the whiteness branch explicitly (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered'), while ALL the structural checks and the time-indexed-type rejection (branch='class-rejected') stay ACTIVE. Supplying lb_lag together with ordered=False is a hard stop · WHY NOTHING IS CONVERTED BEFORE THE GATE: the input's TYPE must survive INTACT as far as the gate, which is the SOLE owner of the rule rejecting time-indexed input; hence the gate comes LAST before the test, and the conversion happens AFTER. A KNOWN LIMITATION: when na_action='omit' or 'drop_blocks' REMOVES values, the subset loses its type ⇒ a time-indexed input WITH gaps, plus an explicit omit, is checked only by the whiteness branch; and in the LONG form of tn_friedman the gate sees the RESHAPED wide matrix, which is correct, since a stacked long vector is NOT a time series · AN INCONSISTENT documented policy FOR NON-FINITE VALUES (live-verified): the wilcox_test routine says of x/y «Non-finite (e.g., infinite or missing) values will be omitted» — but in the TWO-SAMPLE branch the Inf values are KEPT as «very large» (the release notes) ⇒ THE SAME Inf changes meaning depending on the branch. A hard gate: NO Inf/-Inf in any input · AN EXPLICIT MISSING-VALUE POLICY: the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routines remove gaps SILENTLY (live-verified: a gap in one sample runs normally) and the Friedman routine removes WHOLE BLOCKS («if y contains NAs, corresponding blocks are removed») ⇒ silent data loss. Here: na_action='fail' is the DEFAULT hard stop, 'omit' covers the rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis routes and works PAIRWISE in the paired design, and 'drop_blocks' covers Friedman — ALWAYS with a count (n_omitted, or n_blocks_dropped) and a check that at least two blocks remain · A DOCUMENTED CHANGE IN the reference >= 4.6.0 (A DEPARTURE FROM OLD KNOWLEDGE, live-verified): there is no longer a silent fallback to the normal approximation with the warning «cannot compute exact p-value with ties» — «If there are ties, exact inference is performed using the conditional/permutation distribution given the observed ranks, using an implementation of the Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm» (the wilcox_test routine; the reference NEWS 4.6.0, contributed by Torsten Hothorn). The node EXPOSES IT anyway as FIELDS (exact_used/normal_approximation/continuity_correction read FROM the method string; the release notes: «If exact computations are used, the result now has 'exact' in the method element») ⇒ if a future version falls back again, IT IS VISIBLE in the JSON instead of hidden · THE SAME SAMPLE, TWO V VALUES (a live finding in the engine): in the signed-rank test with ZERO differences the statistic is built in TWO WAYS — the exact route ranks the absolute differences with the zeros INSIDE and sums the ranks of the positive ones, while the asymptotic route DROPS the zeros FIRST. MEASURED on x = (0.6, 1, 1.4, 0.5, 1.3, 1.2, 1.3, 1.9) against mu = 1: V = 22 on the exact route against 17 on the asymptotic one. The node exposes zeroes_present and exact_used TOGETHER, and builds rank_means and rank_sums BY THE PATH THAT ACTUALLY RAN · A POST-CHECK OF THE IDENTITY between the chart data and the statistic (if it breaks, the frontend would draw NUMBERS OTHER than the p-value ⇒ a hard stop): for the two-sample rank sum, the rank sum of x minus n_x(n_x+1)/2 equals W, since the reference subtracts m(m+1)/2; for the signed rank, the positive rank sum equals V; for Kruskal-Wallis, the rank sums total N(N+1)/2; and for Friedman they total n_blocks * k(k+1)/2. The ranks are reproduced EXACTLY as the reference builds them — the same rank rounding, and the same shifted concatenation in the two-sample case · SILENTLY WRONG DEGENERACIES (live-verified, all hard-gated): ALL differences from mu zero -> the signed rank degenerates to V = 0, p = 1 WITHOUT an error; a completely constant pooled sample -> rank sum p = 1 / kruskal_test chi-squared = NaN & p = NaN WITHOUT an error (a 0/0 division in the tie correction); EVERY block with identical values -> friedman_test NaN/NaN WITHOUT an error · A SILENT DROP BY stats THAT IS AVOIDED STRUCTURALLY: kruskal_test documents «g is ignored with a warning if x is a list» ⇒ here the input is ALWAYS NORMALISED to a named list of groups (list/matrix/data_frame accepted), so that g can NEVER be ignored silently. Group names: NON-EMPTY and UNIQUE · FRIEDMAN IS AN UNREPLICATED COMPLETE BLOCK DESIGN («exactly one observation in y for each combination of levels of groups and blocks») ⇒ our own gates in the LONG form: NO REPLICATION and NO EMPTY block-and-group pair; at least 2 columns AND at least 2 rows, otherwise the routine throws a cryptic dimension error; and blank or empty labels are forbidden, since neither the groups nor the blocks may carry them. The ranks are WITHIN-BLOCK and are NOT compared across blocks · AN INTERVAL ONLY WHERE IT IS DOCUMENTED: conf_int and conf_level exist ONLY in tn_wilcox — the Kruskal-Wallis and Friedman routines document neither an interval nor an estimate, and nothing is invented. A live-verified trap: at small n the ACHIEVED level differs from the requested one (0.95 becomes 0.9609375) and the interval may come out (-Inf, Inf) WITHOUT a warning ⇒ conf_level, conf_level_achieved and conf_int_finite are exposed EXPLICITLY · digits_rank: when finite, the ranks are computed on the values rounded to that many significant digits — it stabilises tie detection when differences of order 1e-16 would hide them («For stability reasons, it may be advisable to use rounded data or to set the rank rounding to 7 significant digits»). The continuity correction is exposed ONLY as a boolean: its INTEGER form, 0 to 3 Edgeworth terms, is NOT recorded in the method string (live-verified: a value of 2 produces THE SAME «with continuity correction» text) ⇒ the output would be UNVERIFIABLE, and a numeric argument kind would turn True into 1, meaning «one Edgeworth term» — a silent change of meaning · DETERMINISM (charter §5): NO RNG path — no seed, no Monte-Carlo/permutation simulation. The exact distributions are closed-form (psignrank/pwilcox) or, under ties, the DETERMINISTIC Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (the wrapper AND the node path)
Sources: the wilcox_test routine's documentation — «Non-finite (e.g., infinite or missing) values will be omitted»; «By default (if exact is not specified), an exact p-value is computed if the samples contain less than 50 finite values»; «If there are ties, exact inference is performed using the conditional/permutation distribution given the observed ranks, using an implementation of the Streitberg-Röhmel shift algorithm … contributed by Torsten Hothorn»; «For stability reasons, it may be advisable to … » round the ranks to 7 significant digits; Note «the sum of the ranks of the first sample with the minimum value (m(m+1)/2 …) subtracted or not: the engine subtracts»; «With small samples it may not be possible to achieve very high confidence interval coverages» · the kruskal_test routine's documentation — «If x is a list, its elements are taken as the samples to be compared»; «g: … Ignored with a warning if x is a list»; the friedman_test routine — «friedman_test can be used for analyzing unreplicated complete block designs (i.e., there is exactly one observation in y for each combination of levels of groups and blocks)»; «If y is a matrix, groups and blocks are obtained from the column and row indices»; «NAs are not allowed in 'groups' or 'blocks'; if y contains NAs, corresponding blocks are removed» · Streitberg, B. & Röhmel, J. (1986) «Exact Distributions for Permutation and Rank Tests», Statistical Software Newsletter 12(1), 10-17; (1987) «Exakte Verteilungen für Rang- und Randomisierungstests im allgemeinen c-Stichprobenfall», EDV in Medizin und Biologie 18(1), 12-19 — the DETERMINISTIC shift algorithm that stats uses under ties (Rs given by the wilcox_test routine) · Hollander & Wolfe 1973, Nonparametric Statistical Methods, Wiley, pp. 27-33 (one sample) and 68-75 (two samples) — the definition of the pseudomedian (p. 34) that conf_int=True returns; Bauer 1972, JASA 67(339):687-690 (constructing confidence sets using rank statistics) — the exact interval algorithm · Ljung, G.M. & Box, G.E.P. (1978) «On a Measure of Lack of Fit in Time Series Models», Biometrika 65(2), 297-303, doi:10.1093/biomet/65.2.297 — the whiteness precheck of the shared gate; the Box.test routine's documentation Note: «Missing values are not handled» · Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G., «Forecasting: Principles and Practice», 3rd ed., §5.4 — the rule lag = min(10, n/5); IDENTICAL to the DOCUMENTED default of checkresiduals (live-verified help: «If missing, it is set to min(10, n/5) for non-seasonal data»); cross-section ⇒ never the 2m branch · the normative gate spec §3b, gate 4 (cross-section only for the t-test, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman and chi-square; one shared helper) + the catalogue note that the Friedman routine requires either a matrix or explicit blocks · the wrapper footers IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c01_preparation_prechecks/battery_non_parametric and the shared gates module) — the live-verified findings in the engine: a time-indexed matrix accepted by the Friedman routine; the exact against asymptotic V of 22 against 17; a NaN statistic and p-value on constant data; a requested 0.95 level attaining 0.9609375; and a continuity-correction value of 2 left invisible in the method string

cards.method: CORRELATION FILTER: greedy removal of highly correlated variables (over a VALIDATED correlation matrix) + an out-of-sample APPLY with the fitted column names
cards.when: PRE-PROCESSING before a high-dimensional/collinearity-sensitive model (regression, PCA, ML): on an observations x variables matrix (countries x indicators, periods x variables) you drop AS MANY COLUMNS as needed so that NO remaining pairwise |r| exceeds the cutoff; the rule: for every pair above the threshold, the variable with the LARGEST MEAN |correlation| with ALL the others (= the most redundant overall) is deleted; the flow: cf_cor_matrix (a VALIDATED p x p matrix) -> cf_find_correlation (WHICH ones go) -> cf_filter (fit + apply)
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES IN I(1) LEVELS (spurious correlation — supply DIFFERENCES EXPLICITLY; there is NEVER an implicit differencing here); a SIGNIFICANCE test for a correlation, with p-values, intervals and multiplicity -> #81 desc_cor_test; DISTANCES, clustering or MDS, where the object is a distance built from 1 minus the correlation -> #240 dm_correlation_distance (category 29); dimension COMPRESSION rather than SELECTION, keeping all the information in a few axes -> #117; exact LINEAR COMBINATIONS of dependence, found by a QR decomposition — NOT exposed; stateful preprocessing pipelines (EXPLICITLY REJECTED, the normative gate spec §3b); charts and heatmaps (the frontend, §5); p = 1, since at least two variables are required

alternatives.criterion: ALWAYS, unless p is very large: it recomputes the mean correlations at EVERY step and removes FEWER variables («The exact calculations will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower», the findCorrelation routine Details)

ONLY when p is so large that the exact path is prohibitively slow; an EXPLICIT choice — the two paths give DIFFERENT sets (live on the help-page R1, cutoff 0.6: exact -> {x1,x4,x5}; fast -> {x1,x3,x4,x5})
the relation is MONOTONE but not linear, or outliers are present (rank-based, robust); kendall is O(n^2) and is slow at large n; the default pearson = a LINEAR relation

NEW data (test/out-of-sample): it applies THE SAME filter WITHOUT re-estimation (§3b gate 6); CRITICAL — a re-fit on the test set changes the COLUMN SET and the model breaks (live-verified in the tests: a different sample -> a different filter)
you want COMPRESSION (all the variables contribute to a few orthogonal axes) rather than the SELECTION of a subset of columns; the filter keeps INTERPRETABLE original variables, PCA does not
the smaller the cutoff, the more columns leave; read max_abs_offdiag/n_pairs_above_before from cf_cor_matrix first — if max|r| < cutoff NOTHING leaves

output_key_fields: cf_cor_matrix: cor (a p x p VALIDATED matrix — heatmap chart-data) + method/use('everything', PINNED) + n/p/variables + mean_abs_cor (THE greedy criterion, per variable) + max_abs_offdiag/max_abs_pair/max_abs_index + min_cor/max_cor/n_pairs + eigen_min/is_psd (a PSD DIAGNOSTIC, NOT a gate)
cf_find_correlation: remove_index/remove_names AND keep_index/keep_names (= the FITTED PARAMS, §3b gate 6; ALWAYS sorted ascending) + n_variables/n_removed/n_kept/share_removed

cf_find_correlation: max_abs_before vs max_abs_after (+ max_abs_pair_before/after) and n_pairs_above_before vs n_pairs_above_after (ALWAYS 0 — the algorithm's invariant) — the main «before/after» chart-data

cf_filter: data (THE FILTERED DATA, n x n_variables_out — it becomes a handle: the card's SOLE producer/register) + mode ('fit' | 'apply') + keep_names/remove_names + n_variables_in/out + n/cutoff/exact/method/variables
cf_filter in mode='apply': cor and mean_abs_cor are absent, and max_abs_before and max_abs_after blank — DOCUMENTED, and meaning «NO re-estimation»: it is a pure column subselection
interpretation_traps: DETERMINISM #1 (§5): the documented upstream default makes the exact path conditional on having fewer than 100 columns — THE ALGORITHM CHANGES AT 100 COLUMNS. A node that changed path because the user added the hundredth variable would be NON-REPRODUCIBLE ⇒ 'exact' is an EXPLICIT argument with OUR OWN constant default of True, never the upstream one

DETERMINISM #2: the ORDER in which the selector returns its indices depends on the column order (live: the same SET, in a different ORDER, once the columns are reversed) ⇒ CANONICALIZATION, so the indices and names always come back in ascending order. There is no randomness anywhere, and no seed; two identical runs are pinned in the tests, for both the wrapper and the node path

SILENTLY WRONG (the main reason this wrapper exists): the selector REQUIRES A CORRELATION MATRIX, yet with exact=False it SILENTLY accepts RAW DATA (live: a 10x5 random matrix returned «2 3 1» as though those were correlations); ONLY the exact path checks symmetry ⇒ OUR OWN symmetry, diagonal and range checks run ALWAYS, on both paths

SILENTLY WRONG: a non-square 3x4 matrix with exact=False returns an EMPTY selection SILENTLY; p=1 with exact=False does the same, while the exact path at least says «only one variable given»; a diagonal other than 1, and correlations outside [-1,1], pass SILENTLY on BOTH paths — that is, ANYTHING symmetric is accepted as a «correlation» (did you supply a COVARIANCE matrix? convert it first)

SILENTLY WRONG: a CONSTANT, zero-variance column makes the correlation emit ONLY the warning «the standard deviation is zero» and blank the WHOLE row and column (live-verified in the engine); the selector then fails cryptically — «The correlation matrix has some missing values», or a bare type error on the exact path ⇒ a hard gate that NAMES the constant columns

SILENTLY WRONG: a correlation on a single observation returns an ENTIRELY blank matrix WITHOUT even a warning; on two observations every correlation is 1 in absolute value BY DEFINITION, since two points define a line ⇒ a hard gate of n >= 3 in the FIT, while in the APPLY step n >= 1 suffices, because the names are GIVEN rather than estimated
SILENTLY WRONG: a cutoff of 1.5 selects NOTHING silently, so nothing is filtered, while a cutoff at or below 0 removes almost EVERYTHING. The selector does NOT check ⇒ a hard gate, 0 < cutoff < 1

§3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization): keep_names/remove_names ARE the fitted params and are ALWAYS returned; cf_filter(keep=..) applies them to NEW data WITHOUT re-estimation. If the filter is re-estimated on the test set, the COLUMN SET CHANGES (different correlations) and the trained model's coefficients are applied to the WRONG columns (the KNIME «Normalize Model» pattern). That is also why duplicate column labels are a hard gate: the apply would be ambiguous

§3b GATE 3 (non-stationarity): the node is CROSS-SECTION/PANEL. In I(1) LEVELS the sample correlation does NOT converge to a population parameter (spurious correlation, Granger-Newbold 1974; Hamilton-Ma-Xi for why the standardization is undefined) => supply DIFFERENCES EXPLICITLY upstream; NEVER an implicit differencing here
§3b GATE 2 (no implicit standardization): correlation is INVARIANT to linear transformations => there is NO scale/center argument (it would be a no-op implying a non-existent option)

PSD: A DOCUMENTED DEVIATION — a non-positive-semidefinite matrix is exposed as eigen_min/is_psd but does NOT block: the greedy algorithm stays well defined (it compares |r| per pair) and it is LIVE-VERIFIED that EVEN the R1 matrix in the reference documentation itself has a minimum eigenvalue of -0.2634288 (the same holds for published matrices rounded to 2 decimals)

PINNED ARGUMENTS: the verbose switch is off, since turning it on PRINTS («Compare row 1 and column 5 with corr 0.85...»), a violation of §5; the names switch is off, since the documented return value is INVERTED against the live behaviour — we supply BOTH the indices AND the names ourselves; and the correlation is PINNED to complete data, because pairwise completion computes EVERY pair on a DIFFERENT sample and can yield a matrix that is not positive semi-definite, and an inconsistent filter

THE BOUNDARY against #240 (dm_correlation_distance, category 29): there a DISTANCE object, 1 minus the correlation, is produced for clustering — a DIFFERENT object with DIFFERENT semantics, since 1-r reverses the direction and loses the sign, and it does NOT feed the selector here. cf_cor_matrix exists ONLY so that this node is usable end to end
sources: the greedy correlation selector (live-verified in the engine): the cutoff defaults to 0.9, the verbose and names switches to off, and the exact path is conditional on the column count. «If two variables have a high correlation, the function looks at the mean absolute correlation of each variable and removes the variable with the largest mean absolute correlation», and turning the exact path on «will cause the function to re-evaluate the average correlations at each step... will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower». The documented return value is INVERTED against the live behaviour; the reference 5x5 example was reproduced

Kuhn, M. & Johnson, K. (2013) Applied Predictive Modeling, Springer, ch. 3 «Data Pre-Processing» (the Removing Predictors / between-predictor correlations section) — the textbook source of the greedy procedure, as cited in the wrapper's header

the correlation and standard-deviation routines — a constant column produces ONLY the «the standard deviation is zero» warning and a blank entry (live-verified); the completion policy; and the covariance-to-correlation conversion
Granger, C.W.J. & Newbold, P. (1974) «Spurious regressions in econometrics», Journal of Econometrics 2(2) 111-120 — why the node is cross-section/panel and not for I(1) levels

Hamilton, J.D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 — §3b normative gate 3 (non-stationarity ⇒ standardization/sample moments undefined); see #256

the normative gate spec §3b, gate 6 (fit/apply externalization; the KNIME Normalizer «Normalize Model» pattern) + gate 2 (no implicit standardization) + the REJECTION of a stateful preprocessing pipeline

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c00_data_utilities/correlation_filter_greedy) — the seven live-verified silently-wrong behaviours, and the invariant that no remaining correlation exceeds the cutoff (600 random cases, on both the exact and the fast path, with zero violations)
precondition_tools: cf_cor_matrix # FIRST the VALIDATED matrix: max_abs_offdiag/mean_abs_cor/n_pairs show WHETHER filtering is needed and at which cutoff
c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman # gaps are a hard gate here, since they would blank the correlation matrix
c01_preparation_prechecks/unit_root_normality.run_adf_test # IF the columns are time series: confirm stationarity FIRST, otherwise the sample correlation is spurious (§3b gate 3)
