Alternatives: cf_find_correlation with exact=True — the DEFAULT (ALWAYS, unless p is very large: it recomputes the mean correlations at EVERY step and removes FEWER variables («The exact calculations will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower», the findCorrelation routine Details)) · cf_find_correlation with exact=False (ONLY when p is so large that the exact path is prohibitively slow; an EXPLICIT choice — the two paths give DIFFERENT sets (live on the help-page R1, cutoff 0.6: exact -> {x1,x4,x5}; fast -> {x1,x3,x4,x5})) · method = 'spearman' / 'kendall' (the relation is MONOTONE but not linear, or outliers are present (rank-based, robust); kendall is O(n^2) and is slow at large n; the default pearson = a LINEAR relation) · cf_filter(keep = <keep_names of a previous fit>) (NEW data (test/out-of-sample): it applies THE SAME filter WITHOUT re-estimation (§3b gate 6); CRITICAL — a re-fit on the test set changes the COLUMN SET and the model breaks (live-verified in the tests: a different sample -> a different filter)) · #117 pca_composite (prcomp) (you want COMPRESSION (all the variables contribute to a few orthogonal axes) rather than the SELECTION of a subset of columns; the filter keeps INTERPRETABLE original variables, PCA does not) · cutoff 0.75 (aggressive) vs 0.9 (default) vs 0.95 (conservative) (the smaller the cutoff, the more columns leave; read max_abs_offdiag/n_pairs_above_before from cf_cor_matrix first — if max|r| < cutoff NOTHING leaves)
Output: cf_cor_matrix: cor (a p x p VALIDATED matrix — heatmap chart-data) + method/use('everything', PINNED) + n/p/variables + mean_abs_cor (THE greedy criterion, per variable) + max_abs_offdiag/max_abs_pair/max_abs_index + min_cor/max_cor/n_pairs + eigen_min/is_psd (a PSD DIAGNOSTIC, NOT a gate) · cf_find_correlation: remove_index/remove_names AND keep_index/keep_names (= the FITTED PARAMS, §3b gate 6; ALWAYS sorted ascending) + n_variables/n_removed/n_kept/share_removed · cf_find_correlation: max_abs_before vs max_abs_after (+ max_abs_pair_before/after) and n_pairs_above_before vs n_pairs_above_after (ALWAYS 0 — the algorithm's invariant) — the main «before/after» chart-data · cf_filter: data (THE FILTERED DATA, n x n_variables_out — it becomes a handle: the card's SOLE producer/register) + mode ('fit' | 'apply') + keep_names/remove_names + n_variables_in/out + n/cutoff/exact/method/variables · cf_filter in mode='apply': cor and mean_abs_cor are absent, and max_abs_before and max_abs_after blank — DOCUMENTED, and meaning «NO re-estimation»: it is a pure column subselection
Pitfalls: DETERMINISM #1 (§5): the documented upstream default makes the exact path conditional on having fewer than 100 columns — THE ALGORITHM CHANGES AT 100 COLUMNS. A node that changed path because the user added the hundredth variable would be NON-REPRODUCIBLE ⇒ 'exact' is an EXPLICIT argument with OUR OWN constant default of True, never the upstream one · DETERMINISM #2: the ORDER in which the selector returns its indices depends on the column order (live: the same SET, in a different ORDER, once the columns are reversed) ⇒ CANONICALIZATION, so the indices and names always come back in ascending order. There is no randomness anywhere, and no seed; two identical runs are pinned in the tests, for both the wrapper and the node path · SILENTLY WRONG (the main reason this wrapper exists): the selector REQUIRES A CORRELATION MATRIX, yet with exact=False it SILENTLY accepts RAW DATA (live: a 10x5 random matrix returned «2 3 1» as though those were correlations); ONLY the exact path checks symmetry ⇒ OUR OWN symmetry, diagonal and range checks run ALWAYS, on both paths · SILENTLY WRONG: a non-square 3x4 matrix with exact=False returns an EMPTY selection SILENTLY; p=1 with exact=False does the same, while the exact path at least says «only one variable given»; a diagonal other than 1, and correlations outside [-1,1], pass SILENTLY on BOTH paths — that is, ANYTHING symmetric is accepted as a «correlation» (did you supply a COVARIANCE matrix? convert it first) · SILENTLY WRONG: a CONSTANT, zero-variance column makes the correlation emit ONLY the warning «the standard deviation is zero» and blank the WHOLE row and column (live-verified in the engine); the selector then fails cryptically — «The correlation matrix has some missing values», or a bare type error on the exact path ⇒ a hard gate that NAMES the constant columns · SILENTLY WRONG: a correlation on a single observation returns an ENTIRELY blank matrix WITHOUT even a warning; on two observations every correlation is 1 in absolute value BY DEFINITION, since two points define a line ⇒ a hard gate of n >= 3 in the FIT, while in the APPLY step n >= 1 suffices, because the names are GIVEN rather than estimated · SILENTLY WRONG: a cutoff of 1.5 selects NOTHING silently, so nothing is filtered, while a cutoff at or below 0 removes almost EVERYTHING. The selector does NOT check ⇒ a hard gate, 0 < cutoff < 1 · §3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization): keep_names/remove_names ARE the fitted params and are ALWAYS returned; cf_filter(keep=..) applies them to NEW data WITHOUT re-estimation. If the filter is re-estimated on the test set, the COLUMN SET CHANGES (different correlations) and the trained model's coefficients are applied to the WRONG columns (the KNIME «Normalize Model» pattern). That is also why duplicate column labels are a hard gate: the apply would be ambiguous · §3b GATE 3 (non-stationarity): the node is CROSS-SECTION/PANEL. In I(1) LEVELS the sample correlation does NOT converge to a population parameter (spurious correlation, Granger-Newbold 1974; Hamilton-Ma-Xi for why the standardization is undefined) => supply DIFFERENCES EXPLICITLY upstream; NEVER an implicit differencing here · §3b GATE 2 (no implicit standardization): correlation is INVARIANT to linear transformations => there is NO scale/center argument (it would be a no-op implying a non-existent option) · PSD: A DOCUMENTED DEVIATION — a non-positive-semidefinite matrix is exposed as eigen_min/is_psd but does NOT block: the greedy algorithm stays well defined (it compares |r| per pair) and it is LIVE-VERIFIED that EVEN the R1 matrix in the reference documentation itself has a minimum eigenvalue of -0.2634288 (the same holds for published matrices rounded to 2 decimals) · PINNED ARGUMENTS: the verbose switch is off, since turning it on PRINTS («Compare row 1 and column 5 with corr 0.85...»), a violation of §5; the names switch is off, since the documented return value is INVERTED against the live behaviour — we supply BOTH the indices AND the names ourselves; and the correlation is PINNED to complete data, because pairwise completion computes EVERY pair on a DIFFERENT sample and can yield a matrix that is not positive semi-definite, and an inconsistent filter · THE BOUNDARY against #240 (dm_correlation_distance, category 29): there a DISTANCE object, 1 minus the correlation, is produced for clustering — a DIFFERENT object with DIFFERENT semantics, since 1-r reverses the direction and loses the sign, and it does NOT feed the selector here. cf_cor_matrix exists ONLY so that this node is usable end to end
Sources: the greedy correlation selector (live-verified in the engine): the cutoff defaults to 0.9, the verbose and names switches to off, and the exact path is conditional on the column count. «If two variables have a high correlation, the function looks at the mean absolute correlation of each variable and removes the variable with the largest mean absolute correlation», and turning the exact path on «will cause the function to re-evaluate the average correlations at each step... will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower». The documented return value is INVERTED against the live behaviour; the reference 5x5 example was reproduced · Kuhn, M. & Johnson, K. (2013) Applied Predictive Modeling, Springer, ch. 3 «Data Pre-Processing» (the Removing Predictors / between-predictor correlations section) — the textbook source of the greedy procedure, as cited in the wrapper's header · the correlation and standard-deviation routines — a constant column produces ONLY the «the standard deviation is zero» warning and a blank entry (live-verified); the completion policy; and the covariance-to-correlation conversion · Granger, C.W.J. & Newbold, P. (1974) «Spurious regressions in econometrics», Journal of Econometrics 2(2) 111-120 — why the node is cross-section/panel and not for I(1) levels · Hamilton, J.D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 — §3b normative gate 3 (non-stationarity ⇒ standardization/sample moments undefined); see #256 · the normative gate spec §3b, gate 6 (fit/apply externalization; the KNIME Normalizer «Normalize Model» pattern) + gate 2 (no implicit standardization) + the REJECTION of a stateful preprocessing pipeline · wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c00_data_utilities/correlation_filter_greedy) — the seven live-verified silently-wrong behaviours, and the invariant that no remaining correlation exceeds the cutoff (600 random cases, on both the exact and the fast path, with zero violations)

cards.method: DESIGN MATRIX (feature engineering): ORTHOGONAL/RAW polynomials (returning the fitted coefficients), INTERACTIONS without a formula surface, an allowlisted formula path, a COMBINATORIAL factor
cards.when: IMMEDIATELY BEFORE any regression/ML node, when you need NON-LINEARITY (polynomials: the Phillips curve, threshold-like relations) or INTERACTIONS (a*b, regime x variable, country x sector): the node builds the DESIGN MATRIX EXPLICITLY, GATED and — most critically — REPRODUCIBLY OUT OF SAMPLE (it returns AND accepts back the fitted params: coefs_alpha/coefs_norm2 · xlev + contrasts + column_names)
cards.when_not: model ESTIMATION — the node does NOT run a regression, it supplies ONLY the matrix X, and the dependent variable does not belong here, since the formula is ONE-SIDED; spline or semi-parametric bases (ANOTHER family, with its own card); DISCRETISATION of a continuous variable into categories -> #255; calendar dummies -> #254 hd_dummies; filtering of collinear columns -> #252 cf_filter; sparse matrices (a new dependency); stateful preprocessing pipelines (REJECTED, the normative gate spec §3b); charts (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: you want main terms + all interactions up to 'order' from VALIDATED COLUMN NAMES: NO formula comes from the user — the RCE surface DOES NOT EVEN EXIST (the formula is built internally from language objects; ZERO parse/eval)

you GENUINELY need an expression that cannot be stated with names+order: I(x^2), log(x), nested factors, an explicit removal of terms; it passes TWICE through a default-deny allowlist (adapt_formula at L3 + an independent walk in the wrapper) and NEVER accepts a string

you want INTERPRETABLE coefficients on the original scale (x, x², x³); the price is SEVERE collinearity, and the p-values of the lower degrees CHANGE when a higher one is added. The default, False, gives an ORTHOGONAL basis: numerically stable, with uncorrelated columns
NEW data: MANDATORY in order to produce THE SAME basis — a re-fit poly on the new data gives A DIFFERENT BASIS and the trained model's coefficients mean nothing (§3b gate 6)
NEW data with factors: MANDATORY — with FEWER levels in newdata model_matrix produces SILENTLY FEWER COLUMNS (live-verified) and the coefficients land in the WRONG POSITIONS

alternatives.alt: the sum-to-zero contrast instead of the treatment contrast
alternatives.criterion: you want the interactions interpretable as DEVIATIONS FROM THE MEAN, so that the main term stops meaning «relative to the first level»; the Helmert contrast gives successive contrasts, and the polynomial contrast orthogonal polynomials for ORDERED categories
you want ONE COMBINATORIAL FACTOR (e.g. country x regime as A SINGLE categorical column for fixed effects/grouping) instead of column products in a design matrix

the DOWNSTREAM node is regularized (ridge/lasso, cat 20) and rank deficiency is not an error; 'auto' (the default) is STRICT ('stop') in the FIT and TOLERANT ('report') in the APPLY, where an absent level is NORMAL

output_key_fields: ply_polynomial: basis (n x degree — chart data) + column_names (the base name with a degree suffix) + degree and raw + coefs_alpha (of length degree), coefs_norm2 (of length degree+2) and coefs_source ('fitted', 'supplied' or 'raw'), which are THE FITTED PARAMETERS (§3b gate 6), + orthonormality_error and centering_error (ONLY on the fit path) + n/n_unique/x_min/x_max/name

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: design (an n x k BARE numeric matrix) + column_names/n_columns/n_rows + column_term & assign (COLUMN -> TERM; 0 = intercept) + term_labels/n_terms/intercept + formula (deparsed)

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: xlev (THE LEVELS PER FACTOR) + xlev_source ('fitted'|'supplied') + contrasts/contrasts_arg + variables/factor_vars/numeric_vars = THE design matrix's FITTED PARAMS (§3b gate 6)

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: rank + rank_deficient + rank_check/rank_check_arg + column_bound (THE UPPER BOUND checked BEFORE construction) + max_columns/max_levels; ply_interactions additionally order/include_main/built_formula

ply_interaction_categorical: levels + codes (1 to n_levels per row) + counts (chart data) + n_levels/n_used_levels + empty_levels/n_empty_levels/has_empty_levels + indicator, an n x n_levels 0/1 matrix when it was requested, + input_levels (fit and apply) + combinations/drop/sep/lex_order/n
interpretation_traps: §3b GATE 6 — THE NODE'S REASON FOR EXISTING: an ORTHOGONAL polynomial is NOT a function of x alone — it depends on the CENTRES and NORMS (alpha, norm2) computed ON THE TRAINING SAMPLE. Re-fitting the basis on new data would give A DIFFERENT BASIS, and the model's coefficients would then mean nothing. That is why the coefficients are returned AS NUMBERS and accepted back (the KNIME Normalizer «Normalize Model» pattern); the simplified basis DISCARDS them — live, only the shape attributes survive — which is why it is NOT exposed

§3b GATE 6 (b) — A SILENTLY WRONG BEHAVIOUR OF model_matrix: newdata with FEWER factor levels produces FEWER COLUMNS WITHOUT ANY ERROR (live-verified: ~a*g with 3 levels -> (Intercept),a,gy,gz,a:gy,a:gz; the same newdata with 2 levels -> (Intercept),a,gy,a:gy) => the coefficients are applied at the WRONG POSITIONS. That is why xlev + expect_columns are returned/accepted, with a hard gate on an UNKNOWN level («factor a has new level..») AND on a different column set

SECURITY (the project's security rule — NEVER evaluate a user string): ply_interactions EXPOSES NO formula surface; it builds the right-hand side symbolically over names that (a) really exist in the data and (b) pass a strict identifier pattern, then implants it into a TEMPLATE formula whose environment is sealed to the base one ⇒ there is ZERO path from a string to a parse or an evaluation

SECURITY (ply_model_matrix, THREE LAYERS OF DEFENCE): (1) at tier 3 the string passes ONLY through the formula adapter — a default-deny allowlist walk with no evaluation, inside a sealed enclosure; (2) the wrapper does NOT accept a string AT ALL, only an already-parsed formula object; (3) an INDEPENDENT default-deny allowlist walk that runs even in isolation and ADDITIONALLY restricts EVERY symbol to the data's column names. ONLY these are allowed: the formula and arithmetic operators ~ + - * : ^ ( ), the identity wrapper, the logarithms and the exponential, the square root and the absolute value, the polynomial basis, the categorical constructors, and the interaction constructor; the dot shorthand is explicitly rejected; the expression depth is capped at 64; and the head of every call MUST be a plain symbol

SILENTLY WRONG (the polynomial basis): a FRACTIONAL degree does NOT error — it is SILENTLY truncated downwards (live, a degree of 1.5 gave one column); coefficients of the WRONG LENGTH give a column FULL OF BLANKS with no error, hence the gate that alpha has exactly `degree` entries and norm2 exactly `degree+2` (live-verified: degree 3 gives 3 and 5); coefficients supplied TOGETHER WITH raw=True are SILENTLY ignored; and once the degree reaches the number of unique values the ORTHOGONAL basis errors («'degree' must be less than number of unique points») while the RAW one does NOT — it simply produces LINEARLY DEPENDENT columns ⇒ THE SAME gate on both paths

SILENTLY WRONG (gaps): building the model frame SILENTLY DROPS the incomplete rows (live, 6 became 5) and the design matrix CEASES to line up with y ⇒ the missing-value policy is PINNED to fail, plus OUR OWN explicit gap-and-infinity gate BEFORE the call, on the columns actually used only; and dropping unused levels is PINNED off, since enabling it would nullify the recorded level sets

SILENTLY WRONG (RANK DEFICIENCY): empty level combinations produce aliased columns — live-verified, a rank of 2 over 4 columns WITHOUT any error, and a least-squares fit on such a matrix returns blank coefficients silently. The node ALWAYS computes the rank and blocks according to rank_check ('auto' stops in the FIT and reports in the APPLY)

SILENTLY WRONG (the interaction constructor): it accepts a NUMERIC column WITHOUT COMPLAINT and creates ONE LEVEL PER UNIQUE VALUE ⇒ a hard gate, so discretise first (#255); with dropping off, the documented default, the EMPTY levels REMAIN and are reported explicitly in empty_levels, but indicator=True IS BLOCKED whenever empty levels exist, since each one gives a column FULL OF ZEROS, hence rank deficiency and silently blank coefficients

DIMENSION EXPLOSION: an UPPER BOUND on the column count is checked BEFORE the matrix is built — the product of the level counts per term, a numeric column counting as 1 ⇒ a giant matrix is NEVER constructed; max_levels defaults to 30 per categorical column and max_columns to 200 (in ply_interaction_categorical max_levels defaults to 200, and the PRODUCT of the level counts is checked BEFORE the call when dropping is off); and a categorical column with ONLY one level, which would give the cryptic «contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels», is caught BEFOREHAND

ORTHONORMALITY: it is checked — the largest deviation of X'X from the identity, and the largest column sum — ONLY on the FIT path, since OUT OF SAMPLE IT DOES NOT HOLD BY DESIGN: the basis is orthogonal WITH RESPECT TO THE TRAINING SAMPLE, not to every new x. On the apply path the two fields are blank — EXPECTED, not an error

DETERMINISM (§5): NO RNG path (poly = QR/a three-term recursion; model_matrix/interaction = combinatorial) => NO seed argument; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (the wrapper AND the node path). TERMINAL nodes: no register — the fit/apply is EXPLICIT (the user hands back coefs/xlev/expect_columns)
sources: the polynomial-basis routine's documentation (live-verified): the degree defaults to 1, the coefficients are unset, and both the raw and simplified switches default to off; the coefficients — alpha and norm2 — are attached ONLY on the orthogonal path (degree 3 gives 3 alphas and 5 norms, that is degree+2, while the simplified path keeps only the shape attributes); «'degree' must be less than number of unique points»; and applying the basis to new data with the stored coefficients reproduces it exactly

the design-matrix, terms and model-frame routines — the term assignment attribute (column to term, 0 for the intercept), the contrast attribute and argument, the missing-value policy, and the unused-level switch; «contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels»; plus the live-verified silent column loss when new data carries fewer levels, and the silent dropping of incomplete rows (6 became 5)

the interaction constructor's documentation — dropping is off by default and therefore keeps ALL the combinations, the separator is a dot, and the ordering is not lexicographic; plus the QR rank used for the rank-deficiency check
the contrast routines — the four exposed categorical codings: treatment, sum-to-zero, Helmert and polynomial; the default is the treatment coding, relative to the FIRST level
the project's security rule — never evaluate a parsed user string; the formula adapter, a default-deny allowlist walk inside a sealed enclosure, is THE ONLY point at which a string becomes a formula

the normative gate spec §3b, gate 6 (fit/apply externalization: «every scaling, discretisation or polynomial node must return the fitted parameters... otherwise the out-of-sample apply is not reproducible»; the KNIME Normalizer «Normalize Model» pattern) + the live-verified gate «'degree' must be less than number of unique points» + the REJECTION of a stateful prepare-and-bake pipeline

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c00_data_utilities/design_matrix_orthogonal) — the omissions (the simplified basis, the multivariate polynomial, the predict path, the permissive missing-value policies, the unused-level switch, sparse matrices, and the spline bases), the formula's three layers of defence, and every live-verified silently-wrong behaviour
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman # gaps are a hard gate: building the model frame DROPS ROWS SILENTLY (live, 6 became 5) and breaks the alignment with y
ply_interactions # with order = 1: see FIRST how many columns the MAIN terms produce (column_bound/n_columns) before you raise the order — interactions multiply

c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column.bn_quantile_bins # IF you want a CATEGORICAL interaction from a CONTINUOUS variable: discretise FIRST (interaction on a numeric column creates ONE LEVEL PER VALUE)

cards.method: CALENDAR EFFECTS: holidays for G7+CH & financial centres (NYSE/LONDON/ZURICH/TSX) -> NAMED 0/1 columns aligned to a given vector of dates + weekday/business-day flags
cards.when: DAILY/WEEKLY macro or financial series with DETERMINISTIC calendar disturbances (national holidays, exchange closures, the MOVING Easter): you produce EXPLICIT exogenous 0/1 dummies (exog_handle) for ARIMA/regression/GARCH; without them the calendar contaminates the residuals and shows up FALSELY as seasonality or ARCH. The flow: hd_list (WHICH names exist — 120 in total) -> hd_holidays (THE DATES per holiday/year) -> hd_dummies (aligned 0/1 columns + weekday/bizday flags)
cards.when_not: COUNTING business days, date rolling or offsets under a custom calendar -> #112 (bday_create_calendar, bday_count, bday_offset, bday_adjust); general date and frequency algebra -> #111/#113/#78; SEASONAL ADJUSTMENT, where the trading-day and Easter regressors live INSIDE the model -> #4 (category 01); MONTHLY or QUARTERLY data, where a holiday is not a discrete event and you want trading-day or leap-year regressors rather than day dummies; NON-calendar regime dummies -> #255, or #253 ply_interaction_categorical; charts (the frontend, §5); countries outside the shipped catalogue (see hd_list — the catalogue is CLOSED)

alternatives.criterion: you want a DIFFERENT coefficient per holiday (e.g. Christmas vs Thanksgiving have a different effect size); it costs one degree of freedom per holiday

few observations or few events per holiday -> ONE column 'holiday_any' (1 = any holiday); fewer degrees of freedom, a single common effect. The is_holiday vector is returned ALWAYS, whatever the choice
you want BOTH the per-holiday columns AND the aggregate (e.g. per-holiday in the model, aggregate in the chart)
FINANCIAL daily data: a CLOSED MARKET is a STRUCTURAL GAP (not a missing value); it gives ONE column named after the centre, IN ADDITION to the named holidays
you want ONLY the EXTRAORDINARY closures (e.g. 2001-09-11.14) — shock events, not institutional holidays; 'standard' = only the institutional ones; 'all' (the default) = ALL

a NEW sample, out of sample or the next wave: IDENTICAL columns IN THE SAME ORDER, even if some holiday does not fall inside it, and INDEPENDENTLY of the catalogue version (§3b gate 6). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with holidays, calendar and nyse_type
you do not want dummies but a COUNT of business days between dates, date shifting, or the generation of a business-day sequence under a custom calendar

output_key_fields: hd_list: holidays (the NAMES matching the pattern) + n + all_holidays/n_all (120) + countries + count_by_country (bar chart-data; US 18 · CA 6 · GB 4 · DE 5 · FR 6 · IT 6 · JP 33 · CH 5) + n_matched_by_country + calendars (NYSE/LONDON/ZURICH/TSX) + year_min/year_max (1583/2200) + empty
hd_holidays: dates (SORTED, UNIQUE, 'YYYY-MM-DD') + n_dates + date_table (records {source, year, date} — chart-data) + count_by_source + years/n_years
hd_holidays/hd_dummies: holiday_dates = THE FITTED PARAM (§3b gate 6; a named list holiday -> dates); it is passed VERBATIM to hd_dummies(holiday_dates=) for an out-of-sample apply
hd_holidays: empty_sources/n_empty_sources (A SILENT GAP: a holiday that DID NOT YET EXIST -> 0 dates WITHOUT an error) + n_on_weekend/share_on_weekend + dates_per_year

hd_dummies: dummies (n x k 0/1 — chart-data; ROWS = the GIVEN dates in the GIVEN order, COLUMNS = the sources in the GIVEN order) + dummy_levels (column NAMES+ORDER = a fitted param) + n_columns + count_by_column
hd_dummies: is_holiday/n_holiday/share_holiday + is_weekday/n_weekday + is_bizday/n_bizday + n_holiday_on_weekday + wday + mode ('fit'|'apply') + dummy_type + empty_holiday_set/n_holiday_dates

hd_dummies: constant_columns and n_constant_columns are THE ALL-ZERO COLUMNS, where the holiday does not fall inside the sample — they are NOT removed, since that would break the fit/apply contract, but they are FLAGGED: a rank-deficient design, on which a least-squares fit returns a blank coefficient silently
interpretation_traps: TRAP #1 (NAMES RESOLVED BY LOOKUP): the holiday routine resolves a CHARACTER STRING to a function in the caller's scope, so without attaching the library the name is NOT found (live: «object 'USNewYearsDay' of mode 'function' was not found»). THE FIX: we pass the FUNCTION OBJECT itself, which the documentation explicitly allows («a list of the unquoted function names») ⇒ nothing has to be attached. AN ADDITIONAL hard gate: EVERY name is checked against the catalogue listing BEFORE the call, with an explicit message and the nearby names

TRAP #2 (a typed object that does not serialise): the holiday routines return a typed date object, which to_mcp STUBS OUT ⇒ THE DATES WOULD BE LOST. EVERY such object is converted HERE into a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' string before being returned (pinned in the tests: nothing typed leaks)

DETERMINISM (§5): 'year' is MANDATORY — the upstream default is THE CURRENT YEAR FROM THE CLOCK, which is not reproducible. TIME ZONE: the financial centre is PINNED to GMT (live-verified: THE SAME dates under two very different local zones), and neither the zone nor the centre is exposed. There is no randomness, since the computations are purely calendrical; the output is ALWAYS sorted and de-duplicated, and the column order follows the GIVEN argument order; two identical runs are pinned in the tests

SILENTLY WRONG (years): outside [1000, 9999] the date constructor does NOT error — it returns a blank with ONLY the warning «character string is not in a standard unambiguous format», and year 0 and year 10000 both come back blank; the same for a NON-INTEGER year, and for a missing one. OUR OWN HARD gate is [1583, 2200]: the lower bound is the first FULL year of the GREGORIAN calendar, after the reform of 15 October 1582, because the Easter algorithm is GREGORIAN and before 1583 the results would be ANACHRONISTIC

SILENTLY WRONG (dates): an unparsable string, or an impossible date such as 30 February, returns a blank with only a warning ⇒ any invalid date would SILENTLY become a row of ALL ZEROS. A hard gate: either a date value or STRICTLY 'YYYY-MM-DD', UNIQUE, since the alignment index must be, and never a timestamp, since converting a timestamp to a date depends on the TIME ZONE and would shift days

SILENTLY WRONG (the weekday set): an out-of-range weekday does NOT error — every day then comes back as a non-business day ⇒ silently wrong flags. A hard gate keeps the weekday within [0, 6], where 0 is Sunday and 6 Saturday, the default 1 to 5 meaning Monday to Friday

§3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization): holiday_dates, a named list, and dummy_levels, the column NAMES AND ORDER, are returned as plain text and numeric fields AND accepted back through hd_dummies ⇒ an out-of-sample apply with IDENTICAL columns, INDEPENDENTLY of the catalogue version, which the documentation says «is changed from time to time». The two paths are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — otherwise the training and test columns could differ silently

THE ZERO COLUMNS ARE NOT DROPPED: a holiday that does not fall inside the sample gives an all-zero column, and SILENTLY removing it would BREAK the fit/apply contract, since the training and test columns would differ. ALL of them are returned and the problem is flagged in constant_columns — a rank-deficient design, on which a least-squares fit returns a blank coefficient silently, the same pattern as #253

SILENT GAPS THAT ARE NOT ERRORS: a holiday that DID NOT YET EXIST returns 0 dates WITHOUT an error (live: USJuneteenthNationalIndependenceDay before 2021 · CAFamilyDay in 2000 · JPMountainDay/GBEarlyMayBankHoliday in old years · specialHolidayGB in 2024) => the fields empty_sources/n_empty_sources; an EMPTY holiday set => isBizday DEGENERATES into isWeekday (live, without an error) => the fields empty_holiday_set/n_holiday_dates

listHolidays: it applies the regex ANYWHERE inside the name, NOT as a prefix — which is why 'GB' gives 4 while the names that BEGIN with GB are 3 (the 4th is 'specialHolidayGB'); live-verified. An invalid regex -> a labelled stop («invalid regular expression '[', reason 'Missing ]''»)

the NYSE holiday type: the DOCUMENTED default, an empty string, CANNOT be passed EXPLICITLY — the routine's own enum check rejects it («'arg' should be one of “standard”, “special”») ⇒ for nyse_type='all' we OMIT the argument entirely; and nyse_type applies ONLY with calendar='NYSE', otherwise a hard stop rather than a silent no-op

the routine's own naming option WAS OMITTED: it derives the names from the UNQUOTED argument, and with function objects the documentation says that «as a last resort... generated names are used» (H1, H2, ...) AND it PRINTS them (live-verified in the body; a violation of §5) ⇒ we call ONE holiday at a time and build the holiday-to-dates mapping OURSELVES

THE INTERNAL PREFIX IS hdum_, NOT hd_: an hd_call helper ALREADY EXISTS in c07_causality_policy/honest_robust_inference, and ALL the wrappers load into THE SAME source environment ⇒ reusing the prefix would be a SILENT overwrite; the EXPORTED hd_* names were checked and are free
sources: the calendar catalogue's reference manual (live-verified in the engine): the holiday routine takes a year, defaulting to the current one, and one or more holidays given either as names or as UNQUOTED FUNCTION objects, with a printed fallback for generated names; the catalogue listing (a pattern argument, and the note that «the list is changed from time to time»); the NYSE routine's type enum (empty, 'standard', 'special'); the London, Zurich and Toronto calendars; the weekday and business-day predicates, defaulting to Monday-Friday; and the financial-centre argument of the date constructor
LIVE-VERIFIED catalogue counts (120 holidays in total): US 18 · CA 6 · GB 4 (three with the GB prefix, plus the special holiday) · DE 5 · FR 6 · IT 6 · JP 33 · CH 5
The Gregorian reform: the papal bull «Inter gravissimas», in force from 1582-10-15 => 1583 = the 1st FULL Gregorian year; the Easter algorithm used here is Gregorian (the gate's lower bound)

the normative gate spec §3b: the live-verified gate «holiday: object 'X' of mode 'function' was not found» — the holiday routine resolves its names by lookup, so it needs either an attached library or the exported function object — together with gate 6 (fit/apply externalization; the KNIME «Normalize Model» pattern)

the catalogue row «Calendar effects / holiday dummies (national holidays for the G7 and Switzerland, plus the financial centres -> named 0/1 columns)» — ZERO new dependency, with the same verified per-country counts

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c00_data_utilities/calendar_effects_holidays) — traps #1 and #2, the live-verified silent blanking of an invalid date, the time-zone invariance test, the silent gaps (empty_sources, constant_columns, empty_holiday_set), and the reasons for the omissions: the naming option, the energy-market calendar, the clock-reading constructor, the sequence and alignment helpers, the shape moments, and the plots
precondition_tools: hd_list # A MANDATORY FIRST STEP: the VALID holiday names, since an unknown name is a hard gate; 120 in total — US 18 · CA 6 · GB 4 · DE 5 · FR 6 · IT 6 · JP 33 · CH 5 (live-verified)
hd_holidays # THE DATES before the dummies: empty_sources/n_on_weekend show whether the holiday really exists in the requested years and how many fall on Sat/Sun

cards.method: DISCRETISATION (binning) of ONE numeric column: EQUAL-POPULATION bins (sample quantiles, quantile type 7 PINNED) or EQUAL-WIDTH bins (an explicit seq over the range or over a GIVEN fixed domain) + an out-of-sample APPLY of the STORED breaks
cards.when: converting ONE continuous macro variable into DISCRETE REGIMES (regime dummies): «high vs low inflation», «growth quartile», «spread zone», or INTEGER CODES as the input to a categorical node; ONE node PER variable (fan-out from the frontend). BINNING IS FIT + APPLY: the fit LEARNS the boundaries from the sample, bn_apply REUSES them verbatim on a new sample
cards.when_not: NON-STATIONARY I(1) LEVELS with SAMPLE quantiles, where the «quartiles» reflect the POSITION IN TIME rather than an economic regime — supply differences or rates, or use bn_equal_width with EXOGENOUS boundaries; ENDOGENOUS regime detection from the data themselves -> Markov switching or thresholds (category 06), or #244 (category 29); STRUCTURAL CHANGE POINTS in time -> #3 (category 01); MANY columns at once (one node per variable); NON-LINEARITY WITHOUT information loss -> #253 ply_polynomial, since a polynomial discards nothing while binning DOES; ALREADY categorical variables, which need no binning; charts and histograms (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: you want EQUAL-POPULATION bins (each regime has the same number of observations => the same statistical power per dummy): 3 = terciles, 4 = quartiles, 5 = quintiles, 10 = deciles
you want UNEQUAL bins with an economic meaning («lower tail / centre / upper tail»); it MUST be strictly increasing with the endpoints EXACTLY 0 and 1; it does NOT combine with n_bins
you want EQUAL-WIDTH bins (interpretable value ranges instead of equal population); under a skewed distribution the extreme bins may end up EMPTY — they are reported explicitly in empty_bins

you want COMPARABLE bins across COUNTRIES/SAMPLES or on a NON-STATIONARY series: you supply THEORETICAL, EXOGENOUS boundaries (e.g. around a 2% inflation target) instead of sample ones — THE CORRECT ROUTE when §3b gate 3 forbids sample quantiles

alternatives.alt: bn_apply(breaks = <breaks of a previous fit>) [§3b gate 6]
alternatives.criterion: NEW data (test/out-of-sample/another country): THE SAME boundaries => COMPARABLE regime dummies; a re-fit gives DIFFERENT boundaries and the out-of-sample result is NOT reproduced. Supply the fit's labels/right/include_lowest as well

'na' assigns an EXPLICIT blank code and records it (n_out_of_range, out_of_range_labels), for when you want to KNOW which new values fell outside; 'clamp' assigns them to the EXTREME bin, for regimes defined as «below or above X» — but it DISTORTS the extreme-value information. The default is 'fail' (blocked-by-gate)

EXPLICIT consent when the column has many TIES and two quantiles coincide: the UNIQUE boundaries are kept, the bins become FEWER than requested (n_breaks_dropped) and they no longer carry equal population; the default, False, is a hard stop
you want the 0/1 indicator matrix (n x n_bins) DIRECTLY as regressors; the missing and out-of-range rows come back blank, NOT 0, since a 0 would mean «definitely not in this bin»
you want NON-LINEARITY WITHOUT information loss — binning discards the WITHIN-BIN variance, polynomials do not

output_key_fields: bin (INTEGER codes 1.n_bins per observation, named) + bin_label (character per observation) + labels (the bin NAMES) — NEVER a factor (JSON-safe)
breaks (NUMERIC, n_bins+1 boundaries) = THE FITTED PARAM (§3b gate 6); it is handed back verbatim to bn_apply together with labels/right/include_lowest
counts + share (histogram chart-data) + bin_lower/bin_upper/bin_width (THE BOUNDARIES) + bin_min/bin_max/bin_mean/bin_median (the OBSERVED range INSIDE each bin) + empty_bins/n_empty_bins
dummies: an n x n_bins 0/1 matrix when requested, blank on the unassignable rows, + method ('quantile', 'equal_width' or 'apply') + right and include_lowest
out_of_range + n_out_of_range/out_of_range_index/out_of_range_labels + n_clamped + n_assigned + n/n_valid/n_missing/missing_index/n_distinct + column/observations

bn_quantile_bins ADDITIONALLY: probs + quantile_type (ALWAYS 7 — so that two fits are comparable ONLY if they come from the SAME estimator) + n_bins_requested + n_breaks_dropped + dedupe_breaks + data_min/data_max
bn_equal_width ADDITIONALLY: width + range_min/range_max + range_supplied (WHETHER the boundaries are EXOGENOUS or sample-based) + data_min/data_max
interpretation_traps: §3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization) — WHY THERE ARE THREE FUNCTIONS: the fit LEARNS the breaks from the sample; a re-fit on new data gives DIFFERENT boundaries => the regime dummies are NOT comparable and the out-of-sample result is «reproducible ONLY BY LUCK». That is why the breaks are returned AS A NUMERIC FIELD and bn_apply accepts them BACK (the KNIME «Auto-Binner» -> PMML model / Normalizer -> «Normalize Model» pattern)

§3b GATE 3 (NON-STATIONARITY, Hamilton-Ma-Xi NBER WP 32068): on an I(1) series the SAMPLE quantiles do NOT converge to a population parameter => the «quartiles» reflect the POSITION IN TIME (the early period = a low bin) and NOT an economic regime. A documented PRECONDITION: discretise DIFFERENCES/rates, or use bn_equal_width with THEORETICAL exogenous boundaries. NEVER a silent correction here (§3b gate 2: no hidden conversion)

DETERMINISM #1 (§5): THE QUANTILE TYPE IS PINNED TO 7 (the conventional default) and is NOT exposed as an argument: the NINE types of Hyndman & Fan (1996) give DIFFERENT breaks on the SAME data, so a switchable 'type' would break the reproducibility of STORED workflows («stored workflows pin node versions», §5). The type is ALWAYS returned in quantile_type

DETERMINISM #2: the equal-width boundaries are computed EXPLICITLY as n_bins+1 evenly spaced edges — NEVER by asking the cut routine for a bin COUNT, which SILENTLY MOVES the outer limits by 0.1% of the range (documented) AND does not report the boundaries it used, giving a fit that cannot be externalized and breaking gate 6. There is no randomness, sampling or parallelism; two identical runs are pinned in the tests, for both the wrapper and the node

SILENTLY WRONG (a): VALUES OUTSIDE the breaks come back SILENTLY blank — the documentation states that they are coded as missing; in an out-of-sample apply that means LOST OBSERVATIONS WITH NO INDICATION ⇒ an explicit out_of_range policy, defaulting to 'fail'

SILENTLY WRONG (cut b): UNSORTED breaks are sorted SILENTLY («The default method will sort a numeric vector of breaks») AND the labels are matched AFTER the sorting => the REGIME NAMES land on the WRONG BINS. A hard gate: STRICTLY INCREASING breaks

SILENTLY WRONG (c to f): a blank INSIDE the breaks is ignored SILENTLY, giving ONE bin instead of two; DUPLICATE labels are MERGED SILENTLY into ONE level, so every value lands in it; breaks given as a categorical use the LEVEL CODES SILENTLY; include_lowest=False blanks the MINIMUM value SILENTLY; and an infinity in the data gives a blank bin SILENTLY. ALL are hard gates

SILENTLY WRONG (number of bins): n_bins = 1 is not a discretisation — cut with 2 breaks returns ONE level WITHOUT an error => a gate n_bins >= 2 AND STRICTLY < the number of UNIQUE values (otherwise the boundaries coincide)

TIES (the most frequent real cause of failure): on a column with many repetitions the quantiles COINCIDE and the cut routine throws «'breaks' are not unique». The node catches it BEFORE the call, naming the column and counting the duplicates; the ways out are to lower n_bins, or to consent explicitly with dedupe_breaks=True, which then gives FEWER bins, no longer of equal population. In bn_apply duplicates are ALWAYS A HARD STOP — deduping there would change the number of bins relative to the fit

MISSING-VALUE POLICY: na_action='fail' (the default) or 'keep' — NEVER 'omit'. The regime dummies MUST stay ALIGNED with the series or the panel, and removing rows would break the alignment with y — exactly the mistake the model frame makes silently, see #253. With 'keep' the missing POSITIONS are preserved with a blank code and recorded in n_missing and missing_index

right and include_lowest MUST be THE SAME in the apply as in the fit — the fits here are ALWAYS include_lowest=True — otherwise the BOUNDARY observations change bin; and out_of_range='clamp' REQUIRES include_lowest=True, since a value clamped onto the extreme boundary would otherwise come back blank AGAIN

THE OUTPUT IS NEVER a categorical object: it is kept INTERNALLY and DECOMPOSED into INTEGER codes plus text labels (JSON-safe, §5); the ORDERING lives in the order of 'labels', which is why the ordered-result switch is omitted; the label precision is PINNED to 3 significant digits, the reference default, with a post-check on uniqueness and the level count — the routine itself raises the precision as far as 12 digits, and falls back to 'Range_k' labels when the boundaries differ only at the fourteenth digit (live-verified)

A TERMINAL node (no register/chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers (codes/labels per observation, breaks, per-bin counts/share/boundaries/observed min-max-mean-median, an optional 0/1 matrix). The fit/apply is EXPLICIT: the user hands the breaks back
sources: the cut routine's documentation (live-verified): the breaks are required, the labels default to none, the lowest value is excluded by default, the intervals close on the right, the label precision is 3 digits and the result is unordered; values outside the range of the breaks are coded as missing; «The default method will sort a numeric vector of breaks»; «'breaks' are not unique»; «number of intervals and length of 'labels' differ»; and «when breaks is a single number the outer limits are moved away by 0.1% of the range»

the quantile routine's documentation (live-verified, with type 7 as the default): the probabilities default to the quartiles, gaps are not dropped, the result is named, and the precision is 7 digits; missing values are refused unless dropping them is requested explicitly; and the endpoints coincide with the minimum and the maximum for EVERY type

Hyndman, R.J. & Fan, Y. (1996) «Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages», The American Statistician 50(4) 361-365 — the nine types of sample quantiles; type 7 (p_k = (k-1)/(n-1)) is the conventional default. THE PINNING IS A §5 REQUIREMENT (reproducibility of stored workflows)

Hamilton, J.D., Ma, X. & Xi, J., «Principal Component Analysis for a Mix of Stationary and Nonstationary Variables», NBER WP 32068 — §3b normative gate 3: on a non-stationary series the SAMPLE moments/quantiles do not converge to a population parameter (see #256, the correct route for mixed I(0)/I(1) panels)

the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 6 (fit/apply externalization — explicitly «breaks»; the KNIME Normalizer -> «Normalize Model» pattern; KNIME Auto-Binner -> a PMML model) + gate 2 (no implicit conversion) + the live-verified gate «cut: 'breaks' are not unique on a constant/dense column ⇒ dedupe or stop (⚠️ cut is in base, NOT stats)»

the catalogue row «Binning / discretization (equal-width or quantile; terciles and quartiles for regime dummies)» — ZERO new dependency, returning the breaks for the fit/apply contract, with quantile type 7 as the conventional default

wrapper footer IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column) — the eight live-verified silently-wrong behaviours of the cut routine, the reasons for the omissions (the quantile type, gap handling, naming, precision and fuzz; asking cut for a bin count, the ordered result, the label precision and unlabelled output; and the histogram and interval-lookup helpers), and the post-checks of the bin builder

cards.method: PCA for MIXED I(0)/I(1) variables: an h-step-ahead OLS regression per series (a constant + p own lags) -> PCA on the RESIDUALS (Hamilton-Ma-Xi)
cards.when: common CYCLICAL factors behind many macro series whose stationarity is UNKNOWN or MIXED (I(1) levels + I(0) rates in the SAME panel); the method does NOT require the user to classify the series or to choose a per-series transformation — THE SAME regression on ALL of them; the defaults h=24/p=12 (monthly), h=8/p=4 (quarterly)
cards.when_not: ALL the series are demonstrably stationary and on a common scale -> classical PCA, #117; a latent factor with DYNAMICS, mixed frequency or a ragged-edge nowcast -> #15 or #144; charts (the frontend, §5); ONE series, since N>=2 is required; an unbalanced panel with gaps, since a balanced sample is required; isolating the cycle of ONE series -> the Hamilton regression filter (#57, category 10)

alternatives.criterion: ONLY when ALL the series are stationary; on non-stationary levels the standardization is undefined and the Bai-Ng criteria are corrupted (>1 factor at T=100 when the truth is 0)
you need a state-space DFM with factor dynamics, mixed frequency or ragged-edge missing data instead of a static PCA on the cyclical components

an effective T below 600, that is under 50 years of monthly data -> short_sample=True: a large h raises the risk of a spurious factor (Onatski & Wang 2021), and the paper recommends h=12, or h=1 in small samples
the series are ALREADY on a common scale and you want a COVARIANCE matrix; otherwise keep the default 'unit_variance' (= the paper's procedure)

output_key_fields: factor1/scores: the estimated common CYCLICAL factors per time point (T_eff x k) — the main chart-data; the x-axis = time
loadings: N x k sign-normalized (which series loads on which factor); loadings_hmx/factors_hmx = the paper's normalization (lambda'lambda/N = 1, f = N^-1 lambda'C, eq. 9-12)
sdev/var_explained/cum_var/pc1_var + pca_matrix ('correlation' under the default, 'covariance' under 'none')
residuals (T_eff x N) = the CYCLICAL COMPONENTS c-hat_it of eq. (7) + residual_sd/r_squared/sigma/rss/rank per series
coefficients (N x (p+1)) + lag_terms + residual_center/residual_scale: ALL the fitted params as NUMBERS (fit/apply externalization, §3b gate 6)

cards.method: Categorical association / contingency tables: a chi-squared test of independence, Fisher's exact test, nominal vs ordinal association measures with CIs
cards.when: TWO CATEGORICAL answers PER RESPONDENT in a cross-section survey (e.g. a price expectation up/=/down x a plan for a major purchase): the contingency table + sparsity diagnostics (ca_contingency) -> an independence test (ca_chisq if Cochran's rule passes; ca_fisher if it does not) -> the SIZE of the relation with measures + CIs (ca_associations)
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES / time-dependent data (a hard cross-section gate — see the #257 preconditions; the HAC path: sandwich, cat 07); CONTINUOUS variables (discretise first: c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column); QUANTIFICATION of survey balance/Carlson-Parkin shares -> #237 quantification; weighted survey designs (weights/strata/clusters) -> survey (svychisq); STRATIFIED / >=3-dimensional tables (mantelhaen/loglin); a CONTINUOUS vs CATEGORICAL comparison of means -> #250 tests-parametric / #251 tests-nonparametric; charts (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: cochran_ok=False — an expected count below 1, or more than 20% of the cells below 5 — ⇒ an EXACT test instead of the asymptotic chi-squared; a 2x2 table ALSO yields an odds ratio with its interval

alternatives.alt: ca_chisq with simulate_p_value=True and a seed
alternatives.criterion: a sparse AND large table where the exact Fisher test fails («FEXACT error 5/6/7») ⇒ a Monte-Carlo p-value (r2dtable, seeded)
the codes ENCODE AN ORDER (Likert/up-=-down) ⇒ Gamma/Kendall tau-b/Stuart tau-c/Somers' D; on a NOMINAL scale they are uninterpretable (this is NEVER guessed)
ONE of the variables is CONTINUOUS (a comparison of means/medians per group) rather than two categorical ones
a weighted/complex sample (weights/strata/clusters) ⇒ the Rao-Scott correction; #257 presupposes a SIMPLE random sample

output_key_fields: ca_contingency: counts/expected (r x c) + prop_total/prop_row/prop_col + row_sums/col_sums + min_expected/n_cells_below_1/n_cells_below_5/share_below_5 + cochran_ok/strict_ok (THE ROUTING CRITERION chi-squared vs Fisher)

ca_chisq: statistic (OF THE TEST — Yates-corrected when correct=True AND the table is 2x2) / statistic_pearson (ALWAYS the UNCORRECTED Pearson X²) / df / p_value / significant / decision + cramers_v (ALWAYS computed from statistic_pearson ⇒ IDENTICAL to the Cramér's V of ca_associations) + residuals (Pearson) / stdres (approximately standard normal) / contribution / contribution_share (the share of statistic_pearson, which ALWAYS sums to 1) PER CELL — the chart data showing which cell «drives» the X² — plus yates_requested and yates_applied
ca_fisher: p_value/decision + odds_ratio/odds_ratio_lwr/odds_ratio_upr/conf_level (2x2 ONLY, conditional MLE) + is_2x2 + workspace or (simulate_p_value, B, seed)

ca_associations: the nominal block {cramers_v, contingency_coef, tschuprows_t, uncertainty_coef_sym/row/col, gk_tau_row/col}, each as (estimate, lower, upper); phi for a 2x2 table ONLY, and absent otherwise; gamma on the ordinal scale ONLY; plus the full 16-by-3 or 9-by-3 association matrix, with assocs_measures and ordinal_excluded

ALL: x_codes/y_codes + x_labels/y_labels (EXTERNALIZATION OF THE CODING — §3b gate 6) + n/n_input/n_na/na_action + cross_section_gate {lb_statistic, lb_p_value, lb_lag, n, n_na, alpha, tested, decision}
interpretation_traps: NORMATIVE GATE 4 (cross-section only): EVERY function calls the SHARED cross-section gate (the shared gates module) on the ORIGINAL vectors — an explicit rejection of any time-indexed input type, plus a Ljung-Box whiteness precheck at lag = min(10, n/5); autocorrelation INFLATES the Type I error ⇒ a spuriously significant chi-squared. That is why the input is VECTORS OF OBSERVATIONS rather than a ready-made contingency table: the whiteness statistic is not defined on an aggregated table

gate_alpha (default 0.05) — DECOUPLED FROM THE TEST'S alpha: alpha exists ONLY in ca_chisq/ca_fisher (the only ones with a decision); ca_contingency/ca_associations do NOT expose it at all (it would be a silent no-op). The Ljung-Box precheck is a TEST OF SIZE gate_alpha ⇒ by construction it blocks a small share of VALID i.i.d. input; LIVE-MEASURED (the engine, rnorm, 5000 replications): n=200 -> 1.6%/5.7%/10.1%, n=60 -> 2.3%/6.7%/10.8% for 0.01/0.05/0.10

ordered (default True) — AN EXPLICIT DECLARATION OF ROW ORDER: survey answers are the permutable population par excellence, yet a SORTED file makes the whiteness check reject (live-verified), whereas the chi-square, the exact test and Cramér's V are PERMUTATION-INVARIANT, since the contingency table does not change. ordered=False omits the whiteness check explicitly (branch='skipped-by-declaration', decision='pass-unordered'), while the structural checks and the time-indexed-type rejection (branch='class-rejected') stay ALWAYS active. Supplying lb_lag together with ordered=False is a hard stop

SILENTLY WRONG: chisq_test with expected counts < 5 emits ONLY the warning «Chi-squared approximation may be incorrect» and returns a p-value ⇒ OUR OWN HARD gate (rule='cochran' by default: none < 1 AND <=20% of the cells < 5; rule='strict': none < 5) that routes to ca_fisher / simulate_p_value

SILENTLY WRONG: a ONE-row/one-column table ⇒ chisq_test switches SILENTLY to a «Chi-squared test for given probabilities» (goodness-of-fit, df = c-1) — A DIFFERENT TEST; gated with >=2 levels + a post-check df == (r-1)(c-1)

SILENTLY WRONG: cross-tabulation drops the gaps SILENTLY ⇒ an explicit policy, na_action='fail' by default or 'omit' PAIRWISE, with n_input and n_na always in the output; a ZERO MARGIN — an empty row or column — gives a NaN statistic and a blank p with ONLY a warning, and a cryptic type error inside Cramér's V ⇒ a hard gate

A CATEGORICAL INPUT (the most frequent wrong type in a categorical node) ⇒ a hard stop with an EDUCATIONAL message: it names the argument, reports the dtype and the level count — never the storage mode, which live-verified LIES, since a categorical stores as numeric and yet is not numeric — and gives the EXPLICIT conversion to integer codes 1..k in level order, with the level names becoming the labels. The node requires NUMERICALLY CODED VECTORS OF OBSERVATIONS, a requirement of the shared cross-section gate

SILENTLY WRONG: phi on an r x c table does NOT error — it returns sqrt(X²/n), which EXCEEDS 1 (a perfect 3x3 gives 1.414214); it is exposed ONLY for 2x2. Likewise the Yates correction is ignored SILENTLY outside 2x2, so yates_applied reports what ACTUALLY happened; in ca_associations, correct=True outside 2x2 is a hard stop

YATES AGAINST EFFECT SIZE (CRITICAL): Cramér's V is defined (Cramér 1946 §21.9) on the UNCORRECTED Pearson X² — NOT on the Yates-corrected statistic that is the conventional DEFAULT for a 2x2 table (correct=True). The node ALWAYS computes the SIZE measures from statistic_pearson, INDEPENDENTLY of the correction, so that the Cramér's V of ca_chisq COINCIDES — within 1e-12, pinned in a regression test — with the one of ca_associations. LIVE (2x2, n=120): 0.5009034 from the Yates statistic against 0.5175817 from the Pearson one, a 4.4% UNDERSTATEMENT and TWO different numbers for ONE named statistic. Likewise contribution_share is divided by statistic_pearson, which otherwise summed to 1.0678, giving «shares» above 100%. On the Monte-Carlo path the correction is switched off, so the statistic and the Pearson statistic coincide

SILENTLY WRONG: the exact test on an r x c table ignores the alternative SILENTLY — live, a 3x3 with a one-sided alternative gave THE SAME p-value as the two-sided one ⇒ one-sided is allowed ONLY for 2x2, and it is incompatible with simulate_p_value, which is always two-sided

ORDINAL vs NOMINAL: the ordinal measures (Gamma/Kendall tau-b/Stuart tau-c/Somers' D/Pearson/Spearman) change SIGN with the arbitrary order of the categories ⇒ scale='nominal' is the SAFE default and excludes them explicitly (ordinal_excluded). NOTE: the Goodman-Kruskal TAU is a NOMINAL PRE measure (not Kendall's/Stuart's tau) and is ALWAYS returned

THE EXACT NETWORK ALGORITHM allocates its memory up front: a 4x4 table with n=300 fails at the default workspace («FEXACT error 6. LDKEY=620 is too small»); SOME such tables pass with a ten-fold workspace while DENSER ones fail there too («FEXACT error 7»); and a 12x12 fails even at 2e8 ⇒ the only remaining route is simulate_p_value=True, seeded. The node translates the cryptic message into an educational one with the two ways out; and there is a level cap, max_levels, defaulting to 20 within a permitted [2,50]

§3b gate 6 (fit/apply externalization): the node does NOT fit/transform, but it EXTERNALIZES THE CODING — x_codes/y_codes (numeric) + x_labels/y_labels are ALWAYS returned and handed back as x_levels/y_levels in the survey's next wave ⇒ tables COMPARABLE cell by cell. If binning preceded it, bn_apply keeps THE SAME breaks

DETERMINISM: all the default paths are algebraic — and the 'fisher' interval method for Cramér's V is Fisher's z transformation, not a simulation; the TWO Monte-Carlo paths seed the generator AND restore the caller's state afterwards; and the association matrix is PINNED to its most verbose form, since the lower settings return only 3 of the 16 measures and would change the SHAPE of the output
sources: Cochran, W.G. (1954) «Some Methods for Strengthening the Common Chi-Squared Tests», Biometrics 10(4):417-451 — the rule «no expected count < 1, <= 20% of the cells < 5»
Cramér, H. (1946) Mathematical Methods of Statistics, §21.9 — Cramér's V
Goodman, L.A. & Kruskal, W.H. (1954) «Measures of Association for Cross Classifications», JASA 49:732-764 — tau (a NOMINAL PRE measure) and gamma (ORDINAL)
Agresti, A. (2013) Categorical Data Analysis, 3rd ed., ch. 2-3 — nominal vs ordinal measures; why the ordinal ones are uninterpretable on a nominal scale
Fisher, R.A. (1935) The Design of Experiments, ch. II — the exact test

the chisq_test routine's documentation / the fisher_test routine — «For 2 by 2 tables, the null of conditional independence is equivalent to the hypothesis that the odds ratio equals one»; the warning-only behaviour with expected counts < 5; workspace/FEXACT

the association-measures reference — Cramér's V, the contingency coefficient, Tschuprow's T, phi, the uncertainty coefficient, the Goodman-Kruskal tau and gamma, and the full 16-by-3 association matrix
the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 4 (cross-section only); Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4 — the rule lag = min(10, n/5) of the Ljung-Box precheck
precondition_tools: ca_contingency # FIRST the table: min_expected/cochran_ok/strict_ok decide chi-squared vs Fisher
c00_data_utilities/discretisation_numeric_column.bn_quantile_bins # a CONTINUOUS variable -> INTEGER codes BEFORE the node (bn_apply for the 2nd wave, THE SAME breaks)

The node requires NUMERICALLY CODED VECTORS OF OBSERVATIONS, a requirement of the shared cross-section gate · SILENTLY WRONG: phi on an r x c table does NOT error — it returns sqrt(X²/n), which EXCEEDS 1 (a perfect 3x3 gives 1.414214); it is exposed ONLY for 2x2. Likewise the Yates correction is ignored SILENTLY outside 2x2, so yates_applied reports what ACTUALLY happened; in ca_associations, correct=True outside 2x2 is a hard stop · YATES AGAINST EFFECT SIZE (CRITICAL): Cramér's V is defined (Cramér 1946 §21.9) on the UNCORRECTED Pearson X² — NOT on the Yates-corrected statistic that is the conventional DEFAULT for a 2x2 table (correct=True). The node ALWAYS computes the SIZE measures from statistic_pearson, INDEPENDENTLY of the correction, so that the Cramér's V of ca_chisq COINCIDES — within 1e-12, pinned in a regression test — with the one of ca_associations. LIVE (2x2, n=120): 0.5009034 from the Yates statistic against 0.5175817 from the Pearson one, a 4.4% UNDERSTATEMENT and TWO different numbers for ONE named statistic. Likewise contribution_share is divided by statistic_pearson, which otherwise summed to 1.0678, giving «shares» above 100%. On the Monte-Carlo path the correction is switched off, so the statistic and the Pearson statistic coincide · SILENTLY WRONG: the exact test on an r x c table ignores the alternative SILENTLY — live, a 3x3 with a one-sided alternative gave THE SAME p-value as the two-sided one ⇒ one-sided is allowed ONLY for 2x2, and it is incompatible with simulate_p_value, which is always two-sided · ORDINAL vs NOMINAL: the ordinal measures (Gamma/Kendall tau-b/Stuart tau-c/Somers' D/Pearson/Spearman) change SIGN with the arbitrary order of the categories ⇒ scale='nominal' is the SAFE default and excludes them explicitly (ordinal_excluded). NOTE: the Goodman-Kruskal TAU is a NOMINAL PRE measure (not Kendall's/Stuart's tau) and is ALWAYS returned · THE EXACT NETWORK ALGORITHM allocates its memory up front: a 4x4 table with n=300 fails at the default workspace («FEXACT error 6. LDKEY=620 is too small»); SOME such tables pass with a ten-fold workspace while DENSER ones fail there too («FEXACT error 7»); and a 12x12 fails even at 2e8 ⇒ the only remaining route is simulate_p_value=True, seeded. The node translates the cryptic message into an educational one with the two ways out; and there is a level cap, max_levels, defaulting to 20 within a permitted [2,50] · §3b gate 6 (fit/apply externalization): the node does NOT fit/transform, but it EXTERNALIZES THE CODING — x_codes/y_codes (numeric) + x_labels/y_labels are ALWAYS returned and handed back as x_levels/y_levels in the survey's next wave ⇒ tables COMPARABLE cell by cell. If binning preceded it, bn_apply keeps THE SAME breaks · DETERMINISM: all the default paths are algebraic — and the 'fisher' interval method for Cramér's V is Fisher's z transformation, not a simulation; the TWO Monte-Carlo paths seed the generator AND restore the caller's state afterwards; and the association matrix is PINNED to its most verbose form, since the lower settings return only 3 of the 16 measures and would change the SHAPE of the output
Sources: Cochran, W.G. (1954) «Some Methods for Strengthening the Common Chi-Squared Tests», Biometrics 10(4):417-451 — the rule «no expected count < 1, <= 20% of the cells < 5» · Cramér, H. (1946) Mathematical Methods of Statistics, §21.9 — Cramér's V · Goodman, L.A. & Kruskal, W.H. (1954) «Measures of Association for Cross Classifications», JASA 49:732-764 — tau (a NOMINAL PRE measure) and gamma (ORDINAL) · Agresti, A. (2013) Categorical Data Analysis, 3rd ed., ch. 2-3 — nominal vs ordinal measures; why the ordinal ones are uninterpretable on a nominal scale · Fisher, R.A. (1935) The Design of Experiments, ch. II — the exact test · the chisq_test routine's documentation / the fisher_test routine — «For 2 by 2 tables, the null of conditional independence is equivalent to the hypothesis that the odds ratio equals one»; the warning-only behaviour with expected counts < 5; workspace/FEXACT · the association-measures reference — Cramér's V, the contingency coefficient, Tschuprow's T, phi, the uncertainty coefficient, the Goodman-Kruskal tau and gamma, and the full 16-by-3 association matrix · the normative gate spec §3b normative gate 4 (cross-section only); Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, FPP 3rd ed. §5.4 — the rule lag = min(10, n/5) of the Ljung-Box precheck

cards.method: Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen estimators with the log-rank family of tests
cards.when: estimating a survival or cumulative-hazard curve from right-censored durations, and comparing curves across groups without assuming a parametric shape
cards.when_not: you need covariates (-> #Cox); the durations are interval-censored; the outcome is competing risks (-> cumulative incidence); you want a parametric time-to-event distribution

alternatives.criterion: you need to adjust for covariates rather than compare raw curves
more than one mutually exclusive failure type
you want a smooth closed-form survival function and extrapolation

output_key_fields: survival/cumhazard: the step function on the observed event times
lower/upper: pointwise confidence band at conf_level
median_survival: the first time the curve crosses 0.5, None if it never does
logrank: statistic, df and p_value for equality of curves across groups
interpretation_traps: the curve is only identified up to the largest observed time; beyond it the estimate is undefined, not flat
median_survival is None when the curve never reaches 0.5 -- that is heavy censoring, not an error
the log-rank test assumes proportional hazards; with crossing curves it loses power and can be near-zero for a real difference

cards.method: Cox proportional-hazards regression with time-varying covariates and stratification
cards.when: estimating covariate effects on the hazard of an event without committing to a baseline hazard shape; hazard ratios are the quantity of interest
cards.when_not: the proportional-hazards assumption fails and cannot be repaired by stratification (-> AFT); you want an absolute survival prediction rather than a ratio; there are competing risks

alternatives.criterion: you need a closed-form survival function or to extrapolate beyond the data
the hazards are non-proportional in a small number of discrete strata
durations are recorded in coarse intervals with many ties

output_key_fields: params/coef: log hazard ratios; exp(coef) is the hazard ratio
bse, z, p_value, conf_int: Wald inference on the log scale
baseline_cumhazard: the Breslow estimate of the baseline
loglike, concordance: fit and discrimination
interpretation_traps: coefficients are on the LOG hazard scale -- exponentiate before reading them as hazard ratios
a hazard ratio is not a risk ratio and does not integrate to one over time
ties are handled by an approximation; with heavy tying the Efron and Breslow handlers disagree materially
stratification removes the strata's main effect from the estimate entirely -- it is not a control variable

cards.method: Parametric accelerated-failure-time models: Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic and exponential
cards.when: you want a smooth closed-form survival function, the ability to extrapolate beyond the last observed time, or a time-ratio interpretation rather than a hazard ratio
cards.when_not: you are unwilling to commit to a distributional shape (-> Cox); the shape is clearly non-monotonic in a way none of the four families capture

alternatives.criterion: you do not want to assume a baseline shape
the hazard shape is complex and the four families all fit badly
no covariates and no extrapolation needed

output_key_fields: params: coefficients on the LOG time scale; exp(coef) is a time ratio
scale/shape: the fitted distribution parameters
aic, bic, loglike: for choosing among the four families
predicted_median/predicted_mean: fitted survival summaries
interpretation_traps: an AFT coefficient is a TIME ratio, not a hazard ratio -- a positive coefficient lengthens survival
only the Weibull and exponential are simultaneously AFT and proportional-hazards; for the others the two scales disagree
the exponential imposes a constant hazard, which is almost never right for economic durations and shows up as a poor AIC rather than an error
extrapolation beyond the data is the point of the model and also its main risk
sources: Kalbfleisch & Prentice 2002, The Statistical Analysis of Failure Time Data, 2nd ed.

cards.method: Discrete-time hazard models with complementary log-log and logit links
cards.when: durations are recorded in coarse intervals -- months, quarters, waves -- so ties are pervasive and a continuous-time model is a fiction
cards.when_not: durations are measured finely enough for a continuous-time model (-> Cox/AFT); there is no person-period expansion available

alternatives.alt: Cox with an appropriate tie handler
alternatives.criterion: the discreteness is mild and the grid is fine
you want a closed-form continuous survival function
the exit is to more than one competing destination

output_key_fields: params: coefficients on the link scale; cloglog recovers the proportional-hazards parameter
baseline_hazard: the fitted hazard at each duration interval
survival: the implied discrete survivor function
loglike, aic: fit
interpretation_traps: the input must be a PERSON-PERIOD table -- one row per unit per interval at risk -- not one row per unit
with a cloglog link the coefficients are the underlying continuous-time proportional-hazards parameters; with a logit link they are not
the baseline must be modelled explicitly (dummies, polynomial or spline in duration); omitting it forces a flat hazard
unobserved heterogeneity biases duration dependence toward negative -- the estimated hazard falls even when the true one does not
sources: Jenkins 2005, Survival Analysis (unpublished manuscript, University of Essex)

cards.method: Competing risks: cause-specific hazards, cumulative incidence and the Fine-Gray subdistribution model
cards.when: a unit can exit to more than one mutually exclusive destination and treating the other destinations as censoring would overstate the risk of the one you care about
cards.when_not: there is only one failure type (-> Kaplan-Meier/Cox); the destinations are not mutually exclusive

alternatives.criterion: you want the effect on the hazard of one cause among those still at risk
you want the effect on the observable cumulative incidence
wrong here -- it treats competing events as censoring and overstates incidence

output_key_fields: cumulative_incidence: the CIF per cause, which sums with the survivor function to one
cause_specific: per-cause hazard-model coefficients
subdistribution: Fine-Gray coefficients, on the CIF scale
gray_test: statistic and p_value for equality of CIFs across groups
interpretation_traps: ONE minus Kaplan-Meier is NOT the cumulative incidence under competing risks -- it is biased upward, sometimes severely
a cause-specific hazard ratio and a subdistribution hazard ratio answer different questions and routinely point in opposite directions
the CIFs of all causes plus the survivor function must sum to one; a set that does not is a sign the events were not mutually exclusive

cards.method: Frailty and shared-frailty models for unobserved heterogeneity
cards.when: units are clustered, or duration dependence is suspected to be contaminated by unobserved heterogeneity, and you want to separate the two
cards.when_not: there is no clustering and no reason to expect heterogeneity; the sample is too small to identify a frailty variance

alternatives.criterion: you only need correct inference, not a heterogeneity estimate
the clusters are few and you can afford a baseline per cluster
durations are interval-recorded

output_key_fields: params: covariate effects conditional on the frailty
frailty_variance: theta, the dispersion of the unobserved term; zero means no heterogeneity
loglike, aic: fit
lrt_frailty: likelihood-ratio test of theta = 0, which is on the boundary
interpretation_traps: the test of theta = 0 sits on the boundary of the parameter space, so the null distribution is a mixture and the naive p-value is conservative
conditional (frailty) and marginal (population-average) coefficients differ; they are not interchangeable
unobserved heterogeneity and genuine negative duration dependence are only weakly separated -- identification comes from the functional form, not from the data
sources: Hougaard 2000, Analysis of Multivariate Survival Data
Lancaster 1990, The Econometric Analysis of Transition Data

cards.method: Proportional-hazards diagnostics: Schoenfeld residuals and time-interaction tests
cards.when: checking the assumption a Cox model rests on, before its hazard ratios are reported as if they held at every horizon
cards.when_not: the model is not a proportional-hazards model (an AFT needs different diagnostics); the sample has too few events for residual patterns to be readable

alternatives.criterion: the violation is confined to a discrete variable you do not need an estimate for
the violation is a smooth trend in the log hazard ratio
the violation is pervasive across covariates

output_key_fields: schoenfeld: scaled residuals per covariate per event time
zph: per-covariate and global test of a zero slope against time
slope: the fitted trend, which is the direction the hazard ratio drifts
martingale/deviance: residuals for functional-form and outlier checks
interpretation_traps: the global test is not a substitute for the per-covariate tests -- a large violation in one direction can cancel another
the test depends on the time transform: identity, log and rank transforms disagree, and a violation visible under one can vanish under another
a significant test with a very large sample can flag a violation too small to matter; read the slope, not just the p-value
martingale residuals are strongly skewed by construction and must not be read as approximately normal

cards.method: Spell duration dependence and hazard-shape estimation
cards.when: the question is the SHAPE of the hazard over the spell -- whether exit rates rise or fall with elapsed duration, as in unemployment or firm-survival studies
cards.when_not: you only need covariate effects (-> Cox); the spells are too short or too few for a shape to be identified

alternatives.criterion: you want a readable shape with no functional-form commitment
a monotone shape is enough and you want one parameter for it
you must separate true duration dependence from unobserved heterogeneity

output_key_fields: hazard: the estimated hazard on the duration grid
shape: increasing / decreasing / non-monotonic, with the turning point where one exists
weibull_p: the Weibull shape parameter, where p > 1 is positive duration dependence
conf_band: pointwise band on the hazard
interpretation_traps: unobserved heterogeneity biases the estimated hazard DOWNWARD over the spell -- apparent negative duration dependence is the single most common artefact in this literature
the piecewise grid drives the answer: too few intervals hide the shape, too many make it noise
the hazard near the largest observed duration rests on very few units still at risk and its band is correspondingly wide
sources: Van den Berg 2001, Duration models: specification, identification and multiple durations (Handbook of Econometrics 5)

cards.when: estimating demand for differentiated products from market-level shares when price is endogenous and substitution patterns must not be forced into the IIA straitjacket
cards.when_not: you have individual choice data (-> mixed logit); there is one product; you need no substitution structure and a simple logit will do

alternatives.criterion: a known grouping captures substitution and you want a closed form
you observe individual choices rather than market shares
IIA is acceptable and price is exogenous

xi: the structural demand shock recovered by inversion
objective, gradient_norm: GMM objective and first-order condition at the optimum
converged: whether BOTH the inner share inversion and the outer search converged
interpretation_traps: the inner contraction tolerance must be far tighter than the outer one; a loose inner loop produces a smooth-looking optimum that is not one
sigma is identified by variation in the choice set ACROSS markets -- with few markets it is barely identified and the standard error will not say so
a reported optimum with a non-trivial gradient norm is a failed search, not a corner solution

Pitfalls: the inner contraction tolerance must be far tighter than the outer one; a loose inner loop produces a smooth-looking optimum that is not one · sigma is identified by variation in the choice set ACROSS markets -- with few markets it is barely identified and the standard error will not say so · a reported optimum with a non-trivial gradient norm is a failed search, not a corner solution
Sources: Berry, Levinsohn & Pakes 1995 (Econometrica 63:841-890) · Nevo 2000 (Journal of Economics and Management Strategy 9:513) · Conlon & Gortmaker 2020 (RAND Journal of Economics 51:1108) · pyblp

cards.when_not: you already have strong excluded cost shifters; the model is not yet estimated at all (fit a first stage first)

alternatives.criterion: a cheap, transparent default
local competition matters and the BLP sums are too coarse
you have a consistent first-stage estimate and want efficiency

output_key_fields: instruments: the constructed instrument matrix
first_stage_f: weak-instrument diagnostic per endogenous variable
improvement: change in the GMM objective and in the standard errors
interpretation_traps: optimal instruments require a CONSISTENT first-stage estimate; built from a bad first stage they are optimal for the wrong model
differentiation instruments are functions of characteristics, so they are invalid if characteristics are themselves endogenous
a first-stage F below the conventional threshold means the whole demand estimate is untrustworthy, not merely imprecise
sources: Gandhi & Houde 2019, Measuring substitution patterns in differentiated products industries (NBER WP 26375)

cards.method: Own- and cross-price elasticities and diversion ratios
cards.when: translating estimated demand parameters into the quantities policy and merger analysis actually use: how much a product loses to a price rise and where that volume goes
cards.when_not: the demand model has not been estimated yet; you want welfare rather than substitution (-> welfare card)

alternatives.criterion: the question is where volume goes, not how much is lost
only the market-level response to a uniform price change matters

cards.method: Nested logit demand
cards.when: a known product grouping captures substitution well enough, and you want a closed-form estimator that runs in seconds rather than a full random-coefficients search
cards.when_not: the nesting structure is unknown or contested; substitution crosses the nests in ways the structure cannot express (-> BLP)

alternatives.criterion: no grouping is needed and IIA is acceptable
substitution is driven by continuous characteristics, not a discrete grouping
there is a credible hierarchy of groupings

output_key_fields: params: characteristic coefficients and the nesting parameter rho
rho: within-nest correlation; must lie in [0,1) for the model to be consistent with utility maximisation
elasticities: closed-form own and cross elasticities
loglike, aic
interpretation_traps: rho outside [0,1) means the estimates are NOT consistent with random utility maximisation -- it is a specification failure, not a large parameter
the within-nest share is mechanically correlated with the error, so it must be instrumented; ignoring that biases rho toward one
the nesting structure is an assumption the data cannot test from inside the model
sources: Train 2009, Discrete Choice Methods with Simulation

cards.method: Multinomial and conditional logit
cards.when: individual-level choice among a small unordered set, where the regressors vary by chooser (multinomial) or by alternative (conditional)
cards.when_not: the alternatives are ordered (-> ordered choice); IIA is untenable and you need substitution structure (-> mixed or nested logit); shares are market level

alternatives.criterion: IIA fails and you have repeated choices or panel structure
a discrete grouping captures the substitution
the alternatives have a natural order

output_key_fields: params: coefficients, per alternative for multinomial and shared for conditional
marginal_effects: probability derivatives, which are what is interpretable
predicted_probabilities: fitted choice probabilities
loglike, aic, pseudo_r2, hausman_iia
interpretation_traps: multinomial logit coefficients are relative to a BASE alternative and change entirely if the base changes; only the marginal effects are invariant
IIA is a substantive restriction, not a technicality -- the Hausman-McFadden test is low power and passing it is weak evidence
a perfectly predicted alternative drives its coefficient to infinity; the optimiser reports a large number rather than an error
sources: McFadden 1974, Conditional logit analysis of qualitative choice behavior (Frontiers in Econometrics)
