cards.method: Structural and cyclically-adjusted balances with output-gap elasticities
cards.when: separating the part of the fiscal position that reflects the cycle from the part that reflects policy
cards.when_not: the output gap is not credibly estimated, in which case the adjustment is arbitrary; one-offs cannot be identified

alternatives.criterion: the standard adjustment for the cycle
also removes one-off and temporary measures
you want a rule that does not depend on the gap at all

output_key_fields: cyclically_adjusted: the balance net of the cycle
structural: also net of one-offs
cyclical_component: the part attributed to the cycle
elasticity_used: the semi-elasticity applied, which drives the whole adjustment
interpretation_traps: the adjustment is only as good as the OUTPUT GAP, which is unobserved, heavily revised, and estimated with wide uncertainty -- real-time structural balances are revised by large amounts
the aggregate semi-elasticity hides very different revenue and expenditure elasticities; using a single number misstates composition effects
one-off measures are identified by judgement, and that judgement is where most of the discretion in a structural balance lives
sources: Girouard & Andre 2005, Measuring cyclically-adjusted budget balances for OECD countries (OECD Economics Department Working Papers 434)
Mourre, Astarita & Princen 2014, Adjusting the budget balance for the business cycle (European Economy Economic Papers 536)

cards.method: Fiscal-rule compliance simulation and adjustment paths
cards.when: checking whether a projected path satisfies a numerical fiscal rule, and computing the adjustment a rule requires
cards.when_not: there is no numerical rule to test against; the rule's escape clauses dominate and compliance is not well defined

alternatives.criterion: the rule is on the debt ratio
the rule caps expenditure growth
the rule is on the cyclically-adjusted position

output_key_fields: compliant: per-period compliance with each rule
gap_to_rule: distance from the requirement, in output share
adjustment_path: the balance path that would restore compliance
binding_rule: which rule binds first when several apply
interpretation_traps: several rules usually apply at once and they can CONFLICT; reporting compliance with one while another binds is the standard misuse
escape clauses and transition arrangements are part of the rule; a mechanical compliance calculation that ignores them is not the legal test

cards.method: Tax-benefit rule engine: parameters, entities, periods and reform overlays
cards.when: computing a household's tax liability and benefit entitlement from the legislated rules, so a reform can be costed before it is enacted
cards.when_not: you only need an average effective rate from aggregate data; the country's rules are not implemented in the parameter set

alternatives.criterion: you need one summary elasticity, not household detail
the whole point is comparing legislated and counterfactual rules
a simple schedule suffices

output_key_fields: variables: computed tax and benefit variables per entity
entities: the household, family and person structure the rules were applied over
period: the period the calculation refers to
reform_delta: the difference a reform overlay makes, per variable
interpretation_traps: entity structure is LOAD-BEARING: a benefit assessed at family level and a tax assessed at person level cannot be added without an explicit aggregation rule

a reform overlay changes only what it names; every interaction with untouched rules is computed, and those interactions are usually the surprise

cards.method: Disposable income, net-of-tax income and budget constraints
cards.when: tracing how gross income becomes take-home income across the earnings distribution, which is the object every incentive question rests on
cards.when_not: you only need the statutory rate; the rules governing in-work benefits are not implemented

alternatives.criterion: you want rates rather than levels
you want the whole earnings-to-income mapping
no benefits interact and the schedule is the answer

output_key_fields: disposable_income: income after taxes and transfers
budget_constraint: disposable income across an earnings grid
components: the tax and benefit elements that make it up
kinks: earnings points where the slope changes discontinuously
interpretation_traps: the budget constraint is frequently NON-CONVEX, with cliffs where a benefit withdraws entirely -- a smooth approximation hides exactly the behaviour that matters
the result is for a specific household type; there is no such thing as the budget constraint without stating composition, housing costs and hours
benefit take-up is assumed complete by default, which overstates incomes at the bottom
sources: Blundell & MaCurdy 1999, Labor supply (Handbook of Labor Economics 3A)

cards.method: Marginal and participation effective tax rates and work incentives
cards.when: measuring what a household actually keeps from an extra hour, or from taking a job at all -- the two incentive margins policy cares about
cards.when_not: the rules governing withdrawal of the relevant benefits are not implemented; behaviour rather than incentive is the question

alternatives.criterion: the intensive margin, an extra unit of earnings
the extensive margin, moving into work
the ratio of out-of-work to in-work income

output_key_fields: metr: marginal effective tax rate across the earnings grid
ptr: participation tax rate for the modelled transition
replacement_rate: out-of-work income over in-work income
high_metr_share: share of the population above a chosen threshold
interpretation_traps: METRs ABOVE ONE are real and common where several benefits withdraw at once -- they are a finding about the rules, not a computational error
the METR depends on the size of the earnings increment used to compute it; a large increment smooths over cliffs and understates the peak
the participation tax rate depends on the assumed alternative state; 'not working' must be specified precisely
sources: Adam, Browne & Heady 2010, Taxation in the UK (Dimensions of Tax Design, Mirrlees Review)

cards.method: Static distributional impact: winners, losers and decile incidence
cards.when: costing a reform and showing who gains and who loses, before any behavioural response
cards.when_not: the behavioural response is large enough that a static answer is misleading and should be labelled as such

alternatives.criterion: the first-round, mechanical effect
labour supply responds materially
only the exchequer cost is wanted

output_key_fields: decile_impact: mean and median gain by income decile
winners_losers: shares gaining, losing and unaffected
budget_cost: net exchequer cost
poverty_inequality: change in headline poverty and inequality measures
interpretation_traps: a STATIC result assumes nobody changes behaviour; for large reforms that is a strong assumption and the label must travel with the number

cards.method: Behavioural labour-supply response
cards.when: adding a behavioural margin to a reform costing, so the estimate reflects that people change hours and participation when incentives change
cards.when_not: the elasticities are not credible for the population in question; the reform is too small for a behavioural response to matter

alternatives.criterion: the first-round effect is enough
a transparent, parameterised response
you want a utility-consistent model

output_key_fields: labour_supply_change: hours and participation response
revenue_with_behaviour: cost after the response
elasticities_used: the parameters driving the answer
decomposition: mechanical versus behavioural components of the cost
interpretation_traps: the answer is a FUNCTION OF THE ASSUMED ELASTICITIES, which are not estimated here; report them beside the result or the number is uninterpretable
extensive and intensive elasticities differ by an order of magnitude across groups; a single population elasticity is rarely defensible
behavioural responses estimated on past reforms may not transfer to a reform of a different size or salience
sources: Blundell & MaCurdy 1999, Labor supply (Handbook of Labor Economics 3A)

cards.when: making a survey sample match known population totals, so simulated aggregates are comparable with administrative figures
cards.when_not: the survey already matches the controls; the controls themselves are unreliable

alternatives.criterion: few, well-populated cells
several marginal totals must be matched at once
you must prevent extreme weights

cards.when_not: you need facility-level emissions; the multi-regional table is too aggregated for the sector in question

alternatives.criterion: the question is territorial emissions
the question is the footprint of demand
you need product-level rather than sector-level detail

cards.when: attributing a change in emissions or energy use to activity, structure and intensity, so the drivers are separated from the total
cards.when_not: the underlying data are inconsistent between periods; you need a supply-chain rather than an accounting decomposition (-> structural decomposition)

simple and familiar, but leaves a residual

cards.when_not: you have a single scenario and no ensemble to manage; the variables do not follow the standard template

alternatives.criterion: you need to subset and summarise an ensemble
scenarios start from different historical bases
you only need to fill a few missing years

aggregates: regional or variable aggregations

cards.method: Environmental Kuznets curve and emissions-income panels
cards.when: testing whether emissions rise and then fall with income, in a panel where both country and period effects matter
cards.when_not: the panel is too short to separate the quadratic from a trend; the turning point lies outside the observed income range

alternatives.criterion: no turning point is claimed
the inverted-U is the hypothesis
you do not want to impose the quadratic shape

output_key_fields: params: income and income-squared coefficients
turning_point: the income level at the peak, with its confidence interval
in_sample: whether the turning point lies inside the observed income range

the quadratic imposes a symmetric inverted U; a semiparametric fit frequently shows something else entirely
the delta-method interval on the turning point is wide and often includes implausible values -- report it

Alternatives: linear emissions-income elasticity (no turning point is claimed) · quadratic EKC (the inverted-U is the hypothesis) · semiparametric EKC (you do not want to impose the quadratic shape)
Output: params: income and income-squared coefficients · turning_point: the income level at the peak, with its confidence interval · in_sample: whether the turning point lies inside the observed income range · fixed_effects: the effects absorbed
Pitfalls: a turning point OUTSIDE the observed income range is an extrapolation, not a finding, and it is the single most common overclaim in this literature · the quadratic imposes a symmetric inverted U; a semiparametric fit frequently shows something else entirely · the delta-method interval on the turning point is wide and often includes implausible values -- report it
Sources: Grossman & Krueger 1995 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 110:353-377) · Stern 2004 (World Development 32:1419) · Wagner 2008 (Resource and Energy Economics 30:388) · pyfixest

cards.method: Weather normalisation of energy demand with heating and cooling degree days
cards.when: separating the weather-driven part of energy demand from the underlying trend, so consumption can be compared across years
cards.when_not: the weather data does not match the consumption region; the demand is not weather sensitive

alternatives.criterion: the standard, transparent approach
the base temperature must be estimated rather than assumed
the response is not piecewise linear

output_key_fields: normalised: weather-normalised demand
hdd, cdd: the constructed degree-day series
base_temperature: the balance point used or estimated
weather_contribution: the demand attributed to weather
interpretation_traps: the BASE TEMPERATURE is not universal -- it differs by building stock and climate, and assuming the conventional value can misattribute a large share of demand
degree days computed from daily means differ from those computed from hourly data, sometimes materially
normalisation removes weather, not behaviour; a mild year with a price shock is not disentangled by this alone
sources: Hor, Watson & Majithia 2005 (IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 20:2078)

cards.method: Mapping climate scenarios onto macroeconomic paths: transition and physical risk
cards.when: turning a climate scenario into the macro-financial variables a stress test or projection needs
cards.when_not: the scenario has no macro variables and no mapping is available; the horizon is far beyond any credible macro relationship

alternatives.criterion: the scenario already carries macro variables
you must translate physical variables into macro ones
you want output loss as a function of warming

output_key_fields: macro_paths: the mapped macroeconomic variables
transition_component: the part driven by policy and carbon prices
physical_component: the part driven by warming and hazards
assumptions: the elasticities and damage function used
interpretation_traps: transition and physical risk have OPPOSITE time profiles -- strong early transition lowers late physical damage -- so reporting one without the other is systematically misleading
damage functions differ by more than an order of magnitude across the literature; the choice dominates any long-horizon result
these mappings are calibrated, not estimated; treat the output as a scenario, never as a forecast

cards.method: Kaya identity and energy-balance accounting
cards.when: decomposing emissions into population, output per person, energy intensity and carbon intensity -- the standard framing for emissions drivers
cards.when_not: the components are not available on a consistent basis; you need supply-chain detail (-> input-output)

alternatives.criterion: the standard four-factor decomposition
you want a residual-free attribution of the change
the question is energy flows rather than emissions

output_key_fields: factors: the four Kaya components per period
contributions: the change in emissions attributed to each
identity_check: reconstruction error, which should be numerically zero
energy_balance: supply, transformation and final consumption where requested
interpretation_traps: the identity is an ACCOUNTING TAUTOLOGY, not a causal model -- a factor's contribution is not the effect of changing it, because the factors are not independent
a non-zero identity check means the four series are on inconsistent bases or units
carbon intensity of energy and energy intensity of output move together through fuel switching, so their separate contributions are not separable policies
sources: Kaya 1990, Impact of carbon dioxide emission control on GNP growth (IPCC Response Strategies Working Group)

cards.method: Constraint-based structure learning: PC and FCI
cards.when: learning the causal graph from data using conditional independence, when the structure itself is the question rather than an assumed input
cards.when_not: you already know the graph; the sample is too small for conditional independence tests to have power at the needed conditioning-set size

alternatives.criterion: you are willing to assume no latent confounders
latent confounders are possible and must be allowed for
you prefer a global fit criterion to a sequence of tests

output_key_fields: graph: the learned equivalence class
edges: directed, undirected and bidirected edges with their orientation reasons
separating_sets: the conditioning sets that removed each edge
n_tests: how many independence tests were run
interpretation_traps: PC returns an EQUIVALENCE CLASS, not one graph -- an undirected edge means the direction is unidentified, and reading it as a null finding is wrong
PC assumes causal sufficiency (no latent confounders); if that fails the output is not merely imprecise but wrong, which is why FCI exists
the result depends on the ORDER variables are tested in for the original algorithm; stable variants exist and should be preferred
sources: Spirtes, Glymour & Scheines 2000, Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed.
Colombo & Maathuis 2014 (Journal of Machine Learning Research 15:3741)

cards.method: Score-based structure learning: GES, exact search and permutation methods
cards.when: learning structure by optimising a global fit score rather than by a sequence of independence tests, which is often more stable in moderate samples
cards.when_not: the variable count makes exact search infeasible and you need the guarantee it provides; latent confounders are present (-> FCI)

alternatives.criterion: greedy equivalence search, the standard score-based method
few variables and you want the global optimum
you want order-based search with fewer assumptions

output_key_fields: graph: the learned equivalence class
score: the final score and its improvement path
n_variables, search_space: the size of the problem actually solved
converged: whether the search terminated at a local optimum
interpretation_traps: the score assumes a MODEL FAMILY -- BIC assumes linear Gaussian -- and a mis-specified score returns a confident, wrong graph
greedy search finds a local optimum; different starting points give different graphs and the difference is rarely reported
exact search is exponential in the number of variables and is infeasible beyond roughly twenty

cards.method: Functional causal models: ICA-LiNGAM, DirectLiNGAM and VAR-LiNGAM
cards.when: orienting edges the independence-based methods leave undirected, by exploiting non-Gaussianity of the errors
cards.when_not: the errors are Gaussian, where the method is not identified at all; the relationships are strongly nonlinear

alternatives.criterion: you are unwilling to assume linearity and non-Gaussianity
you want a deterministic algorithm with no ICA convergence issues
the data are time series and you want contemporaneous plus lagged structure

output_key_fields: adjacency: the estimated causal ordering and coefficients
causal_order: the topological order recovered
non_gaussianity: per-variable measures -- the assumption the method rests on
bootstrap_probabilities: edge stability across resamples
interpretation_traps: identification comes ENTIRELY from NON-GAUSSIANITY; with Gaussian errors the model is unidentified and the returned ordering is arbitrary -- always check the diagnostic
ICA-LiNGAM depends on ICA convergence and can return different orders across runs; DirectLiNGAM is deterministic
a single fitted graph without bootstrap edge probabilities overstates confidence dramatically

cards.method: Graph identification: backdoor, frontdoor, instruments and estimand derivation
cards.when: deciding, from a stated causal graph, whether an effect is identified at all and which adjustment set estimates it
cards.when_not: you have no graph and are unwilling to state one; the effect is identified by design rather than by adjustment

alternatives.criterion: a sufficient observed adjustment set exists
a full mediating path is observed while confounders are not
an instrument exists in the graph

output_key_fields: identifiable: whether the effect is identified from the graph
estimand: the derived expression to estimate
adjustment_sets: minimal sufficient sets, of which there are usually several
instruments: variables the graph qualifies as instruments
interpretation_traps: identification is a property of the GRAPH, not of the data -- a wrong graph yields a confidently derived, wrong estimand
adjusting for a COLLIDER or a mediator introduces bias rather than removing it; more controls is not safer
several minimal adjustment sets usually exist and they differ in efficiency; if they disagree empirically the graph is wrong

cards.method: Refutation: placebo treatment, random common cause, subset and unobserved confounder
cards.when: attacking your own causal estimate to see whether it survives -- the step that separates a causal claim from a regression coefficient
cards.when_not: the estimate has not been produced yet; the refuters cannot run on the design in question

alternatives.criterion: replace treatment with noise; the effect should vanish
add an irrelevant confounder; the effect should not move
simulate a confounder of stated strength and see what survives

output_key_fields: refutation_results: the estimate under each refuter
passed: whether each refutation behaved as it should
sensitivity: the confounder strength that would nullify the effect
p_values: significance of the change under each refuter
interpretation_traps: a PLACEBO effect that is not near zero means the estimate is driven by something other than the treatment -- this is the single most informative check here
passing every refuter does not prove the graph is right; the refuters test consequences of the assumptions, not the assumptions
the unobserved-confounder refuter requires you to state a confounder strength, and that choice determines the verdict

cards.method: Conditional and unconditional independence testing
cards.when: the primitive every constraint-based discovery method is built on, and a useful diagnostic in its own right
cards.when_not: the relationship is known to be linear and Gaussian, where a partial correlation suffices and the general tests only cost power

alternatives.criterion: linear Gaussian, fast
nonlinear dependence, no distributional assumption
unconditional dependence of any kind

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: the test result
test: which test was applied
conditioning_set: the variables conditioned on
power_warning: flagged when the conditioning set is large relative to the sample
interpretation_traps: conditional independence testing is HARD: power falls sharply as the conditioning set grows, and a non-rejection with a large set is uninformative rather than evidence of independence
distance correlation detects any dependence but says nothing about its direction or form
kernel tests need bandwidth choices that materially affect power, and their permutation null is expensive
sources: Zhang, Peters, Janzing & Scholkopf 2011, Kernel-based conditional independence test (UAI 2011)

cards.method: Series splicing, linking and backcasting
cards.when: two or more overlapping vintages of the same concept must become one continuous series -- rebased indices, reclassified aggregates, a discontinued series continued by a successor
cards.when_not: the series share no overlap and no ratio can be computed; the break is a genuine level change that should be modelled, not spliced away

alternatives.criterion: an overlap period exists
the series are in levels and an additive link is right
no overlap, but a related indicator spans the gap

output_key_fields: spliced: the continuous series
link_factor: the ratio or difference applied, per join
overlap_periods: how many periods the link rested on
breaks: the join dates, retained so the splice is auditable
interpretation_traps: a splice computed on ONE overlapping observation is a rescaling of noise; report the overlap length beside the factor
ratio splicing preserves growth rates and distorts levels; difference splicing does the reverse -- the choice is substantive
a spliced series carries a discontinuity in its second moment even when the level is smooth, which shows up later as a spurious volatility break
sources: Eurostat 2018, Handbook on Rapid Estimates, ch.6

cards.when_not: the data are already chain linked; the components have no consistent price and volume split

alternatives.criterion: the standard national-accounts convention
quarterly data and you follow that convention
the series is strongly seasonal

contributions: additive growth contributions, which remain valid

alternatives.criterion: the number of each weekday in the period matters
only the working/non-working split matters
a holiday moves between periods

trading_day: weekday-count contrasts, summing to zero by construction
leap_year: the February length correction
easter: the moving-holiday proximity variable
interpretation_traps: trading-day regressors are CONTRASTS and must sum to zero, or they are collinear with the mean and the model will not identify them
the Easter regressor depends on an assumed window length before the holiday; the choice changes the estimated effect
applying trading-day adjustment to a stock series rather than a flow series introduces an effect that was not there

WHEN: building the calendar variables a seasonal-adjustment or forecasting model needs, so composition-of-the-month effects do not masquerade as seasonality
NOT when: the data are annual, where calendar effects do not arise; the series is not flow data and has no trading-day sensitivity
Alternatives: trading-day regressors (the number of each weekday in the period matters) · working-day regressor (only the working/non-working split matters) · Easter and moving-holiday regressors (a holiday moves between periods)

the structure is local and nonlinear

cards.method: Deterministic-term generator: seasonal dummies, Fourier harmonics and trends
cards.when: building the deterministic regressors a time-series model needs, consistently between the estimation sample and the forecast horizon
cards.when_not: the model generates its own deterministic terms internally; the series has no deterministic component

alternatives.criterion: few seasons and you want an unrestricted pattern
many seasons or multiple seasonalities, and you want few parameters
a smooth deterministic trend is wanted

output_key_fields: terms: the constructed regressor matrix
out_of_sample: the same terms extended over the forecast horizon
names: column names, so coefficients remain interpretable
rank: the matrix rank, which reveals collinearity with an intercept
interpretation_traps: seasonal dummies plus an intercept are COLLINEAR unless one season is dropped or the dummies are centred; the generator must state which convention it used
the out-of-sample terms must be generated by the SAME rule as the in-sample ones -- regenerating them independently is a classic source of forecast breaks
too many Fourier harmonics reproduce the dummies exactly and lose the parsimony that motivated them

cards.method: Kernel density and empirical distribution grids
cards.when: producing the density or distribution-function values other methods consume -- risk measures, quantile mappings, distributional plots
cards.when_not: you need the density estimated conditionally (-> conditional KDE); the tail beyond the data matters (-> extreme value theory)

alternatives.criterion: a smooth density is wanted
no smoothing, exact at the observations
a coarse, fast summary

output_key_fields: density: the estimated density on the grid
cdf: the distribution function on the same grid
grid: the evaluation points
bandwidth: the smoothing applied
interpretation_traps: kernel density estimates are BIASED AT A HARD BOUNDARY such as zero; reflect or transform first for durations, shares and non-negative variables
the empirical CDF is a step function, so quantiles read off it are not unique between observations

cards.method: Schema validation and data contracts
cards.when: refusing bad data at the door instead of discovering it in a result -- types, ranges, uniqueness and nullability asserted before anything is computed
cards.when_not: the data are already validated upstream; the schema cannot be stated because the shape is genuinely unknown

alternatives.criterion: the shape is known and should be enforced
the shape is unknown and you want to discover it first
one or two checks only

output_key_fields: valid: whether the table satisfied the contract
failures: which rows and columns failed which check
coerced: values changed by type coercion, where it was permitted
schema: the contract that was applied
interpretation_traps: a validator run in permissive mode COERCES rather than refuses, which turns a loud failure into a silent change of data
checks that examine zero rows pass trivially; an empty table must fail validation, not sail through it
validating after the analysis has already run tells you the result was wrong, which is later than it needed to be

cards.method: Record linkage, deduplication and fuzzy matching
cards.when: joining two datasets that share no key, or removing duplicate entities from one, using approximate agreement across several fields
cards.when_not: a reliable shared key exists (join on it); the datasets are so large that blocking is infeasible without a specialised backend

alternatives.criterion: a key exists and only formatting differs
no key, and agreement patterns must be weighted
the task is within one dataset

output_key_fields: matches: the accepted linked pairs with their scores
candidate_pairs: how many comparisons blocking produced
threshold: the score cut-off applied
reduction_ratio: how much blocking reduced the comparison space
interpretation_traps: BLOCKING determines what can ever be matched: a pair excluded by the blocking key can never be linked, however similar it is
the threshold trades false links against missed ones and there is no neutral choice; report the score distribution, not just the count
transitivity fails -- A matches B and B matches C does not make A and C the same entity, and naive clustering will merge them

cards.method: Formula parsing and the design-matrix contract
cards.when: turning a model formula into the design matrix an estimator consumes, with the same treatment of factors, interactions and missing values every time
cards.when_not: the design matrix is already built; the formula language cannot express the term you need

alternatives.criterion: the standard route from specification to matrix
the design is not expressible as a formula
you want splines or polynomials inside the formula

output_key_fields: design: the constructed design matrix
terms: term names and the columns each produced
contrasts: the coding applied to each factor
dropped: rows dropped for missing values
interpretation_traps: FACTOR CODING is a substantive choice -- treatment, sum and Helmert contrasts give different coefficients from the same data and only the fitted values agree
the design matrix drops rows with missing values silently unless told otherwise, so the estimation sample can differ from the input without warning
the same formula applied to new data can produce different columns if a factor level is absent; the levels must be carried, not re-inferred

cards.method: Compositional log-ratio transforms: CLR, ILR and ALR
cards.when: the variables are shares that sum to a constant, so ordinary statistics on them are invalid -- correlations are spuriously negative and variances are not free
cards.when_not: the data are not compositional; there are structural zeros that no log-ratio transform can handle without imputation

alternatives.criterion: you want a symmetric transform keeping all parts
you need a full-rank basis for multivariate methods
one part is a natural reference denominator

output_key_fields: transformed: the data in log-ratio coordinates
basis: the basis used, needed to invert the transform
zeros_handled: how zeros were treated, which is the main practical issue
inverse: the back-transform to the simplex
interpretation_traps: log-ratio transforms are UNDEFINED AT ZERO; zero replacement is a modelling decision that changes results and must be reported, not hidden in a default
the CLR-transformed data are singular by construction -- their covariance matrix is rank deficient, which breaks methods requiring invertibility; ILR exists for that
correlations between raw shares are spuriously negative because the parts sum to a constant; interpreting them is the error this whole card exists to prevent
sources: Aitchison 1986, The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data

cards.when: the panel is larger than comfortable in memory, and the operations are filters, joins and group-bys that a columnar engine can stream
cards.when_not: the data fit comfortably in memory and the added indirection is not worth it; the operation is inherently row-wise and iterative

alternatives.criterion: the data are small
the data are large and the pipeline is relational
the operation cannot be expressed relationally

output_key_fields: result: the materialised output
plan: the query plan, before and after optimisation
rows_scanned: how much data the plan actually read
peak_memory: the high-water mark of the execution
interpretation_traps: a LAZY plan does nothing until collected; timing the plan construction rather than the collection measures nothing
predicate pushdown only works if the filter is expressible in the plan -- a filter applied after collection reads the whole dataset first
type coercion rules differ from row-wise engines, and silent upcasting of integers to floats changes joins on keys

cards.method: Ljung-Box and Box-Pierce portmanteau tests with Durbin-Watson
cards.when: the single most-used whiteness check in applied time series: are the residuals of a fitted model, or the series itself, free of remaining autocorrelation
cards.when_not: the data are cross-sectional; the residuals come from a model with lagged dependent variables, where Durbin-Watson is invalid and Breusch-Godfrey is required

alternatives.criterion: the regression contains lagged dependent variables
a quick first-order check on a static regression
you want the pattern rather than a single test

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: per tested lag
df: degrees of freedom, reduced by the number of estimated model parameters
durbin_watson: the first-order statistic, around 2 under no autocorrelation
decision: whiteness verdict at alpha
interpretation_traps: when testing MODEL RESIDUALS the degrees of freedom must be reduced by the number of estimated ARMA parameters; failing to do so makes the test far too conservative
Durbin-Watson is INVALID with a lagged dependent variable -- it is biased toward 2 and will not detect autocorrelation that is there
the test has power against many alternatives and identifies none of them; a rejection says 'not white', not 'add one more lag'

cards.method: BDS test for independence and nonlinear structure
cards.when: asking whether what remains after a linear model is genuinely independent, or merely linearly uncorrelated with nonlinear structure left in it
cards.when_not: the sample is short -- the test needs several hundred observations to have a reliable null distribution

alternatives.criterion: you only want linear autocorrelation
you suspect nonlinear dependence such as ARCH or chaos
you specifically suspect conditional heteroskedasticity

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: per embedding dimension and distance
embedding_dimension: the dimensions tested
epsilon: the distance thresholds used, in standard deviations
decision: independence verdict
interpretation_traps: the BDS statistic is sensitive to the choice of EPSILON and embedding dimension; report the grid, because a rejection at one setting is not a rejection
rejection means 'not independent and identically distributed' -- it does not identify the nonlinearity, and ARCH is the most common cause by far
applied to residuals of an estimated model the asymptotic distribution changes, and a bootstrap null is needed

cards.method: Long-run variance and HAC bandwidth selection
cards.when: estimating the spectral density at frequency zero -- the quantity every HAC standard error, unit-root test and cointegration statistic depends on
cards.when_not: the data are independent, where the long-run variance is just the variance

alternatives.criterion: the standard default
asymptotically optimal, though slower
strong persistence, where raw kernels are badly biased

output_key_fields: long_run_variance: the estimate
bandwidth: the truncation used and the rule that chose it
kernel: the kernel applied
prewhitened: whether an autoregressive filter was applied first
interpretation_traps: with strong persistence the kernel estimator is severely DOWNWARD biased, which makes HAC standard errors too small exactly when they matter most -- prewhitening is the standard remedy
the automatic bandwidth rules of Andrews and of Newey-West disagree materially and neither is right in general
a bandwidth exceeding the sample length silently truncates to the sample and reports a number that is not the estimator asked for

cards.method: SADF and GSADF explosive-bubble tests with date stamping
cards.when: testing for explosive rather than merely non-stationary behaviour, and dating when the episodes began and ended
cards.when_not: the series has one break rather than a bubble; the sample is too short for the recursive windows to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: the alternative is stationarity, not explosiveness
a single suspected bubble episode
several episodes, which SADF has low power against

output_key_fields: sadf, gsadf: the supremum statistics
critical_values: simulated critical values, which are not tabulated in general
episodes: dated start and end of each explosive period
bsadf: the backward-supremum sequence used for dating
interpretation_traps: critical values must be SIMULATED for the specific sample size and window; using values from a paper with a different sample is simply wrong
SADF has low power when there are multiple bubbles, because a later episode contaminates the recursive windows -- that is what GSADF is for
the minimum window length is a tuning choice that determines how short an episode can be detected and moves the dating

cards.method: Panel cross-sectional dependence: Pesaran CD, LM and scaled LM
cards.when: testing whether panel units share common shocks, which invalidates every standard error that assumes independence across units
cards.when_not: the panel has a single unit; the cross-section is so large relative to time that the pairwise correlations cannot be estimated

alternatives.criterion: large N and small T, the usual macro panel
small N and large T
moderate N, correcting the LM size distortion

output_key_fields: statistic, p_value: the dependence test
average_correlation: mean absolute pairwise residual correlation
test: which variant was applied and why it suits the panel dimensions
decision: independence verdict
interpretation_traps: the LM test is badly OVERSIZED when N is large relative to T -- it rejects almost always, which is why Pesaran's CD exists
rejection means standard errors assuming cross-sectional independence are wrong; Driscoll-Kraay or common-factor methods are the response
the average absolute correlation is the economically informative number; the test statistic alone conflates size and strength

cards.when_not: there is a single regressor; the model is used only for prediction, where collinearity does not hurt

alternatives.criterion: a per-regressor screen
you want to know WHICH regressors are involved
you accept the collinearity and want stable coefficients

output_key_fields: vif, tolerance: per regressor
condition_index: per eigenvalue, largest being the condition number
variance_decomposition: which regressors load on each near-dependency
flagged: regressors above the chosen thresholds
interpretation_traps: a VIF threshold of 10 is a CONVENTION, not a result -- collinearity is a matter of degree and the threshold has no theoretical basis
VIFs identify that collinearity exists but not which regressors are collinear WITH WHICH; only the variance decomposition does that
collinearity does not bias coefficients or harm prediction; it inflates standard errors, and treating it as a bias problem leads to wrong fixes

cards.method: Automatic seasonal-period detection and differencing orders
cards.when: deciding the seasonal period and the differencing orders before a model is fitted, by a stated rule rather than by inspection
cards.when_not: the period is known from the data's frequency; the series is too short for the tests to be reliable

alternatives.criterion: the period is unknown or multiple
you want d chosen by a test
theory or convention fixes the orders

output_key_fields: period: the detected seasonal period or periods
d, D: the selected non-seasonal and seasonal differencing orders
test_path: the sequence of tests and their outcomes, so the choice is auditable
seasonal_strength: the strength measure behind the period detection
interpretation_traps: OVER-DIFFERENCING is as damaging as under-differencing: it induces a non-invertible moving-average unit root that no estimator handles well
seasonal differencing is a strong assumption; a deterministic seasonal pattern is better handled with dummies or harmonics
the automatic rules differ between implementations and a series can get d=1 from one and d=0 from another
sources: Wang, Smith & Hyndman 2006 (Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 13:335)

cards.method: Stability without a known break date: Nyblom-Hansen, Andrews-Ploberger and Quandt-Andrews
cards.when: testing for parameter instability when you do not know, and must not pretend to know, when the break happened
cards.when_not: the break date is known from an event (use a Chow test); the sample is too short for the trimmed search range to contain anything

alternatives.criterion: the break date is known independently
one unknown break
power against a broader class of instability

output_key_fields: statistic: the supremum, average or exponential statistic
break_date: the argmax date, where the supremum test is used
critical_values: from the non-standard distribution these tests require
trimming: the search range, which determines what could be found
interpretation_traps: the null distribution is NON-STANDARD -- these are not chi-squared tests, and using conventional critical values grossly over-rejects
the estimated break date has wide sampling uncertainty; reporting it as a point without an interval overstates precision
TRIMMING excludes the ends of the sample from the search, so a break in the first or last 15% cannot be found at all

cards.method: Long memory: Hurst exponent, rescaled range, detrended fluctuation and variance ratio
cards.when: distinguishing genuine long-range dependence from a short-memory process with a trend or a break, which mimic it closely
cards.when_not: the series is plainly short memory; the sample is too short for the scaling exponent to be estimated over enough scales

alternatives.criterion: the classic estimator, though biased by short memory
the series is non-stationary or trending
the question is a random walk against mean reversion

output_key_fields: hurst: the estimated exponent, 0.5 under independence
method: which estimator produced it
scaling_range: the scales the exponent was fitted over
variance_ratio, p_value: the random-walk test where requested
interpretation_traps: STRUCTURAL BREAKS AND TRENDS MIMIC LONG MEMORY -- an exponent above 0.5 is not evidence of long memory until breaks have been excluded
the estimate depends strongly on the range of scales fitted; reporting the exponent without the scaling range is uninformative
the rescaled-range estimator is biased upward in small samples even for independent data
sources: Hurst 1951 (Transactions of the American Society of Civil Engineers 116:770)

cards.method: Unsupervised anomaly detection: isolation forest, local outlier factor and one-class SVM
cards.when: flagging observations that do not belong, in a multivariate setting where univariate outlier rules see nothing
cards.when_not: the outliers are defined by a known rule; the data are a time series where the anomaly is contextual and needs a temporal model

alternatives.criterion: many observations, mixed feature types
density varies across the space
a tight boundary around a well-defined normal region

output_key_fields: scores: the anomaly score per observation
flagged: observations above the threshold
contamination: the assumed anomaly rate, which sets the threshold
feature_contributions: what drove each flag, where the method provides it
interpretation_traps: the CONTAMINATION parameter effectively sets how many anomalies you find -- it is an assumption, not a discovery, and the flagged count follows it almost mechanically
these methods are unsupervised: 'anomalous' means unusual, not wrong, and the two are frequently different things
distance-based detectors degrade badly in high dimensions as all points become equidistant

cards.method: Time-series feature extraction at scale
cards.when: turning many series into a comparable feature matrix, for clustering, screening or as inputs to a global model
cards.when_not: you have one series and want to understand it, where targeted diagnostics beat a large undirected feature set

alternatives.criterion: one series and a specific question
many series, and you want a comparable matrix
you want a compact, interpretable set

output_key_fields: features: the extracted feature matrix
selected: features surviving the relevance filter, where one is applied
n_features: how many were computed and how many survived
missing_features: features undefined for some series and why
interpretation_traps: computing hundreds of features and selecting on the outcome is MULTIPLE TESTING; the relevance filter's p-values must be adjusted or the selection is spurious

cards.method: Distance correlation and general independence tests
cards.when: detecting dependence of any form, not just linear -- a screen that will not miss a relationship because it is not monotone
cards.when_not: you specifically want a linear measure; the sample is large enough that the permutation null is prohibitive

alternatives.criterion: the relationship is linear
any dependence, no functional form assumed
you want an information-theoretic measure

output_key_fields: dcor: distance correlation, zero if and only if independent
statistic, p_value: the independence test
partial_dcor: partialling out a third set, where supplied
n_permutations: the null the p-value came from
interpretation_traps: distance correlation is ZERO IF AND ONLY IF INDEPENDENT, which Pearson is not -- that is the whole reason to use it
it detects dependence without characterising it; a high value says look at the scatter, not what the relationship is
the permutation null is O(n squared) per replication and becomes prohibitive well before the data are large

cards.method: Entropy diagnostics: sample, permutation, approximate and spectral entropy
cards.when: measuring how predictable or complex a series is, as a model-free screen before deciding what to fit
cards.when_not: the series is very short, where every entropy estimator is badly biased; you need a specific dependence test rather than a complexity summary

alternatives.criterion: robust, ordinal, fast
regularity of amplitude patterns
how concentrated the spectrum is

output_key_fields: entropy: the estimated value per measure
normalised: scaled to the unit interval where the measure permits
parameters: embedding dimension and tolerance, which drive the answer
forecastability: one minus normalised spectral entropy, a rough predictability index
interpretation_traps: sample and approximate entropy depend strongly on the TOLERANCE and embedding dimension; values computed with different settings are not comparable
approximate entropy is biased by self-matching, which is exactly what sample entropy was introduced to remove
entropy is not stationary-invariant: a trend lowers apparent complexity and can be mistaken for structure

cards.method: Recurrence quantification analysis
cards.when: detecting deterministic structure, regime changes and intermittency by quantifying when a system revisits earlier states
cards.when_not: the series is short or heavily noise dominated, where the recurrence plot shows nothing but speckle

alternatives.criterion: you suspect deterministic or regime structure
you want a scalar complexity summary
you specifically want dated regime changes

output_key_fields: recurrence_rate: density of recurrences
determinism: share of recurrences on diagonal lines
laminarity, trapping_time: vertical-structure measures indicating intermittency
entropy: diagonal-line-length entropy
interpretation_traps: the RECURRENCE THRESHOLD determines everything; a common convention fixes the recurrence rate rather than the distance, and the two give different pictures
embedding parameters must be chosen before analysis -- mutual information for the delay, false nearest neighbours for the dimension -- and defaults are rarely right
high determinism is not proof of a deterministic system; coloured noise produces it too

cards.method: Benford digit tests
cards.when: screening reported figures for the digit pattern naturally occurring data usually follow, as a first check for fabrication or rounding
cards.when_not: the data are bounded, assigned or generated by a process with no reason to follow the law -- most identifiers, ages and scores

alternatives.criterion: the standard screen
more power, needs more observations
targeting rounding rather than fabrication

output_key_fields: observed, expected: digit frequencies against the law
chi_square, mad, p_value: conformity statistics
conformity: the conventional verdict band the MAD falls in
n_observations: the count, which drives whether any of this is meaningful
interpretation_traps: BENFORD DOES NOT APPLY to every dataset -- it needs several orders of magnitude and no assignment rule; applying it to bounded data manufactures a failure
a rejection is a screening flag, not evidence of fraud; rounding, thresholds and unit changes all produce it
the chi-squared test rejects almost any large sample; the mean absolute deviation bands are what practitioners actually read
sources: Benford 1938 (Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 78:551)
Nigrini 2012, Benford's Law: Applications for Forensic Accounting, Auditing and Fraud Detection

cards.method: Benchmark forecasters: naive, seasonal naive, drift, mean and window average
cards.when: every skill-based accuracy metric and every 'does the model beat a random walk' claim needs these as the denominator
cards.when_not: you already have a benchmark and only need the sophisticated model

alternatives.criterion: the series is seasonal
the series trends and a random walk with drift is the honest baseline
the series is noisy and mean reverting

output_key_fields: forecast: the benchmark path
intervals: prediction intervals, which for a naive forecast widen with the square root of the horizon
method: which benchmark produced it
residuals: in-sample errors, the scale MASE is computed against
interpretation_traps: a model that fails to beat SEASONAL NAIVE on seasonal data has no value, however sophisticated it looks
naive prediction intervals assume independent errors; with autocorrelated residuals they are far too narrow
MASE is scaled by the in-sample naive error, so a benchmark computed on a different sample makes the metric incomparable
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos 2021, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., ch.5

cards.method: Dynamic regression and regARIMA with exogenous regressors
cards.when: the series is driven by observable exogenous variables and the residual dynamics still need an ARIMA structure
cards.when_not: the exogenous variables are not available over the forecast horizon; the relationship is a cointegrating one and belongs in an error-correction model

alternatives.criterion: no useful exogenous information
regressors plus autocorrelated errors
the regressor's effect is distributed over time

output_key_fields: params: regression coefficients and ARIMA parameters
forecast: conditional on supplied future regressors
residual_diagnostics: whiteness of what remains after both parts
aic, bic
interpretation_traps: forecasting requires FUTURE VALUES of every regressor; using actuals produces an in-sample illusion, and forecasting the regressors adds their error to yours
regressors and ARIMA errors compete to explain the same variation; the coefficient changes materially with the error specification
differencing applies to the regressors too, and applying it to only one side breaks the relationship
sources: Box, Jenkins, Reinsel & Ljung 2015, Time Series Analysis, 5th ed.

cards.method: Intervention analysis and transfer functions
cards.when: measuring the effect of a dated event -- a policy change, a strike, a methodology break -- on the level or dynamics of a series
cards.when_not: the event date is unknown (-> break tests); there are so many interventions that the model is unidentified

alternatives.criterion: a permanent level shift
a one-off effect
the effect builds and decays over several periods

output_key_fields: effect: the estimated intervention effect and its shape over time
params: intervention and ARIMA parameters together
counterfactual: the path implied without the intervention
significance: test of a zero effect
interpretation_traps: the intervention SHAPE -- step, pulse, gradual -- is imposed, not estimated; the wrong shape can make a real effect insignificant
an intervention at the very end of the sample is barely identified because there is almost no post-event data
pre-intervention model misspecification loads onto the intervention estimate, which is why the pre-period fit must be checked first
sources: Enders 2015, Applied Econometric Time Series, 4th ed., ch.5

cards.method: Simulation-based fan charts and scenario paths
cards.when: communicating forecast uncertainty as a distribution of paths rather than a point, and imposing scenarios on that distribution
cards.when_not: the model's analytic intervals are adequate and the extra simulation adds nothing

alternatives.criterion: the model has closed-form intervals and errors are Gaussian
the model is nonlinear or errors are non-Gaussian
you want paths consistent with a stated future

output_key_fields: fan: quantile bands per horizon
paths: the simulated trajectories
scenario_paths: paths conditioned on a stated future
n_simulations: draws behind the bands
interpretation_traps: a fan of quantiles taken HORIZON BY HORIZON is not a set of plausible paths -- no single trajectory follows the median band, and reading it as one is a standard error
bootstrapped innovations preserve non-normality but assume the residuals are independent
conditioning on a scenario changes the distribution of everything else in the model; ignoring that gives paths that are internally inconsistent
sources: Britton, Fisher & Whitley 1998 (Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 38:30-37)

cards.method: Global pooled tree forecasting with lag features
cards.when: many related series, where one model fitted across all of them beats a separate model per series -- the standard modern approach for large forecast portfolios
cards.when_not: you have one series, where a global model has nothing to pool; the series are unrelated and pooling imposes false commonality

alternatives.criterion: few series, each with long history
many short related series
very many series and nonlinear cross-series structure

output_key_fields: forecast: paths per series
feature_importance: which lags and features drive the model
cv_score: cross-validated accuracy over the horizon
n_series: how many series were pooled
interpretation_traps: tree models CANNOT EXTRAPOLATE beyond the range of the training target; a trending series must be differenced or detrended first or forecasts flatten
feature construction must respect the forecast origin -- a lag shorter than the horizon is unavailable at prediction time and leaks
pooling assumes the series share dynamics; scale differences must be handled or large series dominate the fit
sources: Januschowski et al. 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:167-177)
Makridakis, Spiliotis & Assimakopoulos 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:54)

cards.method: Bagged and bootstrap-aggregated forecasts with STL and block bootstrap
cards.when: reducing forecast variance by averaging over bootstrap replicates of the series, which usually beats the single fitted model
cards.when_not: the series is short, where the bootstrap replicates are nearly identical and bagging adds cost without benefit

alternatives.criterion: the model is stable and the series is long
the model is unstable or the series is short
you have several different models rather than replicates

output_key_fields: forecast: the bagged mean or median path
replicate_forecasts: the individual paths, which give an empirical interval
n_replicates: how many were generated
variance_reduction: spread of replicates against the single fit
interpretation_traps: bagging reduces VARIANCE, not bias; a systematically wrong model bagged many times is still systematically wrong
the bootstrap must preserve serial dependence -- an iid bootstrap of the series destroys exactly what is being forecast
the spread of replicate forecasts is not a prediction interval; it omits innovation uncertainty entirely
sources: Bergmeir, Hyndman & Benitez 2016 (International Journal of Forecasting 32:303-312)
Petropoulos, Hyndman & Bergmeir 2018 (European Journal of Operational Research 268:545)

cards.method: Direct multi-step reduction forecasting
cards.when: forecasting each horizon with its own model trained directly on that horizon's target, avoiding the error accumulation of recursive iteration
cards.when_not: the horizon is one; the sample is too short to train a separate model per horizon

alternatives.criterion: one model iterated forward, efficient but accumulates error
one model per horizon, no accumulation but more models
you want a compromise

output_key_fields: forecast: the path assembled from per-horizon models
models: one fitted model per horizon
horizon_scores: accuracy per horizon, which reveals where the strategy pays
strategy: which reduction was used
interpretation_traps: DIRECT and RECURSIVE forecasts differ systematically: recursive accumulates model error, direct loses efficiency by fitting each horizon separately -- neither dominates
the direct strategy fits a different model per horizon, so the resulting path can be non-smooth or even non-monotone in ways a single model would not produce
each horizon's training set is shorter than the last, so late horizons are fitted on less data
sources: Ben Taieb, Bontempi, Atiya & Sorjamaa 2012 (Expert Systems with Applications 39:7067-7083)

cards.method: Conformal prediction intervals for forecasts
cards.when: prediction intervals with a finite-sample coverage guarantee that does not depend on the model being correctly specified
cards.when_not: the residuals are not exchangeable in a way any conformal variant can handle; you need a full predictive density rather than an interval

alternatives.criterion: the model is correct and you want efficiency
you want a guarantee and have data to spare
the error distribution shifts over time

output_key_fields: intervals: lower and upper bounds per horizon
coverage_guarantee: the nominal level the construction guarantees
empirical_coverage: realised coverage on the calibration set
width: interval width, the price of the guarantee
interpretation_traps: standard conformal guarantees rest on EXCHANGEABILITY, which time series violate; the time-series variants weaken this and their guarantee is correspondingly weaker
the guarantee is MARGINAL over the calibration distribution -- it does not hold conditionally on a particular covariate value or regime
a wide conformal interval is the method telling you the model is poor, not a defect of the method
sources: Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer 2005, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World
Stankeviciute, Alaa & van der Schaar 2021, Conformal time-series forecasting (NeurIPS 34)

cards.method: Automatic family selection and forecaster multiplexing
cards.when: choosing among forecasting families by a stated cross-validated rule instead of by habit, over many series at once
cards.when_not: theory or convention fixes the model; the series is too short for time-series cross-validation to leave usable folds

alternatives.criterion: within one family, cheap
across families, honest but expensive
you would rather average than select

output_key_fields: selected: the chosen model per series
cv_scores: cross-validated accuracy per candidate
selection_stability: how often the choice changes across folds
forecast: the path from the selected model
interpretation_traps: selecting on the SAME data used to report accuracy overstates performance; the selection must sit inside the evaluation loop, not outside it
a selection that flips between families across folds is telling you the candidates are indistinguishable -- combination is usually better than picking
cross-validation folds must respect time order; a random split leaks the future into the past

cards.method: Nowcast news and revision decomposition
cards.when: attributing the change in a nowcast to each incoming data release -- the standard output of every central-bank nowcasting system
cards.when_not: there is only one vintage so there is no change to attribute; the model is not a state-space model and has no news structure

alternatives.criterion: attributing a nowcast revision to releases
attributing the nowcast LEVEL to variables
you only need the total revision

output_key_fields: news: the surprise component of each release
impact: the nowcast revision each release caused
weights: the Kalman gain applied to each series
revision_total: the sum, which must reconcile with the observed change
interpretation_traps: NEWS IS NOT THE RELEASE, it is the release minus what the model expected; a large release with no surprise moves the nowcast not at all
the impacts must sum to the total revision -- a residual means the decomposition is being applied across a model or specification change
revisions to previously published data enter as news too, and confusing them with new releases misattributes the move
sources: Banbura, Giannone, Modugno & Reichlin 2013, Now-casting and the real-time data flow (Handbook of Economic Forecasting 2A)

cards.method: Conditional forecasts and scenario analysis
cards.when: forecasting a system subject to a stated future path for some variables -- the standard tool for policy scenarios
cards.when_not: the conditioning path is inconsistent with the model's dynamics, where the implied shocks are implausibly large

alternatives.criterion: no scenario is imposed
the path must hold exactly
the path holds in distribution, within a band

output_key_fields: forecast: the conditional paths
implied_shocks: the shocks required to hit the conditioning path
shock_plausibility: how large those shocks are in standard deviations
unconditional: the baseline, for comparison
interpretation_traps: conditioning REQUIRES shocks to hit the path; if those shocks are several standard deviations the scenario is inconsistent with the estimated model and should be reported as such
which shocks are used to achieve the conditioning is not unique unless specified, and different choices give different paths for everything else
hard conditioning removes all uncertainty about the conditioned variables, which understates the fan for everything correlated with them
sources: Waggoner & Zha 1999 (Review of Economics and Statistics 81:639-651)
Banbura, Giannone & Lenza 2015 (International Journal of Forecasting 31:739)

cards.when: many indicators carry information a small VAR cannot use, and factors extracted from them are added to the system rather than chosen ad hoc
cards.when_not: you have few variables, where a plain VAR suffices; the factors have no economic interpretation and the exercise needs one

alternatives.criterion: few variables and no information problem
hundreds of indicators to summarise
you want to keep the variables rather than compress them

output_key_fields: factors: the extracted factors and their loadings
irf: impulse responses of both factors and observed variables
variance_decomposition: contributions per shock
n_factors: how many were used and the criterion that chose it
interpretation_traps: factors are identified only up to ROTATION, so their individual interpretation requires an explicit normalisation that must be stated
the number of factors is a choice that materially changes the impulse responses; report the criterion and a robustness range
factors estimated from the full sample and then used in a recursive forecast exercise leak future information
sources: Bernanke, Boivin & Eliasz 2005 (Quarterly Journal of Economics 120:387-422)

cards.method: VARMA and VARMAX estimation in state-space form
cards.when: the system has moving-average dynamics a pure VAR would need many lags to approximate, or exogenous variables that belong in the system
cards.when_not: a VAR with a moderate lag order fits adequately; the identification restrictions VARMA needs cannot be justified

alternatives.criterion: simpler, always identified, needs more lags
parsimonious when moving-average dynamics are genuine
exogenous variables and no moving-average part

output_key_fields: params: autoregressive, moving-average and exogenous coefficients
irf: impulse responses
converged: whether the likelihood maximisation actually converged
aic, bic, loglike
interpretation_traps: VARMA models are NOT IDENTIFIED without restrictions -- the same dynamics have many parameterisations, and estimation without them wanders
the likelihood is flat in many directions, so convergence is fragile and starting values matter a great deal
a VAR of sufficient order approximates a VARMA well; the parsimony gain is often not worth the estimation difficulty
sources: Lutkepohl 2005, New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis, ch.11-12

cards.method: Bridge equations and unrestricted MIDAS
cards.when: linking high-frequency indicators to a low-frequency target without a full state-space system -- the workhorse of practical nowcasting
cards.when_not: you want a full system with news decomposition (-> dynamic factor); the frequency mismatch is so large that unrestricted MIDAS has too many parameters

alternatives.criterion: aggregate the indicator, then regress -- simple and transparent
few high-frequency lags, estimated freely
many lags, compressed by a weight function

output_key_fields: forecast: the low-frequency nowcast
params: indicator coefficients at each high-frequency lag
weights: the implied lag weighting
ragged_edge: how the incomplete final period was handled
interpretation_traps: the RAGGED EDGE is the whole problem: the final low-frequency period is incomplete and how the missing high-frequency observations are filled determines the nowcast
unrestricted MIDAS parameter count grows with the frequency ratio and overfits quickly; the restricted forms exist for that reason
aggregating the indicator before regressing discards within-period timing information that the nowcast could have used
sources: Ghysels, Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2004, The MIDAS touch (CIRANO Working Paper)
Baffigi, Golinelli & Parigi 2004 (International Journal of Forecasting 20:447)

cards.method: Large Bayesian VAR with dummy-observation priors, sum-of-coefficients and co-persistence
cards.when: the system has many variables and a flat-prior VAR would be hopelessly overparameterised; shrinkage makes it estimable
cards.when_not: the system is small enough for an unrestricted VAR; the prior cannot be justified and dominates the data

alternatives.criterion: the standard random-walk shrinkage
you want to discourage spurious deterministic trends
you want to allow cointegration without imposing it

output_key_fields: posterior: draws or moments of the coefficients
hyperparameters: the shrinkage actually chosen, often by marginal likelihood
irf: impulse responses with credible bands
forecast: predictive distribution
interpretation_traps: the SHRINKAGE HYPERPARAMETER dominates results in large systems; choosing it by marginal likelihood is defensible, fixing it by convention is not
the sum-of-coefficients and co-persistence priors are dummy observations, so they change the effective sample and must be reported
with many variables the prior contributes most of the information; calling the result data-driven is misleading
sources: Banbura, Giannone & Reichlin 2010 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 25:71-92)

cards.method: Shadow-rate VAR consistent with the effective lower bound
cards.when: the policy rate is stuck at its floor, so a linear VAR treats a censored variable as if it moved freely and gets the transmission wrong
cards.when_not: the sample contains no lower-bound episode; a simple regime split is adequate

alternatives.criterion: no binding lower bound in the sample
the bound binds and you want one consistent model across regimes
you prefer explicit regimes to a latent shadow rate

output_key_fields: shadow_rate: the estimated latent rate, which goes negative at the bound
irf: responses that respect the bound
binding_periods: when the bound was active
params: VAR parameters on the shadow rate
interpretation_traps: the shadow rate is a LATENT construct and different estimators produce very different series -- comparing shadow rates across studies is usually comparing methods
impulse responses are state dependent when the bound binds; reporting one linear response is exactly the error the model exists to avoid
the shadow rate is not a policy instrument and should not be read as one
sources: Wu & Xia 2016 (Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 48:253-291)

cards.method: Sparse and regularised VAR via penalised multi-task regression
cards.when: the VAR has more parameters than observations and you want the data to select which lags and cross-effects matter
cards.when_not: the system is small; the sparsity assumption is untenable because everything genuinely depends on everything

alternatives.criterion: you want shrinkage without exact zeros
you want exact zeros and a sparse structure
you want whole lags or whole equations selected together

output_key_fields: coefficients: the sparse coefficient matrices
sparsity: share of coefficients set exactly to zero
lambda_selected: the penalty and how it was chosen
selected_structure: which lags and cross-effects survived
interpretation_traps: POST-SELECTION INFERENCE IS INVALID: standard errors computed on the selected model ignore the selection and are far too small
the penalty must not treat own lags and cross lags alike; own lags usually deserve less shrinkage and a uniform penalty distorts the dynamics
cross-validation on time series must respect the time order, or the selection leaks the future
sources: Nicholson, Matteson & Bien 2020 (International Journal of Forecasting 36:627)

cards.method: Non-Gaussian higher-moment identification
cards.when: identifying structural shocks from the non-Gaussianity of the reduced-form residuals, without sign or timing restrictions
cards.when_not: the residuals are Gaussian, where the approach is not identified at all; the sample is too short for higher moments to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: an ordering is defensible
variance regimes are available
the residuals are demonstrably non-Gaussian

output_key_fields: b_matrix: the estimated structural impact matrix
irf: structural impulse responses
nongaussianity: per-residual diagnostics, the assumption everything rests on
j_statistic: overidentification test of the moment conditions
interpretation_traps: identification comes ENTIRELY from non-Gaussianity; with Gaussian residuals nothing is identified and the reported matrix is arbitrary -- check the diagnostic first
the shocks are identified only up to PERMUTATION and SIGN; labelling them economically is an additional, separate step

cards.method: Bootstrap and bias-corrected impulse-response bands
cards.when: VAR coefficients are biased in small samples and impulse-response bands built from asymptotics are badly wrong at long horizons
cards.when_not: the sample is very large, where the bias is negligible; the model is not a VAR

alternatives.criterion: large sample, short horizons
small sample, bias correction wanted
heteroskedastic or dependent residuals

output_key_fields: irf: bias-corrected impulse responses
bands: bootstrap confidence bands per horizon
bias_correction: the size of the adjustment applied
coverage_type: pointwise or joint, which is not the same thing
interpretation_traps: POINTWISE bands do not cover the whole response function simultaneously; reading a pointwise band as if it were joint overstates precision at every horizon
the bias correction can push a near-unit-root system into the explosive region, which is why the stationarity adjustment exists and must be applied
bootstrap bands inherit any misspecification of the VAR; they are not robust to a wrong lag order
sources: Kilian & Lutkepohl 2017, Structural Vector Autoregressive Analysis, ch.12
Hall 1992, The Bootstrap and Edgeworth Expansion

cards.method: Lag-augmented local projections with robust inference
cards.when: impulse responses without committing to a VAR, with inference that stays valid whether or not the variables have unit roots
cards.when_not: the horizon is short and a VAR is well specified, where the VAR is more efficient

alternatives.criterion: efficient when the VAR is correct
robust to misspecification but with size distortions at long horizons
valid inference regardless of persistence

output_key_fields: irf: the response per horizon
conf_band: bands valid under persistence
lag_augmentation: the extra lag that delivers the robustness
hac_bandwidth: the truncation used for the serial correlation
interpretation_traps: LAG AUGMENTATION is what makes the inference uniformly valid -- omitting the extra lag reintroduces exactly the size distortion the method removes
local-projection residuals are serially correlated at horizons beyond one by construction; HAC or the appropriate correction is mandatory

cards.method: Markov-switching vector autoregression
cards.when: the system's dynamics or shock variances change between regimes, and the regimes are latent rather than dated
cards.when_not: the regimes are known and dated (use dummies); the sample has too few regime switches for the transition probabilities to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: the regime is driven by an observed variable
change is gradual rather than discrete
discrete latent regimes

smoothed_probabilities: probability of each regime at each date
transition_matrix: regime persistence
expected_duration: mean regime length

the likelihood is multimodal and estimation is sensitive to starting values; a single run is not a result
with few switches in sample the transition probabilities are estimated from a handful of transitions and are very imprecise

cards.method: Maximum-share and spectral identification
cards.when: identifying a shock as the one explaining most of the forecast-error variance of a variable, over a chosen horizon or frequency band
cards.when_not: you have a credible instrument or sign restriction; the target variable and horizon cannot be justified from theory

alternatives.criterion: an ordering is defensible
theory restricts signs
theory says a shock dominates a particular variable's variance

output_key_fields: b_vector: the identified impact vector
irf: responses to the identified shock
variance_share: the share it explains at each horizon
band: the frequency band, where spectral identification is used
interpretation_traps: the identified shock is defined BY THE TARGET AND HORIZON; changing either changes the shock, so both are identifying assumptions and must be justified
the maximising shock need not correspond to any economic shock -- it is a statistical construct that theory must license
over a long horizon the method converges to a permanent-component identification and loses its distinctness from long-run restrictions

cards.method: Combined short-run and long-run restrictions
cards.when: theory delivers both timing restrictions on impact and neutrality restrictions in the long run, and using both identifies more shocks than either alone
cards.when_not: the long-run restrictions rest on unit roots the data do not support; the system is too small for the combined restrictions to be over-identifying

alternatives.criterion: impact timing is all theory gives
neutrality is all theory gives
both are available and you want the extra identification

output_key_fields: b_matrix: the identified impact matrix
irf: structural responses
overidentification_test: where the restrictions exceed what is needed
long_run_matrix: the implied cumulative effects
interpretation_traps: LONG-RUN RESTRICTIONS ARE ESTIMATED FROM AN INFINITE-HORIZON EXTRAPOLATION of a finite sample; they are notoriously imprecise and small VAR misspecifications distort them badly
combining restrictions can over-identify the system, which is testable -- and the test is often ignored when it should be reported
a long-run restriction requires the relevant variable to be genuinely I(1); imposing it on a stationary variable is meaningless

cards.method: Panel and group local projections with Driscoll-Kraay errors
cards.when: estimating dynamic responses across many units, where cross-sectional dependence makes ordinary panel standard errors far too small
cards.when_not: there is one unit; the panel is too short in the time dimension for Driscoll-Kraay to be valid

alternatives.criterion: one time series
many units, common dynamics
responses differ by group and you want them separately

output_key_fields: irf: the pooled or per-group response
conf_band: bands robust to cross-sectional dependence
heterogeneity: variation of responses across units, where estimated
n_units, n_periods: the panel dimensions the inference rests on
interpretation_traps: Driscoll-Kraay standard errors need a LONG TIME DIMENSION; with short T they are badly undersized, which is the opposite of what they are used for
pooling imposes a common response; if the true responses are heterogeneous the pooled estimate is a weighted average that may match no unit
unit fixed effects in a dynamic panel introduce Nickell bias, which grows as T shrinks
sources: Jorda, Schularick & Taylor 2020 (Journal of Monetary Economics 112:22-40)

cards.method: Gregory-Hansen cointegration with a structural break
cards.when: testing for cointegration when the relationship itself may have shifted -- standard tests treat a break as evidence against cointegration
cards.when_not: the break date is known (use a dummy in a standard test); there is more than one break, which the test cannot accommodate

alternatives.criterion: no break suspected
one unknown break in the cointegrating relationship
the break date is known

output_key_fields: statistic: the supremum ADF, Za or Zt statistic
break_date: the estimated break
critical_values: from the non-standard distribution the test requires
model: which break specification -- level, trend or regime -- was fitted
interpretation_traps: the critical values are NOT the standard Engle-Granger ones; using them badly over-rejects and manufactures cointegration
the test allows ONE break; with two or more it loses power and can fail to reject when cointegration with breaks is present
the break date is estimated with wide uncertainty and should not be reported as if it were known
